(أوتوا): past verb, passive, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (نصيبا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (من الكتاب): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (نصيبا). (يدعون): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), passive, with its nāʾib fāʿil. (إلى كتاب): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يدعون). (الله): the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive. (اللام): the lām of causation. (يحكم): imperfect verb, accusative by (أن) implied after the lām, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (بين): adverb of place, accusative, attached to (يحكم), and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يحكم) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (يدعون).
(ثمّ): conjunction. (يتولّى): imperfect verb, nominative; the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma on the alif. (فريق): fāʿil, nominative. (من): preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun ل (نصيبا), (يدعون) imperfect verb, nominative, passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (إلى in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt of فريق «[Translator's note: the printed text is garbled here: material from the parsing of (من الكتاب) and (يدعون) above has intruded; the intended sense is evidently: (من) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt of فريق.]». (الواو): of the ḥāl (circumstantial). (هم): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (معرضون): khabar (predicate), nominative; the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «ألم تر..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أوتوا..» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يدعون..» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the relative الذين أوتوا.
The clause «يحكم ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يتولّى فريق» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يدعون.
The clause «هم معرضون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from فريق منهم.

* Morphology:
(نصيبا): the noun from أنصبه, said when one assigns him a share and portion; its pattern is فعيل (al-Baqara 202).
(يدعون): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion: the lām of the word, the alif, was deleted because it came quiescent before the quiescent wāw of the plural; its pattern is يفعون with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn (see al-Baqara 221).

* Benefits:
1- لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ: the lām is the lām of causation (lām al-taʿlīl). The difference between it and the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd) lies in two matters:
First, it comes in an affirmative context, while the lām of denial comes in a negative context. Second, both of them make the verb accusative by an أن implied after them, but أن is implied optionally after the lām of causation and obligatorily after the lām of denial.
2- The Messenger ﷺ called the Jews to Islam; they asked him about his religion and he answered them that he was upon the creed of Ibrāhīm. The Jews claimed that Ibrāhīm was a Jew, so he asked them to take the Torah as judge, and they refused.
3- In His saying, the Exalted, «مِنَ الْكِتابِ», this مِن is partitive, and it has been said it is explicative; it contains an indication that the Jews had an ample share of the Torah.

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلك): a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject); the reference is to the turning away..
(اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) is for address. (الباء): preposition. (أنّ): a particle resembling the verb, and (هم) is a pronoun, the noun of أنّ. (قالوا): past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم قالوا) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك).
(لن): accusative-governing particle. (تمسّ): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and (نا) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (النار): fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (إلّا): particle of restriction. (أيّاما): adverb of time, accusative, attached to (تمسّنا). (معدودات): naʿt (adjective) of أيام, accusative like it; the sign of the accusative is the kasra. (الواو): conjunction. (غرّ): past verb, and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (في دين): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (غرّ), and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (ما): a relative noun in the position of nominative as fāʿil — or a maṣdar particle, the interpreted maṣdar being the fāʿil. (كانوا): an incomplete past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the noun of kāna. (يفترون): imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive and causal.
The clause «قالوا..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «لن تمسّنا النار» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «غرّهم.. ما كانوا» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause قالوا.
The clause «كانوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the nominal or particle relative (ما).
The clause «يفترون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of kāna.

* Morphology:
(معدودات): plural of معدود, passive participle from the verb عدّ on the pattern مفعول (al-Baqara 203).
(يفترون): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is يفتريون: the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made quiescent by transferring its vowel to the rāʾ; then the yāʾ was deleted because it was quiescent and the wāw after it was quiescent.. Its pattern is يفتعون.

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء): resumptive. (كيف): an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "صنعهم" or "حالهم" «[Note: It may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) by an omitted verb, its implied form being "يصنعون".. The first implied form is more regular.]». (إذا): an adverb stripped of the conditional sense, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied mubtadaʾ, since it is construed as a maṣdar (verbal noun) «[Note: Or it is attached to the implied verb.]». (جمعنا): past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. (نا) is the fāʿil (agent), and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (ليوم): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جمعناهم), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "for the recompense of a day". (لا): the lā of generic negation. (ريب): the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative. (في): preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the omitted khabar of lā. (الواو): conjunction. (وفّيت): past verb, passive..
and (التاء) is for the feminine. (كلّ): nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative. (نفس): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive. (ما): a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (كسبت): past verb.. (التاء) is for the feminine, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هي". (الواو): of the ḥāl. (هم): a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ. (لا): negating. (يظلمون): imperfect verb, passive, nominative.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «كيف (حالهم)» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «جمعناهم» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا ريب فيه» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of يوم.
The clause «وفّيت كلّ نفس» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause لا ريب فيه. In the clause there is an implied linking element, i.e. "every soul was paid in full in it".
The clause «كسبت» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "كسبته".
The clause «هم لا يظلمون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «لا يظلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم.

* Rhetoric:
1- With His saying «فكيف» the interrogative has departed from its literal meaning: it is a rebuttal of their saying mentioned above and an invalidation of what deluded them, by magnifying what will overtake them and making fearsome the horrors that will befall them, i.e. "how then will their state be?"

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(قل): imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "أنت". (الله): the Name of Majesty, a vocative of a single proper name (munādā mufrad ʿalam) from which the vocative particle has been omitted, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of accusative; (الميم) with shadda is redundant (zāʾida), a compensation for the vocative particle. (مالك): badal (substitute) from the Name of Majesty, following its position in the accusative because it is a muḍāf «[Note: Or it is a second vocative, accusative.. and the clause is a badal from the first vocative clause.. Abū Ḥayyān chose this.]». (الملك): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (تؤتي): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت". (الملك): first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (من): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi. (تشاء): imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "أنت". (الواو): conjunction. (تنزع الملك): like تؤتي الملك. (من): preposition. (من): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تنزع). (تشاء): like the first. (الواو): conjunction in both places. (تعزّ من تشاء، تذلّ من تشاء): like تؤتي.. من تشاء. (بيد): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). (الكاف): a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الخير): postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, the noun of إنّ. (على كلّ): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قدير. (شيء): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (قدير): the khabar of إنّ, nominative.
The clause «قل..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «the vocative and what is within its scope» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «تؤتي الملك» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «تشاء (the first)» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (من).
The clause «تنزع الملك» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause تؤتي.
The clause «تشاء (the second)» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (من).
The clause «تعز» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause تؤتي.
The clause «تشاء (the third)» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the third relative (من).
The clause «تذلّ» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause تؤتي.
The clause «تشاء (the fourth)» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the fourth relative (من).
The clause «بيدك الخير» has no grammatical position, being a badal from the clause تؤتي الملك «[Note: Or it is resumptive.]».
The clause «انّك.. قدير» has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(مالك): active participle from ملك; its pattern is فاعل (see al-Fātiḥa, verse 4).
(الملك): either a noun meaning "what is owned" or a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb ملك يملك, of the ضرب class; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.
(الخير): either a noun meaning "what is good" or a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the verb خار يخير, of the ضرب class; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Iktifāʾ (sufficing with one of two): in His saying «بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ», where He singled out good for mention — though evil too is [in His hand] — intending both good and evil, and sufficed with one of them because it points to the other, as in His saying, the Exalted, «سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الْحَرَّ», i.e. "and the cold". He singled out good for mention only because it is what is desired.
2- In the verse there is «the art of muqābala (sustained antithesis)»: He set in contrast «تؤتي» and «تنزع», and «تعز» and «تذل».

* Benefits:
1- قل اللهمّ: the word «اللهم» is a vocative from which the yāʾ of the vocative has been deleted and compensated by the doubled mīm; this treatment is peculiar to the Name of Majesty. The doubled mīm may be joined to the Name of Majesty in two other cases besides the vocative:
The first: that it comes before a particle of reply, to strengthen the reply, as when you say to someone asking about a matter «اللهم نعم» (Yes, by Allah / Indeed yes).
The second: to indicate the rarity of the thing's occurrence, as when you say to someone whose ability in trade you doubt: "You will make a profit — اللهم (only) if you study the affairs of the market and choose your goods well."
2- The compound antithesis «al-muqābala» has spanned the two verses in their entirety, and it has spread through the atmosphere of these two verses a kind of inimitable Quranic music; it has also established contrasting meanings, thereby making them clearer and bringing the absolute power of Allah in all circumstances nearer to the mind.

safi-cedvel:27-27.t:
* I'rab:
(تولج): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت". (الليل): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (في النهار): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تولج). (الواو): conjunction. (تولج النهار في الليل): like تولج الليل في النهار. (الواو): conjunction. (تخرج): like تولج. (الحيّ): mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (من الميّت): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تخرج). (الواو): conjunction. (تخرج الميّت من الحيّ): like تخرج الحيّ من الميّت. (الواو): conjunction. (ترزق): like تولج. (من): a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (تشاء): like تولج. (بغير): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of تشاء «[Note: I.e. "whomever You will to provide for, being generous".. or from the object, i.e. "whomever You will, being honoured" (mukram, with fatḥa on the rāʾ)..
It may also be attached to a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) governed by ترزق, i.e. "You provide him a provision without reckoning", or "You provide him abundantly without reckoning"..]». (حساب): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).
The clause «تولج ... (the first)» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تولج ... the second» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «تخرج (the first)» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «تخرج (the second)» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ترزق» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «تشاء» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).

* Morphology:
(تولج): it contains deletion of the hamza for lightening, like تنفق and تكرم; its origin is تؤولج, with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the hamza.
(الحيّ): an assimilate adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from حيي يحيى, of the فرح class; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn (see al-Baqara 255).

* Rhetoric:
1- The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): if by the living and the dead He meant the Muslim and the unbeliever.
For it has been said in the exegesis of this verse: "You bring forth the believer from the unbeliever and the unbeliever from the believer." If this meaning is intended, the verse contains an explicit metaphor; and if the sperm-drop and the egg are intended, the speech runs on the side of literal truth, not on the side of figurative usage.

safi-cedvel:28-28.t:
* I'rab:
(لا): the prohibitive, jussive-governing lā. (يتّخذ): imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. (المؤمنون): fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); the sign of the nominative is the wāw. (الكافرين): first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ. (أولياء): second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; it does not take tanwīn because it is assimilated to nouns ending in the extended alif of the feminine, on the pattern أفعلاء. (من دون): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أولياء «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from المؤمنين, i.e. "passing over".. It may also be attached to the verb يتّخذ, with (من) for the beginning of the extent.]». (المؤمنين): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ. (الواو): parenthetical. (من): a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (يفعل): imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (ذا): a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) is for address. (الفاء): linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (ليس): an incomplete past verb; its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring back to the conditional noun. (من الله): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from شيء — an adjective that has been placed before the noun it qualifies — i.e. "he is not upon anything of the religion of Allah", so there is an omitted muḍāf in the speech. (في شيء): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of ليس. (إلا): particle of restriction. (أن): maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle. (تتّقوا): imperfect verb, accusative; the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (من): preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تتّقوا). (تقاة): mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, standing in for the maṣdar because it meets it in derivation «[Note: It may be accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "that you fear from them something or a matter that must be guarded against".]».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تتّقوا..) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), its governor being لا يتّخذ, i.e. "let the believer not take the unbeliever as a protector for any reason whatsoever except outward guarding" «[Note: See verse (229) of Sūrat al-Baqara and the i'rab of (إلّا) there, and see the footnote on the construal of the exception.]»; the exception in this case is emptied (mufarragh) for the mafʿūl li-ajlihi.
(الواو): conjunction. (يحذّر): imperfect verb, nominative, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الله): the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (نفس): mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): resumptive. (إلى الله): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (المصير): postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative.
The clause «لا يتّخذ المؤمنون» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «من يفعل (the nominal one)» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.
The clause «يفعل ذلك» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.]».
The clause «ليس من الله» في شيء is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «تتّقوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يحذركم الله..» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «إلى الله المصير» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(أولياء): plural of وليّ, on the measure فعيل, an assimilate adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) formed irregularly, taken from the quadriliteral والى (al-Baqara 107).
(تقاة): it contains ibdāl (letter substitution) and iʿlāl (weak-letter change). The ibdāl is the changing of the wāw into tāʾ; its origin is وقية, taken from الوقاية. The iʿlāl is the changing of the yāʾ into alif because it is voweled and what precedes it has fatḥa. Its pattern is فعلة with ḍamma on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn. In al-Mukhtār: تقى يتقي like قضى يقضي; التقوى and التقى are one thing, and التقاة is التقية; one says اتّقى تقية وتقاة. In al-Qāmūs:
تقيت الشيء أتّقيه, of the ضرب class.

* Rhetoric:
1- «إِلَّا أَنْ تَتَّقُوا», in the form of address by way of iltifāt (shift of person) from the third person, is an emptied exception from the most general of states; the governor is the verb of prohibition, with address taken into account in it, as if it were said: "Do not take them as protectors, outwardly or inwardly, in any state whatever, except the state of your guarding yourselves."
2- «وَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمَصِيرُ»: using the overt noun where a pronoun would be expected, to cultivate awe and instil dread.

* Benefits:
1- We cannot but draw attention to this kind of eloquence, namely this iltifāt from the absent to the addressed, and the profound effect it produces in the soul of the hearer. How many are the rhetorical features of the Qur'an!
2- A lesson in warning: some of the Anṣār used to take Jews as allies and supporters, and they used to declare that openly in the presence of the Messenger and not conceal it. Allah and His Messenger knew the cunning of the Jews and the enmity they harboured towards Islam and the Muslims, so this verse was revealed warning the Muslims and cautioning them against taking unbelievers as protectors.

safi-cedvel:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(قل): imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت". (إن): jussive-governing conditional particle. (تخفوا): imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm); the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (في صدور): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما, and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (أو): conjunction. (تبدوا): imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and parsed like it, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (يعلم): imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and (الهاء) is mafʿūl bihi. (الله): the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (الواو): resumptive. (يعلم): imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "هو". (ما): like the first. (في السموات): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila of ما. (الواو): conjunction. (في الأرض): like في السموات and conjoined to it. (الواو): resumptive. (الله): the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (على كلّ): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قدير). (شيء): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (قدير): khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative.
The clause «قل..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ان تخفوا..» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «تبدوه» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause تخفوا.
The clause «يعلمه الله» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يعلم ما في السموات» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «الله على كلّ شيء قدير» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(تخفوا): it contains deletion of the hamza for lightening; its origin is تؤخفيوا..
It also contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by making quiescent and iʿlāl by deletion: the yāʾ was made quiescent because the ḍamma on it was felt heavy, then it was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, the quiescent yāʾ and the quiescent wāw of the plural. Its pattern is تفعوا with ḍamma on the tāʾ (see al-Baqara 271).
(تبدوه): the same happened in it as in (تخفوا): deletion of the hamza, iʿlāl by making quiescent and iʿlāl by deletion.

* Benefits:
1- The wāw in His saying, the Exalted, «وَيَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ» is the resumptive wāw. The speech was brought as a new start rather than conjoined because the knowledge of Allah the Exalted is not dependent on a condition; it is of the type of mentioning the general after the specific: He mentioned His knowledge of what is in people's breasts, then followed that by mentioning His knowledge of everything.

safi-cedvel:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(يوم): mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" «[Note: Or it is attached to (تودّ), which is what Abū Ḥayyān chose; he judged weak attaching it to (قدير), since His power over everything is not confined to one day rather than another.]». (تجد): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (كلّ): fāʿil (agent), nominative. (نفس): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (عملت): past verb.. (التاء) is the tāʾ of the feminine, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هي". (من خير): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied object of عملت. (محضرا): ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb), from ما, its governor being تجد «[Note: It may be a second object of the verb تجد if it is construed as a verb of the heart.]». (الواو): conjunction. (ما عملت من سوء): like ما عملت من خير «[Note: ما may not be conditional with its apodosis being the clause تودّ with an implied fāʾ, i.e. "then it will wish".]». (تودّ): imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هي". (لو): a non-jussive conditional particle of "impossibility for impossibility" «[Note: The basic rule for (لو) when it comes after the verb ودّ and what has its meaning is that it is maṣdar-forming; that is ruled out here because of the presence of the maṣdar particle (أنّ).]». (أنّ): a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis. (بين): adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and (ها) is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunction. (بين): like the first and conjoined to it, and (الهاء) is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (أمدا): the postponed noun of أنّ, accusative. (بعيدا): naʿt (adjective) of (أمدا), accusative like it.
The interpreted maṣdar from أنّ, its noun and its khabar is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being "ثبت", i.e. "the occurrence of a distant span between it and it were established".
(الواو): resumptive. (يحذّر): imperfect verb, nominative, and (كم) is an attached pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الله): the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (نفس): second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): resumptive. (الله): the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (رؤف): khabar, nominative. (بالعباد): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to رؤوف.
The clause «تجد كلّ نفس» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «عملت ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «عملت (the second)» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the first ṣila clause.
The clause «تودّ ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, its governor being تجد.
The implied clause «(ثبت حصول)» is in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of the verb تودّ «[Note: Abū Ḥayyān said in al-Baḥr: The apodosis of لو is omitted, and the object of تودّ is omitted; the implied form is: "it will wish for the distance between them — were there a distant span between it and it, it would be glad of that"... What the meaning requires is that لو أنّ and what follows it is governed by (تودّ), in the place of the mafʿūl bihi.]».
The clause «يحذّركم الله» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «الله رؤف بالعباد» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(محضرا): it contains deletion of the hamza for lightening; its origin is مؤحضرا. It is a passive participle from the quadriliteral verb أحضر; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(أمدا): a noun for the end-point of a thing, i.e. its limit; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(بعيدا): a derived adjective on the pattern فعيل, from بعد يبعد, of the كرم class (see verse 176 of Sūrat al-Baqara).

* Benefits:
1- We can regard the verb «تجد» in this verse in two ways. The first: that it is transitive to a single object, so that the relative noun «ما» is its object and «محضرا» is a ḥāl from the object.
The second: regarding it as transitive to two objects, the first being the relative noun and the second «محضرا».
2- His saying وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ: this expression is called mushākala (verbal correspondence), because Allah addresses people in what resembles their language and their selves, as in His saying, the Exalted, «وَيَمْكُرُونَ وَيَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْماكِرِينَ»; for Allah does not scheme, but the expression corresponds to the state of the unbelievers. The like of this is frequent in the Noble Qur'an, and it is one of the familiar features of Arabic.

safi-cedvel:181-181.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (سمع) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (قول) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (قالوا) a past verb and its agent; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (فقير) khabar (predicate), nominative; (الواو) a conjunction; (نحن) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (أغنياء) khabar, nominative; it is prevented from taking tanwīn because it is assimilated to the feminine nouns ending in extended alif (al-mamdūda); (السين) a particle of futurity; (نكتب) an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "naḥnu" (we), for majesty; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle «[Note: This i'rab is preferable so that the explicit maṣdar that follows (قتل) is conjoined to an interpreted maṣdar. It is also permissible for ما to be a relative noun, a direct object, with the returning pronoun omitted.]»; (قالوا) like the first.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما قالوا) is in the position of an accusative, a direct object, governed by the verb of writing «[Note: It is said that the writing is literal: the deeds of man are recorded in a book; and it is said that it is figurative, meaning the reckoning of man's deeds.]».
(الواو) a conjunction; (قتل) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the interpreted maṣdar, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الأنبياء) a direct object of the maṣdar قتل, accusative; (بغير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in قتلهم; (حقّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) a conjunction; (نقول) like نكتب; (ذوقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; (عذاب) a direct object, accusative; (الحريق) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «سمع الله ...» has no grammatical position: the response to an implied oath.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّ الله فقير» is in the position of an accusative: the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «نحن أغنياء» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause that is the object of the saying.
The clause «سنكتب..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قالوا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «نقول ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause سنكتب.
The clause «ذوقوا» is in the position of an accusative: the object of the saying.

* Morphology:
(الحريق) the noun from حرق يحرق, of the pattern (bāb) نصر; it means المحرق (with kasra on the rāʾ, i.e. "the burning one"); its wazn is فعيل. It may also be intended as the maṣdar (verbal noun), which is الحرق.

* Rhetoric:
1- «وَنَقُولُ ذُوقُوا عَذابَ الْحَرِيقِ»: tasting (الذوق) is perceiving flavour in the mouth. Originally it applies to what is taken in small amounts, not in large amounts, for the latter is called eating (أكل). Its use was then extended to the perception of all other sensible things and states, by way of implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya).
2- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq): between فقير and أغنياء.

* Benefits:
2- His saying: «وَقَتْلَهُمُ الْأَنْبِياءَ» «[Translator's note: the source numbers this point 2; there is no point 1.]». The grammarians have devoted a chapter to the governing action of the maṣdar, which we summarise as follows:
The maṣdar governs as its verb governs, whether transitive or intransitive. If its verb is intransitive, it needs only an agent, as in «يعجبني اجتهاد سعيد» (Saʿīd's diligence pleases me); here the maṣdar has been annexed to its agent, so سعيد is genitive in form and nominative in position. If it is transitive, it needs an agent and a direct object.
It reaches its object either by itself, as in «ساءني عصيانك أباك» (your disobeying your father grieved me), or by a preposition, as in «ساءني مرورك بمواضع الشبهة» (your passing by places of suspicion grieved me). Its agent may be omitted without the maṣdar bearing its pronoun, as in «سرّني تكريم العاملين» (the honouring of the workers pleased me): the maṣdar has been annexed to its object, and the agent is omitted optionally, i.e. «تكريم الناس العاملين» (people's honouring the workers).
Its object may be omitted, as in the saying of the Exalted: «وَما كانَ اسْتِغْفارُ إِبْراهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَها إِيَّاهُ», i.e. Ibrāhīm's asking his Lord for forgiveness.
The maṣdar governs as its verb does whether it is annexed (muḍāf), made definite with al-, or free of both al- and annexation.
The first is as in the saying of the Exalted: «وَلَوْلا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ», and the third as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: أَوْ إِطْعامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ أَوْ مِسْكِيناً ذا مَتْرَبَةٍ. As for the second, it is as in the poet's saying:
لقد علمت أولى المغيرة أنني ... كررت فلم أنكل عن الضرب مسمعا
(The vanguard of the raiding party knew that I charged and did not shrink from striking Misma.)
The condition for the maṣdar to govern is that it stands in place of its verb, as in «ضربا اللصّ» (strike the thief!), or that it is valid to put the verb, accompanied by the maṣdar-forming أن or ما, in its place. If you say: سرّني فهمك الدرس (your understanding the lesson pleased me), it is valid to say: سرني أن تفهم الدرس. If you say: يسرني عملك الخير (your doing good pleases me), it is valid to say: يسرني أن تعمل الخير. If you say: يعجبني قولك الحق الآن (your speaking the truth now pleases me), it is valid to say: يعجبني ما تقول الحق الآن. If past or future time is intended, it is construed as accompanied by «أن»; if present time is intended, it is construed as accompanied by ما, as has been shown.

safi-cedvel:182-182.t:
* I'rab:
(ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative «[Translator's note: the source reads «في محلّ رفع رفع مبتدأ», with رفع written twice.]», mubtadaʾ (subject); the (اللام) is for distance and the (الكاف) for address; (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle «[Note: It may be a relative noun in the position of a genitive governed by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك).]»; (قدّمت) a past verb ... and the (التاء) is for the feminine; (أيدي) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما قدّمت أيديكم) is in the position of a genitive governed by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك; the bāʾ is causal.
(الواو) a conjunction; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of anna, accusative (manṣūb); (ليس) an incomplete, non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb, its noun a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "huwa"; (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (ظلّام) genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of laysa; (اللام) redundant, for strengthening (al-taqwiya) «[Note: It may be a preposition attached to the intensive form (ظلّام).]»; (العبيد) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the intensive form ظلّام.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله ليس بظلّام ...) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the interpreted maṣdar ما قدّمت ...
The clause «ذلك بما قدّمت أيديكم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قدّمت أيديكم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما), or of the nominal relative.
The clause «ليس بظلّام ...» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar of anna.

* Morphology:
(ظلّام) one of the intensive forms (ṣiyagh al-mubālagha), derived from ظلم يظلم, of the pattern (bāb) ضرب; its wazn is فعّال with a doubled ʿayn. The apparent view is that it is a noun of attribution (ism mansūb) to wrongdoing (al-ẓulm), like حدّاد (smith) and نجار (carpenter), so that the verse does not entail negating only the abundance [of wrongdoing] without negating wrongdoing that is not abundant, which would be unsound.

* Rhetoric:
1- «بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ», i.e. because of your deeds which you sent ahead, such as killing the prophets.
What is meant by the hands is the selves, and expressing them by the hands is a case of expressing the whole by the part.
It is also said that what is meant by the hands is the evil deeds, and this is a case of mursal (non-metaphorical) trope (al-majāz al-mursal) whose relation is causality, because the hand is the cause of the deeds man commits.

* Benefits:
- His saying «لَيْسَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ»: prepositions are of three kinds: original (aṣlī), redundant (zāʾid) and quasi-redundant (shabīh bi-l-zāʾid).
a- The original is the one that needs something to be attached to and cannot be dispensed with either in meaning or in i'rab, as in «كتبت بالقلم» (I wrote with the pen).
b- The redundant is the one that can be dispensed with in i'rab, does not need anything to be attached to, and cannot be dispensed with in meaning, for it is brought to emphasise the content of the statement, as in «ما جاءنا من أحد» (not anyone came to us) and «ليس سعيد بمسافر» (Saʿīd is not travelling).
These are four particles: «من, الباء, الكاف and اللام».
c- The quasi-redundant: it cannot be dispensed with in wording or meaning, yet it does not need anything to be attached to. These are five particles: «ربّ, خلا, عدا, حاشا and لعلّ». It resembles the redundant in not needing attachment, and resembles the original in that its wording and meaning cannot be dispensed with. Whoever wishes to learn more about the places where these particles are redundant should consult their chapter in its proper place in the extended works of the grammarians.

safi-cedvel:110-110.t:
* I'rab:
(كنتم) a defective verb and its ism (subject). (خير) khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative (manṣūb). (أمّة) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (أخرجت) a past verb, passive.. the tāʾ is for the feminine, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هي. (للناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أخرجت). (تأمرون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (بالمعروف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تأمرون), (الواو) conjunction. (تنهون عن المنكر) like تأمرون بالمعروف, and the attachment is to (تنهون), (الواو) conjunction. (تؤمنون بالله) like تأمرون بالمعروف, and the attachment is to (تؤمنون). (الواو) resumptive. (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (آمن) a past verb. (أهل) fāʿil, nominative. (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (اللام) occurring in the answer of لو. (كان) a defective past verb, and its ism is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو, i.e. faith. (خيرا) khabar, accusative. (اللام) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (خيرا), (منهم) like لهم, attached to an omitted khabar. (المؤمنون) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw. (الواو) conjunction. (أكثر) mubtadaʾ, nominative - or a fronted khabar - and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاسقون) khabar, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw - or a postponed mubtadaʾ -
The clause «كنتم خير أمّة» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أخرجت للناس» is in the position of the genitive as naʿt (adjective) of أمة [Note: or in the position of the accusative as naʿt of خير ..., and it may be in the position of the accusative as a second khabar of the defective verb.].
The clause «تأمرون بالمعروف» is in the position of the accusative as a second khabar of the defective verb [Note: or in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of (خير أمة) - because the indefinite noun here has been qualified by the clause - or a naʿt of (خير أمّة), or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).].
The clause «تنهون ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause تأمرون.
The clause «تؤمنون..» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause تأمرون ...
The clause «آمن أهل الكتاب» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كان خيرا لهم» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «منهم المؤمنون» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
The clause «أكثرهم الفاسقون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause منهم المؤمنون.

* Morphology:
(الفاسقون), plural of الفاسق, an active participle from فسق يفسق, of the first and second classes, and of the fifth class; its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Muqābala (correspondence): in the verse is the art of muqābala, for ṭibāq (antithesis) is multiplied between «تأمرون» and «تنهون», between «المعروف» and «المنكر», and between «المؤمنون» and «الفاسقون».

* Benefits:
1- «لكان»: the lām occurs at the beginning of the apodosis of the conditional «لو». Just as the fāʾ occurs in the answer of the jussive-causing conditional particles, the lām occurs in the answer of لو and لولا, which are non-jussive, and it conveys emphasis.

safi-cedvel:111-111.t:
* I'rab:
(لن) a particle of negation and of the accusative. (يضرّوا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (إلّا) a particle of restriction [Note: Some permitted (إلّا) to be a particle of exception and (أذى) excepted from an implied mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: لن يضرّوكم ضررا الّا ضرر أذى (they will not harm you with any harm except the harm of annoyance).]. (أذى) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative, standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. إلّا ضرر أذى; the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif. (الواو) conjunction. (ان) a jussive-causing conditional particle. (يقاتلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (يولّوكم) like يقاتلوكم, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (الأدبار) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (ثمّ) a particle of resumption [Note: It is not far-fetched that (ثمّ) is a particle of resumption, as we shall see in Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt, because the speech is resumed ... or it is a conjunction [Translator's note: the source prints حرذ, evidently a misprint for حرف], conjoining the clause after it to the clause of the condition and apodosis, which is conjoined to the clause لن يضرّوكم.], (لا) negative. (ينصرون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), passive ... and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «لن يضرّوكم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إن يقاتلوكم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يولّوكم الأدبار» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لا ينصرون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(الأدبار) plural of دبر with two ḍammas, a primitive (jāmid) noun; its pattern is فعل with two ḍammas, or with ḍamma then sukūn, and the verb is of the class of نصر.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse is an art called «the art of clarification (fann al-īḍāḥ)», which is that the speaker says something whose surface is ambiguous, then clarifies it in the rest of his speech. The difficulty that the clarification resolves lies in the meanings of the rhetorical figures of the words and in their i'rab. On the surface of the verse there are two difficulties:
One of them from the side of the i'rab, and the other from the side of the meaning.
As for the one from the side of the i'rab, it is the conjoining of what is not jussive to what is jussive. The one from the side of the meaning is that the opening of the verse makes its ending (fāṣila) unnecessary, because their turning their backs at fighting is proof of their being forsaken, and being forsaken and victory do not come together. The answer is that Allah, Glorified is He, informed the believers that this enemy of theirs, if he fights them, will be routed; then He wished to complete the promise by informing them that, along with his turning away now, he will never be given victory in the future, so he is forsaken forever as long as he fights them.
2- We see in the verse «the art of suspension (fann al-taʿlīq)», which is that the speech is suspended for a time. For that reason the word «ثمّ» was chosen rather than the other conjunctions, because it indicates a delay that suits the imperfect verb's indication of the future.
3- The art of semantic correspondence (muṭābaqa maʿnawiyya) between the victory of the believers and the forsaking of the disbelievers.

safi-cedvel:112-112.t:
* I'rab:
(ضربت) a past verb, passive.. and the tāʾ is for the feminine. (على) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ضربت), (الذلّة) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (أينما) a jussive-causing conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (ثقفوا) or to the implied apodosis. (ثقفوا) a past verb, passive, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. (إلا) a particle of exception. (بحبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); it is excepted from all states, i.e.: they were abased in all states except in their state of holding fast to the covenant of Allah. (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of حبل. (الواو) conjunction. (باءوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (بغضب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil in (باءوا), i.e.:
clothed with wrath from Allah. (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt of غضب. (الواو) conjunction. (ضربت عليهم المسكنة) like ضربت عليهم الذلّة. (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); and (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address. (الباء) a preposition. (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the ism (subject) of أنّ. (كانوا) a defective verb ... and the wāw is the ism of kāna. (يكفرون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يكفرون), (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الواو) conjunction. (يقتلون) like يكفرون. (الأنبياء) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (بغير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يقتلون) [Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl of الأنبياء, i.e. wrongfully or unjustly.], (حقّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم كانوا ...) is in the position of the genitive governed by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.
(ذلك) like the first. (الباء) a preposition. (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle. (عصوا) like باءوا. (الواو) conjunction. (كانوا) like the first. (يعتدون) like يكفرون.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما عصوا) is in the position of the genitive governed by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted khabar of the (second) mubtadaʾ ذلك.
The clause «ضربت عليهم الذلّة» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ثقفوا» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) ... and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: أينما ثقفوا ذلّوا (wherever they are found, they are abased).
The clause «باءوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ضربت ...
The clause «ضربت.. المسكنة» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the (first) clause ضربت.
The clause «كانوا يكفرون ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of أنّ.
The clause «يكفرون ...» is in the position of the accusative as khabar of كانوا.
The clause «يقتلون ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause يكفرون.
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم (in both instances)» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «عصوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative.
The clause «كانوا يعتدون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause عصوا.
The clause «يعتدون» is in the position of the accusative as khabar of كانوا.

* Morphology:
See verse (61) of Sūrat al-Baqara, for it contains most of the morphological points of the words occurring in this verse.

* Rhetoric:
1- «ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَسْكَنَةُ» this is from the pitching (ḍarb) of tents and domes.
So in it is an implicit, imaginative metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya takhyīliyya); and the encompassing of abasement and its enveloping them may be likened to that by way of the dependent metaphor (istiʿāra tabaʿiyya).
2- «إِلَّا بِحَبْلٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَحَبْلٍ مِنَ النَّاسِ» i.e. they are not safe from abasement in any state except in the state of their holding fast to Allah the Exalted, or to His Book which came to them, and to the protection (dhimma) of the Muslims, for by that they are safe.
He likened holding fast to the means of safety to holding fast to a firm rope let down from a high place. This is by way of the representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya).

* Benefits:
1- His saying, the Exalted: إِلَّا بِحَبْلٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ the speech does not stand straight except by means of an implied construction, since we must ask about the reason for the presence of the bāʾ and the cause of this exception. Although the grammarians have spoken a great deal on this matter, the presence of the bāʾ stands straight merely with this implied construction: «except if they are found protected by a rope from Allah or having entered into a protection from the Muslims». In this case abasement and wretchedness are lifted from them and they are saved from the wrath of Allah.

safi-cedvel:113-113.t:
* I'rab:
(ليس) an inflexible (jāmid) defective past verb, and (الواو) a pronoun in the position of the nominative as the ism (subject) of ليس [Note: The pronoun refers back to the People of the Book mentioned previously.], (سواء) khabar (predicate) of ليس, accusative (manṣūb). (من أهل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar. (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (أمّة) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (قائمة) naʿt (adjective) of أمة, nominative like it. (يتلون) an imperfect verb, nominative..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (آيات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the kasra. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. (آناء) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يتلون), (الليل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. (يسجدون) like يتلون.
The clause «ليسوا سواء» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «من أهل الكتاب أمّة» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) or explicative [Note: it explains the manner of their not being equal.].
The clause «يتلون» is in the position of the nominative as naʿt of أمّة, or in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «هم يسجدون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl of the wāw in يتلون.
The clause «يسجدون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم.

* Morphology:
(قائمة), feminine of قائم, an active participle from قام يقوم, of the class of نصر. In it the weak letter is regularly changed (ibdāl) into a hamza after the alif of the pattern فاعل. (See verse 18 of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān).
(آناء), plural of أنى with fatḥa on the hamza and the nūn, on the measure of عصا; or إنى with kasra on the hamza and fatḥa on the nūn, on the measure of معى; or أني with fatḥa then sukūn, on the measure of ظبي; or إني with kasra then sukūn, on the measure of حمل; or إنو with kasra and sukūn with the wāw, on the measure of جرو ... So in آناء there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by qalb (conversion), since the yāʾ - or the wāw - was converted into a hamza because it came at the end of the word after a vowelless alif. It is a primitive (jāmid) noun indicating a time or period.

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope): in His saying, the Exalted, «أُمَّةٌ قائِمَةٌ يَتْلُونَ آياتِ اللَّهِ آناءَ اللَّيْلِ وَهُمْ يَسْجُدُونَ», i.e.: while they pray, because recitation is forbidden in actual prostration, and it is not right to praise by means of what has been forbidden. So He expressed the part, which is prostration, and intended the whole, which is the prayer. The relation of the trope here is partiality (juzʾiyya).

* Benefits:
1- ليسوا سواء: «سواء» is used as a predicate of one and more than one, and it means "equal" (مستو). «سواء» comes for equalisation (taswiya), and after it comes the hamza of equalisation, as in «سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ», and what follows the hamza is interpreted as a maṣdar; its implied form here is: your warning and its absence are equal to them. So the maṣdar is the mubtadaʾ and سواء is the khabar. «سواء» means "equal/even" (مستو) when a place is described by it, and the most eloquent usage in this case is to shorten it, so you say: «سوى» on the pattern «فعل», like ماء روى and قوم عدى.

safi-cedvel:66-66.t:
* I'rab:
(ها) a particle of alerting; (أنتم) an overt, detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (ها) like the first; (أولاء) a demonstrative, mabnī on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on its end, its appearance prevented by the original vowel of indeclinability, in the position of accusative as a vocative, the vocative particle having been omitted from it «[Note: This i'rab is not permissible according to the Basrans and Sībawayh, because it is not permissible to omit the vocative particle from a demonstrative; but al-ʿUkbarī, al-Suyūṭī and Abū Ḥayyān.. then al-Jamal in his gloss on al-Jalālayn, cited it according to the school of the Kufans, and we have chosen it because it does not conflict with the meaning and is far from forced interpretation.. Further, the demonstrative may be the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause حاججتم a ḥāl (circumstantial).. or resumptive, explaining the first clause; and they allowed the demonstrative to be a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), with the khabar being the clause حاججتم ... (See verse 85 of Sūrat al-Baqara).]», (حاججتم) a past verb, mabnī on the sukūn.. and (تم) a pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); (في) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (حاججتم) «[Note: It may be an indefinite noun qualified by a description, with the clause after it as its description.]», (اللام) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl of علم — a description that precedes what it describes; (علم) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ); (الفاء) conjunction; (لم تحاجّون) its i'rab was given in the previous verse; (في ما) like the first «[Note: (ما) may be an indefinite noun qualified by a description, with the clause after it as its description.]», (ليس) an incomplete past verb; (لكم به علم) the khabar of ليس, its ism, and a ḥāl of its ism, as given before.
(الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (يعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو; (الواو) conjunction; (أنتم) a detached pronoun, mabnī, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (لا) negating; (تعلمون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «أنتم ...» حاججتم has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The vocative clause «هؤلاء» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «حاججتم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).
The clause «لكم به علم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «لم تحاجّون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive one.
The clause «ليس لكم به علم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «الله يعلم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعلم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «أنتم لا تعلمون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause الله يعلم.
The clause «لا تعلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).

* Benefits:
1- Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said, regarding the words of Allah the Exalted «ها أنتم», that this hāʾ is changed from a hamza to ease pronunciation and to avoid repetition, and because the hāʾ is the sister of the hamza; this is a good view, with little strain or forcedness.

safi-cedvel:67-67.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negating; (كان) an incomplete past verb; (إبراهيم) ism of كان, nominative (marfūʿ); (يهوديّا) khabar of كان, accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the negation; (نصرانيّا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (يهوديّا), accusative like it; (الواو) conjunction; (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) with no governing effect; (كان) like the first, and its ism is a pronoun, its implied form being هو; (حنيفا) khabar of كان, accusative; (مسلما) a second khabar, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (ما كان) like the first, and the ism of كان is a pronoun, its implied form being هو; (من المشركين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar of كان.
The clause «ما كان إبراهيم..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كان حنيفا» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive one.
The clause «ما كان من المشركين» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive one.

safi-cedvel:68-68.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (أولى) ism of إنّ, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الناس) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (بإبراهيم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أولى, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa because it is prevented from

* Morphology:
«[Translator's note: The source text breaks off here mid-sentence and a «Morphology» heading is inserted; what follows is in fact the continuation of the i'rab.]»
(اللام) it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and it conveys emphasis; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ; (اتبعوا) a past verb, mabnī on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الواو) conjunction; (ها) a particle of alerting; (ذا) a demonstrative, mabnī, in the position of nominative, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the relative noun; (النبيّ) a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative or a description of it; (الواو) conjunction; (الذين) like the first and conjoined to it, in the position of nominative; (آمنوا) like اتّبعوا; (الواو) conjunction or resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (وليّ) khabar (predicate), nominative; (المؤمنين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «إنّ أولى الناس..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اتّبعوه» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (الذين).
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «الله وليّ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive one, or resumptive.

* Morphology:
(أولى): an elative (ism tafḍīl) from ولي يلي, of the ضرب class and the وثق class; its pattern is أفعل, and the alif is changed from yāʾ, so it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution.

safi-cedvel:69-69.t:
* I'rab:
(ودّ) a past verb, and (التاء) is the tāʾ of the feminine; (طائفة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (من أهل) a preposition and its genitive noun, naʿt (adjective) of طائفة; (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (لو) a maṣdar particle; (يضلون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The interpreted maṣdar (لو يضلّونكم) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being the verb ودّت.
(الواو) of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (ما) negating; (يضلّون) like the first; (إلّا) a particle of restriction; (أنفس) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (ما يشعرون) like ما يضلّون.
The clause «ودّت طائفة» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يضلّونكم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (لو).
The clause «ما يضلّون إلّا أنفسهم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «ما يشعرون» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the ḥāl clause.

* Morphology:
(طائفة): derived from طاف يطوف, of the نصر class; a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its own root-form; its pattern is فاعلة, and the weak letter was changed to a hamza, as happens with every hollow verb from which a word on the pattern فاعل is derived.
(يضلّون): the hamza of the past form was deleted in it for lightness, following the same course as ينفقون; the original form is يؤضللون (verse 26 of al-Baqara).

safi-cedvel:70-70.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أهل الكتاب لم تكفرون) like its earlier counterpart «[Note: In verse (65) of this sūra.]», (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تكفرون); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (أنتم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (تشهدون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
The clause «يا أهل الكتاب» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لم تكفرون» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «أنتم تشهدون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «تشهدون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).

safi-cedvel:71-71.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أهل الكتاب لم تلبسون) like its earlier counterpart «[Note: In verse (65) of this sūra.]», (الحقّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (بالباطل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تلبسون), the verb being made to carry the meaning of "you mix and blend"; (الواو) conjunction; (تكتمون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الحقّ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (أنتم تعلمون) like أنتم تشهدون in the previous verse.
The clause «يا أهل الكتاب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لم تلبسون ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «تكتمون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative.
The clause «أنتم تعلمون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «تعلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (أنتم).

safi-cedvel:72-72.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (قالت) a past verb.. (التاء) of the feminine; (طائفة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (من أهل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of طائفة; (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (آمنوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الباء) a preposition; (الذي) a relative noun, mabnī, in the position of genitive, attached to (آمنوا); (أنزل) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو, and it is the referent pronoun; (على الذين) like بالذي, attached to (أنزل); (آمنوا) a past verb, mabnī on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (وجه) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (آمنوا); (النهار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (اكفروا آخره) like آمنوا وجه ... and the adverb is attached to the verb اكفروا.. and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; (لعلّ) a particle resembling the verb, for hope, and (هم) an attached pronoun, the ism of لعلّ, in the position of accusative; (يرجعون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «قالت طائفة» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of the saying).
The clause «أنزل» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «اكفروا» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the request clause آمنوا.
The clause «لعلّهم يرجعون» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يرجعون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.

safi-cedvel:183-183.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, naʿt (adjective) of the relative noun in verse (181), or a badal (substitute) from it «[Note: Or it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم", in the position of a nominative, and the clause is resumptive.]»; (قالوا) a past verb and its agent; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (عهد) a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "huwa"; (إلى) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (عهد); (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (لا) negative; (نؤمن) an imperfect verb, accusative, its agent a latent pronoun, implied as "naḥnu"; (لرسول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نؤمن).
The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا نؤمن ...) is in the position of a genitive governed by an omitted preposition, implied as في, attached to (عهد), i.e. He enjoined upon us regarding not believing ...
(حتّى) a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition; (يأتي) an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (muḍmara) أن after حتّى, and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its agent a latent pronoun, implied as "huwa"; (بقربان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأتينا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتينا ...) is in the position of a genitive governed by (حتّى), attached to (نؤمن).
(تأكل) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (الهاء) a pronoun, direct object; (النار) the agent, nominative ... (قل) an imperative verb, its agent a latent pronoun, implied as "anta"; (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (جاء) a past verb and (كم) a pronoun, direct object; (رسل) the agent, nominative; (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاء) «[Note: Or attached to an omitted naʿt of رسل.]», and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (بالبيّنات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاء); (الواو) a conjunction; (الباء) a preposition and (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive, attached to (جاء), and it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to البيّنات with the preposition repeated; (قلتم) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and (تم) a pronoun, the agent; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (اللام) a preposition and (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive, attached to (قتلتموهم); (قتلتم) like قلتم, and (الواو) is redundant (zāʾida), for prolonging the ḍamma on the mīm (ishbāʿ), and (هم) a pronoun, direct object; (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle; (كنتم) an incomplete past verb and its noun; (صادقين) the khabar of kāna, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّ الله عهد» is in the position of an accusative: the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «عهد إلينا» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar of inna.
The clause «لا نؤمن» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the first particle relative (أن).
The clause «يأتينا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second particle relative (أن).
The clause «تأكله النار» is in the position of a genitive: naʿt of قربان.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قد جاءكم» is in the position of an accusative: the object of the saying.
The clause «قلتم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «قتلتموهم» is in the position of a jussive: the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if you are truthful, then why did you kill them. And the clause «كنتم صادقين» has no grammatical position: resumptive — or explicative — and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

* Morphology:
(قربان) a noun for everything by which one draws near to Allah; its wazn is فعلان with ḍamma on the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
1- His saying «تَأْكُلُهُ النَّارُ»: the grammarians parse «آل» «[Translator's note: so in the source, written «آل»; the definite article «ال» is meant.]» as being for prior acquaintance (al-ʿahd). This leads us to review what the grammarians and lexicographers have said about this particle «ال». Although the scholars' statements on this matter are many and scattered, we shall present to the reader a brief, concise summary covering the aspects of this word, because of its benefit to the inquisitive and to every seeker of knowledge.
The definite al-: it comes as generic (jinsiyya), redundant (zāʾida), and of prior acquaintance (ʿahdiyya), and all three are fit to be a sign of the noun. Here is their explanation:
1- The generic al-: it is of three types: a- that which is mentioned to state the reality and quiddity, and which the word «كل» (every) cannot replace, as in «الكلمة قول مفرد» (the word is a single utterance); b- that which comes for comprehending the genus literally and covers its individuals, as in «وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسانُ ضَعِيفاً»; this is the one that the word «كل» can replace, so we can say: وخلق كل إنسان ضعيفا (and every human was created weak), and the statement is correct.
c- that which is for comprehending the genus figuratively and for exaggeration, as in «أنت الرجل علما وأدبا» (you are the man [par excellence] in knowledge and refinement).
3- «[Translator's note: so numbered in the source; 2 is meant.]» The redundant al-: two types: necessary (lāzima) and not necessary.
a- The necessary is of three kinds:
a- That which has accompanied a proper name since its coining, whether by transfer (naql), like «اللّات» and «العزّى», or by improvisation (irtijāl), like «السموأل».
b- That which is in the noun for the present time, namely «الآن» (now).
c- That which is in the relative nouns, such as «الذي, التي and their derivatives» of dual and plural; it is redundant in all three because a single word cannot combine two kinds of definiteness.
As for the not necessary, which is the incidental (ʿāriḍa), it is of two types:
a- Occurring in poetry by necessity, or in prose anomalously (shudhūdhan). In poetry, as in the saying of al-Rammāḥ ibn Mayyāda:
رأيت الوليد بن اليزيد مباركا ... شديدا بأعباء الخلافة كاهله
(I saw al-Walīd ibn al-Yazīd blessed, his shoulders strong in bearing the burdens of the caliphate.)
As for its anomalous use in prose, it is as when you say: «ادخلوا الأول فالأول» (enter, the first and then the first).
b- That which is mentioned at the beginning of a proper name, pointing to its origin, such as «الحارث», «القاسم», «الحسن والحسين» and «النعمان». This is based on hearing (samāʿiyya), so no analogy is drawn from it.
3- The al- of prior acquaintance, which is of three types:
a- For mentioned acquaintance (al-ʿahd al-dhikrī): where the noun made definite by it has been mentioned before, as in «كَما أَرْسَلْنا إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا فَعَصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ».
b- For known acquaintance (al-ʿahd al-ʿilmī), also called «mental acquaintance (al-ʿahd al-dhihnī)»: where the noun made definite by it is already known, as in «إِذْ هُما فِي الْغارِ».
c- For present acquaintance (al-ʿahd al-ḥuḍūrī): where the noun made definite by it is present, as in:
«الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ». To this belong the qualifier of a demonstrative, as in «إن هذا الرجل نبيل» (this man is noble), and the qualifier of «أي» in the vocative, as in «يا أيها الإنسان» (O man).
4- The relative al-: it is a noun in the form of a particle, and it enters upon active and passive participles.
5- The al- that stands in place of annexation (iḍāfa): as in «وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوى», i.e. from its desire.
6- Writing «the definite al-» when it enters upon nouns beginning with lām.
a- If the definite al- enters upon a noun beginning with lām, it is written with two lāms, as in: اللحم (meat), اللبن (milk), اللجين (silver).
b- The relative nouns are all written with a single lām because of their frequent use, except for the dual of الذي, «اللّذين», which is written with two lāms; so reflect.

safi-cedvel:152-152.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) occurring in the answer to an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (صدق) a past verb, and (كم) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (وعد) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إذ) an adverb of past time, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (صدقكم); (تحسّون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (الواو) is the fāʿil, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (بإذن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تحسّون), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (حتّى) a particle of commencement (ḥarf ibtidāʾ) «[Note: They permitted it to be a particle of limit and a preposition, attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is دام, or to the verb تحسّونهم, i.e.: you were slaying them up to the time of your faltering, or that continued for you up to the time of your faltering.. and إذا in this case means إذ.]», (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition «[Note: It is permissible for إذا to mean إذ, and in that case it has no apodosis.]», attached to the apodosis «[Note: There are several views on the implied apodosis: it was said it is "you were defeated", and it was said "He withheld His help from you", and it was said "you were tested", and it was said "your situation became clear to you".. and Abū Ḥayyān chose that the omitted apodosis be "you were divided into two groups".. and what follows indicates it.]»; (فشلتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil; (الواو) conjunction; (تنازعتم) like فشلتم; (في الأمر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تنازعتم); (الواو) conjunction; (عصيتم) like فشلتم; (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (عصيتم); (ما) a maṣdar particle; (أرى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and (كم) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi; (تحبّون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما أراكم ...) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
(من) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (يريد) an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil a latent pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو), and it is the resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid); (الدنيا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif; (الواو) conjunction; (منكم من يريد الآخرة) like its counterpart above; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (صرفكم) like صدقكم; (عن) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (صرفكم); (اللام) of causation (taʿlīl); (يبتلي) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and its fāʿil is "he" (هو).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبتليكم) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (صرفكم).
(الواو) resumptive; (لقد) like the first one; (عفا) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif, its fāʿil a latent pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو); (عنكم) like عنهم, attached to (عفا); (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (ذو) khabar, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the wāw; (فضل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (على المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to فضل, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «صدقكم الله ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «تحسّونهم» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «فشلتم..» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تنازعتم..» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause فشلتم.
The clause «عصيتم» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause فشلتم.
The clause «أراكم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdar relative particle (ما).
The clause «تحبّون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «منكم من يريد..» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) - or parenthetical.
