(حبّ): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb حب يحب, of the ضرب pattern; its wazn is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn (see 165 of Sūrat al-Baqara).
(الشهوات): plural of شهوة, which is a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from the verb اشتهى; its wazn is فعلة, with fatḥa then sukūn; or it is an aurally-transmitted maṣdar of the verb شها يشهو or شهي يشهي, of the فرح pattern.
(البنين): a plural treated like the sound plural, because its singular is ابن, the form of the singular having changed in the plural; but it was treated as the sound plural: nominative with the wāw, and accusative and genitive with the yāʾ. The alif in ابن is additional, and it is a compensation for the deleted lām of the word, which is the wāw; its wazn is افع.
(القناطير): plural of القنطار. It is said that the nūn in it is radical, so its wazn is فعلال, with kasra on the fāʾ; and it is said that it is additional, because it is from قطر يقطر, of the نصر pattern, when it flows: silver and gold are likened to water in abundance and quickness of turnover; on this view its wazn is فنعال. There has been disagreement over the weight of the qinṭār in ancient and modern times, but most commonly it is a hundred raṭl.
(المقنطرة): passive participle of the quadriliteral قنطر; its wazn is مفعللة, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the two lāms.
(الخيل): a collective noun (ism jamʿ) having no singular from its own root; its singular is فرس. It is also said that its singular is خائل, and it is derived from الخيلاء (pride), like طير and طائر.
(المسوّمة): passive participle of the quadriliteral سوّم, and the tāʾ is for the feminine suited to the plural; its wazn is مفعّلة, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(الأنعام): plural of نعم — with fatḥa on the nūn and the ʿayn —; النعم is a collective noun having no singular from its own root; it is treated as masculine and feminine and applies to camels, cattle and sheep, and the plural is أنعام in consideration of its three kinds.
(حسن): an aurally-transmitted maṣdar of the verb حسن يحسن, of the نصر pattern and the كرم pattern; its wazn is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn (ayah 83, al-Baqara).
(المآب): its wazn is مفعل, with fatḥa on the ʿayn; its original form is مأوب, because it is from آب يئوب; then the vowel of the wāw, which is the fatḥa, was moved to the hamza, and it was made quiescent, and the wāw was changed to an alif because it was originally voweled and the letter before it has a fatḥa, so it became مآبا. It is a mīmī maṣdar meaning "return", and it may be a noun of place or a noun of time of the verb آب.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the ayah there is the device of murāʿāt al-naẓīr (congruity), which is that the poet or prose writer brings together a thing and what suits it, while dispensing with mention of contrast, so that it falls outside muqābala (contrast) and muṭābaqa (antithesis). In this ayah He, Glorified is He, has brought together most of the means of enjoyment that lead a person to become absorbed in temptation and to be led along by the urges of unruly souls; they have been made attractive to people and have enticed them with wonders and charms.

* Benefits:
1- Murāʿāt al-naẓīr: that is by enumerating the blessings of this world that man desires. It is counted among the semantic embellishments (al-muḥassināt al-maʿnawiyya) to which the souls of poets were drawn for a period of time. Folk poets still excel at this art and its like, and take it as a means of competing with their peers among poets.
2- القناطير «المقنطرة»: what is meant by the word «المقنطرة» is emphasis, as in their saying «ألف مؤلفة، وبدرة مبدرة» ("a thousand made into thousands, a purse made into purses"). And المسوّمة means «المعلّمة» (marked), from أسامها الله وسوّمها in the sense of "He pastured them".

safi-cedvel:124-124.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ) an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نصركم) in the previous verse [Note: It may be a badal (substitute) of His saying إِذْ هَمَّتْ in verse (122), because the story in both is one on this view ... There is great disagreement among the exegetes in the interpretation of this verse; I quote a summary of it from al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ of Abū Ḥayyān. He said: The apparent sense of this verse is its connection with what precedes it, because it is part of the story of Badr, and this is the view of the majority; so (إذ) is governed by (نصركم). It was also said that this belongs to the completion of the story of Uḥud, so His saying ولقد نصركم الله ببدر is parenthetical between the two passages, because of the urging to reliance on Allah and steadfastness in fighting that it contains. The argument for this view is that on the day of Badr the reinforcement of angels was a thousand, while here it is three thousand and five thousand ... And He said:
يأتوكم من فورهم, i.e. the reinforcement - meaning the reinforcement of the disbelievers - whereas on the day of Badr the Muslims went to them.], (تقول) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت. (للمؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تقول), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ. (الهمزة) for interrogation of denial (istifhām inkārī). (لن) a particle of negation and of the accusative. (يكفي) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle and of the accusative. (يمدّ) an imperfect verb, accusative, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (ربّ) fāʿil, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يمدّكم ربّكم) is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil of يكفي.
(بثلاثة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يمدّكم), (آلاف) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) [Note: It is well known that the tamyīz (specification) of a hundred and a thousand and their multiples is a singular in the genitive by annexation; so the numeral word is not given tanwīn except when the muḍāf ilayhi is deleted, as in this verse. The implied tamyīz in this verse is: ثلاثة آلاف ملك من الملائكة (three thousand angels from among the angels).], (من الملائكة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of the implied tamyīz, which is ملك. (منزلين) ḥāl (circumstantial) of الملائكة, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ [Note: i.e. Allah reinforces you with help in the state of the angels' descending to the earth ...].
The clause «تقول ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لن يكفيكم ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يمدّكم ربّكم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(منزلين), plural of منزل - with fatḥa on the zāy - a passive participle from the quadriliteral أنزل; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn. In the word the hamza was deleted from its beginning, just as it was deleted from the verb.

* Benefits:
- His saying, the Exalted: «أَلَنْ يَكْفِيَكُمْ»: the hamza is for interrogation of disapproval (istinkārī), and it has turned the negation into an affirmation. We have already seen that the hamza departs from its original meaning for which it was coined, which is interrogation. To fix that in the minds of readers, we return to establish it in detail. It occurs for eight meanings:
1- The hamza of equalisation (taswiya): it is the one that comes after the word سواء or what has its meaning, and is followed by a clause in whose place a maṣdar may properly stand, as in: «سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ» 2- Invalidating denial (al-inkār al-ibṭālī): it requires that what follows it - if the interrogation is removed - did not occur, as in His saying, the Exalted: أَفَأَصْفاكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ بِالْبَنِينَ وَاتَّخَذَ مِنَ الْمَلائِكَةِ إِناثاً.
3- Reproachful denial (al-inkār al-tawbīkhī): it is the one where what follows it did occur and its doer is blameworthy, as in: «أَتَعْبُدُونَ ما تَنْحِتُونَ».
4- Affirmation (taqrīr): it is your leading the addressee to acknowledge and confess a matter whose affirmation or negation is settled with him.
5- Mockery (tahakkum), as in «قالُوا يا شُعَيْبُ أَصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا» 6- Command, as in: «أَأَسْلَمْتُمْ», i.e. submit (أسلموا).
7- Wonder (taʿajjub), as in: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلى رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ؟ 8- Finding slow (istibṭāʾ), as in: أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ؟!

safi-cedvel:125-125.t:
* I'rab:
(بلى) a particle of answer, affirming the negated question: ألن يكفيكم.. (إن) a jussive-causing conditional particle. (تصبروا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the sign of the jussive is the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الواو) conjunction. (تتّقوا) like تصبروا and conjoined to it. (الواو) conjunction. (يأتوا) like تصبروا and conjoined to it, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (من فور) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأتوا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh). (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive as naʿt (adjective) of فور or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it. (يمدد) an imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (ربّ) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi. (بخمسة آلاف من الملائكة) like its counterpart in the previous verse. (مسوّمين) ḥāl (circumstantial) of الملائكة, accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «إن تصبروا..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تتقوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تصبروا.
The clause «يأتوكم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تصبروا.
The clause «يمددكم ربّكم» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(الفور), an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb فار يفور, of the class of نصر, meaning to hasten and hurry; from it comes فارت القدر, i.e. the pot's boiling intensified and its contents rushed to come out.. Or it is a noun meaning the immediate moment or the state in which there is no delay. Its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(مسوّمين), plural of مسوّم - with kasra on the wāw - an active participle from the quadriliteral سوّم with doubled ʿayn; its pattern is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn.

* Benefits:
1- بلى is a particle of answer like نعم. The particles of answer are:
«لا، نعم، بلى، إي، أجل، جلل، جير، إنّ».
Each of these particles has characteristics that we can address individually whenever the time comes for one of them.

safi-cedvel:126-126.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (ما) negative. (جعل) a past verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is the reinforcement. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (إلا) a particle of restriction. (بشرى) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif [Note: or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) if (جعل) is transitive to one object.], (اللام) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of بشرى. (الواو) conjunction. (اللام) causal (li-l-taʿlīl). (تطمئن) an imperfect verb, accusative by (أن) concealed after the lām. (قلوب) fāʿil, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الباء) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of القلوب [Note: or attached to (تطمئنّ).].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تطمئنّ قلوبكم) is in the position of the genitive governed by the lām, attached to an omitted verb indicated by the mentioned verb جعل; or it is conjoined to بشرى and was put in the genitive with the lām because a condition of the accusative was lacking.
(الواو) resumptive. (ما) negative. (النصر) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (إلّا) a particle of restriction. (من عند) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (العزيز) naʿt of الله, genitive like it, and likewise الحكيم.
The clause «ما جعله الله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause in the previous verse.
The clause «تطمئنّ قلوبكم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «the implied جعل» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the overt clause جعله.
The clause «ما النّصر إلّا» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:127-127.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) causal (li-l-taʿlīl). (يقطع) an imperfect verb, accusative by (إن) [Translator's note: thus in the source; the particle meant is أن] concealed after the lām, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو, i.e. Allah. (طرفا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (من) a preposition. (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (طرفا), (كفروا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقطع) is in the position of the genitive governed by the lām, attached to the "being" (al-istiqrār) to which (من عند) in the previous verse is attached, i.e. victory is from Allah in order to cut off a portion of those who disbelieved [Note: It may be attached to the maṣdar (النصر) in the previous verse, or to an implied verb, i.e. نصركم ليقطع (He gave you victory to cut off) or أمدّكم (He reinforced you), or to the verb نصركم mentioned in verse (123), what lies between them being parenthetical.].
(أو) a conjunction. (يكبت) like يقطع and conjoined to it, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو. (الفاء) conjunction. (ينقلبوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يكبتهم), and the sign of the accusative is the deletion of the nūn..
and the wāw is the fāʿil. (خائبين) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «يقطع ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يكبتهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يقطع; and the clause «ينقلبوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يكبتهم.

* Morphology:
(طرفا), a noun meaning a group or portion; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(خائبين), plural of خائب, an active participle from خاب يخيب, of the class of ضرب; its pattern is فاعل, and in it the weak letter is regularly converted into a hamza after the alif of فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
«لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفاً مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا» i.e. to destroy a group of them by killing and capture. He likened those of them who were killed and scattered to a thing cut off whose parts have been scattered and whose order has been disrupted. This is of the type of the explicit, dependent metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya).

safi-cedvel:128-128.t:
* I'rab:
(ليس) an inflexible (jāmid) defective past verb. (اللام) a preposition, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of the defective verb. (من الأمر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of شيء - a naʿt (adjective) placed before what it qualifies -. (شيء) the postponed ism (subject) of ليس, nominative (marfūʿ). (أو) a conjunction meaning إلى (until). (يتوب) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن) concealed after أو, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو. (على) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يتوب), (أو) conjunction. (يعذّب) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يتوب), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is "He". (الفاء) causal (taʿlīliyya). (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the ism of إنّ. (ظالمون) khabar, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتوب ...) is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to شيء; the implied form is: ليس شيء من أجلهم منك أو توبة عليهم من الله (nothing on their account is from you, or [it is] a turning in forgiveness to them from Allah).
The clause «ليس لك من الأمر شيء» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يتوب ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «يعذّبهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يتوب.
The clause «إنّهم ظالمون» has no grammatical position, causal.

* Benefits:
1- His saying, the Exalted: «أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ» is accusative by أن optionally concealed after «أو». Among the particles that put the imperfect verb in the accusative, «أن» is distinguished by governing the accusative both overt and concealed, and its governing while concealed is of two kinds: «optional and obligatory». The optional is in six places, or after six particles: the first is the lām of kay, which is the causal lām; the second is the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba), what follows which is a result of what precedes it, also called the lām of becoming (al-ṣayrūra) and the lām of outcome (al-natīja); the third, fourth, fifth and sixth are «the conjunctions الواو، الفاء، ثمّ and أو». The condition for its being in the accusative after them by concealed أن is that it is necessarily conjoined to a pure noun, i.e. a primitive (jāmid) non-derived noun. As for its being obligatorily concealed, that is after five particles:
The first: the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), which some called the lām of negation. The second: the fāʾ of causation. The third: the wāw of accompaniment (al-maʿiyya). The fourth: حتى the preposition which means إلى or the causal lām. The fifth: أو in whose place «إلى or إلّا» may properly stand, as in the saying of the poet:
لاستسهلنّ الصعب أو أدرك المنى ... فما انقادت الآمال إلا لصابر.
(I will surely make the difficult easy until I attain my hopes ... for hopes have yielded only to one who is patient.)

I would have liked to cite evidence for each of the places of the optional and the obligatory, were it not that this might take us out of the aim and moderation in what we are engaged in.

safi-cedvel:192-192.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّنا) its i'rab has preceded in the previous verse, and it is an emphasis of the preceding vocative; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of (إن); (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative, a fronted first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (تدخل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the sukūn, vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "anta"; (النار) a second direct object, accusative (manṣūb); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (أخزيت) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and (التاء) is the agent, and (الهاء) a pronoun, direct object; (الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative; (للظالمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (أنصار) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
The clause «ربّنا إنك ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, seeking mercy — or resumptive.
The clause «إنّك من تدخل ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «ندخل النار» «[Translator's note: so in the source; «تدخل النار» is meant.]» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar of inna.
The clause «قد أخزيته» is in the position of a jussive: the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ما للظالمين من أنصار» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
1- Making the Fire explicit in the place of a pronoun: to magnify its terror; and mentioning "causing to enter" in the context of punishment, to specify its manner and show the extreme of its horror.
2- In the verse is the device of prolixity (al-iṭnāb): which is the excess of wording over meaning for a benefit, in several ways, among them:
a- Mentioning the specific after the general: to draw attention to the merit of the specific.
b- Mentioning the general after the specific: its purpose is to convey comprehensiveness while giving attention to the specific.
c- Clarification after vagueness.
d- Repetition (al-takrīr): «ربّنا» is mentioned repeatedly, for humble entreaty, to show complete submission, and to present the acknowledgement of His Lordship, the Exalted, together with faith in Him.
e- Parenthesis (al-iʿtirāḍ): which is to bring, in the midst of speech or between two pieces of speech connected in meaning, a clause with no grammatical position for a secondary benefit.
And precaution (al-iḥtirās): which is every addition that comes to ward off something the speech might suggest that is not intended.
3- «وَما لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصارٍ»: in the verse is the device of putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun. He put «the wrongdoers» in the place of the pronoun referring to those made to enter, to blame them and to indicate that the cause of their entering the Fire is their wrongdoing and their putting things in other than their proper places.

safi-cedvel:193-193.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّنا) its i'rab has passed «[Note: in verse (191) of this sūra.]»; (إننا) like إنك in the previous verse; (سمعنا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn.. and (نا) is the fāʿil (agent); (مناديا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (ينادي) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ, its agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "huwa"; (للإيمان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينادي) «[Note: The lām is in the sense of إلى (to); it is said to be causal.. and it is said to be in the sense of the bāʾ.]»; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle «[Note: And the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of a genitive governed by an omitted preposition, namely the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun «[Translator's note: the footnote breaks off here in the source.]»]»; (آمنوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the agent; (بربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (آمنوا), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) a conjunction, linking the effect to the cause; (آمنّا) like سمعنا; (ربّنا) its i'rab has passed; (الفاء) a conjunction linking the effect to the cause; (اغفر) an imperative verb of supplication, its agent a latent pronoun, implied as "anta"; (اللام) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (اغفر); (ذنوب) a direct object, accusative, and (نا) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (كفّر عنّا سيّئاتنا) like اغفر لنا ذنوبنا, the preposition being attached to (كفّر), and the sign of the accusative in the object being the kasra; (الواو) a conjunction; (توفّ) an imperative of supplication, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and (نا) a pronoun, direct object, and the agent is "anta"; (مع) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (توفّنا); (الأبرار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «ربّنا إننا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption repeated to seek mercy.
The clause «إننا سمعنا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «سمعنا مناديا» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «ينادي ...» is in the position of an accusative: naʿt (adjective) of (مناديا) «[Note: attached to (ينادي). (أن) may be a particle of explanation (tafsīr), and the clause after it has no grammatical position: explicative.]».
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «آمنّا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آمنوا.
The clause «ربّنا (the second)» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, seeking mercy.
The clause «اغفر ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آمنا «[Note: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī made it a second direct object of the verb سمعنا.
It may be the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if You accept our faith, then forgive ...]».
The clause «كفّر ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اغفر.
The clause «توفّنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اغفر.

* Morphology:
(مناديا) active participle from the quadriliteral نادى; its wazn is مفاعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(توفّنا) it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion suited to the indeclinable form: in its imperfect it was يتوفّاه الله (Allah takes him [in death]), and the weak letter was deleted in the imperative; its wazn is تفعنا.
(الأبرار) plural of برّ, from the verb برّ يبرّ, of the patterns (bāb) نصر and ضرب; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn, and it is an adjective resembling the active participle (ṣifa mushabbaha) ... As for بارّ, the active participle of برّ, its plural is بررة, whose wazn is فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ, the ʿayn and the lām.

safi-cedvel:194-194.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّنا) its i'rab has passed «[Note: in verse (191) of this sūra.]»; (الواو) a conjunction; (آتنا) like قنا in the previous verse «[Translator's note: قنا occurs in verse 191, not 193.]»; (ما) a relative noun «[Note: It may be a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of an accusative, a direct object, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e.: the outcome of Your promise.]», indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (وعدت) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and (التاء) is the fāʿil (agent), and (نا) a pronoun, direct object; (على رسل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وعدتنا), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. on the tongues of Your messengers, and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) the prohibitive lā, jussive-governing; (تخز) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, its agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "anta", and (نا) a pronoun, direct object; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (تخزنا); (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of inna; (لا) negative; (تخلف) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its agent a latent pronoun, implied as "anta"; (الميعاد) a direct object, accusative.
The clause «ربّنا» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, of supplication.
The clause «آتنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause توفّنا in the previous verse.
The clause «وعدتنا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the nominal or particle relative (ما).
The clause «لا تخزنا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتنا..
The clause «إنّك لا تخلف ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) ...
The clause «لا تخلف ...» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar (predicate) of inna..

* Rhetoric:
1- In this noble verse is the device of «al-isjāl» (affirmation by record), an unparalleled device. Its definition is that the speaker intends some purpose and brings words that establish that purpose:
The Master, Glorified and Exalted, has recorded, on the tongues of His servants, the fulfilment of what He promised on the tongue of His Messenger, and that is in His saying «ما وَعَدْتَنا»; you find that this promise has become binding, its binding never to be undone.

safi-cedvel:164-164.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (منّ) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (على المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (منّ), the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ; (إذ) an adverb of past time, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (منّ); (بعث) a past verb, its fāʿil a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو); (في) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (بعث); (رسولا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (من أنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (رسولا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (يتلو) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the wāw, and its fāʿil is "he"; (عليهم) like فيهم, attached to (يتلو); (آيات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the kasra, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (يزكّي) like يتلو, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunction; (يعلّمهم) like يزكيهم; (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (الحكمة) conjoined to الكتاب, accusative like it; (الواو) of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (إن) lightened from the heavy (inna), inoperative; (كانوا) a deficient past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the noun of kāna; (من) a preposition; (قبل) a noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to the notion of "being settled" (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached; (اللام) is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), which signals that (إن) is lightened; (في ضلال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of كانوا; (مبين) a naʿt of ضلال, genitive like it.
The clause «منّ الله» has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «بعث ...» is in the position of genitive, (إذ) being annexed to it.
The clause «يتلو ...» is in the position of accusative, either as a ḥāl of (رسولا) or as a naʿt of it.
The clause «يزكّيهم» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يتلو.
The clause «يعلّمهم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يتلو.
The clause «كانوا ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the accusative pronoun in يعلّمهم.

* Morphology:
(ضلال): a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb ضلّ يضلّ, of the ḍaraba class (bāb ḍaraba); its pattern is فعال with a fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this noble verse there is an art among the arts of rhetoric known as the art of tajrīd (abstraction): the speaker extracts from something possessing a quality another thing like it in that quality, to intensify the perfection of that quality in it, as though it were more eloquent than simply describing it by that quality. Here it is in His saying «من», the preposition.

* Benefits:
1- In this verse there are two benefits worth pointing out:
First: «وَإِنْ كانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ لَفِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ»: this lām in the word «لفي» is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); its origin is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ), and it is called "distinguishing" only because it distinguishes between «إن» lightened from the heavy and the negative إن, as in «وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنا مُحْضَرُونَ». When «إن» enters upon a verb it is necessarily inoperative. Most commonly the verb is an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: وَإِنْ كانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ. It may be an abrogating imperfect verb, as in «إِنْ يَكادُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ». Less common than that is for it to be a non-abrogating past verb, and less common still for it to be a non-abrogating imperfect verb, which by consensus is not taken as a basis for analogy, as in «إن يرينك لنفسك».
Second: in the verse there is the art of tajrīd, which is that the speaker extracts from himself another who represents him in ability or otherwise, as in the saying of Shawqī:
قم ناج جلّق وأنشد رسم من بانوا ... مشت على الرسم أحداث وأزمان
(Rise, speak intimately to Jilliq [Damascus] and recite to the traces of those who have departed; events and ages have trodden upon the traces.)
Poets frequently resort to it at the openings of odes.

safi-cedvel:165-165.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial (al-istifhām al-inkārī); (الواو) resumptive; (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when" (حين), containing the sense of condition, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis قلتم; (أصابت) a past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (مصيبة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (أصبتم) a past verb and its fāʿil; (مثلي) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (قلتم) like أصبتم; (أنّى) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate), the meaning being (from where is this?); (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (قل) an imperative verb, its fāʿil a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "you" (أنت); (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (من عند) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (أنفس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (انّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (على كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قدير; (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (قدير) the khabar of inna, nominative.
The clause «أصابتكم مصيبة.» is in the position of genitive, (لمّا) being annexed to it.
The clause «قد أصبتم.» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of مصيبة.
The clause «قلتم.» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivizing condition.
The clause «أنّى هذا» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported by the verb "to say" (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قل» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «هو من عند ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «إنّ الله.. قدير..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Benefits:
1- «أو لمّا»: in this word three words have come together: the hamza of interrogation, the wāw of conjunction, and لمّا meaning "when". What concerns us in explaining this benefit is «لمّا», for it has three technical uses:
The first: that it is jussivizing; it is specific to entering upon the imperfect verb and puts it in the jussive. It is one of the four jussivizing particles that put a single imperfect verb in the jussive, namely «لم، لما، the lām of command and the prohibitive لا». Like «لم», it has the special property of converting the time of the imperfect into the past.
The second: it is specific to the past verb. The grammarians have two views about it: some say that it is an adverb meaning «حين» ("when"), and others hold that it is a particle linking two clauses, as in «لمّا جاءني أكرمته» ("When he came to me, I honoured him"). The third: that it is a particle of exception, as in «إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ»; this is specific to entering upon the nominal clause.

safi-cedvel:166-166.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (أصاب) a past verb, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "it" (هو), and it is the resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid); (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أصاب); (التقى) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الجمعان) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the alif; (الفاء) redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate), because the mubtadaʾ resembles a condition; (بإذن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ whose implied form is "it" (هو) «[Note: This is the choice of Abū Ḥayyān.. and it is permissible for the preposition to be attached to the khabar of ما, i.e. what befell you ...
occurred by Allah's permission.]»; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) the lām of causation (taʿlīl); (يعلم) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām, its fāʿil a latent pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو), i.e. Allah; (المؤمنين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعلم..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to what بإذن الله is attached to, because it is conjoined to it «[Note: It is permissible to attach it to an omitted verb, i.e. He did that as a test and so that He might know the believers.]».
The clause «ما أصابكم ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أصابكم ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «(هو) بإذن الله» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).
The clause «يعلم..» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the maṣdar relative particle (أن).
The clause «التقى الجمعان» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

* Benefits:
1- «فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ»: this fāʾ suggests that it links an apodosis, and an objector might object to that by saying: there is no apodosis except for a condition, and there is no condition in this verse. But we answer this objection by saying that, in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَما أَصابَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعانِ», «ما», even though it is closer to being a relative, is imbued with the spirit of condition and resembles it; therefore it was acceptable for the fāʾ to come in its answer, and thus it is established that the fāʾ links the answer.
2- The saying of Allah the Exalted: «يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ ما لَيْسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ» is decisive proof that speech is of two kinds, the speech of the tongue and the speech of the heart, and that the hypocrite always and forever shows what he does not conceal «[Translator's note: so in the source (يبدي ما لا يخفي); presumably "shows what he does not hold inwardly" is meant.]», and says words with his tongue while knowing the falsity and slander of those words and that they are entirely different from what he harbours in his heart; had he believed, he would have known that Allah knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal. «[Translator's note: this verse is part of the following verse (3:167).]»

safi-cedvel:167-167.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (ليعلم) like the one in the previous verse.
The interpreted maṣdar is genitive by the lām and attached to (mutaʿalliq) what the previous interpreted maṣdar is attached to, because it is conjoined to it.
(الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (نافقوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (الواو) conjunction - or resumptive -; (قيل) a past verb in the passive; (اللام) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (قيل); (تعالوا) an inert (jāmid) imperative verb ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (قاتلوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قاتلوا) «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of قاتلوا, i.e. fight, proceeding in the way of Allah.]»; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (أو) a conjunction; (ادفعوا) like قاتلوا; (قالوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (لو) a non-jussivizing conditional particle; (نعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "we" (نحن); (قتالا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو; (اتّبعنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. (نا) is the fāʿil, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (هم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject), in the position of nominative; (للكفر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أقرب); (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative «[Note: Or it is indeclinable on the fatḥa - according to some views - and it took on indeclinability from the adverb, since it became of the type of the compound adverb, like صباح مساء and بين بين ... [Translator's note: the wording of this footnote is garbled in the source (إذا أصح for إذ أصبح); translated according to its evident sense.]», attached to (أقرب); (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the tanwīn is the tanwīn of compensation (tanwīn al-ʿiwaḍ) for an omitted clause; (أقرب) khabar (predicate), nominative; (من) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أقرب); (للإيمان) like للكفر «[Note: The two prepositions, though identical in form and meaning, are attached to a single governor because it is specific to the elative pattern (afʿal al-tafḍīl), so it is equivalent to two governors; and they are للكفر and للإيمان.]»; (يقولون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (بأفواه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of يقولون, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ما) a relative noun «[Note: Or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of it.]», in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (ليس) an inert, deficient past verb, and its noun is a latent pronoun whose implied form is "it" (هو); (في قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of ليس, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (أعلم) khabar, nominative; (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun «[Note: Or a maṣdar particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive.]», indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (أعلم); (يكتمون) like يقولون.
The clause «يعلم الذين ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdar relative particle (أن).
The clause «نافقوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «قيل لهم..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause «[Note: It is permissible for it to be resumptive, with no grammatical position.]».
The clause «تعالوا ...» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) «[Note: Because it is originally the speech reported by the verb "to say" (maqūl al-qawl) ... The majority said that it explains an implied nāʾib fāʿil, i.e. "the saying was said".]».
The clause «قاتلوا ...» is in the position of nominative as a badal (substitute) from the clause تعالوا.
The clause «ادفعوا» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause قاتلوا.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لو نعلم..» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «اتّبعناكم» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivizing condition.
The clause «هم ... أقرب» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يقولون» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ليس في قلوبهم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «الله أعلم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يكتمون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the nominal or particle relative.

* Morphology:
(أعلم): an adjective on the pattern أفعل, but not for comparison (tafḍīl); it means عليم or عالم ("knowing") (see verse 140 of al-Baqara).

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz mursal (metonymic trope): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ ما لَيْسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ»,
i.e. they say with their tongues, the mouths being the place of the tongues; so He expressed the place and meant what resides in it. The relation is thus one of location (maḥalliyya).

safi-cedvel:85-85.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (من) a conditional noun making the verb jussive, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (يبتغ) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو; (غير) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) «[Note: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (دينا) — a naʿt (adjective) that preceded what it qualifies — and (دينا) is a mafʿūl bihi whose governor is يبتغ.]», (الإسلام) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (دينا) a tamyīz (specification) of غير, because it is a vague word «[Note: It may be a badal (substitute) of the mafʿūl bihi غير.]», accusative; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لن) a particle of negation that makes the verb subjunctive; (يقبل) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative (marfūʿ), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو; (من) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يقبل); (الواو) conjunction; (هو) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (في الآخرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to الخاسرين; (من الخاسرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ هو.
«[Translator's note: The source describes (يقبل) as nominative; after لن it is subjunctive (manṣūb).]»
The clause «من يبتغ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يبتغ ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من «[Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.]».
The clause «لن يقبل منه» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of a jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «هو ...» من الخاسرين is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the apodosis clause.

* Morphology:
(يبتغ): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion because of the jussive; its pattern is يفتع.

safi-cedvel:86-86.t:
* I'rab:
(كيف) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it carries the meaning of disapproval and deeming something far-fetched; (يهدي) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (قوما) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (كفروا) a past verb, mabnī on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; () an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كفروا) «[Translator's note: The parsed word is missing from the source here; it is (بعد).]», (إيمان) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (شهدوا) like كفروا; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (الرسول) ism of أنّ, accusative; (حقّ) khabar of أنّ, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الرسول حقّ) is in the position of genitive by an omitted bāʾ, attached to (شهدوا).
(الواو) conjunction; (جاء) a past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (البيّنات) fāʿil, nominative. (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (لا) negating; (يهدي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو; (القوم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الظالمين) naʿt (adjective) of القوم, accusative like it, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «يهدي الله» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفروا» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of (قوما).
The clause «شهدوا» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause كفروا «[Note: The clause may be the ṣila (relative clause) of an implied maṣdar particle.. with the interpreted maṣdar in the position of genitive, conjoined to the explicit maṣdar إيمان.. i.e. after their faith and their testimony that the Messenger is true.. As for conjoining the clause شهدوا to the clause كفروا, the implied sense is: how will He guide them after the two matters have come together, disbelief and testimony to the truthfulness of the Messenger.. Further, some allowed the clause to be a ḥāl, with قد implied.]».
The clause «جاءهم البيّنات» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause شهدوا «[Note: Or the wāw is of the ḥāl and the clause is a ḥāl, with قد implied.]».
The clause «الله لا يهدي..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يهدي..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Benefits:
2- كيف: it is the interrogative كيف; it is a vague, non-fully-declinable (ghayr mutamakkin) noun used to ask about the state of a thing, mabnī on the fatḥa. Questioning with it is of two kinds:
Real: as in «كيف حالك؟»; or not real, which is for several considerations. In this verse it is for negation, and it may be for wonder and disapproval, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ؟». As for its i'rab, it is as follows:
- It occurs as khabar of a mubtadaʾ, as in «كيف أنت»?; or as a fronted khabar of كان, as in «كيف كنت»; or as a fronted second object of «ظنّ» and its sisters, as in «كيف ظننت أخاك»; or as a third object of «أعلم» and its sisters, as in «كيف أعلمت فرسك», because the second of the two objects of ظنّ and the third of the objects of أعلم is originally a khabar. «[Translator's note: The source writes «خبر أنّ في الأصل»; the sense is "originally a khabar".]»
It may come before the bāʾ among the prepositions, which is then a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; so you say «كيف بخالد»: كيف is in the position of nominative as a fronted khabar, and بخالد: the bāʾ is redundant and خالد is a mubtadaʾ, nominative in position and genitive in form. It may be in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), as in the words of Allah the Exalted: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحابِ الْفِيلِ; and it occurs as a ḥāl, as in «كيف مضى أخوك», i.e. in what state did he go ... ?

safi-cedvel:87-87.t:
* I'rab:
(أولاء) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and (الكاف) a particle of address; (جزاء) a second mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of (أنّ); (لعنة) the postponed ism of أنّ, accusative (manṣūb); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) a conjunction in both places; (الملائكة، الناس) two nouns conjoined to the Name of Majesty, genitive like it; (أجمعين) a semantic tawkīd (emphasis) of what precedes, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ «[Note: See verse (161) of Sūrat al-Baqara.]» and the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ عليهم لعنة الله) is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ جزاء.
The clause «أولئك جزاؤهم..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جزاؤهم أنّ عليهم لعنة الله» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).

safi-cedvel:88-88.t:
* I'rab:
(خالدين): a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), of the pronoun in (عليهم) — in the previous verse — the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خالدين, and the pronoun refers to the curse, or to the Fire indicated by it; (لا) negating; (يخفّف) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative (marfūʿ); (عنهم) like فيها, attached to (يخفّف); (العذاب) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) negating, repeated to emphasize the negation; (هم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (ينظرون) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative.. and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «لا يخفّف عنهم العذاب» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in خالدين, or has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم ينظرون» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause لا يخفّف.. or has no grammatical position.
The clause «ينظرون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

safi-cedvel:89-89.t:
* I'rab:
(إلّا) a particle of exception; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as the excepted; (تابوا) a past verb, mabnī on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تابوا); (ذا) a demonstrative, mabnī, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address; (الواو) conjunction; (أصلحوا) like تابوا; (الفاء) causal (taʿlīliyya); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, ism of إنّ, accusative (manṣūb); (غفور) khabar of إنّ, nominative (marfūʿ); (رحيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «تابوا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «أصلحوا» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «انّ الله غفور» has no grammatical position: a causal explanation of something implied, i.e. فالله يغفر لهم إنّ الله غفور رحيم (so Allah forgives them; indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful).

safi-cedvel:90-90.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as the ism of إنّ; (كفروا) a past verb, mabnī on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (بعد) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كفروا); (إيمان) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (ازدادوا) like كفروا; (كفرا) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (لن) a particle of negation that makes the verb subjunctive; (تقبل) an imperfect verb, passive, subjunctive (manṣūb); (توبة) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (أولئك هم الضالّون) like أولئك هم الفاسقون «[Note: In verse (82) of this sūra.]».
The clause «إنّ الذين كفروا..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «ازدادوا..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «لن تقبل توبتهم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «أولئك هم الضالون» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لن تقبل.

* Morphology:
(توبة): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb تاب يتوب, of the نصر class; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn; and there are other maṣdars: توب without tāʾ marbūṭa, تابة, and متابا — which is a mīmī maṣdar — and تتوبة with kasra on the wāw.

* Benefits:
1- The commentators paused at length before the words of Allah the Exalted لن تقبل توبتهم, given that Allah has opened the door of repentance to His servants however much they have done wrong and sinned. Some of them got out of this difficulty by taking this verse to refer to the hour of death, «since a text has come concerning this specifically, so the repentance of one on the point of death is not accepted by the text of the Noble Qur'an».
2- The conjunctive wāw that precedes a condition conjoins this condition to another condition that is understood, as when you say «أكرم فلانا ولو أساء» (honour so-and-so even if he does wrong): honouring the wrongdoer entails honouring the doer of good, since he is more deserving of honour.

safi-cedvel:195-195.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (استجاب) a past verb; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb استجاب; (ربّ) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of anna; (لا) negative; (أضيع) an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "anā"; (عمل) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (عامل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (من) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of عامل; (من ذكر) a preposition and its genitive noun, a badal (substitute) from the preceding preposition and genitive noun, with the preposition repeated «[Note: Some allowed (من) to be redundant (zāʾida) because it rests on a negation, with (ذكر) accusative in position as a ḥāl (circumstantial) ... or the preposition and its genitive noun is a tamyīz (specification) of the second-person pronoun in (منكم).]»; (أو) a conjunction; (أنثى) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ذكر, genitive like it, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddara) on the alif; (بعض) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (من بعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ بعض.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّي لا أضيع ...) is in the position of a genitive governed by an omitted preposition, attached to (استجاب ...), i.e. their Lord answered them with [the assurance] that I do not let be lost ...
(الفاء) resumptive; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ; (هاجروا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, and the wāw is the agent; (الواو) a conjunction; (أخرجوا) a passive past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma ... and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (من ديار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أخرجوا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (أوذوا) like أخرجوا; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أوذوا), and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (قاتلوا) like هاجروا; (الواو) a conjunction; (قتلوا) like أخرجوا; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (أكفرنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of a nominative ... and the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis, its agent a latent pronoun, implied as "anā"; (عنهم) like له «[Translator's note: so in the source: «مثل له».]», attached to (أكفّر); (سيّئات) a direct object, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the kasra, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (لأدخلنّهم) like لأكفّرنّ ... and (هم) is the first direct object; (جنّات) a second direct object, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (تجري) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ; (من تحت) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from الأنهار, and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; there is a muḍāf omitted, i.e. from beneath its trees; (الأنهار) the agent, nominative; (ثوابا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar «[Note: It may be in the place of a ḥāl from the object pronoun in (أدخلنّهم), i.e. rewarded ... or a ḥāl from جنّات, i.e. given as a reward ... or a badal from جنّات, by making the verb include the meaning of أعطينّهم (I shall surely give them).]», because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) or a noun for that with which one is rewarded; (من عند) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt of (ثوابا); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (حسن) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الثواب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «استجاب ...» ربّهم has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا أضيع ...» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar of anna.
The clause «بعضكم من بعض» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from عامل, or in the position of a genitive, a naʿt of it «[Note: It may be resumptive, and so have no position ... or parenthetical, with the clause الذين هاجروا conjoined to the resumptive clause.]».
The clause «الذين هاجروا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هاجروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أوذوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause هاجروا.
The clause «أخرجوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause هاجروا.
The clause «قاتلوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause هاجروا.
The clause «قتلوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause هاجروا.
The clause «أكفّرنّ ...» has no grammatical position: the response to an implied oath ... and the implied oath clause together with its response is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين) «[Note: This is a refutation of whoever says that an oath clause cannot be the khabar of a mubtadaʾ.]».
The clause «أدخلنّهم..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that is the response to the oath.
The clause «تجري ... الأنهار» is in the position of an accusative: naʿt of جنّات.
The clause «الله عنده حسن الثواب» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «عنده حسن الثواب» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Morphology:
(أوذوا) it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion; its original is أوذيوا — with kasra on the dhāl and ḍamma on the yāʾ. The ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made quiescent and its vowel transferred to the dhāl; when two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ and the wāw of the plural, the yāʾ was deleted and it became أوذوا ... It contains another change: the conversion of the second hamza in the madda into a wāw when it was made passive. Its original is آذى — without the wāw of the plural — and in the passive أوذي with a yāʾ at its end; then the second hamza was lightened and it became أوذي; then the wāw of the plural was attached and it became أوذوا — after the change by deletion. Its wazn is أفعوا.

* Rhetoric:
1- «فَاسْتَجابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ أَنِّي لا أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عامِلٍ مِنْكُمْ»: in this noble verse there is a shift of address (iltifāt) from the third person to the first and second persons. That is to show complete attention to the matter of the answer and to honour those who call upon Him with the honour of being addressed. The intent is to confirm it by stating its cause and to indicate that it turns on their deeds, which they put forward before the supplication, not on supplication alone.
2- The close of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān has come beautiful and fine. Just as the close of Sūrat al-Baqara came comprising and containing supplication, the close of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān came comprising and containing a number of beneficial counsels. This is part of the excellence of the conclusion (ḥusn al-khitām), so that it remains firmly in the ears.

safi-cedvel:15-15.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb, and the agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (you); (الهمزة) for interrogation; (أنبّئ) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنا" (I), and (كم) an attached pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بخير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنبّئ); (من) a preposition; (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, attached to (خير); and (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address; (اللام) a preposition; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (اتّقوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of جنات «[Note: Or attached to the omitted fronted khabar; or attached to خير if the relative noun is attached to it and (جنّات) is parsed as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي".]» — an adjective that has come before the noun it qualifies —; (ربّ) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (جنّات) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative «[Note: Or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو".]»; (تجري) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (من تحت) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تجري), and (ها) muḍāf ilayhi; (الأنهار) fāʿil, nominative; (خالدين) ḥāl, accusative, of the relative noun, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (في) a preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to خالدين; (الواو) conjunction; (أزواج) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to جنّات, nominative like it; (مطهّرة) naʿt (adjective) of أزواج, nominative like it; (الواو) conjunction; (رضوان) maʿṭūf to جنّات, nominative like it; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt of رضوان; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (بصير) khabar, nominative; (بالعباد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to بصير.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أأنبّئكم» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «للذين اتّقوا ... جنّات» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) «[Note: Or in the position of a genitive as badal (substitute) of خير.]».
The clause «تجري من تحتها الأنهار» is in the position of a nominative as naʿt of جنّات.
The clause «الله بصير» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مطهّرة): feminine of مطهّر, a passive participle of the quadriliteral طهّر; its wazn is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn (ayah 25, al-Baqara).
(رضوان): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb رضي يرضى, of the فرح pattern; its wazn is فعلان, with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and kasra on it is permissible in the maṣdar.

* Benefits:
- The verbs that take three objects are «اعلم» and «أرى», on which there is consensus; Sībawayh added «نبأ» and «أنبأ»; al-Farrāʾ added in his Maʿānī «خبر» and «أخبر»; and the Kufans added (حدّث).

safi-cedvel:16-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative as khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم" (they) «[Note: Or in the position of a genitive: either as naʿt (adjective) of the preceding relative noun in the previous ayah, or as badal (substitute) of it; or as naʿt of العباد. It is also permissible for it to be in the position of an accusative by an omitted verb, with the intention of praise.]»; (يقولون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ربّ) the one addressed (munādā), with the vocative particle omitted, and it is muḍāf, accusative, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis, and (نا) a pronoun, the noun of إنّ, in the position of an accusative; (آمنّا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and (نا) is the fāʿil; (الفاء) a causal conjunction «[Note: Or linking the apodosis of a condition.]»; (اغفر) an imperative verb of supplication, and the agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت"; (اللام) a preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اغفر); (ذنوب) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and (نا) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (قنا) like اغفر, indeclinable on the deletion of the weak letter, and (نا) mafʿūl bihi; (عذاب) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (النار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «(هم) الذين يقولون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يقولون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «the vocative and its response» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّنا آمنا» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «آمنا» is in the position of a nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «اغفر لنا» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause آمنا «[Note: ʿAbbās Ḥasan said in his book al-Naḥw al-Wāfī, vol. 3, p. 464: "And it — i.e. the fāʾ — often conveys, along with order and immediate succession, causation, i.e. indicating causality (in that the conjoined element is caused by what it is conjoined to); and this predominates in two things: the conjoining of clauses, and in a derived conjoined element." End quote. It is permissible for the clause to be the apodosis of an implied condition.]».
The clause «قنا» is conjoined to the clause اغفر لنا and takes its grammatical position.

* Morphology:
(عذاب): a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from the quadriliteral عذّب, whose regular maṣdar is تعذيب; its wazn is فعال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ (al-Baqara 7).

* Benefits:
1- The verb whose first radical is weak is the "mithāl", such as وقى and وعد. When the imperative is formed from it, its fāʾ, which is a wāw or a yāʾ, is deleted; and since the imperative is indeclinable on the deletion of the weak letter from its end, the result will be that its fāʾ is deleted and its lām is deleted, as in وقى, which becomes ق, and وعى, ع, etc.

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(الصابرين) naʿt (adjective) of (الذين اتّقوا), genitive «[Note: in ayah (15) of this sūra; or of (الذين يقولون) (in the preceding ayah), in the two cases of the genitive and the accusative.]», the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (الواو) conjunction in the four places; (الصادقين، القانتين، المنفقين، المستغفرين) words conjoined to الصابرين, genitive like it, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (بالأسحار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) المستغفرين, for it is an active participle.

* Morphology:
(المنفقين): plural of منفق, an active participle of أنفق; its wazn is مفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn; it contains the deletion of the hamza for lightness, its original form being المؤنفقين «[Note: See ayah (3) of Sūrat al-Baqara, the word (ينفقون).]».
(المستغفرين): plural of مستغفر, an active participle of استغفر, and it is on the same wazn as the word المنفقين [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. formed the same way, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the letter before the last].
(الأسحار): plural of سحر, with two fatḥas, an underived (jāmid) noun; it was so named because of the hiddenness in it, as السحر (magic) is a name for the hidden thing; its wazn is فعل, with two fatḥas.

* Rhetoric:
1- Placing the wāw between the enumerated qualities indicates the independence of each of them and their perfection in them, or the difference between those qualified by them.

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(شهد) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis, and (الهاء) a pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative as the noun of أنّ; (لا إله إلّا هو) its i'rab has been given before «[Note: ayah (2) of this sūra.]».
The interpreted maṣdar from (أنّ), its noun and its khabar, is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, the implied form being: بأنّه لا إله ...; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) (شهد).
(الواو) conjunction; (الملائكة) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, nominative like it; and (أولو) maʿṭūf to the Name of Majesty by the wāw, nominative like it, the sign of the nominative being the wāw, for it is treated like the sound masculine plural; (العلم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (قائما) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the detached pronoun after إلّا «[Note: Or a ḥāl of the Name of Majesty, the agent of شهد.]»; (بالقسط) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قائما), the active participle; (لا إله إلّا هو) its i'rab has been given before; (العزيز) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو", and the clause is a badal (substitute) of the detached pronoun هو «[Note: Or a badal of the detached pronoun هو.]» [Translator's note: so in the source; the footnote presumably means العزيز alone as a badal of هو]; (الحكيم) a second khabar, nominative «[Note: Or a badal of العزيز, nominative like it.]».
The clause «شهد الله» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو» is in the position of a nominative as khabar of أنّ.
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, repeated for emphasis.

* Morphology:
(قائما): active participle of قام — in every hollow verb the weak letter is changed into a hamza in the فاعل form — and its original form is قاوم.
(القسط): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb قسط يقسط, of the two patterns نصر and ضرب; its wazn is فعل, with kasra then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the ayah there is radd al-ʿajuz ʿalā al-ṣadr (returning the end to the beginning): العزيز is returned to His words, the Exalted, «لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ», i.e. to His uniqueness in the Oneness that requires might; and «الحكيم» is returned to His words, the Exalted, «قائِماً بِالْقِسْطِ», for He, the Exalted, is Wise, and no injustice or deviation encroaches upon Him.

safi-cedvel:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إنّ الله): its i'rab has already been given «[Note: In verse (42) of this sūra.]». (يبشّر): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (بكلمة): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يبشّر). (من): preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of كلمة. (اسم): mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (المسيح): khabar (predicate), nominative. (عيسى): badal (substitute) from المسيح, nominative like it; the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma. (ابن): naʿt of عيسى or a badal from it, nominative like it «[Note: Al-ʿUkbarī said: "ابن مريم is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. هو ابن; it may not be a badal from what precedes it nor an adjective, because ابن مريم is not a name..." End quote. But the meaning in the verse may admit predication and may admit description of the word عيسى; and the retention of the alif in (ابن) in the Quranic orthography may be intended to treat ابن as a khabar, not an adjective — but the mubtadaʾ is then not the word عيسى but the latent pronoun هو.]». (مريم): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, because it is a diptote on account of being a proper name and feminine. (وجيها): ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), from the word كلمة. (في الدنيا): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (وجيها) because it is a derived adjective; the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied on the alif. (الواو): conjunction. (الآخرة): conjoined to الدنيا, genitive like it. (الواو): conjunction. (من المقرّبين): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl conjoined to the first ḥāl; the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «قالت الملائكة..» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يا مريم» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّ الله يبشّرك» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «يبشّرك» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «اسمه المسيح» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt of كلمة.

* Morphology:
(المسيح): some said it is a Hebrew word meaning "the blessed". Others said it is an intensive form of the active participle on the pattern فعيل, according to one of two views, because he traversed (masaḥa) the earth by wandering, or because he would wipe (yamsaḥu) one with an affliction and he would be healed; or it is فعيل with the meaning of the passive, according to another view, because he was anointed with blessing, or because he was flat-footed, or because his face was anointed with comeliness; then it was transferred from the adjective to the name.
(عيسى): it has been said that it is taken from العيس, which is whiteness overlaid with redness (and see verse 87 of Sūrat al-Baqara).
(وجيها): an assimilate adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha); its pattern is فعيل, from the verb وجه يوجه, of the كرم class.
(المقرّبين): plural of المقرّب, passive participle from the quadriliteral قرّب; its pattern is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

* Benefits:
- إذ is an adverb of time, e.g. «جئت إذ طلعت الشمس» (I came when the sun rose). It may be an adverb for the future, as in His saying, the Exalted, «فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ إِذِ الْأَغْلالُ فِي أَعْناقِهِمْ». It may occupy the place of the muḍāf ilayhi, so that a noun of time is annexed to it, as in His saying, the Exalted, رَبَّنا لا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنا. It is necessarily annexed to clauses, and part of the clause or all of it may be deleted and compensated for by the tanwīn of compensation, as in His saying, the Exalted, «فَلَوْلا إِذا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ وَأَنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ», i.e. "when the soul reaches the throat, you are looking on".
Some have added that it may be for causation, citing as evidence the saying of al-Farazdaq:
فأصبحوا قد أعاد الله نعمتهم ... إذ هم قريش وإذ ما مثلهم بشر
(So they came to be, Allah having restored their bounty, since they are Quraysh and since no human is like them.)
Likewise it is reported to be for surprise, namely the one occurring after «بينا» and «بينما», as in the saying of the poet:
استقدر الله خيرا وأرضينّ به ... فبينما العسر إذ دارت مياسير
(Ask Allah to decree good and be content with it; for while there is hardship, lo! ease comes round.)
In this case its being a particle is preferred.

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): conjunction. (يكلّم): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is "هو". (الناس): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (في المهد): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of يكلّم «[Note: The preposition and its genitive noun may not be attached to the verb يكلّم, because the meaning would be far-fetched.]». (الواو): conjunction. (كهلا): conjoined to the omitted ḥāl, accusative. (الواو): conjunction. (من الصالحين): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the word كلمة — in the previous verse; the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ, and this ḥāl is conjoined to (وجيها).
