The clause «قاتل معه ربّيّون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ كأيّ [Note: The clause may be a naʿt of نبيّ in the position of the genitive, and the khabar of كأيّ is the clause معه ربّيّون ... or the khabar is omitted, its implied form being مضى (passed away) or صبر (was patient) ... etc., and the clause معه ربّيّون becomes a second naʿt of نبيّ.].
The clause «ما وهنوا» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause قاتل [Note: This clause takes a position in the i'rab, just as the clause it is conjoined to, which is the clause قاتل, takes one in the other case mentioned in footnote no. (5).].
The clause «أصابهم ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «ما ضعفوا» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause ما وهنوا.
The clause «ما استكانوا» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause ما وهنوا.
The clause «الله يحبّ ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يحبّ الصابرين» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Morphology:
(كأيّ، كأيّن), without nūn or with nūn, an allusion to a number. For its various states and the many opinions about it, refer to the books of grammar and the references of the language.
(ربّيّون), plural of ربّي, attributive (nisba) to الربّ (the Lord); it was also said that it is attributive to الربة with kasra on the rāʾ, which is the group.
(And see verse 79 of this sūra).
(استكانوا), in it there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by qalb (conversion). Its origin is استكينوا with fatḥa on the yāʾ; then its vowel was transferred to the kāf, then it was converted to alif because it was voweled originally.

* Benefits:
1- «كأي» is like the predicative كم (kam al-khabariyya) in meaning, as in «وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ آيَةٍ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ». It is originally compounded of the kāf of simile and «أيّ», and because the tanwīn became part of its composition it was written with the nūn, so it is now a single word; it may be written «كأيّ» according to its origin. There is another dialect form in it, where it is pronounced «كأين», as in the saying of the poet:
وكائن ترى من صامت لك معجب ... زيادته أو نقصه في التكلم
(How many a silent man you see who pleases you ... his excess or deficiency shows when he speaks.)
It has the meaning of «كم» and agrees with it in five matters: vagueness, need for a tamyīz, indeclinability, obligatory placement at the head of the sentence, and conveying abundance, which is the usual case, as in His saying, the Exalted: وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ قاتَلَ مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ. It differs from it in five matters:
The first: that كأين is compound while كم is simple. The second: that its tamyīz is usually genitive with «من», as has passed in the verse and before it «وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا». The third: that it does not occur as interrogative, according to the majority. The fourth: that it does not occur in the genitive. The fifth: that its khabar does not occur as a single word but as a clause, as has passed in the verses mentioned.

safi-cedvel:101-101.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (كيف) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) «[Note: The interrogative came for rebuke and to bring the believers to wonder.]», (تكفرون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الواو) of the ḥāl; (أنتم) a detached pronoun, mabnī, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (تتلى) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تتلى); (آيات) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (فيكم) like عليكم, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); (رسول) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) resumptive; (من) a conditional noun making the verb jussive, mabnī, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (يعتصم) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is هو; (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يعتصم); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قد) a particle of verification; (هدي) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو, referring to (من); (إلى صراط) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (هدي); (مستقيم) naʿt (adjective) of صراط, genitive like it.
The clause «تكفرون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer to the vocative in the previous verse.
The clause «أنتم تتلى» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «تتلى ... آيات» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنتم.
The clause «فيكم رسوله» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the ḥāl clause.
The clause «من يعتصم..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعتصم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.]».
The clause «هدي ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
1- From the history of the Jews.
The Jews never cease — whenever the opportunity arises for them — to sow the seeds of discord among the members of society, as a means of weakening people's standing and raising the standing of the Jews. This kind of corruption was frequent in the time of the Messenger; one of their men strove to spoil relations within the ranks of the Anṣār, between al-Aws and al-Khazraj, until they almost fought one another, had it not been for the Messenger going out to them and bringing them back into the fold of love and harmony and casting the call of the Jāhiliyya behind their backs.

safi-cedvel:102-102.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab was given «[Note: In verse (100) of this sūra.]», (اتّقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (حقّ) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative; (تقاته) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).. and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive; (تموتنّ) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw, deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil, and the nūn is the nūn of emphasis, with no grammatical position; (الّا) a particle of restriction; (الواو) of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (أنتم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (مسلمون) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «اتّقوا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «لا تموتنّ» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «أنتم مسلمون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

safi-cedvel:103-103.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (اعتصموا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (بحبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اعتصموا); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (جميعا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), of the fāʿil in (اعتصموا); (الواو) conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive; (تفرّقوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and one of the two tāʾs was deleted from the verb; (الواو) conjunction — or resumptive; (اذكروا) like اعتصموا; (نعمة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl of نعمة; (إذ) an adverb for the past, mabnī, in the position of accusative, attached to نعمة — because it includes the meaning of the maṣdar (verbal noun) — or a badal (substitute) of نعمة; (كنتم) an incomplete past verb, mabnī on the sukūn, and (تم) an attached pronoun, ism of كان, in the position of nominative; (أعداء) khabar of كنتم, accusative; (الفاء) conjunction; (ألّف) a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو; (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (ألّف); (قلوب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunction; (أصبحتم) like كنتم; (بنعمة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of (إخوانا) «[Note: al-ʿUkbarī allowed the attachment to be to an omitted khabar of أصبح, with (إخوانا) a ḥāl of the pronoun of the addressee, i.e. you became clothed in His favour.. as brothers.. As for his statement that the verb (أصبح) may be complete, that is far-fetched.]», and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إخوانا) khabar of أصبح, accusative.
The clause «اعتصموا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer to the vocative in the previous verse.
The clause «لا تفرّقوا» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اعتصموا.
The clause «اذكروا» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اعتصموا, or it is resumptive with no grammatical position.
The clause «كنتم أعداء» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ألّف» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause كنتم.
The clause «أصبحتم ... إخوانا» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause ألّف.
(الواو) conjunction — or resumptive; (كنتم) like the first; (على شفا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of كنتم, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (حفرة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (من النار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of حفرة; (الفاء) conjunction; (أنقذ) like ألّف, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (من) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنقذ); (الكاف) a preposition «[Note: The kāf may be a noun meaning مثل (like), so that it is a naʿt of the omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), in the position of accusative.]», (ذا) a demonstrative, mabnī, in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e.: يبيّن الله لكم آياته بيانا كذلك (Allah makes clear to you His signs with a clarification like that), and (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address; يبيّن an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (لكم) like عليكم, attached to (يبيّن); (آيات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (لعلّ) a particle resembling the verb, for hope, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of accusative, ism of لعلّ; (تهتدون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «كنتم على شفا ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the first clause كنتم ... or has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أنقذكم» is conjoined to the clause كنتم على شفا and takes its position.
The clause «يبيّن الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لعلّكم تهتدون» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «تهتدون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.

* Morphology:
(تفرّقوا): its original form is تتفرّقوا, one of the two tāʾs having been deleted from the verb for lightness.
(شفا): the alif in it is originally a wāw; its dual is شفوان and it is pluralized as أشفاء ...
And in al-Miṣbāḥ: the شفا of anything is its edge; it is a noun from شفا يشفو, of the نصر class; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(حفرة): a noun for what is dug in the ground; its pattern is فعلة with ḍamma then sukūn; its plural is حفر with ḍamma then fatḥa.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the speech there is a representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya): the state of the believers in seeking support from one of the things mentioned, and their confidence in its protection, is likened to the state of one hanging down from a high place holding fast to a firm rope that is safe from breaking, without regard to any figurative usage in the individual words; and the expressions used for the thing likened-to were borrowed for the thing likened.
2- Antithesis (ṭibāq): between أعداء (enemies) and اخوان (brothers).

* Benefits:
1- العصام and العصمة: refuge and shelter. It is stated in fiqh al-lugha (the philology of the language) that when ʿayn and ṣād occur as the first and second radicals of a word, they indicate strength, impregnability and the like, as in رجل عصامي (a self-made man) and ذو عصبية قوية (having strong partisanship), and in العصا (the stick), العصيان (disobedience), العصر (pressing), المعصرة (the press), and عصفت الريح فهي عاصفة (the wind blew violently, so it is a storm). This is one of the secrets of our eloquent language, the language of the Revelation and the language of concise comprehensive speech.
2- حَقَّ تُقاتِهِ: the description came annexed to what it describes, for the firm establishment of the description and intensification by it on the one hand, and for musical sound (jaras) on the other. Expression through sound in His verses, Exalted is He, is not to be denied, because Allah willed that His Book be accompanied by all the elements of influence upon the heart and mind of the hearer, so He made musical sound one of the elements and factors of this influence.
3- شَفا حُفْرَةٍ: «الشفا» may be treated as masculine or feminine; the pronoun referring to it came feminine: «فأنقذكم منها». If we regard «الشفا» as feminine, the referring pronoun agrees with what it refers to; and if we regard الشفا as masculine, it has acquired femininity from what it is annexed to, namely «الحفرة». This is a regular way in the world of grammar and language: a masculine muḍāf may acquire femininity from a feminine muḍāf ilayhi, just as a feminine muḍāf may acquire masculinity from a masculine muḍāf ilayhi. An example of the first is the saying of the poet:
وما حب الديار شغفن قلبي ... ولكن حب من سكن الديارا
(It is not love of the dwellings that has infatuated my heart, but love of the one who dwelt in the dwellings.)

safi-cedvel:104-104.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction — or resumptive; (اللام) the lām of command; (تكن) an incomplete imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) — or complete; (من) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of أمة — a naʿt (adjective) that preceded what it qualifies «[Note: Or attached to (تكن) if it is complete ... and some allowed it to be attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of the incomplete verb تكن.]», (أمّة) ism of the incomplete تكن — or fāʿil (agent) of the complete تكن; (يدعون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ...
and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إلى الخير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يدعون); (الواو) conjunction; (يأمرون) like يدعون; (بالمعروف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأمرون); (الواو) conjunction; (ينهون عن المنكر) like يدعون إلى الخير; (الواو) resumptive or of the ḥāl; (أولاء) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) «[Note: Or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is المفلحون, and the clause هم المفلحون is the khabar of أولئك.]», (المفلحون) khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «لتكن منكم أمّة» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اعتصموا «[Note: In verse (103) of this sūra.]» ... or it has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يدعون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of the incomplete تكن — or in the position of nominative as a naʿt of أمة if (تكن) is parsed as complete «[Note: Likewise it is a naʿt of أمة if the khabar is taken to be the preposition and its genitive noun (منكم).]».
The clause «يأمرون ...» is conjoined to the clause يدعون and takes its position.
The clause «ينهون ...» is conjoined to the clause يدعون and takes its position.
The clause «أولئك ... المفلحون» has no grammatical position: resumptive ... or is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

* Morphology:
(الخير): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb خار يخير, of the ضرب class; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; it is the opposite of evil; its plural is خيور with ḍamma on the khāʾ.
(المنكر): passive participle of the four-letter أنكر, meaning he found fault with it and forbade it; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the second radical; its plurals are منكرات and مناكر.

* Rhetoric:
1- «وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ»: the conjunction in the verse is of the type of conjoining the specific to the general, to show their superiority over all other good deeds, like the conjoining of Jibrīl and Mīkāl to the angels, peace be upon them.
The detail of that is that calling to good is general, and following it with commanding the right and forbidding the wrong signals that these two are singled out for extra attention, and shows their superiority over the other good deeds.
- Contrast (muqābala): He set in correspondence command and prohibition, and the right (al-maʿrūf) and the wrong (al-munkar).

* Benefits:
1- «وَلْتَكُنْ»: the lām of command is originally with kasra, but when it occurs after the wāw and the fāʾ it is mostly made quiescent, as in «فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي»; it may be made quiescent after ثمّ. The lām of command enters upon the verb specific to the third person, active and passive, and upon the first person other than him (the speaker alone), its entry upon it being easier and lighter, as in «وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطاياكُمْ»; that is because a single person does not command himself, but if someone else is with him the matter becomes easier, because the other shares in what he commands. Less frequent than that is the entry of the lām upon the active verb of the addressee, because it has a special form, namely «افعل». «[Translator's note: The source writes «وعلى المخاطب غيره»; from the example «وَلْنَحْمِلْ» and the following explanation, the first person (the speaker with others) is evidently meant.]»
Then, requesting an action or its abandonment, when it is from the lower to the higher, is called a supplication (duʿāʾ), out of courtesy, and «the lām» and «lā» are called two particles of supplication, as in «لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنا رَبُّكَ» and as in «لا تؤاخذنا بما فعل السفهاء منا»; likewise a command in the imperative form is called a verb of «supplication», as in «رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي». This way is part of the etiquette of speaking, especially with Allah.

safi-cedvel:177-177.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الذين) a relative noun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna; (اشتروا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, which was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (الكفر) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (بالإيمان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اشتروا), by making it imply the meaning of بدّلوا ("they exchanged"); (لن يضرّوا الله شيئا): its i'rab has been given in the previous verse; (الواو) conjunction; (لهم عذاب أليم): the i'rab of its counterpart has been given in the previous verse.
The clause إنّ الذين اشتروا ... has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause اشتروا ... has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause لن يضرّوا ... is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «لهم عذاب ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لن يضرّوا.

* Rhetoric:
- «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الْكُفْرَ بِالْإِيْمانِ», i.e. they took it in exchange for it, out of desire for what they took and turning away from what they left; "buying" is by way of an implied metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya).

safi-cedvel:178-178.t:
«[Note: It is written thus in the muṣḥaf, but the orthographically correct form is to write it separately (أنّ ما), whether ما is relative or maṣdar, so that it is not confused with the redundant, restraining ما.]» .
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لا) the prohibitive, jussivizing lā «[Note: Because there is a reading with the tāʾ (تحسبنّ).]»; (يحسبنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive ... and (النون) is the heavy nūn of emphasis; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); (كفروا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma..
and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the noun of anna «[Note: Or it is a maṣdar particle which, with what follows it, is interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of accusative as the noun of anna, i.e.:
that Our granting them respite is good.]»; (نملي) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, its fāʿil a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "we" (نحن), for majesty; (اللام) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نملي) ... and the resumptive pronoun of the relative is omitted, its implied form being نمليه; (خير) the khabar (predicate) of anna, nominative; (لأنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خير, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إنّما) a restraining particle and the particle restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa), with no governing effect; (نملي لهم) like the first one; (اللام) a particle of causation (taʿlīl); (يزدادوا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (أن) after the lām, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (إثما) a tamyīz (specification), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ ما نملي ...) stands in place of the two objects of يحسب.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يزدادوا ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to the second (نملي).
(الواو) conjunction; (لهم عذاب مهين): the i'rab of its counterpart has been given «[Note: In verse (176) of this sūra.]».
The clause «لا يحسبنّ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «نملي ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the nominal or particle relative.
The clause «إنّما نملي ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive and giving a reason.
The clause «لهم عذاب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the second clause نملي.

* Rhetoric:
1- «أَنَّما نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ»: borrowed from أملى لفرسه, said when one lengthens the tether for one's horse so that it may graze as it wishes. He likened granting them respite and leaving the rope on their withers to the horse whose rope is let out so that it may run as it pleases; He omitted the thing likened, namely respite and leaving alone, and kept what it is likened to, namely letting out the rope (الإملاء). This is of the type of explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya).

* Benefits:
1- The saying of Allah the Exalted: «أَنَّما نُمْلِي لَهُمْ»: أنّ, which resembles the verb, and «ما», maṣdar or relative - both are permissible - ought by rights to be written separately, but they have remained joined in order to preserve the script of the Noble Qur'an and to protect it from change. There is much of this kind in the script of the Qur'an, and changing the script in what is not the Qur'an does no harm.

safi-cedvel:179-179.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative; (كان) a deficient past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of kāna, nominative (marfūʿ); (اللام) the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd) or of rejection; (يذر) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (أن) after the lām of denial, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو); (المؤمنين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يذر ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna, i.e. Allah was not intending to leave the believers.
(على) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (يذر); (أنتم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (عليه) a preposition and a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition; (يميز) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن), its fāʿil a latent pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو); (الخبيث) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من الطيّب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يميز).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يميز ...) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (يذر).
(الواو) conjunction; (ما كان الله ليطلع) like ما كان الله ليذر, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (على الغيب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يطلع); (الواو) conjunction; (لكنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for rectification (istidrāk); (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of lākinna, accusative; (يجتبي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, its fāʿil a latent pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو); (من رسل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يجتبي), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (يشاء) an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil is "he"; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (آمنوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (آمنوا); (الواو) conjunction; (رسل) conjoined to the Name of Majesty, genitive like it, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) resumptive; (إن) a jussivizing conditional particle; (تؤمنوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (الواو) conjunction; (تتّقوا) an imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to the verb تؤمنوا.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (اللام) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; (أجر) mubtadaʾ, nominative; (عظيم) a naʿt (adjective) of أجر, nominative like it.
The clause «ما كان الله ليذر ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يذر ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdar relative particle (أن).
The clause «أنتم عليه» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يميز ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the maṣdar relative particle (أن).
The clause «ما كان الله ليطلعكم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يطلعكم ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the maṣdar relative particle (أن).
The clause «لكنّ الله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the second clause ما كان..
The clause «يجتبي ...» has no grammatical position, being the khabar of lākinna «[Translator's note: so in the source; as the khabar of lākinna, the clause would be in the position of nominative.]».
The clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied non-jussivizing condition, i.e.: when the one chosen by Allah comes to you, then believe in him.
The clause «تؤمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تتّقوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تؤمنوا.
The clause «لكم أجر» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined to the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
The saying of Allah the Exalted: «حَتَّى يَمِيزَ الْخَبِيثَ».
The imperfect verb is put in the accusative by an «أن» that must be implied after «حتى» when it is the prepositional حتى, meaning (إلى "until", or the lām of causation), as in «قالُوا: لَنْ نَبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عاكِفِينَ حَتَّى يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنا مُوسى» and the saying «أطع الله حتى تفوز برضاه» ("Obey Allah so that you may attain His good pleasure"). It may mean «إلّا» ("except"), as in the saying of the poet:
ليس العطاء من الفضول سماحة ... حتى تجود وما لديك قليل
(Giving from one's surplus is not generosity, unless you give when what you have is little.)
For the verb after it to be put in the accusative by an implied أن, it is required that it be future, either relative to the speaker's speech or relative to what precedes it.
If the verb is meant in the sense of the present, then «أن» is not implied; rather the verb after it is definitely nominative, as in «مرض فلان حتى ما يرجونه» ("So-and-so fell ill, so that they no longer hope for him"). In this case حتى is a particle of commencement and what follows it is nominative because it is free of any accusative or jussive governor; it is a particle with which clauses begin.
The sign that the verb is for the present is that it is correct to put the fāʾ in place of «حتى», as in your saying «مرض فلان فلا يرجونه».

safi-cedvel:180-180.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction or resumptive; (لا يحسبنّ الذين): its i'rab has been given «[Note: In verse (178) of this sūra.]»; (يبخلون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يبخلون); (آتى) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (من فضل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (آتاهم), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (هو) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no governing effect; (خيرا) second mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يحسبنّ, while the first object is omitted, the context of the speech indicating it, namely "the stinginess" (البخل); (اللام) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (خيرا); (بل) a particle of digression (iḍrāb), stripped of conjunction; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (شرّ) khabar (predicate), nominative; (لهم) like the first one, attached to شرّ.
(السين) a particle of futurity; (يطوّقون) an imperfect verb in the passive, nominative ... and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (بخلوا) a past verb and its fāʿil; (الباء) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (بخلوا); (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (يطوّقون); (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) parenthetical; (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; (ميراث) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (السموات) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (الأرض) conjoined to السموات, genitive like it; (الواو) conjunction; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (بما) like the first one, attached to خبير «[Note: It is permissible for (ما) to be a maṣdar particle ... and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to خبير.]»; (تعملون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (خبير) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الله, nominative.
The clause «لا يحسبنّ الذين ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لا يحسبنّ الذين كفروا ... and what lies between the two clauses has the status of a parenthesis «[Note: It is permissible for the clause to be resumptive.]».
The clause «يبخلون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «آتاهم الله» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «هو شرّ لهم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «سيطوّقون ...» has no grammatical position, giving a reason (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «بخلوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «لله ميراث ...» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.
The clause «الله ... خبير» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause سيطوّقون.
The clause «تعملون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the nominal or particle relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(ميراث): a noun for what is left after death, from ورث يرث, of the wathiqa class (bāb wathiqa). The word involves a phonetic change by substitution (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb): its original form is موراث, on the pattern مفعال with a kasra on the mīm; when the wāw came vowelless after a kasra, it was changed into a yāʾ, and it became ميراث.

* Rhetoric:
1- «وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ»: using the majestic Name overtly where a pronoun would be expected, in order to instil awe.
And the iltifāt (shift) from the third person to the second person in His saying «تعملون», to intensify the threat and to signal the severity of the wrath of the All-Merciful arising from the mention of their vile deeds.
2- Muqābala (contrast): He set in antithesis خير and شر, and السموات and الأرض.

* Benefits:
1- A difference in reading:
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «ولا يحسبنّ» there are two readings, the second of them being «ولا يحسبنّ» «[Translator's note: both readings appear identically in the source; the second is evidently the reading with the tāʾ (ولا تحسبنّ).]». The difference in reading results in omission and implication in the two objects of حسب, and behind that lies a precise and useful discussion in «Mughnī al-Labīb», in its fifth chapter. If it indicates anything, it indicates the convolutedness of the grammarians and their contrivance in matters which it would have been better, for them and for readers, to simplify as far as they could. Their long, tedious disagreement may be dispensed with by the saying of one of them:
It is permissible to omit one of the two objects of the verbs of the heart (afʿāl al-qulūb) for brevity, if there is evidence indicating it. The majority permitted that by analogy with the verbs whose object is omitted, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted:
«هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَالَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ» and His saying «كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا وَلا تُسْرِفُوا». Whoever has an interest in this labour should consult Mughnī al-Labīb.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أنى يَكُونُ لِي غُلاَمٌ}: it («يكون») may be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) one, and in that case there are two views on its khabar (predicate). The first: it is «أنَّى», because it means "how" (كيف) or means "from where" (مِنْ أين); on this view «لي» is an explication (tabyīn). The second: the khabar is the preposition and its genitive noun, and «كيف» [Translator's note: i.e. «أنَّى» in the sense of كيف] is accusative (manṣūb) as an adverbial (ẓarf). It may also be the complete (tāmma) one, so that the adverbial and the preposition with its genitive noun are both attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يكون», since it is complete, i.e. "How will a boy come about for me?" And it [«لي»] may be attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «غلام», because had it come after it, it would have been a naʿt (adjective) of it.
And His words: {وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِي الكبر} are a circumstantial clause. In another place it is {وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الكبر} [Maryam: 8], because whatever has reached you, you have reached it. It was also said: because events seek out a person. And it was said: it is of the inverted (maqlūb) type, as in the poet's words:
1264 - مثلُ القنافِذِ هَدَّاجون قد بَلَغَتْ ... نجرانُ أو بُلِّغَتْ سَوْءاتِهِمْ هَجَرُ
(Like hedgehogs, creeping along at night; Najrān has reached — or Hajar has been reached by — their foul deeds.)
But there is no need for that.
In this sura he put his own state first and his wife's state last, while in Maryam it is the reverse. It was said: the opening of the verses in Maryam matches this arrangement, since he first mentioned the weakening of his bones, the blazing of his grey hair and his fear for his kinsmen after him, and then said: {وَكَانَتِ امرأتي عَاقِراً}. When he mentioned the two again in another question, he mentioned old age [last] so that «عِتِيَّاً» would match the verse-endings, and this is a deliberate device in eloquence. Moreover, conjunction with wāw does not entail chronological order, so no regard was paid to putting first or last.
Al-ghulām (the boy) is a person young in age, the one whose moustache [Translator's note: a word is missing in the source here, marked by dots; presumably "has sprouted"]. Applying it to an infant or to a middle-aged man is figurative: to the infant by way of good omen for what he will become, and to the middle-aged man in view of what he used to be. Laylā al-Akhyaliyya said:
1265 - شَفاها من الداءِ العُضالِ الذي بها ... غلامٌ إذا هَزَّ القناةَ شَفاها
(She was cured of the chronic illness she had by a "boy" who, when he shakes the spear, cures her.)
Some of them said: as long as the child is in its mother's womb it is called «جنين» (fetus). Allah the Exalted said: {وَإِذْ أَنتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ} [al-Najm: 32]; it is so called because it is concealed (ijtinān) in the womb. When it is born it is called «صبي» (infant); when weaned it is called «غلام» up to seven years; then it is called «يافع» (adolescent) until it reaches ten years; then «حَزَوَّر» is applied to it up to fifteen; then it becomes «قُمُدّ» up to twenty-five years; then «عَنَطْنَط» up to thirty. The poet said:
1266 - وبالجَعْدِ حتى صارَ جَعْداً عَنَطْنَطاً ... إذا قامَ ساوى غاربَ الفحلِ غارِبُهْ
(And with the curly-haired one, until he became a tall, curly-haired youth whose withers, when he stood, were level with the withers of the stallion.)
Then «حُمُل» up to forty, then «كَهْل» (middle-aged) up to fifty, then «شيخ» (old man) up to eighty, then «هَمّ» (decrepit) after that.
The derivation of al-ghulām is from al-ghulma and al-ightilām, which is the desire for intercourse; since he is caused by it, his name was taken from its wording. One says «اغتَلَم الفحلُ», i.e. the stallion's lust for mating became intense; and «اغتلَم البحرُ», i.e. the sea surged and its waves clashed, borrowed from it. Its regular plural of paucity is أَغْلِمة and of multitude غِلْمان; it has also been pluralised irregularly as غِلْمة — and is this form a broken plural or a collective noun (ism jamʿ)? Al-Farrāʾ said: "One says: a boy plainly in his ghulūma, ghulūmiyya and ghulāmiyya." He said: "The Arabs make the maṣdar (verbal noun) of every noun that has no known verb on this pattern, so they say: a slave plainly in his ʿubūda, ʿubūdiyya and ʿubādiyya" — he means that the Arabs did not use a verb from this.
Al-kibar is the maṣdar of كَبِرَ يكبَر كِبَراً, i.e. he advanced in age. The poet said:
1267 - صغيرَيْنِ نَرْعَى البَهْمَ يا ليتَ أَنَّنا ... إلى اليومِ لم نَكْبَرْ ولم تَكْبَر البَهْمُ
(As two little ones we tended the lambs; would that to this day we had not grown old, nor the lambs grown old.)
His words: {وامرأتي عَاقِرٌ} are a circumstantial clause, either from the yāʾ in «لي», so the ḥāl is multiple according to whoever holds that possible, or from the yāʾ in «بلغني». Al-ʿāqir is one to whom no child is born, whether man or woman, derived from al-ʿaqr, which is killing, as if they imagined in him the killing of his children. The verb in this sense is intransitive; as for عَقَرْتُ in the sense of "I slaughtered (naḥartu)", it is transitive. Allah the Exalted said: {فَعَقَرُواْ الناقة} [al-Aʿrāf: 77], and the poet said:
1268 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... عَقَرْتَ بعيري يا امرأ القيسِ فانْزِلِ
(… You have hamstrung my camel, O Imruʾ al-Qays, so dismount!)
It was also said: «عاقِر» is relational (ʿalā al-nasab), i.e. possessed of barrenness (ʿuqr), and it has the meaning of a mafʿūl (passive), i.e. معقورة; for that reason the feminine tāʾ was not attached to it.
Al-ʿuqr / al-ʿaqr, with ḍamma and fatḥa on the ʿayn, is the root (origin) of a thing; from it come ʿuqr al-dār (the heart of the home) and ʿuqr al-ḥawḍ (the bottom of the basin). In the ḥadīth: "No people were ever attacked in the heart of their home (ʿuqr dārihim) but that they were humiliated." And عَقَرْتُه means: I struck its ʿuqr, i.e. its base, like رَأَسْته, i.e. I struck its head. Al-ʿuqr is also the last child, and likewise "the egg of al-ʿuqr" (bayḍat al-ʿuqr). Al-ʿuqār is wine, because it figuratively "wounds" (taʿqir) the mind. Among their expressions is «رَفَعَ فلانٌ عقيرَتَه», i.e. his voice; this is because a man's leg was wounded (ʿaqara) and he raised his voice, so this was borrowed for everyone who raises his voice. Some of them said: "One says: عَقُرَتْ المرأةُ تَعْقُر عَقْراً وعقارةً (the woman became barren)." Al-Farrāʾ recited:
1269 - أرزامُ بابٍ عَقُرَتْ أَعْواما ... فَعَلَّقَتْ بُنَيَّها تَسْماما
(A woman of the household who was barren for years, then attached her little son to amulets.) [Translator's note: the wording of this verse is obscure in the source; the gloss is approximate.]
And one says عَقَر الرجلُ, عَقُر and عَقِر when his wife does not conceive; so they made the verb predicated of the man wider [in its forms] than that predicated of the woman. Al-Zajjāj said: «عاقِر» means "possessed of barrenness". He said: "Because for فَعُلْتُ the active participles are on the pattern فَعيلة, such as طريفة and كريمة; «عاقر» is only in the sense of 'possessed of barrenness'." I say: this is an explicit statement that the verb predicated of the woman can only be عَقُرت with ḍamma on the qāf, since if fatḥa or kasra on it were permitted, the pattern «فاعِل» from it would be permitted without interpreting it as relational. Among the instances of «عاقر» used as a description of a man is the saying of ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl:
1270 - لَبِئْسَ الفتى إنْ كنُت أعوَر عاقِراً ... جَباناً فما عُذْري لدى كلِّ مَحْضَرِ
(What an evil young man I would be if I were one-eyed, barren and cowardly — what excuse would I have at every gathering?)
His words: {كَذَلِكَ الله يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ}: there are two views on the kāf. The first: it is in the position of the accusative, and there are the two well-known analyses of it. One of them, which most of the grammarians hold, is that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being: "Allah does what He wills of wondrous acts, the like of that act", namely the creation of a child between a decrepit old man and a barren old woman.
The second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of that maṣdar, i.e. "He does the act, it being like that". This is the doctrine of Sībawayh, and its explanation has preceded.
The second of the two views on the kāf: it is in the position of the nominative as a fronted khabar, and the Name of Majesty is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). Al-Zamakhsharī rendered it as "After the manner of this description is Allah", with «يفعل ما يشاء» being an explanation of it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya rendered it: "Like this astonishing power is the power of Allah". The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rendered it, saying: "That is by the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. Allah's strange making is like that making, so «يفعل ما يشاء» is an elucidation of the vagueness in the demonstrative." So on the first view the speech is one sentence, and on the second it is two sentences.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that the reference by «ذلك» is to the state of Zakariyyā and the state of his wife, as if he said: 'My Lord, in what way will we have a boy while we are in such-and-such a state?' and He said to him: 'Just as you two are, the boy will come about for you.' On this interpretation the speech is complete at His words «كذلك», and His words {الله يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ} are an explanatory sentence establishing in the soul the occurrence of this astonishing matter." End of quote. On what he mentioned, «كذلك» is attached to an omitted element, and «الله يفعل» is a sentence composed of a mubtadaʾ and a khabar.

semin-durr:22-22.t: Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read it with a fatḥa on the bāʾ: «حَبَطَتْ», and it is a well-known dialectal form.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
The words of the Exalted: {يُدْعَوْنَ}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الذين أُوتوا». His words «ليحكُمَ» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يُدْعَوْن. His words «ثم يَتَوَّلى» are conjoined to «يُدْعَوْن», and «منهم» is a naʿt (adjective) of فريق.
His words {وَهُمْ مُّعْرِضُونَ} may be an adjective conjoined to the adjective before it, so that the wāw is conjunctive; or it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «منهم», since that occurs as an adjective, so that the wāw is the wāw of the ḥāl; [and it may be a ḥāl from «فريق», which is permissible even though it is indefinite, because it is specified by the adjective before it]. If it is a ḥāl, it may be corroborative (muʾakkida), because turning away (al-tawallī) and averting (al-iʿrāḍ) have one meaning; or it may be clarifying (mubayyina), because what each of them relates to differs. They said: because the turning away is from the one who calls, and the averting is from what one is called to. It is also possible that this clause is resumptive with no grammatical position: He informed about them with that.
Al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar and al-Jaḥdarī read «لِيُحْكَمَ» as passive, and what stands in place of the fāʿil (agent) is the adverbial phrase (ẓarf), i.e.: so that judgement may take place between them.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
The words of the Exalted: {ذلك بِأَنَّهُمْ}: two aspects are permissible in «ذلك». The sounder of them: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the preposition-phrase after it is its khabar (predicate), i.e.: that turning away is because of these false sayings that have no reality. The second: that «ذلك» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: the matter is that; this is the view of al-Zajjāj. On this view, his words «بأنهم» are attached to that implied element, namely "the matter" and the like. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "On this view his words «بأنهم» are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the sense of pointing contained in «ذا», i.e.: that matter being deserved because of their saying"; then he said: "and this is weak". I say: rather, it is not permissible at all.
Here «معدودات» comes in the plural form, while in al-Baqara it is {مَّعْدُودَةً} [verse: 80], as a variation in eloquence. That is because a broken plural of non-rational beings may be treated at times like a feminine singular and at other times like a feminine plural; so one says «هذه جبالٌ راسيةٌ» ("these are firm mountains"), or if you wish «راسيات», and «جِمال ماشية» ("walking camels"), or if you wish «ما شيات». The plural was assigned to this place because it is a place of denouncing them for what they did and said, so He brought the plural wording as an intensification in rebuking them and rebuking whoever does as they do.
His words: {وَغَرَّهُمْ فِي دِينِهِمْ}: al-ghurūr is deception. One says from it: غَرَّه يَغِرُّه غُرورا, so he is غارّ (deceiver) and مغرور (deceived). Al-gharūr with fatḥa is an intensive form, like al-ḍarūb. Al-ghirr is the young (male) and al-gharīra the young (female), because both are easily deceived; and al-ghirra is taken from this. One says: «أخَذَه على غِرَّة», i.e. (he seized him) through heedlessness and deception. Al-ghurra is a whiteness in the face; one says from it: وَجْهٌ أَغرُّ (a blazed face), رجل [أغرُّ] and, for a woman, «غَرَّاء»; the regular plural is غُرّ and the irregular one غُرَّان. He (the poet) said:
1211 - ثيابُ بني عوفٍ طَهارى نَقِيَّةٌ ... وأوجُهُهم عند المَشاهِدِ غُرَّانُ
(The clothes of Banū ʿAwf are pure and clean, and their faces at the gatherings are bright.)
The ghurra of everything is its most precious part. In the ḥadīth: «وجَعَلَ في الجنين غُرَّةً عبداً أو أَمَة» ("and he fixed for the foetus a ghurra: a male or a female slave"). It was also said: al-ghurra is the choicest. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said in explaining this ḥadīth: "It can only be a white one among slaves", as though he took it from al-ghurra, which is the whiteness in the face.
His words: {مَّا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ}: «ما» may be maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar) or meaning "that which", with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e.: that which they used to fabricate.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَكَيْفَ إِذَا}: «كيف» is accusative by a concealed verb, its implied form being: "How will their state be?" — so al-Ḥawfī estimated it. This allows the "being" (kawn) to be complete (tāmm), so that the two aspects mentioned earlier at His words {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 28] apply to «كيف», namely likening it to the ḥāl (circumstantial) or to the adverb (ẓarf); or it may be the defective (nāqiṣa) one, so that «كيف» is its khabar (predicate). Some estimated the verb as "How will they do?", so «كيف» follows the two aspects already mentioned. And «كيف» may be a fronted khabar whose mubtadaʾ (subject) is omitted, its implied form being: "So how is their state?".
His words: {إِذَا جَمَعْنَاهُمْ}: a pure adverb without the implication of a condition, and what governs it is what governs «كيف» if we say that it is accusative by an implied verb, as already set out. If we say that it is the khabar of a concealed mubtadaʾ and is accusative in the manner of adverbs, then what governs «إذا» is the "being established" (al-istiqrār) that governs «كيف», since it is like an adverb. And if we say that it is a noun that is not an adverb but serves merely for asking, then what governs it is the very mubtadaʾ we estimated, i.e.: how is their state at the time of their gathering.
His words: {لِيَوْمٍ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) جمعناهم, i.e.: for the judgement of a day, or for the recompense of a day; and {لاَّ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} is an adjective of the adverb.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {اجعل لي آيَةً}: al-jaʿl may be in the sense of "making into" (taṣyīr), so it takes two objects: the first of them is «آية» and the second is the preposition with its genitive noun before it. Fronting is obligatory here, because if the two were resolved into a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), nothing would license beginning with this indefinite noun, «آية», except the fronting of this preposition with its genitive noun; and the ruling for the two after the abrogating particle (nāsikh) enters is the same as before it. The implied form is: "Make a sign among the signs for me." It may also be in the sense of creating and taking, i.e. "Create for me a sign", so it takes one object. On this view there are two views on «لي»: the first, that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) al-jaʿl; the second, that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «آية», because had it come after it, it could have been a naʿt (adjective) of it. It may also be for explication (bayān). Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr gave the yāʾ a fatḥa, and the rest made it quiescent.
His words: {أَلاَّ تُكَلِّمَ}: «أنْ» and what falls in its scope are in the position of the nominative as the khabar of His words «آيتُك», i.e. "your sign is your not speaking to people". The majority read «تُكَلِّم» in the accusative by the maṣdar-forming «أنْ». Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it in the nominative, and there are two views on it. The first: «أنْ» is lightened from the heavy one (anna), and its noun is then an omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), while the negated clause after it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «أنْ». Similar to it are {أَفَلاَ يَرَوْنَ أَلاَّ يَرْجِعُ} [Ṭā Hā: 89] and {وحسبوا أَلاَّ تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ} [al-Māʾida: 71], and the separation between «أنْ» and the verb serving as its khabar is by a particle of negation. But its being the lightened one is weakened by its not occurring after a verb of certainty. The second: it is the accusative-governing «أنْ», treated like its sister «ما» [i.e. left without governing]; similar to it is {لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يُتِمَّ الرضاعة} [al-Baqara: 233]. «أنْ» and what falls in its scope are also in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «آيتُك».
The words of Allah the Exalted: {ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ}: the correct view is that this type — namely times the whole of which is taken up by the event occurring in them — is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), contrary to the Kufans, who make it accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It was said: "There is an omitted conjoined element (maʿṭūf), its implied form being: three days and their nights, and it was omitted, as in the words of Allah the Exalted {تَقِيكُمُ الحر} [al-Naḥl: 81] and similar cases; this is indicated by His words in Sūrat Maryam: {ثَلاَثَ لَيَالٍ سَوِيّاً} [Maryam: 10]." But it may be said: the whole is taken from the two passages together, so there is no need to claim an omission; for on this implied form that you mentioned we would need to supply a conjoined element in the other verse, its implied form being: three nights and their days.
His words: {إِلاَّ رَمْزاً}: there are two views on it. The first: it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because gesturing (ramz) is not of the genus of speech, since ramz is pointing with an eye, an eyebrow or the like. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned nothing else, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya preferred it, beginning with it, for he said: "The speech meant in the verse is only uttering with the tongue, not making known what is in the soul, so the reality of this exception is that it is disconnected." Then he said: "The jurists held that pointing and the like take the ruling of speech in oaths and the like; on that basis the exception comes out connected."
The second view: it is connected, because "speech" in the language is applied to a number of meanings, among which are gesturing and pointing. They recited for that:
1271 - إذا كَلَّمَتْني بالعيونِ الفواترِ ... رَدَدْتُ عليها بالدموعِ البوادِرِ
(When she spoke to me with languid eyes, I answered her with hastening tears.)
Another said:
1272 - أرادَتْ كلاماً فاتَّقَتْ من رقيبها ... فلم يَكُ إلا وَمْؤُها بالحواجبِ
(She wanted to speak, but was wary of her watcher, so there was nothing but her signalling with the eyebrows.)
And later poets have used this; Ḥabīb [Abū Tammām] said:
1273 - كَلَّمْتُه بجفونٍ غيرِ ناطقة ... فكانَ مِنْ رَدِّهِ ما قالَ حاجِبُهْ
(I spoke to him with eyelids that did not utter, and his reply was what his eyebrow said.)
Al-Zamakhsharī began with this view, preferring it. He said: "Since it fulfilled the function of speech and what is understood from speech was understood from it, it was called speech. It may also be a disconnected exception."
Al-ramz is pointing and signalling with an eye, eyebrow or hand; from it the profligate woman is called al-rāmiza and al-rammāza, and in the ḥadīth: "He forbade the earnings of the rammāza." One says of it: رَمَزَت تَرْمُزُ / تَرْمِزُ, with ḍamma or kasra on the middle radical in the imperfect. The root meaning of al-ramz is moving; one says رَمَزَ and ارتَمَزَ, i.e. it moved, and from it the sea is called al-rāmūz because of its movement and turbulence. Al-Rāghib said: "Al-ramz is a signal with the lip, a hidden sound, and winking with the eyebrow. «ما ارمازَّ» means: he did not utter even a ramz. A rammāza battalion is one from which nothing is heard but a murmur because of its great size." I say: its being a hidden sound, as al-Rāghib said, is supported by what came in the exegesis, that he was prevented from raising his voice.
The generality read «رَمْزاً» with fatḥa on the rāʾ and sukūn on the mīm. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and ʿAlqama ibn Qays read «رُمُزاً» with ḍamma on both, and there are two views on it. The first: it is a maṣdar on the pattern fuʿl with the middle radical originally quiescent, and then the middle radical was given ḍamma for harmony (itbāʿ), as they say al-yusur and al-ʿusur for al-yusr and al-ʿusr; there has already been discussion of this by the morphologists. The second: it is the plural of رَمُوز, like رُسُل as the plural of رسول; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was read with ḍamma on both, i.e. [on] the rāʾ, and it is the plural of رُمُزة with two ḍammas, and that was kept in the plural; and it may be that the mīm was quiescent originally and he merely made the ḍamma follow the ḍamma; and it may be a maṣdar, not a plural, given ḍamma for harmony like al-yusr and al-yusur." I say: his words from "the plural of رُمُزة" up to "originally" are muddled speech from which no sound meaning can be understood. Al-Aʿmash read «رَمَزاً» with fatḥa on both, and al-Zamakhsharī explained it as the plural of رامِز, like خادِم and خَدَم.
On this view, its accusative is as a ḥāl from both the agent — the pronoun of Zakariyyā — and the object — the people — together, as if: "except signalling to one another", like the poet's words:
1274 - متى ما تَلْقَني فَرْدَيْن تَرْجُفْ ... رَوانِفُ إليَتَيْكَ وتُسْتَطارا
(Whenever you meet me, the two of us alone, the flesh of your buttocks will quiver and be sent flying.)
And like his words:
1275 - فَلَئِنْ لَقِيتُكَ خالِيَيْنِ لَتَعْلَمَنْ ... أيِّي وأيُّك فارسُ الأَحْزَابِ
(If I meet you, the two of us alone, you will surely know which of us — I or you — is the horseman of the confederates.)
The words of Allah the Exalted: {كَثِيراً} is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl from the pronoun of that maṣdar — and this is known — or a naʿt of an omitted time, its implied form being: much remembrance, or a long time.
The bāʾ in His words {بالعشي} is in the sense of «في», i.e. in the evening and the early morning. Al-ʿashiyy is said of the time from the sun's declining until its setting; so said al-Zamakhsharī. Al-Rāghib said: "Al-ʿashiyy is from the sun's declining until morning," but the first is the well-known view. Al-Wāḥidī said: "Al-ʿashiyy is the plural of ʿashiyya, which is the end of the day."
The generality read «والإِبكار» with kasra on the hamza; it is the maṣdar of أبْكَر يُبْكِر إبكاراً [Translator's note: the source prints بَكَّر يُبَكِّر, but the maṣdar إبكار belongs to أبْكَر, as the author himself says below], i.e. he went out early in the morning (bukra). Like it are بَكَر, without doubling, and ابْتَكَر. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
1276 - أَمِنْ آلِ نُعْمٍ أَنْتَ غادٍ فَمُبْكِرُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Is it from the family of Nuʿm that you are setting out in the morning, leaving early …)
This is from أبْكَر. He also said:
1277 - أيها الرائحُ المُجِدُّ ابتكاراً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O you who travel in earnest, setting out early …)
Another said:
1278 - بَكَرْنَ بُكوراً واسْتَحَرْنَ بسُحْرَةٍ ... فهنَّ ووادي الرَّسِّ كاليدِ في الفم
(They set out early in the morning and journeyed at the last part of the night; they and the valley of al-Rass are like the hand in the mouth.)
It was read irregularly (shādhdh): «والأَبْكار» with fatḥa on the hamza, the plural of «بَكَر» with fatḥa on the first and second radicals. When by it this time of a specific day is meant, it is barred from nunation and from inflection, so it is used only as an adverbial. You say: "I came to you on Friday bakara (early)." The reason for its being a diptote is definiteness and deviation (ʿadl) from «أل». If an indefinite time is meant, it takes nunation, e.g. "I came to you one early morning (bakaran) among the early mornings." Its counterpart is سَحَر and أسحار in all that preceded. This reading suits His word «العشيّ» according to whoever makes it the plural of «عَشِيَّة», so that the two plurals correspond.
The time of al-ibkār is from the rising of the dawn until forenoon (al-ḍuḥā). Al-Rāghib said: "The root of the word is al-bukra, the beginning of the day; the verb was derived from its wording, so it was said: بَكَر فلانٌ بُكوراً when he went out early in the morning; al-bakūr is one who goes very early; and بَكَّر في حاجته, ابتَكَر and باكَرَ. The meaning of haste was conceived in it because it precedes the other times of the day, so anyone who hastens is called bakir." I say: the apparent sense of this wording, and likewise of others' wording, is that al-bakar is specific to the time from sunrise until forenoon; so if it is meant to be from the first rising of the dawn until forenoon, that is contrary to the root sense. Al-Wāḥidī stated this explicitly, saying: this is the meaning of al-ibkār; then what is between the rising of the dawn and forenoon is called ibkār, just as it is called iṣbāḥ.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَأَمَّا الذين كَفَرُواْ}: there are two views on the position of this relative noun. The more evident of them is that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is the fāʾ and what lies within its scope. The second is that it is accusative by an implied (muqaddar) verb, the question belonging to the chapter of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), since the verb after it has already governed its pronoun. This is a weak view, because «أمَّا» is followed only by a mubtadaʾ, and since only a mubtadaʾ follows it, it is impossible to construe the noun after it as governed by an implied verb. Whoever permits this resorts to the contrivance of implying the verb after the noun rather than before it — he says: so that «أمَّا» is not followed by a verb, for verbs never follow it at all. So in your saying «أمَّا زيداً فضَربتُه» he supposes: «أمَّا زيداً ضربْتُ فضربتُه», and likewise here he supposes: «فأمَّا الذين كفروا أعذَّب فأعذِّبهم»; thus he implies the governing word after the ṣila (relative clause) and does not imply it before the relative noun, for the reason I mentioned. This ought not to be permitted, since there is no need for it, and it involves committing a very weak construction in the most eloquent of speech. Some readers of the irregular (shādhdh) readings read {وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ} [Fuṣṣilat: 17] with «ثمود» in the accusative, and people judged that reading weak.

In His words {ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ} up to {كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ} there is iltifāt (a shift of person) from the third person to direct address. That is because Allah the Exalted first mentioned those who denied ʿĪsā and fabricated lies against him — namely the Jews, may they be cursed — and also first mentioned those who believed in him — namely the Disciples, may Allah be pleased with them — and after that He decreed, by way of informing, that He would make the followers of ʿĪsā above those who opposed him. Had the composition continued along the context without iltifāt, it would have been: «ثم إليَّ مَرْجِعُهم فأَحْكُمُ بينهم فيما كانوا» (then to Me is their return, and I will judge between them in what they used to …). But He shifted to direct address because it is more eloquent in giving glad tidings and more deterring in giving warning.

In the order of these four predicates — I mean «مُتَوَفِّيك», «رافعُك», «مُطَهِّرك» and «جاعلُ» — [Translator's note: the printed text reads «وجاعلُ هذا الترتيبَ», apparently a textual corruption; the sense is "in this order"] there is a very fine meaning. That is, Allah the Exalted gave him glad tidings first that He would take him (mutawaffīhi) and take charge of his affair, so that the disbelievers threatening him with death would have no power or way over him; then secondly that He would raise him to Himself, that is, to His heaven, the abode of His prophets and angels and the place of His worship, so that he would dwell there and worship his Lord together with those who worship Him; then thirdly that He would purify him from the filth of the disbelievers, their harm and what they accused him of; then fourthly that He would raise his followers above those who opposed them, so that thereby his joy would be complete and his gladness perfected. He put the glad tidings concerning his own self before the glad tidings concerning others, because to a person his own self is more important and its affair of greater concern: {قوا أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَاراً} [al-Taḥrīm: 6], and «ابدَأْ بِنَفْسِكَ ثم بِمَنْ تَعول» ("Begin with yourself, then with those you support").

semin-durr:57-57.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَأَمَّا الذين آمَنُوا}: what is said about it is like what was said about the relative noun before it. Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read «فيوفِّيهم» with the yāʾ of the third person, and the rest read it with the nūn. The reading of Ḥafṣ is by way of iltifāt (a shift of person) from the first person to the third, as a varied display of eloquence. The reading of the rest runs in keeping with the consistency of the composition already mentioned; but there He used the first person singular, and here the first person singular who magnifies Himself [Translator's note: i.e. the plural of majesty «نُوَفِّيهم»], out of care for the believers and to raise their standing, since they are honoured in His sight.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {ذلك نَتْلُوهُ}: it is possible that «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «نتلوه» the khabar (predicate), with «من الآيات» a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a second khabar. It is possible that «ذلك» is accusative by an implied (muqaddar) verb explained by what follows it, so that the question belongs to ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), and «من الآيات» is a ḥāl or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هُو من الآيات» (it is among the signs). But the nominative as a mubtadaʾ is better, because it requires no implying, and in their view «زيدٌ ضربتُه» is better than «زيداً ضربته». It is possible that «ذلكَ» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, meaning: «الأمر ذلك» (the matter is that); on this view «نَتْلوه» is a ḥāl of the demonstrative, and «من الآيات» a ḥāl of the object of «نَتْلوه». It is possible that «ذلك» is a relative noun meaning «الذي», with «نَتْلوه» the ṣila (relative clause) and the returning pronoun; it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the prepositional phrase after it, i.e. «الذي نتلوه عليك كائنٌ من الآيات» (what We recite to you is among the signs), that is, the miracles indicating your prophethood. Al-Zajjāj permitted this and al-Zamakhsharī followed him; this is the doctrine of the Kufans. As for the Basrans, they do not permit any demonstrative to be a relative noun except «ذا» alone, under conditions whose mention has preceded. It is possible that «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, «من الآيات» its khabar, and «نتلوه» a clause in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, the governing word being the meaning of the demonstrative.

As for «مِنْ», there are two views on it. The more evident is that it is partitive, because what is recited to him, peace be upon him, of the story of ʿĪsā is some of his miracles and some of the Qurʾān; this is a clear view. The second is that it is for explaining the genus; Ibn ʿAṭiyya inclined to this and began with it. Al-Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "That is not feasible here in terms of meaning except by way of metaphor, because rendering explicative «مِنْ» by a relative noun is not evident here; for if you said: «ذلك نتلوه عليك الذي هو الآيات والذكر الحكيم» (that We recite to you, which is the signs and the wise reminder), you would need an interpretation, namely that part of the signs and the reminder is made 'signs' and 'reminder', and that is metaphor."

«الحكيمُ» is an intensive form transferred from the fāʿil pattern, like «ضريب» from «ضارب». The Book is described by it metaphorically, because this attribute in reality belongs to the One who sent it down and who speaks it; so it is described by the attribute of the One from whom it comes, namely the Creator, Blessed and Exalted is He. Or because it speaks with wisdom, or because it is made firm (uḥkima) in its composition. They also permitted that it be in the sense of mufʿil, i.e. «مُحْكِم», because of His saying: {كِتَابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ}; except that faʿīl in the sense of mufʿil is rare, only a few small words having come in it. They said: «عَقَدْتُ العَسَلَ فهو عَقِيد ومُعْقَد» (I thickened the honey, so it is thickened), and «احتبسْتُ الفرسَ في سبيلِ الله فهو حَبِيس ومُحْبَس» (I endowed the horse in the way of Allah, so it is endowed).

In His saying {نَتْلُوهُ} there is iltifāt (a shift of person) from the third person to the first, because an overt noun has preceded it, namely His saying {والله لاَ يُحِبُّ الظالمين}. So said al-Shaykh, but this is open to question, since it is possible that {والله لاَ يُحِبُّ الظالمين} was brought in as a parenthesis between the parts of this story.

His saying {نَتْلُوهُ} admits two views. One is that, although it is imperfect in form, it is past in meaning, i.e. "that which We have related of the story of ʿĪsā and what happened to him, We recited it to you", like His saying {واتبعوا مَا تَتْلُواْ الشياطين} [al-Baqara: 102]. The second is that it keeps its proper sense, because the discourse is not yet complete and the story of ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, has not been finished, since a remainder of it is left.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِنَّ مَثَلَ عيسى}: a resumptive clause having no technical (syntactic) connection with what precedes it, but rather a connection of meaning. Some claimed that it is the answer to an oath, that oath being His saying {والذكر الحكيم}, as though it were said: "I swear by the wise Reminder, the likeness of ʿĪsā is …". On this view the discourse would be complete at His saying «من الآيات», and then an oath would begin anew, so that the wāw would be a preposition, not a conjunction. This is far-fetched or impossible, since it involves dismantling the composition of the Qurʾān and taking away its splendour and eloquence.

His saying: {خَلَقَهُ مِن تُرَابٍ}: there are two views on this clause. The more evident is that it explains the point of resemblance between the two likenesses, so it then has no grammatical position. The second is that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of Ādam, peace be upon him, with «قد» implied along with it, the governing word being the meaning of the comparison. The hāʾ in «خَلَقه» refers back to Ādam, not to ʿĪsā, since that would corrupt the meaning. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is not permissible for «خلقه» to be a ṣila (relative clause) for Ādam nor a ḥāl of him. Al-Zajjāj said: 'Since the past cannot be a state in which you currently are; rather it is speech cut off from it, containing an explanation of the matter.'" Al-Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is open to question," but he did not explain the point of the question. What appears from this objection is that the criticism — namely his saying "the past cannot be a state in which you currently are" — is not binding, since implying «قد» with it brings it close to the ḥāl. An answer to what al-Zajjāj said may appear from the words of al-Zamakhsharī: "The meaning is: He fashioned him (qaddarahu) as a body of clay, then said to him: Be — i.e. He brought him into being as a human." Al-Shaykh said: "If creation (khalq) meant bringing into being and not fashioning, He would not have said «كن» (Be), because what has been created is not told 'Be', nor brought into being — unless the meaning of «ثم قال له كن» is an expression for breathing the spirit into him."

I say: al-Wāḥidī treated this question and dealt with it thoroughly. He said: "This — meaning His saying «خلقه من تراب» — is neither a ṣila for Ādam nor an adjective, because the ṣila belongs to the vague nouns and the adjective to indefinite nouns; rather it is a new statement by way of explaining the state of Ādam, peace be upon him." He said: "Al-Zajjāj said: 'This is as you say in speech: «مَثَلُك كمثلِ زيد» (your likeness is as the likeness of Zayd), meaning that you resemble him in some act, and then you relate the story of Zayd, saying: he did such and such.'"

His saying: {كُن فَيَكُونُ}: they differed over who was told «كن». Most hold that it was Ādam, peace be upon him. On this view a difficulty arises in the wording of the verse, because He says «كن» to him only before creating him, not after; yet here He says «خَلَقه» and then «قال له: كن». The answer is that Allah the Exalted informed us first that He created Ādam without male or female; then He began another statement which He wished to tell us, saying: "I inform you also, after My first statement, that I said to him 'Be', and he was." So He brought «ثم» for the sense of the statement that came first and the statement that came later in mention, since the creating preceded His saying «كن». This is as you say: «أُخْبِرُك أني أُعطيك اليوم ألفاً، ثم أُخبرك أني أعطتيك أمسِ قبلَه ألفاً» (I tell you that I am giving you a thousand today, then I tell you that I gave you a thousand yesterday, before it) [Translator's note: «أعطتيك» is as printed; the sense is «أعطيتك»]. Yesterday precedes today, and «ثم» was brought only because the statement about today precedes the statement about yesterday, and the statement about yesterday came after the statement about today had passed. Similar is His saying:
{خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا} [al-Zumar: 6]; and He had created «ها» after creating «زوجها» [Translator's note: so printed; the point is that the mate was in fact created before the descendants addressed by «خلقكم»], but this relates to the telling, not the creating, because the interpretation is: "I tell you that I have created you from a single soul — since Ḥawwāʾ was created from his rib — then I tell you that I created its mate from it." Similar to this, from what has come in poetry, is the saying:

1311 - إنَّ مَنْ ساد ثم ساد أبوه ... ثم قد سادَ قبل ذلك جَدُّهُ
(Truly, he who became chief, then his father became chief, then before that his grandfather had become chief.)

It is known that the father precedes him and the grandfather precedes the father, so the ordering refers to the telling, not to the existence. It is also possible that what is meant is that He created him as a mould of earth, then said to him: "Be a human", and then the composition is sound. Some said: the one told «كن» is ʿĪsā, and on this there is no difficulty.

His saying: {فَيَكُونُ}: it is possible that it keeps its proper sense of being future, the meaning being "and he will be as Allah commands", so «فيكونُ» is a narration of the state in which Ādam would be. It is possible that «فيكونُ» means «فكان» (and he was); most of the exegetes and grammarians hold this, and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him, explained it so.

As for «المَثَل» here: some explained it as meaning state and affair. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "That is: the affair of ʿĪsā and his strange state is like the affair of Ādam." On this explanation the kāf keeps its proper sense of being a particle of comparison. Some explained «المَثَل» as meaning description (ṣifa). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This in my view is an error and a weakness in understanding the speech. The meaning is only that the likeness which souls and minds conceive of ʿĪsā is like what is conceived of Ādam, since all people are agreed [that] Allah created him from earth without a male. Likewise His saying {مَّثَلُ الجنة} [al-Raʿd: 35] is an expression for what is conceived of it. The kāf in «كمثل» is a noun, according to the meaning we have mentioned." Al-Shaykh said: "No difference appears to me between these words of his and those of whoever made «المَثَل» mean affair and state, or mean description." I say: it has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara that «المَثَل» is sometimes used to express description and sometimes not, which shows that the two are different; its explanation and people's wording about it have passed. This is indicated by what the author of «ريّ الظمآن» related from al-Fārisī; he said: "It was said: «المَثَل» means description, and your saying 'the description of ʿĪsā is like the description of Ādam' is regular speech; most lexicographers and exegetes hold this. But Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī differed from them all and said: «المَثَل» in the sense of description cannot be validated in the language; «المَثَل» is only comparison, and around this the derived forms of the word turn; there is no sense of description in resemblance. The meaning of «المَثَل» in their speech is that it is a saying which its speaker sends forth for a piece of wisdom, by which he compares matters and sets states against one another." I say: so he distinguished between the word «المَثَل» in its technical usage and description.

Some said the kāf is redundant (zāʾida), and some said «مَثَلاً» is redundant. So three views have been obtained concerning the kāf; the most evident is that it keeps its proper sense as a particle and is not redundant, and its verification has preceded.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how was he likened to him, when he came into being without a father, while Ādam came into being without father or mother? I say: he is like him in one of the two sides, and his being singled out from him by the other side does not prevent his being likened to him, because likeness is a sharing in some of the qualities; and because he was likened to him in that he came into being in a way outside the continuing norm, and in that they are peers; and because coming into being without father and mother is stranger and more contrary to the norm than coming into being without a father, so He likened the strange to the stranger, that it might be more decisive against the opponent and more effective in cutting off the root of his doubt. It is related of one of the scholars that he was taken captive among the Byzantines, and he said to them: 'Why do you worship ʿĪsā?' They said: 'Because he has no father.' He said: 'Then Ādam is more deserving, since he had no parents.' They said: 'He used to bring the dead to life.' He said: 'Then Ḥizqīl is more deserving, because ʿĪsā brought four persons to life, while Ḥizqīl brought eight thousand to life.' They said: 'He used to heal the one born blind and the leper.' He said: 'Then Jirjīs is more deserving, because he was cooked and burned, then came out safe.'"

His saying: {مِن تُرَابٍ}: there are two views on it. The more evident is that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خلقه», i.e. the beginning of his creation is from this genus. The second is that it is a ḥāl of the object of «خلقه», its implied form being «خَلَقه كائناً مِنْ تراب» (He created him being from earth); but the meaning does not support this.

semin-durr:179-179.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَّا كَانَ الله لِيَذَرَ}: this is called the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), and the imperfect verb after it is put in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أن», which may not be made overt. The difference between it and the lām of purpose (lām kay) is that the condition for this one, on the well-known view, is that it come after a negated kāna (being); some stipulate that the kāna be in the past, and some do not stipulate kāna at all. These views have proofs and objections mentioned in the books of grammar, with which I have dispensed here by what I mentioned in «Sharḥ al-Tashīl».
