Regarding the khabar (predicate) of «كان» in this place and what resembles it there are two views. The first, the view of the Basrans, is that it is omitted, and that the lām strengthens the transitivity of that implied khabar because of its weakness; the implied form being: "Allah was not wanting (مريداً) that He leave", so «أن يذر» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «مُريداً», and the implied sense is: Allah was not wanting to leave the believers. The second is the view of the Kufans: that the lām is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation, and that the verb after it is the khabar of «كان»; and the lām, according to them, is what itself governs the accusative in the verb, not an implied «أَنْ»; the implied form according to them being: Allah was not leaving the believers.

Abū al-Baqāʾ declared the Kufan view weak on the grounds that the accusative is found after this lām: "If the accusative is by the lām itself, then it is not redundant; and if the accusative is by an implied «أَنْ», it is corrupt in meaning, because «أَنْ» and what falls in its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the khabar in the chapter of «كان» is, in meaning, the noun [of kāna]; it would then follow that the maṣdar, which is one of the abstract meanings, is true of its noun, which is impossible."

As for his saying "If the accusative is by it, then it is not redundant", that is not conceded, because governing does not preclude redundancy. Do you not see that the prepositions are made redundant while they govern? Likewise «أَنْ» according to al-Akhfash, and «كان» in the poet's saying:
1500 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وجيرانٍ لنا كانوا كرامِ
(… and neighbours of ours who were noble.)
The verification of this has preceded in more than one place.

And «يَذَرُ» is a verb that is not conjugated [fully], like «يَدَعُ», being dispensed with by the conjugation of its synonym, which is «ترك». The wāw was deleted from «يَذَرُ» without any morphological cause; it was only treated on the pattern of «يَدَعُ» because it has its meaning. From «يَدَعُ» the wāw was deleted for a cause, namely the wāw falling between a yāʾ and an implied kasra; whereas the wāw in «يَذَرُ» fell between a yāʾ and an original fatḥa. The verification of the discussion of this has preceded at His saying, the Exalted: {وَذَرُواْ مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الربا} [al-Baqara: 278].

His saying: {حتى يَمِيزَ}: «حتى» here, it is said, is for pure termination (ghāya) in the sense of «إلى», and the verb after it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ»; its verification has preceded in al-Baqara. The termination here is problematic on the apparent wording, because the meaning would become that He, the Exalted, does not leave the believers in the state you are in up to this limit, which is the distinguishing between the wicked and the good; and its implication would be that when the limit is reached, He leaves the believers in the state you are in.

This is the apparent sense of what they said about it being for termination, and the meaning is decidedly not that; this would become parallel to your saying: «لا أُكَلِّم زيداً حتى يَقْدُمَ عمروٌ» (I will not speak to Zayd until ʿAmr arrives), where the speaking is negated up to ʿAmr's arrival. The answer to it: «حتى» is a termination for what is understood from the meaning of this speech, and its meaning is that He, the Exalted, sifts what is among you by trial and testing until He distinguishes the wicked from the good.

Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read here and in al-Anfāl «يُمَيِّز» with the shadda (doubling), and the rest without it. Also from Ibn Kathīr: «يُميز» from أماز. So these are three dialects: one says مازَه, مَيَّزه and أمازه. The doubling and the hamza are not for transfer [i.e. not to make the verb transitive], because the verb before them is already transitive; rather faʿʿala with doubling and afʿala are in the sense of the bare form. Are ماز and مَيّز of one meaning or of two different meanings? Two views. Then those who hold there is a difference disagreed: some said one does not say «ماز» except of many from many; as for one from one, it is مَيَّزت. Hence Abū Muʿādh said: one says «مَيَّزْتُ بين الشيئين ومِزْتُ بين الأشياء» (I distinguished between the two things, and I distinguished among the things). Others said the reverse of this: مِزْتُ بين الشيئين ومَيَّزْتُ بين الأشياءِ, and this is the analogical one, since the doubling signals multiplicity, which suits multiple things. Some preferred «مَيَّز» with doubling on the grounds that it is more frequently used; hence the maṣdar is used only from it, so they said: التمييز, and did not say «المَيْز» — meaning they did not say it in attested usage; otherwise it is permissible by analogy.

His saying: {وَلَكِنَّ الله}: this is a rectification (istidrāk) from the meaning of the preceding speech, because when He, the Exalted, said {وَمَا كَانَ الله لِيُطْلِعَكُمْ}, it might be imagined that He does not let anyone see His unseen, owing to the generality of the address, so He made the rectification of the messengers. The meaning: but Allah chooses, i.e. selects, from His messengers whom He wills, and lets him see the unseen. So it is the opposite of what precedes in meaning. It has preceded that it [lākin] occurs between two opposites and two contradictories, and regarding two differing things there is disagreement.

And «يَجْتَبي»: selects and chooses; the pattern yaftaʿil from جَبَوْتُ المالَ والماءَ and جَبَيْتُهما, two dialects. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «وجَبَتْهُما», apparently a misprint for «جَبَيْتُهما»; translated according to the evident sense.] So the yāʾ in «يَجْتَبي» may be original, or may be converted from a wāw because of the kasra before it.

The mafʿūl bihi of «يشاءُ» is omitted, and one should imply what suits the meaning; the implied form being: whom He wills to let see the unseen.

semin-durr:180-180.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ الذين يَبْخَلُونَ}: Ḥamza read it in the second person (with the address), and the rest in the third person. As for Ḥamza's reading, «الذين» is the first object and «خيراً» the second, and a muḍāf must be omitted so that the khabar (predicate) is true of the mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "and do not think the miserliness of those who are miserly …". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak, because it involves implying the miserliness before mentioning what indicates it." This is open to question, because the indication of the omitted item may come before and may come after, and this is not at all of the chapter of implied pronouns (iḍmār) such that it would be stipulated that what indicates that pronoun come first.

And «هو» has two analyses. The first: it is a separating pronoun (faṣl) between the two objects of «تحسبن». The second, said by Abū al-Baqāʾ: it is a tawkīd (emphasis); this is a mistake, because a pronoun does not emphasise an overt noun, and the first object is an overt noun, but it has been omitted as stated before. Some express this by saying "the first object was implied (uḍmira)", meaning it was omitted, so do not be misled by this wording. And «هو» in this question must be a faṣl, because it cannot avoid being either a mubtadaʾ, a badal (substitute) or a tawkīd. The first is excluded because of the accusative of what follows it, namely «خيراً»; likewise the second, because it would have to agree with what precedes it in case-inflection, so one should say «إياه» not «هو»; likewise the third, for what preceded.

As for the reading of the majority, it is possible that the verb be attributed to an absent pronoun: either the Messenger or some thinker; and it is possible that it be attributed to «الذين». If it is attributed to an absent pronoun, then «الذين» is the first object on the omission of a muḍāf, as stated in Ḥamza's reading, i.e. the miserliness of those; the implied form being: and let not the Messenger, or anyone, think the miserliness of those who are miserly to be good. And «هو» is a faṣl as stated, so the two readings coincide in meaning and in analysis. If it is attributed to «الذين», then regarding the first object there are two analyses. The first: it is omitted because «يبخلون» indicates it, as if it were said: «ولا يَحْسَبَنَّ الباخِلون بخلَهم هو خيراً لهم» (let not the misers think their miserliness to be good for them), with «هو» a faṣl. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«يبخلون» indicates this miserliness, just as «السفيه» indicates «السَّفَه» in the poet's saying:
1501 - إذا نُهِي السَّفيهُ جرى إليه ... وخالَفَ والسفيهُ إلى خلافِ
(When the foolish one is forbidden, he runs towards it [folly] and opposes — the foolish one inclines to opposition.)
i.e. he ran towards folly." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "The indication in the two is not equal, for two reasons. First: the indication of the verb on the maṣdar is stronger than the indication of the active participle on it, and more frequent; and that [the participle indicating it] is found only in this verse, or another if it has come. Second: the verse has an implied pronoun (iḍmār), not an omission, while the verse [of the Quran] has an omission."

The second analysis: the object is «هو» itself, which is the pronoun of the miserliness indicated by «يبخلون», like His saying: {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ للتقوى} [al-Māʾida: 8]. Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and it is also a mistake, because it ought to come in the form of the accusative, so that one says «إياه», since it is accusative by «يَحْسَبَنَّ»; and there is no need for us to claim that it is of the chapter of borrowing the nominative pronoun in place of the accusative, as in their saying «ما أنا كأنت، ولا أنت كأنا» (I am not like you, nor are you like me), where the nominative pronoun was borrowed in place of the genitive pronoun.

There is another, strange analysis of the verse, produced by the Shaykh. He said: "It is that the question be of the chapter of iʿmāl (tanāzuʿ, contention of two governors) when we make the verb attributed to «الذين». That is, «يَحْسَبَنَّ» requires two objects and «يَبْخلون» requires an object through a preposition. So His saying {مَآ آتَاهُمُ الله مِن فَضْلِهِ} is required by «يحسبن» as a first object, with «هو» a faṣl and «خيراً» the second object; and it is required by «يبخلون» through the mediation of the preposition. So the second was made to govern, on the more eloquent [usage] and according to what came in the Quran, namely «يبخلون», which was made transitive by the preposition and took its governed item; and the first governed item of «يحسبن» was deleted while its second governed item remained, because there was no contention over it — the contention occurred only over the first. Its deletion alone was allowed, just as the deletion of the two objects was allowed in Sībawayh's question: «متى رأيت أو قلت: زيد منطلق» (When did you see, or say: Zayd is departing?), where «رأيت» and «قلت» contend over «زيدُ منطلقٌ»; whereas in the verse they contend only over the first. The implied meaning is: «ولا يَحْسَبَنَّ ما آتاهم الله من فضله هو خيراً لهم الناسُ الذي يَبْخلون به» (and let not the people who are miserly with what Allah has given them of His bounty think it to be good for them). On this implied form «هو» is a faṣl for the omitted «ما آتاهم», not for their implied miserliness as in the view of the majority. A parallel of this construction is: «ظنَّ الذي مَرَّ بِهندٍ هي المنطلقةَ», the meaning being: the person who passed by Hind thought her to be the one departing. So what the two verbs contended over is the first object; the second verb was made to govern it, and the first remained requiring it [the first object] as omitted and requiring the second [object] as stated, since no contention occurred over it." End [of his words].

Besides the strangeness of this analysis and its lengthening with the parallel and the implied form, it is open to question. That is because the grammarians stated explicitly that when we make the second govern, and the first needs a pronoun of the contended item: if it requires it in the nominative, it is implied in it; and if it requires it in other than the nominative, it is deleted — unless it is one of the two objects of «ظَنَّ», in which case it is not deleted but made a pronoun and placed later. They gave as the reason that if it were deleted, a predicate would remain without what it is predicated of, or the reverse. This is the view of the Basrans, and there is room for discussion in it: someone may say that it was deleted for brevity (ikhtiṣār), not for restriction (iqtiṣār), and you permit the deletion of one of them for brevity outside of tanāzuʿ, so let it be permitted in tanāzuʿ, since there is no difference. In that case the Shaykh's analysis is strengthened by this discussion; or else one adopts the view of the Kufans, for they permit deletion in what we are dealing with.

Makkī mentioned the preferring of each of the two readings, and said:
[Translator's note: the quotation from Makkī is missing in the source text; it breaks off here and the text continues with the next topic.]

And «ميراث» is a maṣdar like «المِيعاد»; its yāʾ is from a wāw, converted because of the kasra before it while it is sukūn-bearing, since it is from الوراثة, like «الميقات» and «الميزان» from الوقت and الوزن.

Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read: «يَعْمَلُون» in the third person, following on from His saying {الذين يَبْخَلُونَ}, and the rest in the second person. In this there are two analyses. The first: it is iltifāt (a shift of person), the ones meant being those who are miserly. The second: it refers back to His saying {وَإِن تُؤْمِنُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ}.

semin-durr:181-181.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قَوْلَ الذين قالوا إِنَّ}: the governor of «إنَّ» is «قالوا»; so «إنَّ» and what falls in its scope is in the position of the accusative by «قالوا», not by «قول». Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted that the question be of the chapter of tanāzuʿ (contention of two governors), I mean between the maṣdar (verbal noun), which is «قول», and the verb, which is «قالوا», the two contending over «أَنْ» and what is in its scope. He said: "It may be governed by the muḍāf «قول», because it is a maṣdar; this is an analysis on the view of the Kufans in letting the first [governor] govern, which is a weak view, and it grows weaker here in that the second is a verb and the first a maṣdar, and the governing of the verb is stronger." The apparent sense of his words is that the question is one of tanāzuʿ, and the weakness in his view is only from the side of letting the first govern; so if we supposed the second to govern, it ought to be permissible in his view. But another obstacle prevents that, namely: when the second needs a pronoun of the contended item, it takes it and it may not be deleted, and here it is not mentioned; so this indicates that in his view it is not of tanāzuʿ except on the view of the Kufans, which is weak as he mentioned. [Translator's note: the bracketed «[هذا]» is in the printed source.] And see how they emphasised the clause containing what they attributed to Him, the Exalted, and the absence of that in what they attributed to themselves, as though it were with people a known matter.

His saying: {سَنَكْتُبُ}: Ḥamza read with yāʾ, passive (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), with «ما» and its ṣila (relative clause) standing in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent); and «قَتْلُهم» in the nominative, conjoined to the relative noun; and «يقول» with the yāʾ of the third person. The rest read with nūn, for the majestic speaker, so «ما» is in the position of the accusative, and «قتلَهم» in the accusative conjoined to it, and «نقولُ» likewise with nūn. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read: «سَتُكْتب» with the tāʾ of the feminine, interpreting «ما قالوا» as «مقالتهم» (their saying). Ibn Masʿūd read, and so it is in his codex: «سنكتب ما يقولون ويُقال». And al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj: «سَيَكْتب» in the third person, active, i.e. Allah the Exalted or the angel. And «ما» in all of that may be a nominal relative, which is the apparent view, with the referent pronoun deleted because the conditions for deletion are complete, the implied form being: we shall write that which they say. It may also be maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e. their saying, meaning by it in that case the object, i.e. what they said, as in their expression «ضَرْب الأمير» («the emir's striking», i.e. what the emir has struck).

semin-durr:42-42.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذْ قَالَتِ الملائكة}: if you wish, you may make this adverbial conjoined (nasaq) to the adverbial before it, namely His words {إِذْ قَالَتِ امرأت عِمْرَانَ}; and if you wish, you may make it accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb. Abū al-Baqāʾ said this.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿUmar read: «وإذ قال الملائكة» without the feminine tāʾ; the explanation of that has preceded under {فَنَادَاهُ الملائكة}. The object of the saying (maʿmūl al-qawl) is the sentence emphasised with «إنّ» in His words {إِنَّ الله اصطفاك}. He repeated the choosing (iṣṭifāʾ) to raise her rank.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He chose you first when He accepted you from your mother, reared you and singled you out for exalted honour; and He chose you last over the women of the worlds by granting you ʿĪsā without a father, which had not happened to any woman."
اصْطَفَى is the iftaʿala form from al-ṣafwa (the pure, choice part); the tāʾ was changed to ṭāʾ because of the emphatic (iṭbāq) letter, and its explanation has preceded in al-Baqara. The reason for its being made transitive with «على» has also preceded, even though it is originally made transitive with «مِنْ». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "He repeated «اصطفى» [either] for tawkīd (emphasis), or to make clear over whom He chose her." Al-Wāḥidī said: "He repeated the choosing because the meanings of the two choosings differ: the first choosing is general, and the righteous women enter into it; the second is a choosing through the special qualities by which she was singled out." [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark of al-Wāḥidī's words is missing in the source.]

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His words: {ذلك مِنْ أَنَبَآءِ الغيب نُوحِيهِ}: several views are possible here. The first: «ذلك» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "The matter is that." On this view, «مِنْ أنباءِ الغيب» may be part of the completion of this speech, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the demonstrative; or the pause may be on «ذلك», with «مِنْ أنباءِ الغيب» attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows it, and the sentence «نوحيه» is then either explanatory, elucidating the sentence before it, or a ḥāl.
The second: «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, «من أنباء الغيب» is its khabar, and the sentence «نوحيه» is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). The pronoun in «نوحيه» refers back to al-ghayb (the unseen), i.e. the matter and affair is that We reveal the unseen to you, inform you of it and acquaint you with the stories of those before you, although you never studied with people of learning and reports; for that reason the imperfect is used in «نوحيه». This is better than referring it back to «ذلك», because referring it to the unseen covers the stories that have preceded and those that have not, whereas if you referred it to «ذلك» it would be restricted to what has passed and preceded.
The third: «نوحيه» is the khabar, and «من أنباء الغيب» is on its two preceding views: either a ḥāl from «ذلك» or attached to «نوحيه». On this view a third view is also possible for it: that it be made a ḥāl from the object of «نوحيه», i.e. "We reveal it, it being part of the reports of the unseen."
His words: {إِذْ يُلْقُون}: there are two views on it. The first, which is the apparent one: it is accusative (manṣūb) by the notion of "being settled" (al-istiqrār) that governs the adverbial serving as khabar. The second, held by al-Fārisī: it is accusative by «كنت». This is surprising from him, because he claims that it [kāna] is stripped of indicating an event, so how can it govern the adverbial, when the adverbial is a container for events? What appears is that al-Fārisī only permitted this on the basis of what may possibly be meant in the verse, namely that «كان» is complete (tāmma), in the sense of: "and you did not exist at that time".
The pronoun in «لديهم» refers back to those who disputed over Maryam, even though they have not been mentioned, because the context has indicated them. This statement and the like of it — such as the words of Allah the Exalted {وَمَا كُنْتَ بِجَانِبِ الطور} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 46] and {وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ أجمعوا أَمْرَهُمْ} [Yūsuf: 102] — even though its negation is known necessarily, runs in the manner of mockery of those who deny revelation. That is: since it is known that you were not contemporary with those people and did not study with anyone in learning, nothing remains for your knowledge of it except by way of revelation.
Al-aqlām is the plural of «قَلَم», which is faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl, i.e. maqlūm (cut). Al-qalm is cutting; similar to it are al-qabaḍ and al-naqaṣ in the sense of the thing seized and the thing diminished. It was called qalam because it is cut (yuqlam); from it comes «قَلَّمْتُ ظُفْرِي», i.e. I cut my nail and evened it. Zuhayr said:
1279 - لدى أَسَدٍ شاكي السلاحِ مُقَذَّفٍ ... له لِبَدٌ أضفارُهُ لمْ تُقَلَّمِ
(Beside a lion bristling with weapons, thick-fleshed, with a mane, whose claws have not been clipped.)
It was also said: the pen was called qalam by likening it to al-qulāma, which is a weak plant, because it is pared thin and so becomes weak. There is disagreement about what is meant by al-aqlām here: are they the pens one writes with, or arrows used for casting lots, like al-azlām?
His words: {أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ}: this sentence is in the position of the accusative, because it is attached to an omitted verb, and that verb is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, its implied form being: "they cast their pens, looking [to see] which of them would take charge of Maryam", or "[to] know". Al-Zamakhsharī permitted supplying «يقولون» (saying), so that it would be reported speech governed by it; this is indicated by His words {يُلْقُون}. His words {وَمَا كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ} are like His words {وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يُلْقُون}.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
The words of the Exalted: {اللهم}: the Basrans and the Kufans disagreed about this noble word. The Basrans said: the origin is يا الله; the vocative particle was omitted and this doubled mīm was substituted for it. This is peculiar to this noble name, so substituting the mīm for the vocative particle is not permissible in any other. As proof that it is a substitute for «يا», they adduced that the two are not combined, so one does not say يا اللهمَّ except under poetic necessity, as in his words:
1212 - وما عليكِ أَنْ تقولي كلما ... سَبَّحْتِ أو هَلَّلْتِ يا اللهم ما
أرْدُدْ علينَا شَيْخَنا مُسَلَّما
(What harm is there for you in saying, whenever you glorify or proclaim His oneness: "O Allah, return our old man to us safe and sound".)
The Kufans said: the doubled mīm is the remnant of an omitted verb, its implied form being «أُمَّنا بخير», i.e.: "aim at us with good", from your saying «أمَّمْتُ زيداً», i.e. I aimed at him; and from it: {ولا آمِّينَ البيت الحرام} [al-Māʾida: 2], i.e.: those heading for it. On this view, combining «يا» and the mīm is not a poetic necessity in their opinion, since the mīm is not a substitute for it. The Basrans refuted them in this on the ground that «اللهم أُمَّنَا بخير» has been heard, and the Exalted said: {اللهم إِن كَانَ هذا هُوَ الحق مِنْ عِندِكَ فَأَمْطِرْ} [al-Anfāl: 32], where what is asked for is stated explicitly; had the mīm been the remnant of «أمَّنا», the meaning would have been corrupted. So its falsity is evident.
This is one of the nouns that are bound to the vocative, so it is not permissible for it to occur elsewhere; yet under poetic necessity it has occurred as a fāʿil (agent). Al-Farrāʾ recited:
1213 - كحَلْفَةٍ من أبي دِثار ... يَسْمَعُها اللهُمَ الكُبارُ
(Like an oath from Abū Dithār, which Allah the Most Great hears.)
Here he used it as a fāʿil of his words «يَسْمَعُها». Lightening its mīm is not permissible, but al-Farrāʾ allowed it and recited the verse «يَسْمَعُها اللَهُمَ الكُبار» with a light mīm, since the metre cannot be set right except thus. One of them said: "This is a gross error, because the mīm is the remnant of «أُمَّنا», which is al-Farrāʾ's opinion; so how could al-Farrāʾ allow it?" And he answered regarding the verse that the transmission is not like that; rather the transmission is: يَسْمَعُها لاهُه الكُبارُ. I say: this [does not contradict the other transmission, for just as this one is sound], that one is sound. Al-Zajjāj refuted al-Farrāʾ's position on the ground that if the origin were «يا لله أُمَّنا», it would have been pronounced so somewhere as an indication of the origin, as they said, for وَيْلُمِّه: ويلٌ لأُمِه.
Among the rules of this word also is that its use became so frequent that the alif and lām were dropped from it in their saying «لاهُمَّ», i.e.: اللهم. The poet said:
1214 - لا هُمَّ إنَّ عامرَ بنَ جَهْمِ ... أَحْرَم حَجَّاً في ثيابٍ دُسْمِ
(O Allah, ʿĀmir ibn Jahm entered the state of iḥrām for the pilgrimage in greasy garments.)
And another said:
1215 - لا هُمَّ إنَّ جُرْهُما عِبادُكا ... الناسُ طَرْفٌ وهمُ بِلادُكا
(O Allah, Jurhum are Your servants; the people are newcomers, while they are Your land.)
There are many investigations concerning this word whose place is elsewhere.
His words: {مَالِكَ الملك}: there are several aspects in it. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) from «اللهم». The second: that it is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). The third: that it is a second one addressed in the vocative, from which the vocative particle has been omitted, i.e.: يا مالكَ المُلك; and this is in reality the badal, since the badal is on the intention of repeating the governing element, except that the difference is that this one is not a follower (tābiʿ). The fourth: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «اللهم» according to its position, which is why it is accusative. This is not the position of Sībawayh, for Sībawayh does not allow describing this word because of the mīm at its end, since it has taken it out of the class of its counterparts among nouns. Al-Mubarrad allowed it and al-Zajjāj chose it; they said: because the mīm is a substitute for «يا», and the one addressed with «يا» may be described, so likewise with what substitutes for it; moreover, the noun has not changed from its rule — do you not see that it remains indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma just as it was indeclinable with «يا»?
Al-Fārisī defended [Sībawayh] on the ground that there is nothing among the described nouns of the pattern of «اللهم»; so since it differs from what described nouns are like and has entered the domain of sound-words (aṣwāt), which are not described, it must not be described. And the analogy for singular definite nouns in the vocative is that they are not described, as some people held, because they stand in the place of what is not described; and just as, when it stood in the place of what is not inflected, it was not inflected, likewise when it stood in the place of what is not described, it was not described. As for his words:
1216 - يا حكمُ الوارثُ عن عبد الملكْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O Ḥakam, the heir of ʿAbd al-Malik …)
and his words:
1217 - يا حَكَمُ بنَ المنذرِ بنَ الجارودْ ... سُرادِقُ المجدِ عليك مَمْدُودْ
(O Ḥakam son of al-Mundhir son of al-Jārūd, the pavilion of glory is spread over you.)
and [his words]:
1218 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . يا عُمَرُ الجَوادا
(… O ʿUmar, the generous one.)
— the first is on the implication of «أنت», the second on a second vocative, and the third on the concealment of «أعني» ("I mean"). So since the basic rule for this noun is that it is not described, for the reason we mentioned, «اللهم» is more entitled not to be described, because before the mīm was joined to it, it stood in the place of what is not described; and when the mīm was joined to it, it was cast together with it in a special form, and its rule became the rule of sound-words, and the rule of sound-words is that they are not described, such as «غاق» (the crow's caw). This, with the mīm joined to it, is like a sound joined to a sound, such as «حَيَّهَلَ»; so it has the right not to be described, just as «حيهل» is not described. End of what Abū ʿAlī used to defend Sībawayh, even though it does not stand up as a preventing argument.
His words: {تُؤْتِي}: this clause and what is conjoined to it may be resumptive, explaining His words {مَالِكَ الملك}; or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the one addressed. There is disagreement over a ḥāl being accusative from the one addressed in the vocative; the sound view is that it is permissible, because it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and just as the ḥāl serves to explain the state of the fāʿil, it serves to explain the state of the object. For this reason the skilled grammarians parsed the words of al-Nābigha:
1219 - يا دارمَيَّةَ بالعَلْياءِ فالسَّنَدِ ... أَقْوَت وطالَ عليها سالِفُ الأبدِ
(O abode of Mayya at al-ʿAlyāʾ and then al-Sanad, it has become deserted and long ages have passed over it.)
saying that «بالعلياء» is a ḥāl from «دارمَيَّة», and likewise «أَقْوت».
The third of the aspects of «تُؤتي» is that it is the khabar (predicate) of a concealed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: أنت تُؤتي ("You give"), so the clause is nominal; in that case it may be resumptive or circumstantial.
His words: {تَشَآءُ}, i.e.: You will to give it, and You will to take it away; the object after "willing" was omitted because it is known.
His words: {بِيَدِكَ الخير}: [it was said: in the speech there is the omission of a conjoined element, its implied form being: "and evil"; it was omitted, as in His words]: {تَقِيكُمُ الحر} [al-Naḥl: 81], i.e.: and the cold; and as in his words:
1220 - كأنَّ الحَصَا مِنْ خلفِها وأمامِها ... إذا نَجَلْتهُ رِجْلُها خَذْفَ أَعْسَرا
(As though the pebbles behind her and before her, when her foot kicks them, are the flicking of a left-handed man.)
i.e.: and her hand.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how did He say «بيدِك الخيرُ», mentioning good without evil? I say: because the speech concerns only the good which Allah drives to the believers, and that is what the disbelievers denied; so He said: in Your hand is the good; You give it to Your friends in spite of Your enemies." End.
This is a very good answer. Then he mentioned further words agreeing with his doctrine, which we have no need of. It was also said: this is one of the courtesies of the Qurʾān, in that it explicitly states only what is beloved to His creation; similar to it are his words: «والشرُّ ليس إليك» ("and evil is not ascribed to You") «[Translator's note: from a prophetic ḥadīth]», and His words: {وَإِذَا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 80].
Al-nazʿ is pulling; one says: نَزَعَهُ يَنْزِعُه نَزْعاً when he pulled it away from him. It is used to express inclination, and from it: «نَزَعَتْ نفسُه إلى كذا» ("his soul inclined to such-and-such"), as though a puller pulled it. It is used to express removal: «نَزَعَ الله عنك الشَّر», i.e.: He removed it; {يَنزِعُ عَنْهُمَا لِبَاسَهُمَا} [al-Aʿrāf: 27], i.e.: removing; and like this verse, for the meaning is: and He removes sovereignty.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
The words of the Exalted: {تُولِجُ}: like His words «تُؤْتِي», and what applies to it has already been discussed. One says: وَلَجَ يَلِجُ وُلوجاً, and لِجَةً like عِدَة, and وَلْجاً like وَعْد; and اتَّلَجَ يَتَّلِجُ اتِّلاجاً, the origin being اوْتَلَجَ يَوْتَلِجُ اوْتِلاَجاً, the wāw being changed into tāʾ before the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form, as in اتَّعَدَ يَتَّعِدُ اتِّعاداً. The poet said:
1221 - فإنَّ القوافِي تَتَّلِجْنَ مَوالِجاً ... تضايَقُ عنها أَنْ تَوَلَّجَها الإِبَرْ
(Rhymes enter into entrances so narrow that needles would be too tight to pass through them.)
Al-wulūj is entering, and al-īlāj is causing to enter, and the meaning of the verse is accordingly. As for the one who said that its meaning is decrease, he only meant that this is by way of what necessarily follows (al-lāzim), because when the Blessed and Exalted causes something of this to enter into that, He has decreased what is taken from the one from which what is inserted into the other was taken. Some claimed that «تُولِج» means "You raise" and that «في» means «على» ("upon"), and that is nothing.
His words: {مِنَ الميت}: the readers differed over this word in degrees. Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read the word «المَيْت» without the feminine tāʾ, lightened, throughout the whole Qurʾān, whether it describes animate beings, as in {تُخْرِجُ الحي مِنَ الميت}, or inanimate things, as in the words of the Exalted {إلى بَلَدٍ مَّيِّتٍ} [Fāṭir: 9] and {لِبَلَدٍ مَّيِّتٍ} [al-Aʿrāf: 57], indefinite or definite as mentioned — except for the words of the Exalted {إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ مَّيِّتُونَ} [al-Zumar: 30] and His words {وَمَا هُوَ بِمَيِّتٍ} [verse: 17] in Ibrāhīm, referring to one who has not yet died, for all of them read these with the doubled yāʾ. Likewise the word «الميتة» in His words {وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ الأرض الميتة} [Yā Sīn: 33] — but not the «الميتة» mentioned together with blood, for that one was read doubled only by some readers of the irregular (shādhdh) readings, and it has already been mentioned in al-Baqara; likewise His words {وَإِن يَكُن مَّيْتَةً} [al-Anʿām: 139], {بَلْدَةً مَّيْتاً} [al-Zukhruf: 11] and {إِلاَّ أَن يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً} [al-Anʿām: 145], for these are lightened according to everyone. Nāfiʿ read all of that doubled. The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim agreed with Ibn Kathīr and those with him in al-Anʿām in His words {أَوَ مَن كَانَ مَيْتاً فَأَحْيَيْنَاهُ} [verse: 122], in al-Ḥujurāt in {أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتاً} [verse: 12], and {الأرض الميتة} in Yā Sīn, and they agreed with Nāfiʿ in everything else. So they combined the two dialectal forms, signalling that each of the two readings is sound. The two have one meaning, because the pattern fayʿil may be lightened in weak-lettered roots by dropping one of its two yāʾs, so one says هَيْن and هيِّن, لَيْن and ليِّن, مَيْت and مَيِّت. From this are the words of the poet, who combined the two forms:
1222 - ليسَ مَنْ ماتَ فاستراحَ بميْتٍ ... إنَّما المَيْتُ مَيِّتُ الأَحْيَاءِ
إنما المَيْتُ مَنْ يعيشُ كئيباً ... كاسِفاً بالُهُ قليلُ الرَّجاءِ
(Whoever has died and found rest is not dead; the dead is only the dead among the living. The dead is only he who lives in sorrow, his mind gloomy, his hope small.)
Some claimed that «مَيْتاً» with the light form is for one on whom death has fallen, and that the doubled form is used both for one who has died and for one who has not died, as in the words of the Exalted {إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ مَّيِّتُونَ} [al-Zumar: 30]. This is refuted by what has preceded of the reading of the two brothers and Ḥafṣ, since they lightened it in a place where death cannot be meant, namely His words {أَوَ مَن كَانَ مَيْتاً} [al-Anʿām: 122], since what is meant by it is disbelief, figuratively.
This is with respect to the readers. If you wish, you may set it out with respect to the word «الميت» itself and say: this word, with respect to the reading of the Seven, is of three kinds. A kind about whose doubling there is no disagreement, namely what has not died, such as {وَمَا هُوَ بِمَيِّتٍ} and {إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ مَّيِّتُونَ}; a kind about whose lightening there is no disagreement, namely what preceded in His words {الميتة والدم}, {إِلاَّ أَن يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً}, His words {وَإِن يَكُن مَّيْتَةً} and His words {فَأَنشَرْنَا بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتاً}; and a kind in which there is disagreement, namely everything else, the details of which have already been given.
It has also preceded that the origin of ميِّت is مَيْوِت, which was assimilated, and that there is disagreement about its pattern: whether its pattern is fayʿil, which is the position of the Basrans, or faʿīl, which is the position of the Kufans, its origin being مَوِيت. They (the Kufans) said: because fayʿil is absent among sound roots, so it is all the more fitting that it not be found among weak ones. The Basrans answered their claim that it has no counterpart among sound roots by noting that قَضاة as the plural of «قاض» has no counterpart among sound roots. The explanation of this answer is: we do not concede that a weak form must have a counterpart among sound ones; and what shows the absence of such a necessary link is «قُضاة», plural of قاضٍ — and concerning «قضاة» there is a long disagreement which this is not the place to mention. The Basrans objected against them that if its pattern were faʿīl, it would have had to remain sound, just as its counterparts with wāw remained sound, such as طَوِيل, عَوِيل and قَوِيم; so since it was made weak by changing and assimilation, it cannot be claimed that its origin is faʿīl, because it differs from its counterparts. This is a good refutation.
His words: {وَتَرْزُقُ مَن تَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ}: the bāʾ may be for a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent), i.e.: You provide for him while You have not reckoned with him, i.e. You have not straitened him; or from the object, i.e.: not being straitened. Discussion of the like of this has preceded in full in al-Baqara at the words of the Exalted {والله يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ} [al-Baqara: 212], which makes repeating it unnecessary.
This verse comprises kinds of rhetorical embellishment (badīʿ). Among them: identical paronomasia (al-tajnīs al-mumāthil) in His words «مالكَ المُلْك تُؤتي المُلَكْ وتَنْزِعُ الملك». Among them: antithesis (al-ṭibāq), which is combining two opposites or what resembles them; that is in His words «تُؤْتي الملك وتَنْزِع», in «تُعِزُّ وتُذِلٌّ», in His words «بيدك الخيرُ», i.e. "and evil" according to some, in His words «الليل والنهار», and in His words «الحي والميت». Among them: returning the ends upon the beginnings and the beginnings upon the ends (radd al-aʿjāz ʿalā al-ṣudūr), in His words {وَتُولِجُ الليل فِي النهار وَتُولِجُ النهار فِي الليل} and in His words {وَتُخْرِجُ الحي مِنَ الميت وَتُخْرِجُ الميت مِنَ الحي}; similar to it is: «عاداتُ الساداتِ ساداتُ العاداتِ» ("the habits of the masters are the masters of habits"). Among the meanings it contains is emphasis, by putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun in His words «تؤتى الملك» etc.; and, in its figurative usage, putting a particle in the place of what has its meaning; and omission because the meaning is understood.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
The discussion of this has already preceded in detail. But al-Jurjānī reported here that «ألم» is an allusion to the letters of the alphabet, as if He were saying: "These letters are your book", or something like this; and {لا إله إِلاَّ هُوَ الحي القيوم نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ الكتاب} [Āl ʿImrān: 2-3] indicates the predicate (khabar) of these letters whose mention He left out. That, in its construction (naẓm), is like His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَمَن شَرَحَ الله صَدْرَهُ لِلإِسْلاَمِ فَهُوَ على نُورٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ} [al-Zumar: 22], where He left out the answer because His saying {فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْقَاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ مِّن ذِكْرِ الله} [al-Zumar: 22] indicates it, its implied form being: "like one whose heart has hardened?" And of this is the saying of the poet:

1156 - فلا تَدْفِنوني إنَّ دَفْني مُحَرَّمٌ ... عليكم ولكنْ خامِري أمُّ عامرِ
(Do not bury me, for burying me is forbidden to you; rather [leave me to the one told]: "Hide, Umm ʿĀmir!")

i.e. "but leave me to the one to whom it is said: «خامري أم عامر» 'Hide, Umm ʿĀmir' [i.e. the hyena]". End of quotation.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: On this view — meaning the view of al-Jurjānī — it is fitting that «نَزَّل» be the khabar of His saying «الله», so that the discourse is connected to this meaning. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What al-Jurjānī mentioned is open to question, because his examples do not truly resemble the meaning he aimed at. What he said about the verse is possible, but the most excellent [view] of the verse is that «ألم» does not attach what follows it to itself in meaning, and that His saying {الله لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ الحي القيوم} [Āl ʿImrān: 2] is a discourse that begins decisively, a clause refuting the Christians of Najrān." I say: This that the Shaykh rejected of the Qāḍī al-Jurjānī['s view] is what al-Jurjānī chose and prided himself on, and he made it the best of the views he related in his book «نظم القرآن» (The Construction of the Quran).

semin-durr:45-45.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِذْ قَالَتِ الملائكة}: there are several views on this adverbial. The first: it is accusative (manṣūb) by «يختصمون». The second: it is a badal (substitute) from «إذ يختصمون»; this is the view of al-Zajjāj. Both of these views are far-fetched, in that they entail that the time of the disputing and the time of the saying were the same, which was not the case, because at the time of the disputing she was very young, and the time of the angels' saying was long after that. Al-Zamakhsharī sensed this objection and answered that the disputing and the glad tidings occurred within a broad period of time, just as you say: "I met him in such-and-such a year", meaning that the meeting only took place in part of the year; and so is this. The third: it is a badal from the first «إذ قالت الملائكة»; al-Zamakhsharī began with this, as though preferring it, but it is far-fetched because of the great amount of separation between the badal and what it substitutes for. The fourth: it is accusative by an implied verb.
Al-waḥy is swift indication; because it includes swiftness, one says «أمرٌ وَحْيٌ» (a swift matter). It was also said: it is the casting of the meaning of speech to one whom one wishes to inform. Waḥy may be by gesture and pointing; the poet said:
1280 - لأوْحَتْ إلينا والأنامِلُ رُسْلُها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(She would have signalled to us, her fingertips being her messengers …)
And the words of Allah the Exalted: {فأوحى إِلَيْهِمْ أَن سَبِّحُواْ}, i.e. he pointed to them. It may be by writing; Zuhayr said:
1281 - أتى العُجْمَ والآفاقَ منه قصائدٌ ... بَقَيْنَ بقاءَ الوَحْي في الحَجَر الأَصَمِّ
(Odes from him reached the non-Arabs and the horizons, and remained as writing remains in solid rock.)
Al-waḥy is also applied to the written thing; the poet said:
1282 - فَمَدافِعُ الرَّيَّانِ عُرِّي رَسْمُها ... خَلَقاً كما ضَمِنَ الوُحِيَّ سِلامُها
(And the watercourses of al-Rayyān — their traces have been laid bare, worn out, as their stones hold the inscriptions.)
It was said: al-wuḥiyy is the plural of waḥy, like fals and fulūs, and the ḥāʾ was given kasra for harmony (itbāʿ). Al-waḥy is also inspiration (ilhām): {وأوحى رَبُّكَ إلى النحل} [al-Naḥl: 68]. Revelation to the messengers takes various forms mentioned in the exegesis.
His words: {بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنْهُ}: [«منه»] is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) as a naʿt (adjective) of «كلمة». What is meant by the word (kalima) here is ʿĪsā; he was called a word because he came into existence through it, namely His words {كُنْ فَيَكُونُ}; so it is of the type of applying the cause to what is caused. «اسمه» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «المسيح» is its khabar (predicate). «عيسى» is a badal from it, or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It cannot be a second khabar, because multiple predicates require a multiple subject, and the subject here is singular, namely His word «اسمه»; had «عيسى» been another khabar, it would have been «أسماؤه», or «أسماؤها» with the feminine referring to the word." I say: this is according to one opinion; as for whoever permits that, he has parsed «عيسى» as a second khabar. Some parsed it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "he is ʿĪsā". So these are three views on «عيسى». On the third view a fourth view is possible, namely the accusative by an implied «أَعْني» (I mean), because everything that may be cut off [from what precedes] in the nominative may be cut off in the accusative.
The alif and lām in «المسيح» are for predominance (ghalaba), as they are in al-Ṣaʿiq and al-ʿAyyūq. There are two views on it. The first: it is faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil, converted from it for intensiveness; it was said: because he "wiped" (masaḥa) the earth by travelling, and it was said: because he would wipe the afflicted person and he would be healed. It was also said: [faʿīl] in the sense of mafʿūl, because he was wiped (anointed) with blessing, or because he was flat-footed (masīḥ al-qadam); the poet said:
1283 - باتَ يُقاسيها غلامٌ كالزَلَمْ ... خَدَلَّجُ الساقَيْنِ ممسوحُ القَدَمْ
(A lad like a lot-arrow spent the night toiling with her [the camels], thick-calved, flat-footed.)
Or because his face was "wiped" with comeliness; the poet said:
1284 - على وَجْهِ مَيٍّ مَسْحَةٌ من مَلاحة ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(On the face of Mayy there is a trace of comeliness …)
The second: its pattern is mafʿil from al-siyāḥa (travelling). On all of this, it is transferred from the adjective. Abū ʿUbayd said: its origin in Hebrew is «مسيخاً», and it was altered. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "On this view it is an improvised (murtajal) name, not derived from al-masḥ nor from al-siyāḥa." I say: his saying "not derived" is correct, but it does not necessarily follow from that that it is improvised, since it is possible that in their language it was transferred from something they had.
He used the pronoun in His word «اسمه» in the masculine, even though it refers back to «الكلمة» (feminine), out of regard for the meaning, since what is meant by it is masculine.
«ابن مريم» may be a naʿt of «عيسى». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«عيسى» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; what calls for this is that His words «ابن مريم» are a naʿt of «عيسى», since people have agreed on writing it without an alif. As for [taking it] as badal or ʿaṭf bayān, «ابن مريم» cannot be a naʿt of «عيسى», because the name here is not meant to be the person. This line of thought is Abū ʿAlī's, and the opening of the statement is open to question." End of quote. I say: he made its being a naʿt necessary because it is written without an alif, then said: "As for badal or ʿaṭf bayān, «ابن مريم» cannot be a naʿt of «عيسى»" — meaning «عيسى» as a badal from «المسيح» — so he made it not a naʿt of it despite the existence of the evidence he mentioned, namely its being written without an alif.
Abū al-Baqāʾ prohibited «ابن مريم» from being a badal or a naʿt of «عيسى». He said: "Because «ابن مريم» is not a name; do you not see that you do not say 'This man is Ibn ʿAmr' unless it has been attached to him as a proper name?" I say: this reasoning he mentioned only holds for its not being a badal; as for its being a naʿt, it does not prevent that. Rather, if it were a name, its being a naʿt would be impossible, since it would then take the ruling of proper names, and proper names are not used as descriptions. Do you not see that if you named a man "Ibn ʿAmr", «ابن عمرو» could not then occur as a naʿt?
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it said «اسمه المسيح عيسى ابن مريم», when these are three things, of which the name is ʿĪsā, while al-Masīḥ and «ابن» are a title (laqab) and a description? I say: the name is a mark for the thing named by which it is known and distinguished from others; so it is as if it were said: the one who is known and distinguished from all others by the sum of these three." End of quote. It is clear from his words that the sum of the three expressions is the predication about his name, meaning that none of them stands independently as khabar; rather it is of the type: "This is sweet-sour" and "This is ambidextrous (aʿsar yasar)". Its counterpart is the poet's words:
1285 - كيف أصبحْتَ كيف أمسَيْتَ مِمَّا ... يزرعُ الوُدَّ في فؤادِ الكريمِ
("How are you this morning? How are you this evening?" is among what sows affection in the heart of the noble.)
That is, the sum of "how are you this morning" and "how are you this evening". Just as a multiple subject in wording without a conjunction is permissible while the meaning is on the sum, so it is with the khabar. I have recited verses on this, such as his words:
1286 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . فهذا بَتِّي ... مُقَيِّظٌ مُصَيِّفٌ مُشَتِّي
(… for this is my cloak, for the hot season, the summer and the winter.)
Some claimed that «المسيح» is not a name [or] a title for him, but rather an adjective like al-ḍārib and al-ẓarīf. He said: "On this view there is fronting and postponement in the speech, since «المسيح» is a naʿt of «عيسى», and the implied form is: his name is ʿĪsā al-Masīḥ." This is not permissible — I mean putting the adjective before the noun it qualifies — but he means it is originally an adjective of it; and when the Arabs put first what is originally an adjective, they make it built upon the governor before it and make the noun qualified a badal from what was originally its adjective, as in his words:
1287 - وبالطوِيلِ العمْر ... عُمْراً حَيْدَرا
(And by the long-lived … one of short life.) [Translator's note: the verse is fragmentary in the source.]
The original is: «وبالعمرِ الطويلِ». This is with definite nouns; with indefinite nouns they put the adjective in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The Shaykh said: "«المسيح» cannot be a naʿt in this construction, because what is predicated on this view is a wording, while al-Masīḥ is a description of the thing signified, not of the signifier, since the wording ʿĪsā is not al-Masīḥ. Whoever said that they are two names said: al-Masīḥ was put before ʿĪsā because of its fame." [Translator's note: the source does not mark clearly where the Shaykh's quotation ends.] Ibn al-Anbārī said: "His title was put first and begun with only because al-Masīḥ is better known than ʿĪsā, since it seldom falls on another named person with whom he could be confused, whereas ʿĪsā may fall on a large number; so he put it first because of its fame. Do you not see that the titles of the caliphs are better known than their names?" This indicates that al-Masīḥ, according to Ibn al-Anbārī, is [a title], not a name. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: "ʿĪsā is Arabised from Aysūʿ. If you make it Arabic, you do not give it nunation whether definite or indefinite, because it contains the feminine alif, and it would be derived from عاسَه يَعُوسه when he managed it and looked after it." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Deriving them — meaning al-Masīḥ and ʿĪsā — from al-masḥ and al-ʿays is like one writing on water." The discussion of ʿĪsā and Maryam, their derivation and what people have mentioned about that has preceded in Sūrat al-Baqara, which makes repeating it unnecessary.
His words: {وَجِيهاً} is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise His words {وَمِنَ المقربين}.

semin-durr:182-182.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ذلك بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), its implied form being: "that is deserved because of what [your hands] sent forth"; so did Abū al-Baqāʾ imply it, and it is open to question, its like having preceded. And «ما» may be a relative noun or an indefinite qualified noun (mawṣūfa). And «ذلك» points to what preceded of their punishment. This clause admits two analyses. The first: that it be in the position of the accusative by the saying [«ونقول»], conjoined to «ذُوقوا», as if it were said: and We shall also say to them: that is because of what your hands sent forth — they are rebuked with that, and He mentioned to them the cause that made the punishment obligatory for them. The second: that it not be included in the reported speech, but be an address to the contemporaries of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day the verse was revealed. The hands were mentioned because most deeds are carried out with them.

His saying: {وَأَنَّ الله}: conjoined to «ما» which is genitive by the bāʾ, i.e. that punishment comes about because of your earning and His not wronging you. Here there is a question: «ظَلاَّماً» is an intensive form that requires multiplicity, so it is more specific than «ظالم», and negating the more specific does not entail negating the more general. If you say «زيدٌ ليس بظلاَّم» it means: he does not wrong much, while it remains possible that he is a wrongdoer; and if you say «ليس بظالم», wrongdoing is negated at its root. So how did He, the Exalted, say {لَيْسَ بِظَلاَّمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ}? There are five answers to this, of which Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned four.

The first: that «فَعَّال» is sometimes not meant for multiplicity, as in the saying of Ṭarafa:
1502 - ولَسْتُ بِحَلاَّلِ التِّلاعِ لبيته ... ولكنْ متى يَسْتَرْفِدِ القومُ أَرْفِدِ
(I am not one who settles in the hollows of the land to hide away; rather whenever the people seek help, I help.)
[Translator's note: the printed text reads «لبيته»; the verse is more commonly transmitted with «مخافةً» in this place.] He does not mean here that he camps in the hollows a little, because that is repelled by the end of the verse, which indicates the negation of miserliness in every case; also, the completeness of the praise is not achieved by intending multiplicity. The second: that it is for multiplicity, but since it is set against "the servants", who are many, it was fitting that the many be set against the many. The third: that if He negated much wrongdoing, little wrongdoing is necessarily negated, because one who wrongs does so only to benefit from the wrongdoing; so if he abandons much wrongdoing despite its greater benefit — in the case of one to whom benefit and harm are possible — he would be more abandoning of little wrongdoing, which has [less] benefit. The fourth: that it be on the pattern of relation (nasab), i.e. no wrongdoing is ascribed to Him, so it is of the type بَزَّار (cloth-seller) and عَطَّار (perfumer), as if it were said: He is not one possessed of wrongdoing at all. The fifth: al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr said: "The punishment that He threatened to inflict on them, if it were wrongdoing, would be enormous; so He negated it at the measure of its enormity, had it been real."

Al-Rāghib said, after distinguishing between the two plurals of «عَبْد», namely عبيد and عِباد: "So العبيد, when annexed to Allah the Exalted, is more general than العباد; hence He said {وَمَآ أَنَاْ بِظَلاَّمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ}, drawing attention to the fact that He does not wrong those devoted to His worship nor those who ascribed themselves to other than Him, of those who named themselves ʿAbd al-Shams and ʿAbd al-Lāt." Al-Rāghib had earlier given the difference between «عبيد» and «عِباد», saying: "The plural of العبد who is enslaved is «عبيد», and it is said also «عِبِدَّى»; and the plural of العبد who is the worshipper is «عِباد»." The derivation of this word, its plurals and what has been said about it have preceded.

semin-durr:183-183.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين قالوا}: its position admits the three case-labels. The genitive is from three analyses. The first: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «الذين» which is genitive by the annexation of «قول» to it. The second: it is a badal (substitute) of it. The third: it is a naʿt of «العبيد», i.e. He is not a wrongdoer to the servants who said such-and-such; al-Zajjāj said this. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This corrupts the meaning and the arrangement."

The nominative: by cutting off (qaṭʿ), with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. they are those who. Likewise the accusative, also by cutting off, with an implied suitable verb, i.e. «أَذُمُّ الذين» (I censure those who).

His saying: {أَلاَّ نُؤْمِنَ}: regarding «أَنْ» there are two analyses. The first: it is on the omission of the preposition, the original being: «في أن لا نؤمِنَ»; and then the two well-known views come into it: whether it is in the position of the genitive or of the accusative. The second: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), on the implication of «عهد» with the meaning of «أَلْزَمَ» (to oblige); you say «عَهِدْتُ إليه كذا», i.e. I obliged him to it. On this it is in the position of the accusative only.

And «أَنْ» is written joined and separated, in consideration of the origin or of the assimilation (idghām). Abū al-Baqāʾ reported that some omit it in writing, content with the shadda. Makkī related from al-Mubarrad that if it is assimilated with nasalisation (ghunna) it is written joined, otherwise separated. It is reported from some that if it is the lightened one (mukhaffafa) it is written separated, and if it is the one that governs the accusative (nāṣiba) it is written joined; the difference being that the lightened one has an implied pronoun with it, which is as it were a separator between the two, unlike the nāṣiba. And the saying of the orthographers in such a case, "it is written joined", is an expression for its total omission in writing, in consideration of the pronunciation with assimilation — not that they write it joined while keeping part of its form, writing «أَنْلا». The proof of that is that when they spoke of joining in «أم من» and «أم ما» and the like, they only meant writing one letter, so they write «أمّن» and «أمَّا». Abū al-Baqāʾ understood that the joining in this is an expression for their writing part of its form attached to «لا»; the proof that he understood that is that he said: "Some omit it in writing, content with the shadda", so he made omission a third division beside joining and separating; and no one holds this.

«نُؤْمِنُ» is made transitive with the lām because it implies the meaning of acknowledging; this has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara.

ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read: «بقُرُبان» with two ḍammas. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "By assimilation (itbāʿ) to the ḍamma of the qāf; it is not a dialect, because there is not in the language fuʿulān with ḍamma on the fāʾ and the ʿayn. Sībawayh related «السُّلُطان» with ḍamma on the lām and said: that is by assimilation." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Sībawayh did not say that that is by assimilation; rather he said: 'We do not know in the language fiʿilān nor fuʿulān; but fuʿulān has come, and it is rare; they said «السُّلُطان», and it is a noun.' The commentator on Sībawayh's words said: 'The speaker of this dialect neither makes it sukūn nor assimilates.' Likewise the morphologists mentioned that it is an independent pattern; they said: fuʿulān has come only as a noun, and it is rare, as in «سُلُطان»." [Translator's note: the printed text has «هذه اللغمة», evidently a misprint for «هذه اللغة» (this dialect).]

I say: as for Ibn ʿAṭiyya, it is conceded that he erred in the report from Sībawayh about «سُلُطان» specifically; but his statement about «قُرُبان» is correct, because the morphologists excepted only السُّلُطان.

And القُرْبان is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), then the object was named by it, like الرَّهْن (pledge), which is originally a maṣdar; there is no need for the omission of a muḍāf. Abū al-Baqāʾ claimed that it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. with the offering of an offering; he said: "i.e. He prescribes that for us." And «تأكلُه النارُ» is a naʿt of «قُرْبان», and attributing the eating to it [the fire] is figurative (majāz): its annihilating things is expressed as eating.

«من قبلي» and «بالبينات» are both attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جاءكم», and the bāʾ admits accompaniment and transitivity, i.e. accompanied by the signs.

semin-durr:184-184.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَقَدْ كُذِّبَ رُسُلٌ}: this is not the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition; rather the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then be consoled" and the like, because this has already passed and been realised. There is long discussion of it, whose like has preceded for you. The clause beginning «جاؤوا» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «رُسُل», and «من قبلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كُذِّبَ». The bāʾ in «بالبينات» admits the two analyses, like its counterpart.

The majority of people read: «والزبرِ والكتابِ» without mentioning the genitive bāʾ; Ibn ʿĀmir read: «وبالزبرِ», repeating it, and Hishām alone from him: «وبالكتاب», repeating it as well; and it is so in the codices of the Syrians, like the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, may Allah have mercy on him. The matter here is easy: whoever did not bring it was content with the conjunction, and whoever brought it, that was for emphasis.

And الزُّبُر: plural of زَبُور with fatḥa; one also says زُبور with ḍamma. Are they of one meaning or different? The discussion of them will come at His saying {وَآتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ زَبُوراً} [verse 163] in al-Nisāʾ.

The derivation of the word is from «زَبَرْتُ», i.e. I wrote; زَبَرْتُه: I read it; زَبَرْتُه: I wrote it beautifully; زَبَرْتُه: I rebuked him. So زَبور with fatḥa is faʿūl in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle), like الرَّكوب in the sense of المركوب (ridden) and الحَلوب in the sense of المَحْلوب (milked). Imruʾ al-Qays said:
1503 - لِمَنْ طَلَلٌ أبصرْتُه فشَجاني ... كخَطِّ زَبورٍ في عَسيبِ يماني
(Whose is the ruin I saw that grieved me, like the lines of writing on a Yemeni palm-stalk?)
It is also said: the derivation of the word is from الزُّبْرَة, which is a piece of iron left as it is. And «المنير» is the active participle of أنار, i.e. to shine.

semin-durr:60-60.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {الحق مِن رَّبِّكَ}: it is possible that this is a clause standing on its own, the meaning being: the established truth that does not fade away is from your Lord, and among what has come from your Lord is the story of ʿĪsā and his mother, so it is an established truth. It is possible that «الحق» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هو» (it), meaning what We have related to you of the account of ʿĪsā and his mother. On this view «من ربك» admits two views: one is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and so is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted word; the second is that it is a second khabar, according to whoever permits that. The like of this clause has preceded in al-Baqara, as has the prohibition to him, peace be upon him, from doubting, though he was not one who doubted; [this] is by way of firing him up and stirring him to remain firm on the truth he is upon, or because what is meant by it is someone other than him.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَمَنْ حَآجَّكَ}: two views are possible on «مَنْ». One is that it is conditional, and this is the evident one, i.e. "if anyone disputes with you, say to him such and such". It is also possible that it is a relative noun meaning «الذي», the fāʾ having entered the khabar (predicate) only because it contains the sense of a condition. «المُحاجَّة» is of the mufāʿala pattern, which takes place between two parties, and the matter was indeed so.

His saying: «فيه» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «حاجَّك», i.e. "argued with you about his affair". There are two views on the hāʾ in it. The more evident is that it refers back to ʿĪsā, peace be upon him. The second is that it refers back to «الحق» (the truth); this may be supported by its being the nearest thing mentioned, but the first is more evident, because ʿĪsā is the one being spoken about and he is the subject of the story.

His saying: {مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَكَ} is also attached to «حاجَّك». «ما» may be a nominal relative, in which case the fāʿil (agent) of «جاءك» is a pronoun referring back to it, i.e. «من بعد الذي جاءك هو» (after that which came to you), and «من العلم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of «جاءك». It may also be a particle relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī), and then it is said: this entails either the verb being devoid of a fāʿil, or a pronoun referring back to a particle, because «جاءك» must have a fāʿil, and we have nothing to which it could fittingly refer except «ما», which is a particle. The answer is that the fāʿil may be His saying «من العلم», with «من» redundant (zāʾida), i.e. «بعد ما جاءك العلم», meaning: after the coming of the knowledge. But this can only be derived on the view of al-Akhfash, because he does not stipulate any condition for its redundancy. The «مِنْ» in «من العلم» may be partitive, which is the evident view, or for explaining the genus.

His saying: {تَعَالَوْاْ}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the lām, because it is an imperative of «تعالَى يَتَعالى», like «ترامى يترامى». The original of its alif is a yāʾ, and the original of this yāʾ is a wāw, because it is derived from «العلوّ» (height), which is elevation [Translator's note: the printed text reads «الارتقاع»; «الارتفاع» is presumably meant], as its explanation will come under derivation. Whenever the wāw occurs as fourth letter or beyond, it is changed into yāʾ, so «تعالَوَ» became «تعالَيَ»; then the weak letter was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa, so it was changed into alif, giving «تعالَى», like «ترامى» and «تغازَى». When you command one person with it you say «تعالَ يا زيدُ», dropping the alif. Likewise when you command a masculine plural you say «تعالَوا», because when you dropped the alif on account of the imperative you kept the fatḥa as an indication of it. Or, if you wish, you may say: the original is «تعالَيُوا» — the original of this yāʾ being a wāw, as has preceded — then the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy and so was dropped; two quiescent letters met, so the first of them, the yāʾ, was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents, and the fatḥa was left as it was. Or, if you wish, you may say: since the original was «تعالَيُوا», the weak letter — the yāʾ — was vowelled with the letter before it having fatḥa, so it was changed into alif; then two quiescents met, so the first of them, the alif, was dropped, and the fatḥa remained to indicate it.

The difference between this and the first way is that in the first way the alif was dropped on account of the imperative, even had no wāw of the pronoun been attached to it, while in this one it was dropped because of its meeting with the wāw of the pronoun.

Likewise when you command a single woman you say to her «تعالَيْ»; this yāʾ is the yāʾ of the feminine agent, one of the pronouns, and the morphology is as preceded, except that here you say: the kasra on the yāʾ in place of the ḍamma there. As for commanding a dual, the yāʾ stays, and you say «يا زيدان تعالَيا», and «يا هندان تعاليا» as well, masculine and feminine duals being alike in it. Likewise in commanding a group of women the yāʾ stays; you say «يا نسوة تعالَيْن», and Allah the Exalted said: {فَتَعَالَيْنَ أُمَتِّعْكُنَّ} [al-Aḥzāb: 28], since there is nothing requiring either dropping or change; this is evident from the rules that have been laid down.

Al-Ḥasan, Abū al-Sammāl and Abū Wāqid read «تعالُوا» with ḍamma on the lām. They explained it on the basis that the original is «تعالَيُوا», as has preceded; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was transferred to the lām after stripping it of its own vowel, leaving «تعالُوا» with ḍamma on the lām. Al-Zamakhsharī said in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: "On the basis of this reading al-Ḥamdānī said:

1312 - . . . . . . . . . . ... تعالِي أقاسمْك الهمومَ تعالِي
(… Come, let me share the cares with you, come!)

with kasra on the lām." Some people faulted him for citing as evidence the poetry of this late muwallad (post-classical) poet, but it is not a fault, for he mentioned it only by way of corroboration. This is like what preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara when he recited a verse of Ḥabīb [Translator's note: Abū Tammām]:

1313 - هما أَظْلَمَا حالَيَّ ثَمَّتَ أَجْلَيا ... . . . . . . . . . .
(They two darkened my two states, then they cleared them …)

and he himself excused himself for it in the way I have reported from him. So how can he be faulted for something he knew, drew attention to, and excused himself for?

What appears to me in explaining this reading is that they forgot the omitted letter, until it was as though they imagined that the word was built on that form and that the lām was in reality the last letter; so it was treated as a real final letter, given ḍamma before the wāw of the pronoun and kasra before its yāʾ, as you see. What indicates what I have said is that they said concerning «لَمْ أُبَلْ» [Translator's note: printed «أُبَلَهْ», apparently with the pausal hāʾ] that the original is «أبالي», because it is the imperfect of «بالَى»; when the jussive particle entered, they dropped the weak letter for it according to the rule, then forgot that letter and gave the lām sukūn for the jussive, because it was as if it were really the last letter; when the lām became quiescent, two quiescents met — it and the alif before it — so the alif was dropped because of the meeting of the two quiescents. This explanation is better, because it covers both this reading and the verse mentioned. According to what his own explanation requires, it would be said: the original is «تعالَيِي»; the kasra on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was transferred to the lām after stripping it of its vowel, then the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents.

«تعالَ» is a true verb and not a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), because the overt nominative pronouns attach to it. It was said: its origin is a request to approach from an elevated place, as a good omen and to bring the one called nearer, because it is from height and elevation; then it was extended and used for a mere request to come, so that it is even said to someone one wishes to humiliate, as when you say to an enemy «تعالَ», and to non-rational beings such as cattle and the like. It was also said: it is a call to an elevated place, then it was extended until it was used for a request to approach any place, even a low one.

{نَدْعُ} is jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the imperative, since it is valid to say: «إنْ تتعالَوا نَدْعُ» (if you come, we will call).

His saying: {ثُمَّ نَبْتَهِلْ}: He brought «ثم» here to alert them concerning their being addressed about mutual imprecation (mubāhala) with him [Translator's note: so printed, «على خطابهم»; the text may be corrupt], as though he were saying to them: do not hasten, and take your time; perhaps the truth will become clear to you. For that reason He brought the particle of delay.

«الابتهال» is of the iftiʿāl pattern from «البُهْلة»; «البهلة», with fatḥa or ḍamma on the bāʾ, is the curse. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Then we will invoke curses mutually by saying: the curse of Allah be on whoever of us and of you is the liar. «البهلة», with fatḥa and ḍamma, is the curse; «بَهَله الله» means Allah cursed him and removed him far from His mercy, from your saying «أبهله» when one neglects him; and «ناقة باهل» is a she-camel with no udder-binding on her. This is the origin of «الابتهال»; then it was used for every supplication in which one exerts oneself, even if it is not mutual cursing." I say: how excellent it is that iftiʿāl is made here to mean tafāʿul, for the meaning only comes out on that basis; tafāʿala and iftaʿala are sisters in places, such as «اجتَوَروا» and «تجاوروا», and «اشْتَوروا» and «تشاوروا»; for that reason the wāw of «اجتَوَر» and «اشْتَوَر» remained sound. His saying "even if it is not mutual cursing" means that it has become well known in the language: so-and-so «يَبْتَهِل» to Allah for the fulfilment of his need, and «يبتهل» for the removal of his distress.

Al-Rāghib said: "The origin of «البَهْل» is a thing's being left untended. «الباهل» is the camel let loose from its hobble or from a brand, or the she-camel whose udder is left free of the udder-binding." And he recited a line by a woman:

«أتيتُكَ باهِلاً غيرَ ذاتِ صِرار»
(I came to you free, without an udder-binding.)

"«أَبْهَلْتُ فلاناً» means: I left him to his own will, by comparison with the camel let loose. «البَهْل» and «الابتهال» in supplication are giving oneself free rein in it and humbling oneself, as in «ثم نبتهلْ فنجعلْ». Whoever explained «الابتهال» as cursing did so because giving oneself free rein in this place is for the sake of cursing. The poet said:

1314 - . . . . . . . . . . ... نَظَرَ الدهرُ إليهم فابْتَهَلْ
(… Fate looked upon them and gave itself free rein [against them].)"

I say: this hemistich is by Labīd, and the beginning of the verse is:

1315 - مِنْ قُرومٍ سادةٍ في قومِهم ... نَظَرَ الدهرُ إليهمْ فابْتَهَلْ
(Of noble stallions, chiefs among their people; Fate looked upon them and gave itself free rein.)

What is apparent from this is that «الابتهال» is general for every supplication, whether cursing or other, and then was specified in this verse for cursing. What is apparent from al-Zamakhsharī's wording is that its origin is its specific use for cursing, then it was used loosely for exertion in supplication, whether cursing or other. What is apparent from the statements of the lexicographers is what al-Rāghib mentioned. Abū Bakr ibn Durayd said in his Maqṣūra:

1316 - لم أَرَ كالمُزْنِ سَواماً بُهَّلا ... تَحْسَبُهَا مَرْعِيَّةً وَهِي سُدى
(I have not seen the like of the rain-clouds as grazing herds left untended: you would think them shepherded, yet they roam at will.)

«بُهَّلاً» is the plural of «باهِلة», i.e. left untended; fāʿila is pluralised on fuʿʿal, as in «ضُرَّب». «السُّدى» also means left untended.

His saying: {فَنَجْعَل}: this is the one that takes two objects, meaning «نُصَيِّر» (we make), and «على الكاذبين» is the second object.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His words: {وَيُكَلِّمُ} and His words: {مِنَ الصالحين}: these are four aḥwāl (circumstantials) put in the accusative from His words «بكلمة». He made the ḥāl masculine only by construing according to the meaning, since what is meant by it is the child and the thing brought into being, just as He made the pronoun in «اسمه» masculine. The first ḥāl was brought according to the norm, as an explicit noun, and the rest are interpretable as one. The second is a preposition with its genitive noun; it was brought in this form because it occurs as a pause (fāṣila) in the speech, and had it been brought as an explicit noun, the harmony of the pauses would have been lost. The third is a verbal clause, and the verb is conjoined to the noun because it is interpretable as one. It is like the words of Allah the Exalted: {أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الطير فَوْقَهُمْ صَافَّاتٍ وَيَقْبِضْنَ} [al-Mulk: 19], i.e. "and folding [their wings]" (qābiḍāt). Similar to it, in conjoining a noun to a verb because it is interpretable as one, are the words of al-Nābigha:
1288 - فأَلْفَيْتُه يوماً يُبيرُ عدوَّه ... وبَحْرَ عطاءٍ يَسْتَخِفُّ المعابِرا
(I found him one day destroying his enemy, and a sea of giving that sweeps away the ferry-boats.)
Close to it is:
1289 - باتَ يُغَشِّيها بعَضْبٍ باتِرٍ ... يَقْصِدُ في أَسْوُقِها وجائِرُ
(He spent the night covering them with a sharp, cutting sword, aiming straight at their legs and swerving.)
Since the meaning is: "destroying (mubīran) his enemy" and "aiming straight (qāṣidin)". He brought the third as a verbal clause because it is in its proper rank, since the ḥāl is a description in meaning; and it has preceded that when descriptions differing in being explicit or interpreted come together, the noun is put first, then the adverbial or its equivalent, then the clause. So He did the same here: He put first the noun, «وجيهاً», then the preposition with its genitive noun, then the verb. He brought it as an imperfect because it indicates renewal time after time, unlike eminence (wajāha), where what is meant is its permanence and stability, and the noun suffices for that; and the preposition with its genitive noun is close to the single word, so He put it second, since what is intended is the permanence of his being brought near. The doubling in «المقرَّبين» is for transitivity, not for intensiveness, because of what has preceded, that doubling for intensiveness does not give the verb an object, whereas this has given it an object, as you see — unlike «قَطَّعْتُ الأثوابَ» (I cut the garments to pieces), where transitivity was present before that. The fourth was brought with His words {مِنَ الصالحين} out of regard for the pause, as preceded with «المقرَّبين». The meaning is: Allah gives you glad tidings of this word, described by these beautiful attributes.
Abū al-Baqāʾ prohibited their being aḥwāl from «المسيح», from «عيسى» or from «ابن مريم». He said: "Because they are predicates, and what governs them is the inception (al-ibtidāʾ), or the mubtadaʾ (subject), or both, and none of these governs a ḥāl." He also prohibited its being a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «اسمه». He said: "Because of the separation occurring between them, and because of the absence of a governor of the ḥāl." I say: his doctrine is also that the ḥāl does not come from the muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct), and that is what he means by his words "because of the absence of a governor". The ḥāl came from an indefinite noun because it is specified by the naʿt (adjective) after it. The apparent sense of al-Wāḥidī's words, in what he reported from al-Farrāʾ, is that they may be aḥwāl from «عيسى», for he said: "Al-Farrāʾ calls this 'cutting off' (qaṭʿ), as if He had said: ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, the eminent one (al-wajīh), cutting the definiteness off from it." The apparent sense of this indicates that «وجيهاً» was originally an attribute of «عيسى» and was cut off from it, and the ḥāl is a description in meaning.
His words: {فِي الدنيا} are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «وجيهاً», because of the verbal meaning in it. Al-wajīh is one possessed of standing (jāh), which is strength, protection and honour. One says وَجُه الرجلُ يَوْجُه وَجَاهَةً. Its derivation is from al-wajh (the face), because it is the noblest of the limbs; al-jāh is inverted from it, so its pattern is ʿafal.
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فِي المهد}: two views are possible on it. The first, which is the apparent one: it is attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يكلّم», i.e. "he will speak to them as a small child and as a mature man"; on this view «كهلاً» is conjoined (nasaq) to this interpreted ḥāl. The second: it is an adverbial (ẓarf) of the speaking, like the other complements (faḍalāt); on this view «كهلاً» is conjoined to «وجيهاً», and so there would be five aḥwāl.
Al-kahl is one who has reached the age of maturity (kuhūla); its beginning is thirty — it was also said thirty-two, and it was said thirty-three, and it was said forty — and its end is sixty, after which he enters the age of old age. Its derivation is from «اكْتَهَلَ النباتُ» when the plant grew tall and flourished; from it comes al-kāhil (the upper back). The author of al-Mujmal said: "اكتهل الرجلُ: grey hair streaked him, from their saying اكْتَهلت الروضةُ when blossoms covered the meadow; and the woman is kahla." Al-Rāghib said: "Al-kahl is one whom grey hair has streaked; and اكتهلَ النباتُ when the plant is close to drying, as the mature man is close to grey hair." And he recited the words of al-Aʿshā describing a meadow:
1290 - يُضاحِكُ الشمسَ منها كوكبٌ شَرِقٌ ... مُؤَزَّرٌ بعميمِ النبتِ مُكْتَهِلُ
(A radiant blossom from it laughs with the sun, wrapped in luxuriant growth, in full bloom.)
The discussion of the child's passing through stages, from his being in the womb until his old age, has preceded at the mention of «غلام», so we will not repeat it.
Some of them said: "As long as he is in his mother's womb he is janīn (fetus); when born, walīd (newborn); if he has not completed a week, ṣadīʿ; as long as he is suckling, raḍīʿ; then he is faṭīm at weaning; if he is not suckled, maḥwash; when he crawls, dārij; when his milk teeth fall out, thaghūr; when they grow back after falling out, mathghūr and mutghūr; when he passes ten, mutaraʿriʿ and nāshiʾ; if he has not reached puberty, yāfiʿ and murāhiq; when he reaches puberty, ḥazuwwur; and ghulām is applied to him in all his stages after birth.
