The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, as a naʿt (adjective) of «مفازة», i.e. in a place of safety being from the punishment, on our making «مفازة» a place, i.e. a place of success. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "because المفازة is a place, and a place [noun] does not govern", meaning: so it cannot be attached to it, but to something omitted as a naʿt of it. However, making it a naʿt is problematic, because المفازة is not described as being from the punishment — unless that omitted item to which the preposition is attached is implied as something specific [so that] the meaning is sound, its implied form being: in a place of safety that saves from the punishment. And in this there is the well-known difficulty, namely that the omitted item in such a case is implied only as general being (kawn muṭlaq).

The second analysis: it is attached to «مفازة» itself, as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of الفوز (escape, success); you say «فزت منه», i.e. I escaped from it. Its being feminine with the tāʾ does no harm, because it is built on it, and it is not the [tāʾ] indicating singularity. So it is like the poet's saying:
1513 - فلولا رجاءُ النصرِ منك ورهبةٌ ... عقابَك قد كانوا لنا كالمَوارِدِ
(Were it not for hope of help from you, and fear of your punishment, they would have been to us like watering-places.)
He made «رهبةٌ» govern «عقابَك», which is an explicit object; so this [case] is all the more fitting. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The implied form would be: so do not think them successful; so the maṣdar is in the place of the active participle." End. If he means an explanation of the meaning, then [very well]; but if he means that the attachment is valid only by this implied form, there is no need for it, since the maṣdar is independent in that, in wording and meaning.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ الكتاب}: the majority read «نَزَّل» with doubling (tashdīd) and «الكتاب» in the accusative. Al-Aʿmash, al-Nakhaʿī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «نَزَلَ» with the zāy undoubled and «الكتاب» in the nominative. As for the first reading, it has already been stated that this clause may be a khabar (predicate) or may be resumptive (mustaʾnafa). As for the second reading, what is apparent is that the clause in it is resumptive, and it may be a khabar, in which case the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, its implied form being: «نَزَل الكتابُ من عنده» "the Book came down from Him".

His saying: {بالحق}: there are two analyses of it. The first: that the bāʾ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it, the bāʾ then being causal, i.e. "He sent it down because of the truth". The second: that it is attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial): either from the agent, i.e. "He sent it down being in the right", or from the object, i.e. "He sent it down bound up with the truth", as in «جاء بكرٌ بثيابه» "Bakr came with his clothes", i.e. bound up with them.

Makkī said: "The bāʾ is not attached to «نَزَّلَ», because it is already transitive to two objects, one of them by a particle, so it does not extend to a third." What Makkī mentioned is not evident, for a verb extends to its attached elements through various particles according to what is [meant], and it has been stated that the meaning of the bāʾ is causal; so what impediment prevents that?

His saying: {مُصَدِّقاً}: there are several analyses of it. The first: that it is accusative as a ḥāl from «الكتاب»; if it is said that «بالحق» is a ḥāl, this is a second ḥāl according to those who permit multiple ḥāls, and if that is not said, it is a first ḥāl. The second: that it is accusative as a ḥāl by way of substitution (badal) from the position of «بالحق»; that is according to those who forbid multiple ḥāls without conjunction or substitution. The third: that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in «بالحق», if we make it a ḥāl, because it then bears a pronoun, as it stands in place of the ḥāl that bears it; it would then be an interlocking ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila), i.e. a ḥāl from a ḥāl. On all these views it is a confirmatory ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), because it cannot be otherwise, so transience is inconceivable in it. It is a parallel of his saying:

1158 - أنا ابنُ دارةَ معروفاً بها نسبي ... وهَلْ بدارَةَ يا لَلْناسِ مِنْ عارِ
(I am the son of Dāra, my lineage being known by her — and is there, O people, any shame in Dāra?)

His saying: {لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ} is the object of «مصدِّقا»; the lām was added in the object to strengthen the governing word, because it is secondary [in governance], being an active participle, as in His saying, the Exalted: {فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ} [Hūd: 107]. We claimed that only because this root is transitive by itself.

His saying: {التوراة والإنجيل}: people differ about these two words: do derivation and morphological analysis enter them, or do they not enter them because they are foreign (aʿjamī)? A group, such as al-Zamakhsharī and others, held the second, saying: because these two words are Hebrew names for these two noble books. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The strained effort to derive them from «الوَرْي» and «النَّجْل», and to weigh them on the patterns tafʿila and ifʿīl, is valid only after they are established as Arabic." [The Shaykh said: "His words are correct, except that there is a point to be added, namely his saying 'tafʿila': he did not mention the doctrine of the Basrans,] which is that its pattern is fawʿala, nor did he point out whether tafʿila has kasra or fatḥa on the ʿayn." I say: He did not need to point it out because both are well known; he only mentioned what is unusual.

What supports al-Zamakhsharī's statement that it is foreign is what al-Wāḥidī transmitted, namely that «التوراة», «الإنجيل» and «الزبور» are Syriac and they Arabized them. He said: "For that reason they say for them in Syriac: «تُوري ايكليونُ زَفوتا»", and they Arabized them into what you see.

Then those who hold that they are derived differ. Some said: «التَوْرَاة» is derived from their saying «ورِي الزَّنْدُ» "the fire-stick gave fire", when it is struck and fire appears from it. One says «وَرِيَ الزَّنْدُ» and «أَوْرَيْتُه أنا» "I made it give fire". The Exalted said: {أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ النار التي تُورُونَ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 71]; so its triliteral form is intransitive and its quadriliteral form is transitive. The Exalted said: {فالموريات قَدْحاً} [al-ʿĀdiyāt: 2]. One also says «وَرَيْتُ بكل زِنادي» "I struck fire with all my fire-sticks", where the triliteral is used transitively; but al-Māzinī claims that one does not go beyond this expression with it, i.e. one does not draw analogies from it so as to say, for example, «وَرَيْتُ النارَ». Once that is established: since the Torah contains light and illumination by which one is brought out of error [into] guidance, just as one is brought by light out of darkness into light, this Book was named «التوراة». This is the view of al-Farrāʾ, and it is the doctrine of the majority of people.

Others said: rather, it is derived from «وَرَّيْتُ في كلامي» "I spoke allusively", from «التورية», which is indirect allusion (taʿrīḍ). In the hadith: «كان إذا أراد سفراً وَرَّى بغيره» "When he intended a journey, he would allude to another". The Torah was named thus because most of it is intimations and allusions. This was the view of al-Muʾarrij al-Sadūsī and a group.

Regarding its pattern there are three views. The first, which is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, is that its pattern is fawʿala; words of this pattern are attested, such as «الدَّوْخَلة», «القَوْصرة», «الدَّوْسَرة» and «الصَّوْمَعَة». The original is «وَوْرَيَة» with two wāws, because it is either from «وَرِي الزَّنْدُ» or from «وَرَيْتُ في كلامي». The first wāw was changed into a tāʾ, and the weak letter was vowelled with what precedes it having fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif, and the word became «تَوْرَاة» as you see. It was written with yāʾ as an indication of the origin, just as it was given imāla (inclination toward i) for that reason. The Arabs have substituted tāʾ for wāw in [other] words, such as «تَوْلَج», «تَيْقور», «تُخَمَة», «تُكَأَة», «تُراث», «تُجاه» and «تُكْلان», from «الوُلوج», «الوَقار», «الوَخَامة», «الوِكاء», «الوِراثة», «الوَجْه» and «الوَكالة». A parallel of the change of wāw into tāʾ in «التوراة» is its change also in their word for what a woman sees in her purity after menstruation: «التَّرِيَّة»; it is faʿīla from the word «الوراء», because it is seen after the yellowness and the turbidity.

The second, which is the view of al-Farrāʾ, is that its pattern is tafʿila with kasra on the ʿayn; then the kasra was changed into fatḥa, which is a dialect of Ṭayyiʾ: they say «ناصَاة» for «الناصية», and «بَقَى» for «بَقِي». The poet said:

1159 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... بحِرْبٍ كناصاة الأغَرِّ المُشَهَّرِ
(… with a war [or: spear] like the forelock of the famous white-blazed [horse].)

Another said:

1160 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . .
نفوساً بُنَتْ على الكَرَمِ
(… souls built upon nobility.)

And al-Farrāʾ recited:

1161 - وما الدنيا بباقاةٍ علينا ... وما حيٌّ على الدنيا بباقٍ
(This world will not remain for us, nor will any living being remain in this world.)

The Basrans rejected this in two ways. The first: that this form — I mean the form tafʿila — is very rare, unlike fawʿala, which is frequent, so construing it on the more frequent is preferable. The second: that it entails the addition of the tāʾ at the beginning, and the tāʾ is added at the beginning only in places of which this is not one; unlike its being changed [from wāw] at the beginning of a word, which is established. That is because when a wāw occurs at the beginning, it is changed either into a hamza, as in «أُجوه», «أُقِّتَتْ», «أَحَدَ», «أَناة», «إشاح» and «إعاء» for «وجوه», «وُقِّتَتْ», «وَحَدَ», «وَنَاة», «وِشاح» and «وِعاء»; or into a tāʾ, as in «تُجاه» and «تُخَمة» … etc. So following what is familiar is preferable to following what is unfamiliar.

The third: that its pattern is tafʿala with fatḥa on the ʿayn; this is the doctrine of the Kufans, just as they say «تَتْفَلَة» with fatḥa for «تَتْفُلة» with ḍamma. There is no need for this, and it is also a claim without proof.

Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn ʿĀmir in the transmission of Ibn Dhakwān pronounced «التوراة», wherever it occurs in the Quran, with full imāla; Ḥamza, and Warsh from Nāfiʿ, pronounced it with intermediate imāla (bayna bayna); there is disagreement in the transmission from Qālūn: intermediate imāla and fatḥ are both transmitted from him; and the rest read it with fatḥ only. The rationale of the imāla, if we say that its alif is changed from a yāʾ, is evident; and if we say that it is foreign without derivation, the rationale of the imāla is the resemblance of its alif to the alif of femininity, in that it occurs as the fourth letter. So the cause of its imāla is either the change [from yāʾ] or the resemblance to the alif of femininity.

«الإنجيل»: it has been said that it is ifʿīl, like «إجْفيل». Regarding its pattern there are views. The first: that it is derived from «النَّجْل», which is the water that seeps from the ground and comes out of it; and from it is «النَّجْل» for the offspring. It was named «الإنجيل» because it is extracted from the Preserved Tablet. It has been said: from «النَّجْل» meaning the origin, and from it is «النَّجْل» for the parent; so it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād), since it is applied to both the offspring and the parent. Al-Aʿshā said:

1162 - أَنْجَبَ أيَّامُ والِداهُ به ... إذ نَجَلاه فنِعْمَ ما نَجَلا
(Noble were the days when his two parents begot him — how excellent was what they begot!)

It has been said: from «النَّجَل», which is wideness; and from it is «العَيْنُ النجلاءُ» "the wide eye", because of its wideness. The Gospel was named thus because in it there is a latitude that was not in the Torah, since things that had been forbidden were made lawful in it.

It has been said: it is derived from «التَناجل», which is mutual contention; one says «تَنَاجل الناسُ», i.e. they contended. The Gospel was named thus because of people's disagreement about it. Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī said this.

The majority read «إنجيل» with kasra on the hamza. Al-Ḥasan read it with fatḥa. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This indicates that it is foreign, because «أفعيل» with fatḥa on the hamza does not exist among the patterns of the Arabs." I say: unlike «إفعيل» with kasra, which exists, as in «إِجْفيل», «إخْريط» and «إصْليت».

Al-Zamakhsharī distinguished between «نَزَّل» and «أنزل», as is his habit, saying: "If you say: Why was it said «نَزَّل الكتابَ» but «وأنزل التوراة والإِنجيل»? I say: Because the Quran came down in instalments, while the two [earlier] Books came down all at once." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "The rejection of this view has already preceded in al-Baqara, [where it was shown] that transitivization by doubling indicates neither multiplicity nor instalments. Both «أَنْزَل» and «نَزَّل» have come in the Quran; the Exalted said: {وَأَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الذكر} [al-Naḥl: 44] and {نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ الكتاب} [Āl ʿImrān: 3]. What indicates that they have one meaning is the reading of whoever read the occurrences of «يُنَزِّلُ» with doubling in the undoubled form, except what was excepted. Had one of them indicated instalments and the other descent all at once, the reports would contradict each other, which is impossible." I say: Al-Wāḥidī preceded al-Zamakhsharī to this very distinction.

semin-durr:191-191.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين يَذْكُرُونَ}: there are five analyses in it. The first of them: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «أُولِي», so it is genitive. The second: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. they are those who. The third: it is accusative by an implied «أعني» (I mean). These two analyses are called cutting off (qaṭʿ), and that has preceded many times. The fourth: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: they say: our Lord; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The fifth: it is a badal (substitute) of «أُولي»; Makkī mentioned it. The first of the analyses is the best.

And {قِيَاماً وَقُعُوداً} are two ḥāls (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَذْكُرون». And {وعلى جُنُوبِهِمْ} is also a ḥāl, so it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted; the meaning is: they remember Him standing, sitting and lying down. So He conjoined the interpreted ḥāl to the explicit one — the reverse of the other verse, namely His saying {دَعَانَا لِجَنبِهِ أَوْ قَاعِداً أَوْ قَآئِماً} [Yūnus: 12], where He conjoined the explicit one to the interpreted one. «قياماً» and «قعوداً» are plurals of «قائم» and «قاعد». It has also been permitted that they be maṣdars (verbal nouns), in which case they are interpreted in the sense of "possessors of standing and sitting"; and there is no need for this.

His saying: {وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ}: there are two analyses in it. The more evident of them: it is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), so it has no grammatical position. The second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, conjoined to «قياماً», i.e. they remember Him, reflecting. If it is said: this is an affirmative imperfect, so how did the wāw enter upon it? The answer is that this is the wāw of conjunction, and what is forbidden is only the wāw of the ḥāl.

And «خَلْق» has two analyses. The first: it is a maṣdar on its original [meaning], i.e. they reflect on the making of these wondrous created things; it is then a maṣdar annexed to its object. The second: it is in the sense of the object, i.e. on what is created of the heavens and the earth; and its annexation is, in meaning, to the container (ẓarf), i.e. they reflect on what Allah has deposited in these two containers of stars and other things. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And it may be in the sense of the created, and it is then of the annexation of a thing to what it is in meaning." This is incoherent speech, since a thing is not annexed to itself, and whatever suggests that is interpreted [otherwise].

His saying: «ربَّنا»: this clause is in the position of the accusative by an omitted saying, its implied form being: they say. The clause of saying has two analyses. The more evident: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «يتفكرون», i.e. they reflect, saying: our Lord. If we parse «يتفكرون» as a ḥāl as preceded, then the two ḥāls are nested (mutadākhila). The second analysis: it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «الذين», on our view that it is a mubtadaʾ, as reported earlier from Abū al-Baqāʾ.

And «هذا» in His saying {مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذا} points to the creation (الخَلْق) if the created is meant by it. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted, while it is pointed to by «هذا», that it be a maṣdar in its [original] state, not in the sense of the created; this is open to question. Or [it points] to the heavens and the earth, even though they are two things each of which is a plural, because they are interpreted as: this wondrous creation; or because they are in the sense of a plural, so they are pointed to as a plural word is pointed to. [Translator's note: so in the text; the point appears to be that «هذا» is singular though it refers to two things.]

His saying: {بَاطِلاً}: regarding its accusative there are five analyses. The first: a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. a vain creating; it has preceded that Sībawayh makes the like of this a ḥāl from the pronoun of that maṣdar. The second: it is a ḥāl from the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), which is «هذا». The third: it is on the dropping of a genitive-governing particle, namely the bāʾ; the meaning being: You did not create them in vain, but with truth and power. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «خلتقهما», a misprint for «خلقتهما».] The fourth: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), since «فاعِل» sometimes comes as a maṣdar, like العاقبة and العافية. The fifth: it is a second object of «خَلَق»; they said: «خلق», when it is in the sense of «جعل» that takes two objects, takes two objects. This is not known among the scholars of Arabic; rather what is known is that «جَعَلَ», when it is in the sense of «خَلَقَ», takes one object only. The best of these parsings is that it be a ḥāl from «هذا», and it is a ḥāl that cannot be dispensed with, because if it were deleted the speech would be defective; it is like His saying {وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السماوات والأرض وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لاَعِبِينَ} [al-Dukhān: 38].

And {سُبْحَانَكَ}: its parsing has preceded, and it is parenthetical between His saying «ربنا» and His saying «فَقِنا». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The fāʾ entered for the meaning of requital (jazāʾ); the implied form being: when we have declared You transcendent, or declared You one, then protect us." There is no need for this; rather the causation in it is evident: from their saying {رَبَّنَآ مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذا بَاطِلاً سُبْحَانَكَ} resulted their request for protection from the Fire. It is also said: it is for ordering the request upon the meaning of the verb contained in «سبحان», i.e. glory be to You, so protect us. And whoever held that it is for ordering upon what the vocative contains went far [from the mark].

semin-durr:192-192.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَن تُدْخِلِ}: «مَنْ» is conditional, an advanced object, necessarily advanced because it has the head of the sentence; and «تُدْخِل» is jussive (majzūm) by it. And {فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُ} is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). Abū al-Baqāʾ related from some two strange views. The first: that «مَنْ» be accusative by an implied verb explained by His saying «فقد أَخْزَيْتَه». This is a mistake, because among the conditions of ishtighāl (preoccupation) is the validity of the explaining [verb] having power over what is accusative; and the apodosis does not govern what is before the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), because it does not precede the condition. The second: that «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the condition and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of this mubtadaʾ. These two analyses are a mistake; and Allah knows best. On all the views, this conditional clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «إنَّ».

One says خَزَيْتُه and أَخْزَيْتُه, as triliteral and quadriliteral, and the quadriliteral is more frequent. خَزِيَ الرجلُ يَخْزَى خِزْياً when he is disgraced, and خَزاية when he is ashamed; so the verb is one, and it is distinguished only by the maṣdar (verbal noun), as preceded.

His saying: {وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصَارٍ}: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), because the two conditions are present. Regarding the noun it governs there are two analyses. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the preposition-phrase before it; advancing it here is permissible, not obligatory, because the negation is what licenses [the indefinite], and what made its advancing good is that its mubtadaʾ is a verse-end (fāṣila). The second: it is a fāʿil (agent) of the preposition-phrase before it, because it relies on the negation; and this is permissible according to all.

semin-durr:66-66.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {هاأنتم هؤلاء}: discussion of this verse involves difficulty and complexity, so for that reason it requires extended treatment. Let us begin first by establishing its readings and explaining its meaning, since the i'rab depends on that. So I say: the readers fall into four grades on it. The first grade is that of the Kufans, Ibn ʿĀmir, and al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr: «ها أنتم» with an alif after the hāʾ and a fully pronounced hamza after it. The second grade is that of Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn from Nāfiʿ: with an alif after the hāʾ and a hamza after it eased to the intermediate sound (bayna bayna). The third grade is that of Warsh, who has two ways: one with a hamza eased bayna bayna after the hāʾ without an alif between them; the second with a clear alif after the hāʾ without any hamza at all. The fourth grade is that of Qunbul, with a fully pronounced hamza after the hāʾ without an alif.

As for the meaning: Qatāda, al-Suddī, al-Rabīʿ and a large group said: what they have knowledge of is their religion, which they found in their books and whose soundness was established for them; and what they have no knowledge of is the law of Ibrāhīm and what he was upon, which is not in their books, which their messengers did not bring them, and whose contemporaries they were not so as to know his religion; so their disputing about it is mere obstinacy and arrogance. It was also said: what they have knowledge of is the affair of our Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ, because it is present with them in their books with his description, and what they have no knowledge of is the affair of Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He means: there you are, these foolish persons; and the explanation of your foolishness and the paucity of your minds is that you have argued [Translator's note: printed «جادلم», a misprint for «جادلتم»] about what you have knowledge of, of what the Torah and the Gospel speak of; so why do you dispute about what you have no knowledge of, and of which your Book does not speak, namely the religion of Ibrāhīm?"

People differed about this hāʾ. Some said: it is the «ها» of alerting (tanbīh) that enters demonstratives; separation between it and demonstratives by detached nominative pronouns is frequent, as in «ها أنت ذا قائماً», «ها نحن», and «ها هم هؤلاء قائمون»; and it is sometimes repeated with the demonstrative after entering the pronouns, for emphasis, as in this verse. Separation by other than that is rare, as in his saying:

1322 - تَعَلَّمَنْ هالعمرُ الله ذا قَسَماً ... قاقدِرْ بذَرْعِك وانظرْ أينَ تنْسَلِكُ
(Know well — ha, by the life of Allah, this is an oath — so measure by your own reach and look where you are going.) [Translator's note: «قاقدر» is as printed; the known form is «فاقدر»]

And al-Nābigha said:

1323 - ها إنَّ تا عِذْرَةٌ إن لا تكن نَفَعَتْ ... فإنَّ صاحبَها قد تاهَ في البلد
(Lo, this is an excuse; if it has not availed, then its owner has gone astray in the land.)

Others said: it is substituted for the interrogative hamza, the original being «أأنتم», and it is an interrogative of disapproval. Substitution of hāʾ for hamza is frequent, even though it is not analogical: they said «هَرَقْت», «هَرَحْت» and «هَبَرْت» [Translator's note: for «أَرَقْت», «أَرَحْت», «أَبَرْت»]. This is the view of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash and a group, and Abū Jaʿfar [Translator's note: al-Naḥḥās] considered it good. But it is open to question in that this has not been established for the interrogative hamza: it has not been heard from them «هَتَضْرِبُ زيداً» in the sense of «أتضرب زيداً» (do you hit Zayd?). If that is not established, how can this be construed on it? This is the sense of the objection al-Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] raised against these imams. But once substitution of hāʾ for hamza is established, the matter is easy, and no regard is paid to whether it is an interrogative hamza or something else.

This — I mean its being an interrogative hamza replaced by hāʾ — is evident on the reading of Qunbul and Warsh, because they do not insert an alif between the hāʾ and the hamza of «أنتم»; for the insertion of the alif is only due to the heaviness of two successive hamzas, and when the hamza was replaced by hāʾ the heaviness was removed in pronunciation, so a separating alif was not needed. Substitution of hāʾ for the interrogative hamza has indeed occurred; the poet said:

1324 - وأتَى صواحِبُها يَقُلْنَ: هذا الذي ... مَنَحَ المودَة غيرَنا وجَفانا
(And her companions came, saying: Is this the one who granted his affection to others than us and shunned us?)

meaning «أذا الذي». Making it, on their reading, the «ها» of alerting is weak, because the dropping of its alif has not been preserved: one does not say «هذا زيد» with the alif of «ها» dropped [Translator's note: i.e. pronounced «هَذا» without the long ā] — so it was said. I say: Ibn ʿĀmir dropped it in three places, except that he gave ḍamma to the remaining hāʾ after dropping the alif; he read in continuous recitation {ياأيه الساحر} [al-Zukhruf: 49], {أَيُّهَ المؤمنون} [verse 31] in al-Nūr, and {أَيُّهَ الثقلان} [verse 31] in al-Raḥmān. But he did that only in following the script, because the alif was dropped in the written text of the Syrian copy of the Muṣḥaf in these three. In sum, the dropping of the alif of the «ها» of alerting is established.

As for those who keep the alif between the hāʾ and the hamza of «أنتم», the evident view is that «ها» is for alerting, and it is weak that it be a substitute for the interrogative hamza, because of what preceded, namely that the alif is only inserted on account of heaviness, and the heaviness has been removed by replacing the hamza with hāʾ. Some said: "What reflection requires is that «ها» in the reading of the Kufans, al-Bazzī and Ibn Dhakwān be for alerting, because the alif is present in their reading and it is not their practice to separate two hamzas by an alif; and that in the reading of Qunbul and Warsh it be substituted for a hamza, because Qunbul reads with a hamza after the hāʾ, and had «ها» been for alerting he would have brought an alif after the hāʾ. He did not ease the hamza, as he eased it in «أأنذرتهم» and the like, only because replacing the first with hāʾ made that unnecessary for him; and because Warsh did in it what he did in «أأنذرتهم» and the like, easing the hamza and not inserting the alif; and it is as though the reason for his reading with the alif is construing it as substitution, like the second way in «أأنذرتهم» and the like.

As for those other than the ones mentioned — namely Abū ʿAmr, Qālūn and Hishām — it is possible that «ها» is for alerting, and possible that it is a substitute for the interrogative hamza. As for the first way: because the «ها» of alerting entered «أنتم», Hishām pronounced the hamza fully, as he pronounced it fully in «هؤلاء» and the like, while Qālūn and Abū ʿAmr lightened it because it became medial through the particle of alerting entering it, and lightening a medial hamza is strong. As for the second way, the hāʾ is a substitute for the interrogative hamza, because they separate two hamzas by an alif; so Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn are following their own principle in inserting the alif and easing, and Hishām his own principle in inserting the alif and full pronunciation. The second way, namely easing [Translator's note: so printed], was not read, because replacing the first hamza with hāʾ makes it unnecessary."

Others said: "It is possible that «ها» in the reading of all of them is substituted for a hamza, and possible that it is the one of alerting that entered «أنتم»"; Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, al-Mahdawī and Makkī mentioned this, among others. As for the possibility of these two ways in the reading of Abū ʿAmr, Qālūn from Nāfiʿ, and Hishām from Ibn ʿĀmir, its explanation and clarification have preceded. As for their possibility in the reading of the others, I say: as for the Kufans, al-Bazzī and Ibn Dhakwān, the explanation of «ها» being for alerting in their reading has preceded. The explanation of its being a substitute for the hamza in their reading is that the original is «أأنتم», and they separated with the alif according to the dialect of the one who said:

1325 - . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . أاأنت أَمْ أُمُّ سالمِ
(… is it you, or Umm Sālim?)

and they paid no attention to the replacement of the first hamza by hāʾ, because the substitution in it is accidental. Even though separation is not their practice, they combined the two dialects. As for the explanation of «ها» being a substitute for the hamza in the reading of Qunbul and Warsh, it has preceded. As for the explanation of its being for alerting in their reading even though there is no alif in it, it is that the alif was dropped because of frequent use; and on the view of one who substitutes, like Warsh, one of the two alifs was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents.

Abū Shāma said: "I say: the better view for this word in all its readings is that «ها» is for alerting, because if we made it a substitute for a hamza, that hamza would be an interrogative hamza, whereas «ها أنتم», wherever it has come in the Qurʾān, has come only for statement, not for question. Nothing prevents this except the easing of those who ease and the dropping of those who drop. As for the easing, its likening to His saying {لأَعْنَتَكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 220] and the like has preceded. As for the dropping, he would say: «ها» is like «أَما», both being particles of alerting, and the permissibility of dropping the alif of «أما» is established, so likewise the dropping of the alif of «ها»; on that basis is their saying «أمَ واللهِ لأفعلن» (lo, by Allah, I will do it). The Basrans construed their saying «هَلُمَّ» as originally «هالمَّ», then the alif of «ها» was dropped; so likewise «ها أنتم»." I say: these are good words, except that his saying "«ها أنتم» wherever it has come is a statement, not a question" is not conceded; rather that is possible, and a question is possible. End.

Al-Farrāʾ also mentioned here an inquiry concerning shortening and lengthening. He said: "Whoever keeps the alif in «ها» and holds it to be for alerting, and whose practice is to shorten in the separated case (al-munfaṣil), then the analogy for him here is to shorten the alif, whether he pronounces the hamza fully or eases it. As for whoever makes it for alerting and whose practice is lengthening in the separated case, or who makes the hāʾ a substitute for an interrogative hamza, the analogy for him is to lengthen, whether he pronounces the hamza fully or eases it." As for Warsh, two ways have preceded from him: replacing the hamza of «أنتم» with an alif, and easing it bayna bayna; when he replaces, he lengthens, and when he eases, he shortens. This suffices for what concerns the readings and the branching of the readers' practices on them; they have said more than this, but this is not its place.

When you have understood all that preceded, there are several views on the i'rab of this verse. The first: «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «هؤلاء» its khabar (predicate), and the clause «حاججتم» is a resumptive clause explaining the first clause, meaning: you are these foolish persons, and the explanation of your foolishness and the paucity of your minds is that you have argued about what you have knowledge of, of what the Torah and the Gospel speak of; so why do you dispute about what you have no knowledge of? Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned that.

The second: «أنتم هؤلاء» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause «حاجَجْتم» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). This is indicated by the Arabs' explicitly keeping the ḥāl in its place in their saying «ها أنا ذا قائماً» (here I am, standing); in their view this ḥāl is one of the necessary ḥāls which the speech cannot do without.

The third: «أنتم هؤلاء» is also as preceded, but «هؤلاء» here is a relative noun that is not complete except with a ṣila (relative clause) and a returning pronoun [Translator's note: the printed text reads «بصفة», presumably for «بصلة»], these being the clause «حاجَجْتُم». Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it; this is only tenable according to the Kufans, its implied form being «ها أنتم الذين حاجَجْتُم» (there you are, the ones who disputed).

The fourth: «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ, «حاججتم» its khabar, and «هؤلاء» a vocative. This too is only tenable according to the Kufans, because the vocative particle is not dropped from demonstratives; but the Kufans permitted it and recited:

1326 - إنَّ الأُولى وُصِفوا قومي لهم فبِهِمْ ... هذا اعتصِمْ تَلْقَ مَنْ عاداكَ مَخذولا
(Those who have been described are my people; [it is] theirs, so with them — O you — take refuge, and you will find whoever is hostile to you forsaken.)

meaning «يا هذا اعتصم», and the saying of another:

1327 - لا يَغُرَّنْكُمُ أولاءِ من القو ... مِ جُنوحٌ للسِّلْمِ فَهْو خِداعُ
(Let not — O you there — an inclination to peace on the part of the people deceive you, for it is a trick.)

meaning «يا أولاء».

The fifth: «هؤلاء» is accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) with an implied verb, «أنتم» a mubtadaʾ and «حاجَجْتم» its khabar, the clause of specification being parenthetical.

The sixth: it is on the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being «ها أنتم مثل هؤلاء» (there you are, like these), the clause after it explaining the point of resemblance, or being a ḥāl.

The seventh: «أنتم» is a fronted khabar and «هؤلاء» a postponed mubtadaʾ.

These seven views have been mentioned before, together with those to whom they are attributed and the refutation of some who held some of them, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary, in Sūrat al-Baqara at His saying {ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ هؤلاء تَقْتُلُونَ} [al-Baqara: 85]; I have repeated it only as a reminder, so do turn to it.

His saying: {فِيمَا لَيْسَ لَكُمْ بِهِ عِلْمٌ}: «ما» may mean «الذي», or be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective; it may not be maṣdariyya, because the pronoun refers back to it, and it is a particle according to the majority. «لكم» may be a fronted khabar and «علم» a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being the ṣila of «ما» or its adjective. It is also possible that «لكم» alone is the ṣila or the adjective, with «علم» its fāʿil (agent), since it rests on something. «به» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted word, because it is a ḥāl of «علم», since had it come after it, it would validly be made its naʿt (adjective). It may not be attached to «علم», because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the maṣdar's governed word does not precede it. But if you make it attached to an omitted word explained by the maṣdar, that is permissible, and it is called «بيان» (explanation).

semin-durr:29-29.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَيَعْلَمُ}: resumptive, and not conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); that is because His knowledge of what is in the heavens and what is in the earth does not depend on a condition, so it was brought as a resumptive clause. His words {وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السماوات وَمَا فِي الأرض} are of the type of mentioning the general after the specific, the specific being {مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ}.
Here He put concealing before disclosing, made the breasts their place, and made knowledge the apodosis — unlike what is in al-Baqara, where He put disclosing before concealing, made the self their bearer, and made the reckoning the apodosis. All of that is variation in eloquence and diversity in fine expression.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
The words of the Exalted: {يَوْمَ تَجِدُ}: there are several aspects concerning what puts it in the accusative. The first: that it is accusative by قدير, i.e.: All-Powerful on that tremendous day. It is not to be said that this entails restricting His power to a time, because if He is powerful on that day which strips everyone of his power, then it is all the more fitting and proper that He be powerful on other days. Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī held this.
The second: that it is accusative by يُحَذِّركم, i.e.: He makes you fear His punishment on that day. Abū Isḥāq inclined to [this] and preferred it. It may not be accusative by the later يحذِّركم. Ibn al-Anbārī said: "Because «اليوم» cannot be accusative by the يحذِّركم mentioned in this verse, since what comes after the wāw of conjunction does not govern what precedes it." On what Abū Isḥāq mentioned, what lies between the adverb and what governs it would be parenthetical, and it is long speech, and separation by the like of it is unlikely. This is from the side of grammatical craft; as for the side of meaning, it is not sound, because the warning exists now while the day is promised, so how could the two meet?
The third: that it is (governed) by al-maṣīr (the return); al-Zajjāj also inclined to this, as did Ibn al-Anbārī, Makkī and others. This is weak according to the rules of the Basrans, because it entails separating the maṣdar (verbal noun) from what it governs with long speech. It may be said: parenthetical clauses are not regarded as separating, and this is of that kind.
The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied «اذكر» ("remember"), as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not as an adverb. Al-Ṭabarī estimated what governs it as «اتقوا» ("fear"); and this estimate has what it has, since it is against the basic rule while there is no need for it.
The fifth: that what governs it is the implied muḍāf before «نفسَه», i.e.: Allah warns you of the punishment of Himself on the day you find; so what governs it is «عقاب», not «يحذركم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. And in his words {لا يحذِّركم} «[Translator's note: so in the text; i.e. his saying "not يحذّركم"]» there is an escape from what I raised against Abū Isḥāq, as verified earlier.
The sixth: that it is accusative by تودُّ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«يومَ تجد» is accusative by تود, and the pronoun in «بينه» refers to the day, i.e.: on the Day of Resurrection, when every soul finds its good and its evil [present], it wishes that between it and that day and its terror there were a distant span." This which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned is an evident aspect whose excellence is not hidden; but in this question there is a weak disagreement. The majority of the Basrans and Kufans allow it, while al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ held it forbidden. The rule of this question is: when the fāʿil (agent) is a pronoun referring back to something connected to what the verb governs, as in «ثوبي أخويك يلبَسان» ("your two brothers' garments, they wear"), the fāʿil is the alif, a pronoun referring to «أخويك», which is connected to the object of يلبسان. Similar is «غلامَ هند ضربَتْ» ("Hind's servant, she struck"): the fāʿil of «ضربَتْ» is a pronoun referring to «هند», which is connected to غلام, made accusative by ضربَتْ. The verse is of this kind: the fāʿil of «تودُّ» is a pronoun referring to «نفس», which is connected to يوم because it is in a clause to which the adverb is annexed, and the adverb is accusative by تودُّ. The implied form is: on the day of every soul's finding its good and its evil brought present, it wishes such-and-such.
The majority argued for permissibility from what has been heard, namely the words of the poet:
1230 - أَجَلُ المرءِ يستحِثُّ ولا يَدْ ... ري إذا يبتغي حصولَ الأماني
(A man's appointed term he hastens on without knowing it, when he seeks the attainment of his hopes.)
The fāʿil of «يستحثُّ» is a pronoun referring to «المرء», which is connected to «أجَل», made accusative by «يستحثُّ». Those who forbid it argued that the governed element is a complement (faḍla) that may be dispensed with, while the pronoun's referring back to it in these questions requires that it must be mentioned; so these two considerations conflict. For this reason there is consensus on forbidding «زيداً ضرب» and «زيداً ظَنَّ قائماً», meaning "he struck himself" and "he thought himself (standing)". This is a clear proof for the one who forbids it, were it not for what refutes it from what has been heard, as in the line I recited to you just now. In the difference between «غلام زيدٍ ضَرَبَ» and «زيداً ضرب», where the first is allowed and the second forbidden by the requirement of the stated cause, there is obscurity and difficulty, and this is not the place to mention it.
His words: {تَجِدُ}: it may be the verb transitive to one object, meaning "to come upon", in which case «مُحْضراً» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); this is the evident view. It may also be the verb of knowing, transitive to two objects, the first being «ما عَمِلَتْ» and the second «مُحْضَراً»; that is not strong in meaning.
In «ما» two aspects are permissible. The more evident: that it means "that which", the returning pronoun then being implied, i.e.: what it did (ʿamilathu); it was omitted because the conditions are complete. «من خير» is a ḥāl either from the relative noun or from its returning pronoun; and «من» may be for clarifying the genus. «ما» may also be maṣdariyya, the maṣdar then standing in the place of the object, its implied form being: on the day every soul finds its deed, i.e. what it has done; then there is no returning pronoun, according to the majority.
His words: {وَمَا عَمِلَتْ مِن سواء تَوَدُّ}: this «ما» may be conjoined to the «ما» before it, with the two considerations mentioned regarding it, i.e.: and it finds that which it did, or: and it finds its deed, i.e. what it did, of evil. If we make «تجد» transitive to two objects, the second is omitted, i.e.: and it finds that which it did of evil brought present, or finds its deed brought present, as in «علمت زيداً ذاهباً وبكراً», i.e.: and Bakr going; you omitted its second object because it is indicated by its mention with the first. If we make it transitive to one object, the ḥāl from the relative noun is likewise omitted, i.e.: it finds it brought present, i.e. in this state; this parallels your saying «أكرمْتُ زيداً ضاحكاً وعمراً», i.e.: and ʿAmr laughing — you omitted the ḥāl of the second because the ḥāl of the first indicates it. On this view the clause «تودُّ» has two aspects. The first: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «عَمِلَتْ», i.e.: and what it did, while being wishing, i.e. wishing to be far from the evil. The second: that it is resumptive; Allah informed about it with that. «ما» may also be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being the clause «تود», i.e.: and that which it did — or: and its deed — it wishes that between it and that there were a distant span.
The pronoun in «بينه» has two aspects. The first, which is the evident one, is that it refers to «ما عَمِلَتْ»; al-Zamakhsharī referred it to «اليوم». The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "Al-Zamakhsharī went far in referring it to «اليوم», because one of the two categories brought present on that day is the good which he did, and distancing the time of bringing the good present is not sought except figuratively — since the day comprises bringing present both good and evil, it wishes it distant so as to be safe from the evil, even if the good does not come to it. It is more fitting to refer it to what it did of evil, because that is the nearest thing mentioned, and because the meaning is that on that day one wishes to be distant from the evil."
If it is asked: may this «ما» be conditional? The answer is that al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya forbade that, making the reason for the prohibition the absence of [jussive] in the verb occurring as the apodosis, namely «تودُّ». This is nothing, because scholars have stated that when the verb of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) is past and the apodosis imperfect, two aspects are permissible in that imperfect verb: the jussive and the nominative; both have been heard from the tongue of the Arabs. Of this is the line of Zuhayr:
1231 - وإنْ أتاه خليلٌ يومَ مسألةٍ ... يقولُ لا غائِبٌ مالي ولا حَرِمُ
(And if a needy friend comes to him on a day of asking, he says: my wealth is neither absent nor forbidden.)
Of the jussive are the words of the Exalted {مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ الحياة الدنيا وَزِينَتَهَا نُوَفِّ} [Hūd: 15] and {مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الآخرة نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ وَمَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الدنيا نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا} [al-Shūrā: 20]. This shows that what prevents it from being conditional is not the nominative of «تود». The Shaykh answered that it is not conditional — not for the reason al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned, but for another reason. Let us mention here what he mentioned. He said: "I was asked about al-Zamakhsharī's statement" — and he mentioned it — then he said: "Let us mention here what is needed, after first presenting what ought to be presented in this question. We say: when the verb of the protasis is past and after it comes an imperfect verb with which the sentence of condition and apodosis is completed, the jussive is permissible in that imperfect verb, and the nominative is permissible in it. An example is: «إن قام زيد يقمْ ويقومُ عمرو» ("if Zayd stands, ʿAmr will stand"). As for the jussive, it is as the apodosis; we know of no disagreement about it, nor about its being eloquent — except what the author of the book al-Iʿrāb mentioned from some grammarians, that it does not occur in eloquent speech but only occurs with «كان», as in the words of the Exalted {مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ الحياة الدنيا وَزِينَتَهَا نُوَفِّ}, because it is the root of verbs, and that this is not permissible with other verbs. The evident meaning of Sībawayh's words and those of the body of grammarians is that this is not restricted to «كان», but all verbs are in that respect like «كان». Sībawayh recited, from al-Farazdaq:
1232 - دَسَّتْ رسولاً بأنَّ القوم إنْ قَدَروا ... عليك يَشْفُوا صدرواً ذاتَ توْغيرِ
(She secretly sent a messenger saying that the people, if they get power over you, will relieve breasts full of rancour.)
And he also said:
1233 - تَعَشَّ فإنْ عاهَدْتني لا تخونُني ... نكنْ مثلَ مَنْ يا ذئبُ يصطحبان
(Have your supper; then if you pledge to me that you will not betray me, O wolf, we will be like two who keep company.)
As for the nominative, it has been heard from the tongue of the Arabs often, and one of our colleagues said: it is better than the jussive. Of it is Zuhayr's line recited earlier; and similar is his words:
1234 - وإنْ شُلَّ رَيْعانُ الجميعِ مخافةً ... نَقُولُ جِهارا وَيْلَكم لا تُنَفِّروا
(And if the vanguard of the host is driven off in fear, we say openly: woe to you, do not scatter!)
and the words of Abū Ṣakhr:
1235 - ولا بالذي إنْ بان عنه حبيبُه ... يقولُ ويُخْفي الصبرَ إني لجازعُ
(Nor is he one who, if his beloved parts from him, says — hiding patience — "I am indeed distressed".)
And another said:
1236 - وإن بَعُدُوا لا يأمَنُون اقترابَه ... تَشَوُّفَ أهلِ الغائبِ المُتَنَظَّرِ
(And if they are far, they do not feel safe from his approach, with the eager watching of the family of an awaited absent one.)
And another said:
1237 - فإنْ كان لا يُرضيك حتى تَردَّني ... إلى قطريٍّ لا إخالُك راضياً
(If nothing pleases you until you send me back to Qaṭarī, I do not think you will ever be pleased.)
And another said:
1238 - إنْ يَسْألوا الخيرَ يُعْطُوه وإنْ خَبِروا ... في الجَهْد أُدْرِكُ منهم طيبُ أَخْبارِ
(If they ask for good, they are given it; and if they are tested in hardship, good reports of them are obtained.)"
I say: he presented this line thus among the lines that show the imperfect in the nominative, and what shows that this was his intent is that after reciting all these lines he said: "So this nominative, as you have seen, is frequent." End. Yet this line has nothing whatever to do with that, because [the imperfect in it is jussive, namely «يُعْطُوه», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; so he ought to have] recited it when he recited «دَسَّت رسولاً» and his words «تَعالَ فإن عاهَدْتني», the two lines.
Then he said: "So this nominative is frequent, as you have seen, and the texts of the leading scholars state its permissibility in speech, though their interpretations differ, as we shall mention. Our colleague Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Nūr ibn Rashīd al-Mālaqī, the author of the book Raṣf al-Mabānī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'I know of nothing of it that has come in (prose) speech; and if it comes, its analogy is the jussive, because that is the basic government in the imperfect, whether the past verb precedes or follows.' He interpreted what was heard as being on the implication of the fāʾ, and made it like the words of the poet:
1239 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... إنَّك إِنْ يُصْرَعْ أخوك تُصْرَعُ
(… you, if your brother is thrown down, are thrown down.)
according to the position of those who held that the fāʾ is omitted from it. As for the earlier scholars, they differed in explaining the nominative. Sībawayh held that it is by way of fronting (taqdīm), and that the apodosis is not mentioned according to him. Al-Mubarrad and the Kufans held that it is itself the apodosis, the fāʾ only having been dropped from it, and the fāʾ what follows it «[Translator's note: so in the text; the sense is evidently "the fāʾ and what follows it being the apodosis"]», as in the words of the Exalted {وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ الله مِنْهُ} [al-Māʾida: 95]; so in concealment it was given its rule in overt expression. Others held that the imperfect is itself the apodosis, like the previous view, except that there is no implied fāʾ with it. They said: but since the protasis verb is past, on which the conditional particle shows no overt government, they considered the conditional particle weak and did not let it govern the apodosis because of its weakness. So the nominative imperfect, according to this speaker, is the apodosis itself, without an intention of fronting and without implying the fāʾ; it is not jussive only for the reason stated. This view and the one before it are weak.
What we have said comes down to this: the nominative of the imperfect does not prevent what precedes it from being a condition. But «وما عملت» is prevented from being a condition for another reason, not because «تود» is nominative. That is as we set out according to Sībawayh's position, namely that the nominative verb is intended as fronted, and it is then an indication of the apodosis, not the apodosis itself. So we say: if «تود» is intended as fronted, this leads to the pronoun preceding the overt noun it refers to outside the exceptional chapters in Arabic. Do you not see that the pronoun in His words «وبينه» refers to the conditional noun, which is «ما»? The implied form then becomes: «تود كلُّ نفسٍ لو أن بينها وبينه أمداً بعيداً ما عَمِلت من سوء» ("every soul wishes that between it and it there were a distant span, whatever evil it did"); this estimate entails the pronoun preceding the overt noun, and that is not permissible.
If you say: why is that not permissible, when the pronoun has come after the conditional noun, even if it is intended as fronted? The pronoun's referring back to the overt noun before it has been achieved, and this parallels «ضربَ زيداً غلامهُ» ("his servant struck Zayd"), where the rank of the fāʿil is to come first but it must come later so that the pronoun's reference is sound. The answer is: the indicating clause's containing the pronoun of the conditional noun requires that it come after it so that the pronoun can refer back; and from this it follows that the conditional clause requires the indicating clause, whereas the conditional clause requires only the apodosis clause, not what indicates it. Do you not see that it does not govern the indicating clause, but governs the apodosis clause, while the indicating clause has no grammatical position? Since that is so, the matter is self-contradictory: inasmuch as it is an indicating clause, the protasis verb does not require it; and inasmuch as the pronoun refers to the conditional noun, it does require it; so they contradict each other. This is unlike «ضرب زيداً غلامهُ», for it is a single clause, and the verb governs both the fāʿil and the object together, so each of them requires the other. For this reason some allowed «ضرب غلامُها هنداً» ("her servant struck Hind"), because the fāʿil annexed to the pronoun and the object to which the pronoun refers share the governing element, while «ضربَ غلامُها جارَ هِندٍ» ("her servant struck Hind's neighbour") is forbidden because they do not share the governing element. This is the difference between the two questions. Nothing like «أودُّ لو أَنْ أكرمَه أياً ضربَتْ هندٌ» is preserved from the tongue of the Arabs, because it entails the pronoun preceding what it explains outside the places mentioned by the grammarians; therefore its postponement is not permissible. End."
Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be conditional, paying no attention to what they used to forbid it. He said: "The second: that it is a condition, and «تودُّ» is nominative on the intention of the fāʾ, i.e.: then it wishes. It may also be nominative without estimating a particle, because the condition here is past, and when the jussive wording does not appear in the condition, both aspects are permissible in the apodosis: the jussive and the nominative." End. The verification of the matter has preceded, and the evident thing is that he agrees with the third view in explaining the nominative of the imperfect, as verified earlier.
ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «وَدَّت» in the past form. On this reading two aspects are permissible in «ما». The first: that it is conditional, and its position then has two possibilities. The first: the accusative by the verb after it, the implied form being: whatever evil it did, it wished; so «ودَّت» is the apodosis. The second possibility: the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the pronoun returning to the mubtadaʾ omitted, its implied form being: وما عملته; this is permissible in eloquent speech specifically with conditional nouns according to al-Farrāʾ — I mean omitting the pronoun returning to the mubtadaʾ when it is made accusative by a verb — as in «أيُّهم تَضْرِبْ أُكْرمه» ("whichever of them you strike, I will honour him") with أيهم nominative; when the mubtadaʾ is other than that, it is weak, as in «زيدٌ ضربْتُ».
Further explanation of this question will come in two places in the Qurʾān: one is the reading of whoever read {أَفَحُكْمُ الجاهلية يَبْغُونَ} [al-Māʾida: 50]; and the second is {وَكُلٌّ وَعَدَ الله الحسنى} [verse: 10] in al-Ḥadīd, and the disagreement of scholars about that.
The second of the two aspects of «ما» is that it is a relative noun, meaning: that which it did of evil, it wished that between it and that there were a distant span. Its position on this view is the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «وَدَّتْ» the khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī chose it, for he said: "But taking it as mubtadaʾ and khabar is more fitting in meaning, because it is the narration of what will be on that day, and firmer because it agrees with the reading of the generality." End.
If you say: why was «ما» not prevented from being conditional on this reading, as it was prevented on the reading of the generality? The answer is: if the reason was the nominative of the verb and its lack of jussive, as al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya held, it is absent in this reading, because the past verb is indeclinable (mabnī) in wording, and the conditional particle shows no government in it. If the reason is that it is intended as fronted, so that the pronoun would refer to something later in both wording and rank, that too is absent here, since nothing calls for it.
«لو» here is in its usual sense, being a particle for what would have occurred because of the occurrence of something else. On this view there are two omissions in the speech. The first: the omission of the object of «يود»; the second: the omission of the apodosis of «لو». The implied form of both is: it wishes the distance between it and that — if there were between it and that a distant span, it would be pleased with that, or it would rejoice, and the like. The disagreement about «لو» after the verb of wishing and what has its meaning, namely that it may be maṣdariyya, as set out in al-Baqara, is unlikely to apply here, because after it there is a maṣdar particle, namely أَنْ. The Shaykh said: "A maṣdar particle does not directly adjoin a maṣdar particle except rarely, as in the words of the Exalted {إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِّثْلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمْ تَنطِقُونَ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 23]." I say: his words "except rarely" suggest its permissibility, but it is not permissible at all; as for the noble verse he adduced, the grammarians have stated that «ما» in it is redundant (zāʾida). The discussion has preceded about the «أَنَّ» occurring after this «لو»: whether its position is the nominative as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, as Sībawayh held, or whether it is in the position of the nominative as a fāʿil of an implied verb, i.e.: if it were established that between it…; and what scholars said about that.
Some claimed that «لو» here is maṣdariyya, it and what is in its domain being in the position of the object of «تود», i.e.: it wishes the distance between it and that. That has the same difficulty, namely a maṣdar particle entering upon its like; but the meaning is that the wishing has power over «لو» and what is in its domain, were it not for the technical obstacle.
Al-amad is the limit of a thing and its end; its plural is آماد, like جَبَل and أَجْبال; the hamza was changed into alif because it occurs vowelless after the hamza of «أَفْعال». Al-Rāghib said: "Al-amad and al-abad are close to each other, but al-abad expresses a duration of time which has no defined limit and is not restricted, so one does not say 'the abad of such-and-such'; while al-amad is a duration which has an unknown limit when used absolutely, and is confined when one says 'the amad of such-and-such', as one says 'the time of such-and-such'. The difference between al-amad and al-zamān (time) is that al-amad is said with regard to the end, while al-zamān is general for the beginning and the end. For this reason some said: al-madā and al-amad are close to each other."

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِن قَبْلُ}: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أَنْزَل», and the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive) of the adverb is omitted because the meaning is understood, its implied form being «مِنْ قبلِك» "before you" or «من قبلِ الكتاب» "before the Book". «الكتاب» has become predominantly applied to the Quran, like «الثريا» [for the Pleiades]. It is in origin a maṣdar (verbal noun) occurring in the place of the mafʿūl bihi (object), i.e. "that which is written". He mentioned the one to whom it was sent down in His saying «نَزَّل عليك», but did not mention him in His saying {وَأَنزَلَ التوراة والإنجيل}, to honour our Prophet ﷺ.

His saying: {هُدًى}: there are two analyses of it. The first: that it is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the governor in it being «أنْزَل», i.e. "He sent down these two Books for the sake of guidance". It may also be attached, in terms of meaning, to «نَزَّلَ» and «أنزل» together, so that the case belongs to the chapter of contention (tanāzuʿ), with the second [verb] made to govern and the omission from the first, its implied form being: «نَزَّلَ عليك له» "He sent down upon you for it", i.e. for guidance, and He omitted it. It may also be attached to both verbs together with a technical attachment, not by way of contention, but in the sense that it is the reason for both verbs together, as when you say: «أكرمْتُ زيداً وضربْتُ عمراً إكراماً لك» "I honoured Zayd and struck ʿAmr out of honour for you", meaning that the honour is the reason both for the honouring and for the striking.

The second: that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «التوراة» and «الإنجيل». It was not put in the dual because it is a maṣdar, and in it are the well-known analyses: omission of the muḍāf, i.e. "possessors of guidance"; or by way of hyperbole, in that the two were made guidance itself; or by making them mean "two guiding [Books]". It has been said: it is a ḥāl from «الكتاب», «التوراة» and «الإنجيل». It has been said: it is a ḥāl from «الإنجيل» only, and it was omitted from what precedes it because this indicates it. Someone said: The discourse is complete at His saying, the Exalted: {مِن قَبْلُ}, so one pauses on it and begins His saying {هُدًى لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَنزَلَ الفرقان}, i.e. "and He sent down the Criterion as guidance for people". This construal is not correct, because it leads to placing the governed word before the conjunction, which is barred: if you said «قام زيد مكتوفةً وضُرِبَتْ هندٌ» meaning «وضُرِبَت هند مكتوفةً» "Zayd stood, and Hind was struck, bound", it would not be valid at all; and so is this.

His saying: {لِّلنَّاسِ} may be attached to «هُدَى» itself, because this root is made transitive with the lām, as in His saying, the Exalted: {يِهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ} [al-Isrāʾ: 9]; or it may be attached to something omitted, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «هدىً».

His saying: {وَأَنزَلَ الفرقان}: it is possible that all the heavenly Books are meant by it; it was not put in the plural because it is a maṣdar meaning «الفَرْق» "distinguishing", like «الغفران» and «الكفران». It may be a maṣdar occurring in the place of the agent or of the object, and the first is more evident. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or He repeated the mention of the Quran by what is a description of it and a praise — its being a distinguisher between truth and falsehood — after He had mentioned it by the generic noun, to magnify its standing and to show its excellence." I say: Someone might believe that in these words of his there is a refutation of his first statement, where he said that «نَزَّل» entails instalments and «أنزل» entails sending down all at once — since he allowed that the Quran is meant by «الفرقان», and «أنزل» has come with it. But one should not believe that, because he did not say that «أَنْزل» is only for sending down all at once; rather, he says that «نَزَّل» with doubling entails separation [into parts], while «أَنْزل» admits that and admits sending down all at once.

His saying: {لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ}: «عذابٌ» may be nominative as a fāʿil (agent) of the preposition-phrase before it, because [the phrase] occurs as the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ»; and it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause being the khabar of «إنَّ». The first is preferable, because it is of the kind of predicating with what is close to single words. «انتقام» is the iftiʿāl form from «النِّقْمة», which is assault and domination; for that reason some have expressed it as punishment. One says «نَقَم» and «نَقِمَ» — with fatḥa, which is the more eloquent, and with kasra — and it has been read with both. Further explanation will come in al-Māʾida.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying, the Exalted: {فِي الأرض}: it may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يَخْفَى», or it may be attached to something omitted, as a naʿt (adjective) of «شيء».

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فِي الأرحام}: it may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُصَوِّركم», which is the apparent [analysis]; and it may be attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «يُصَوِّركم», i.e. "He forms you while you are lumps of flesh in the wombs".

Ṭāwūs read «تَصَوَّركم» as a past verb, its meaning being "He formed you for Himself and for His worship". The form tafaʿʿala comes in the sense of faʿʿala, as in their saying «تأثَّلْتُ مالاً وأثَّلته» "I acquired wealth as a stock", i.e. I made it «أَثْلَة», i.e. a root; and likewise «وَلَّى» and «تَوَلَّى». «التصوير» is the tafʿīl form from «صارَه يَصُوره», i.e. he inclined it and bent it; and the meaning of «صَوَّره» is: He gave it a form. «الصورة» is the shape upon which a thing is, consisting of a particular composition and a regulated structure.

[Translator's note: the source prints «تأثَّلْثُ»; «تأثَّلْتُ» is evidently intended.]

His saying: {كَيْفَ يَشَآءُ}: in this verse there are several analyses. The most evident of them: that «كيف» is for the conditional apodosis (jazāʾ); it has been used conditionally in their speech, in their saying «كيفَ تَصْنَعُ أصنعُ، وكيف تكونُ أكونُ» "However you act, I act; however you are, I am" — except that it does not make [the verb] jussive. Its apodosis is omitted because what precedes it indicates it; and so is the object of «يشاء», for the reason already stated, that it is not mentioned except for something unusual. The implied form is: «كيف يشاء تصويرَكم يصوِّرُكم» "However He wills to form you, He forms you"; «تصويركم» was omitted because it is the object of «يشاء», and «يصوركم» because the first «يصوركم» indicates it. Its parallel is their saying «أنت ظالم إنْ فعلْتَ» "you are a wrongdoer if you do [it]", its implied form being: «أنت ظالم إن فعلت فأنت ظالم». And according to those who permit the advancing of the apodosis in an explicit condition, the preceding «يصوِّركم» is made the apodosis itself.

«كيف» is accusative as a ḥāl by the verb after it, and the meaning is: "In whatever state He willed to form you, He formed you". The discussion of that preceded at His saying {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 28]. It is not permissible for «كيف» to be governed by «يُصَوِّركم», because it has the front position of the discourse (ṣadr al-kalām), and what has the front position of the discourse is governed only by one of two things: either a preposition, as in «بمَنْ تمر؟» "By whom are you passing?", or a muḍāf, as in «غلامُ مَنْ عندك؟» "Whose servant is with you?"

The second: that «كيف» is an adverb (ẓarf) of «يشاء», and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of the name of Allah the Exalted, its implied form being: "He forms you according to [His] will", i.e. willing. The third: likewise, except that it is a ḥāl from the object of «يصوِّركم», its implied form being: "He forms you, you passing through [stages] according to His will". Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned these two analyses; and when someone else mentioned its being a ḥāl from the pronoun of the name of Allah, he construed it by saying: "He forms you in the wombs, being able to form you, being Master of that". The fourth: that the clause is in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun), the meaning being: "He forms you in the wombs with a forming according to [His] will, and as He wills" — so said al-Ḥawfī. In his saying "the clause is in the position of the maṣdar" there is laxity, because clauses do not stand in the place of maṣdars; what he means is that «كيف» indicates that, but since it is within the clause, he attributed that to the clause. His saying {هُوَ الذي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ}: this clause may be resumptive (mustaʾnafa), introduced merely to give information about that, or it may be in the position of the nominative as a second khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ».

semin-durr:193-193.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِياً يُنَادِي}: «سمع», if it enters upon what can validly be heard, as in «سمعت كلامك وقراءتك» (I heard your speech and your recitation), takes one object; and if it enters upon what cannot validly be heard, being a person or thing, it is not valid to restrict it to that alone; rather there must be an indication of something heard, as in «سمعت رجلاً يقول كذا» (I heard a man say such-and-such) and «سمعت زيداً يتكلم» (I heard Zayd speaking).

The grammarians have two views on this question. The first: it takes in this case too one object, and the clause occurring after the accusative is a naʿt (adjective) if before it is an indefinite, and a ḥāl (circumstantial) if it is definite. The second, the view of al-Fārisī and a group: it takes two objects, the clause being in the position of the second of them. So on the view of the majority «يُنادي» is in the position of the accusative because it is a naʿt of an accusative before it; and on al-Fārisī's view it is in the position of the accusative as a second object.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "You say: سمعت رجلاً يقول كذا and سمعت زيداً يتكلم, so you make the verb fall on the man and omit the thing heard, because you described him with what is heard, or made it a ḥāl from him, so it spared you from mentioning it; were it not for the description or the ḥāl, there would be no avoiding it, and [you would have] to say: I heard so-and-so's speech or his saying." This is the view of the majority, whose mention I gave you earlier. However, the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] objected to him, saying: "His saying 'were it not for the description or the ḥāl …' to the end is not so; rather there may be neither description nor ḥāl, and yet «سمع» enters upon a person, not upon something heard, as in His saying, the Exalted: {هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ إِذْ تَدْعُونَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 72], where the mention of the time-adverbial of the calling sufficed in place of the thing heard."

Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted that «يُنادي» be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun latent (mustatir) in «منادياً».

If it is said: what is the benefit in combining «منادٍ» and «ينادي»? Al-Zamakhsharī answered that He mentioned the calling unrestricted, then restricted by faith, to magnify the standing of the caller, because there is no caller greater than a caller to faith. That is because when "the caller" is left unrestricted, the mind goes to a caller to war, or to extinguishing a rebellion, or to aiding the distressed, or to coping with some calamity, or to some benefits; but when you say «ينادِي للإِيمان» (calling to faith), you have raised the standing of the caller and magnified it.

Abū al-Baqāʾ answered it with three answers. The first: emphasis, as in «قم قائماً» (stand up, standing). The second: that there is joined to it what makes the repetition good, namely «للإِيمان». The third: that if it were restricted to the noun, it would be possible that we heard someone known for calling mention something that is not a call; so when He said «يُنادِي», it was established that they heard his call in this state.

The object of «ينادي» is omitted, i.e. calling the people. It is also possible that no object is intended, as in {أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا} [al-Najm: 44]. «نادى» and «دعا» are made transitive with the lām at one time and with «إلى» at another; likewise «ندب».

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "That is because the meaning of the end of the extent and the meaning of specification both occur." So the lām is in its proper place, and there is no need to say that it is in the sense of «إلى», nor that it is in the sense of the bāʾ, nor that it is the lām of cause, i.e. for the sake of faith, as some held.

His saying: {أَنْ آمِنُواْ}: regarding «أَنْ» there are two views. The first: it is explicative (tafsīriyya), because it occurred after a verb having the meaning of saying but not its letters; on this it has no position in parsing. The second: it is the maṣdariyya (infinitival) joined to an imperative verb. There is a question about joining it to [the imperative], in that when a maṣdar is formed from it and what follows it, the indication of command is lost. They cited as proof of its joining to the imperative their saying «كَتَبْتُ إليه بأنْ قم» (I wrote to him to stand), where it is maṣdariyya and nothing else, otherwise the preposition would be left suspended. This has a place that is more fitting for it. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «مصرية», a misprint for «مصدرية».] And when it is said to be maṣdariyya, the original is to reach it with the bāʾ, i.e. «بأن آمنوا», so the two well-known views apply to it: genitive and accusative.

His saying: {فَآمَنَّا} is conjoined to «سمعنا», and conjunction by the fāʾ signals the swiftness of acceptance and that faith was caused by the hearing without delay; the meaning: so we believed in our Lord.

His saying: {مَعَ الأبرار} is an adverbial attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes it, i.e. take us counted in their company. It is also said: it is used figuratively here for time. It may be a ḥāl from the object, so it is attached to something omitted. Makkī and Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted that it be a naʿt of something omitted, i.e. righteous ones with the righteous, like the poet's saying:
1514 - كأنَّك مِنْ جِمالِ بني أُقَيْشٍ ... يُقَعْقَعُ خلفَ رِجْلَيْه بشَنِّ
(As if you were [a camel] of the camels of Banū Uqaysh, with an old waterskin rattled behind its legs.)
i.e. as if you were a camel of the camels. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And «أبراراً» would be a ḥāl"; and there is no need to claim that. And الأبرار may be the plural of «بارّ», like صاحِب and أَصْحاب, or of بَرّ on the measure of «كَتِف», as in كَتِف and أكتاف. [Translator's note: so in the text; «بَرّ» is not itself on the measure of «كَتِف»; the intended form is presumably «بَرِر», of which «بَرّ» is the contracted form.]

semin-durr:194-194.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {على رُسُلِكَ}: there are three analyses in it. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «وَعَدْتَنا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This «على» is the complement (ṣila) of the promise, as in your saying: Allah promised Paradise upon obedience; and the meaning is: what You promised us for believing Your messengers." The second: that it be attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object; al-Zamakhsharī implied it by his saying: "sent down upon Your messengers, or laid upon Your messengers, because the messengers are charged with that: {فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْهِ مَا حُمِّلَ} [al-Nūr: 54]." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] refuted him on the grounds that what he implied as omitted is a specific being (kawn muqayyad), and it is known from the rules that the adverbial and the preposition-phrase, when they occur as ḥāls, naʿts (adjectives), khabars (predicates) or ṣilas (relative clauses), are attached to a general being (kawn muṭlaq); and the preposition-phrase here occurred as a ḥāl, so how is what it is attached to implied as a specific being, namely «مُنَزَّل» or «محمول»? The third, mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ: that «على» be attached to «آتِنا»; and he implied an omitted muḍāf, saying: "on the tongues of Your messengers"; and this is good.

And الميعاد: a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) in the sense of الوعد (promise). And «يوم القيامة» has two analyses. The first: it is accusative by «لا تُخْزِنا». The second, permitted by the Shaykh: that it be of the chapter of iʿmāl (contention of two governors), since it is fit to be accusative by «لا تُخْزِنا» and by «آتِنا ما وعدتنا», when what is promised is Paradise. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «مصوبٌ», a misprint for «منصوبٌ».] Al-Aʿmash read: «رُسْلِك» with sukūn on the sīn.

semin-durr:67-67.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مَا كَانَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ يَهُودِيّاً وَلاَ نَصْرَانِيّاً}: He began with the Jews because their law is older, and He repeated «لا» in His saying {وَلاَ نَصْرَانِيّاً} for tawkīd (emphasis) and to make clear that each of the two religions was negated of him separately.

His saying: {وَلَكِن} is a rectification (istidrāk) stating what he was upon, and it has fallen here in the best position, since it stands between two opposites with respect to belief in truth and falsehood. Since the address was to the Jews and the Christians, He brought another negative clause to indicate that he was not on the religion of any of the polytheists, such as the Arabs who worshipped idols, the Magians who worshipped idols [Translator's note: so printed; the Magians are usually described as fire-worshippers], and the Sabians who worshipped the stars. By this the question of whoever asked is dismissed: what benefit is there in His saying {وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ المشركين} after His saying «ما كان يهودياً ولا نصرانياً»? He brought the khabar (predicate) of «كان» in the plural, saying {وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ المشركين}, because it is a verse-end (fāṣila); had that not been observed, agreement would have been required between it and what the rectification was made against in His saying {يَهُودِيّاً وَلاَ نَصْرَانِيّاً}, so that the two negations would correspond.

semin-durr:68-68.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {بِإِبْرَاهِيمَ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أَوْلى». «أولى» is an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) from «الوَلْي», which is nearness; the meaning is: the nearest of people to him and the most especially connected with him. Its alif is changed from a yāʾ, because its first radical is a wāw. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Since there is nothing in the language whose third and first radicals are both wāw, except «واو»", meaning the name of the letter of the alphabet, like the middle letter of «قول», or the name of the meaning-particle, such as the wāw of conjunction. The morphologists disagree about its middle radical: is it also a wāw, or a yāʾ? I have dealt with it, with its proofs, in «شرح التسهيل».

«لَلَّذين اتَّبعوه» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», and «هذا النبي» is conjoined to the relative noun, as is «والذين آمنوا». Although the Prophet ﷺ and the believers, may Allah be pleased with them, are included among those who followed Ibrāhīm, they were singled out for mention to honour and ennoble them; so it is of the type of {وملائكته وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ} [al-Baqara: 98].

Al-Zamakhsharī reported that it was read «وهذا النبيِّ» in the accusative and in the genitive. The accusative is conjoined to the object of «اتبعوه», so that the Prophet ﷺ is one whom others followed as they followed Ibrāhīm, the implied meaning being: "those who followed Ibrāhīm and this Prophet"; and His saying «والذين آمنوا» would be conjoined to His saying «للَّذين اتبعوه». The genitive is conjoined to «إبراهيم», i.e. the people nearest to Ibrāhīm and to this Prophet are those who followed him. This is open to question in that the pronoun in «اتبعوه» ought then to be dual, so that it would be said «اتبعوهما» (followed them both) — unless it is said that it is of the type of {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [al-Tawba: 62].

semin-durr:69-69.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَدَّت طَّآئِفَةٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب}: on {مِّنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب} there are two views. One is that «مِنْ» is partitive, and this is the evident one. The second is that it is for explaining the genus; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this, meaning that what is meant by «طائفة» is all of the People of the Book. Al-Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "That is far from what the wording indicates." On the view that it is partitive, this prepositional phrase is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «طائفة»; on the view that it is explicative, it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted word. As for «لو», it has preceded that it may be maṣdariyya, or may keep its proper sense of being a particle for what would have occurred because of the occurrence of something else.

Abū Muslim al-Iṣbahānī said: "«وَدَّ» in the sense of «تمنى» (to wish) is used with «لو» and «أن», and sometimes the two are combined, so one says «وَدِدْت أن لو فعلت» (I wished that you had done); its maṣdar is «الوَدادة», and the noun from it is «وُدّ». In the sense of «أحَبَّ» (to love) it is transitive in the way «أحب» is transitive; its maṣdar is «المَوَدَّة» and the noun from it is «وَدّ». The two sometimes overlap in the maṣdar and the noun."
