Al-Rāghib said: "When it means «أَحَبَّ», it is never permissible to bring «لو» in with it." Al-Rummānī said: "When «وَدَّ» means «تمنى», it is suitable for the present and the future, and «لو» is permissible; when it refers to the past [Translator's note: printed «بمعنى الماضي»], «أَنْ» is not permissible, because «أَنْ» is for the future." This is open to question, because «أنْ» [Translator's note: printed «أنَّ»; the argument concerns «أَنْ»] is connected with the past verb.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَرَسُولاً}: there are two views on «رسول». The first: it is an adjective in the sense of mursal (one sent), an adjective on the pattern faʿūl like al-ṣabūr and al-shakūr. The second: it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun). Among the instances of «رسول» coming as a maṣdar are the poet's words:
1291 - لقد كَذَبَ الواشُون ما بُحْتُ عندَهم ... بِسِرٍّ ولا أَرْسَلْتُهمْ برسولِ
(The slanderers have lied: I did not divulge a secret to them, nor did I send them with a message.)
i.e. with a message (risāla). Another said:
1292 - أُبَلِّغْ أبا سلمى رسولاً تَرُوعه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I will convey to Abū Salmā a message that will alarm him …)
i.e. I will convey to him a message. From it are the words of Allah the Exalted: {إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ العالمين} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 16] on one of the two interpretations, i.e. "we are the bearers of the message of the Lord of the worlds". On the two views, the discussion of the iʿrāb of «رسول» is arranged as follows.
On the first, there are six views on its accusative. The first: it is conjoined to «يعلّمه», if we parse that as a ḥāl (circumstantial) conjoined to «وجيهاً», since the implied form is: "eminent, teaching and sent"; al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It is built on the iʿrāb of «ويعلّمه», and we have shown the weakness of the iʿrāb of whoever says that «ويعلّمه» is conjoined to «وجيهاً», because of the excessive separation between the two conjoined elements."
The second: it is conjoined (nasaq) to «كهلاً», which is a ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «ويكلّم», i.e. "he will speak to people as an infant, as a mature man, and as one sent to the Children of Israel". Ibn ʿAṭiyya permitted that, and the Shaykh considered it far-fetched because of the long separation between the conjoined element and what it is conjoined to. I say: it appears that this is not permissible in terms of meaning, since the implied form would become: "he will speak to people while being a messenger to them", whereas he only became a messenger long after that. If it is said: it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), as in their saying "I passed by a man with a falcon, hunting with it tomorrow" and His words {فادخلوها خَالِدِينَ} [al-Zumar: 73] — it is replied: the norm for the ḥāl is that it be concurrent, and it is anticipated only where there is no ambiguity.
The third: it is accusative by an implied verb suited to the meaning, its implied form being: "and We will make him a messenger". When they saw that it could not properly be conjoined to the objects of teaching, they implied for it a governor that suits it. This is as they said regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: {والذين تَبَوَّءُوا الدار والإيمان} [al-Ḥashr: 9], and the poet's words:
1293 - يا ليتَ زوجَك قد غدا ... متقلِّداً سيفاً ورمحا
(Would that your husband had set out in the morning, girded with a sword and a spear.)
and another's words:
1294 - عَلَفْتُها تِبْناً وماءً باردا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I fed her straw and cold water …)
and his words:
1295 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وزَجَّجْنَ الحواجبَ والعُيونا
(… and they thinned out their eyebrows and their eyes.)
i.e. "and they firmly held faith", "and carrying a spear", "and I gave her cold water to drink", "and they applied kohl to their eyes" — this according to one of the two interpretations of these examples.
The fourth: it is accusative by an implied verb from the wording of «رسول», and that verb is itself governed by an implied saying, which is part of the speech of ʿĪsā.
The fifth: «الرسول» contains the meaning of uttering, so it is as if it were said: "and uttering that I have come to you". What al-Zamakhsharī said clarifies these last two views. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "If you say: on which of the preceding accusatives do you construe «ورسولاً ومصدقاً», when His words {أَنِّي قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ} and {لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ} refuse its being construed on them? I say: it is one of the tight spots, and there are two views on it. One of them: you imply for it «وأُرْسِلْتُ» (and I have been sent), intending a saying; its implied form: 'and He will teach him the Book and the wisdom, and he will say: I have been sent as a messenger [declaring] that I have come to you, and confirming what is before me.' The second: «الرسول» and «المصدِّق» contain the meaning of uttering, so it is as if it were said: 'and uttering that I have come to you and confirming what is before me.'" End of quote. He needed to imply all of that only to make the meaning and wording sound; that is because the accusatives before it cannot apparently be conjoined to, since the preceding pronouns are of the absent [third person], while the two pronouns accompanying these two accusatives are of the speaker; so he needed that analysis so that the pronouns would be harmonious. The Shaykh said: "This view is weak, since it involves implying two things — the saying and its object, which is «أُرْسِلْتُ» — and dispensing with them by a noun in the accusative as an emphatic ḥāl, since it is understood from his words «وأُرْسِلْتُ» that he is a messenger, so it is an emphatic ḥāl." The Shaykh chose the third view. He said: "Since it involves nothing but implying a verb indicated by the meaning, and His words {أَنِّي قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ} are governed by «رسول», i.e. uttering that I have come to you" — on the reading of the majority.
The sixth: it is a ḥāl from the object of «ويعلّمه», on the basis of the wāw being redundant (zāʾida), as if it were said: "and He will teach him the Book, while being a messenger". Al-Akhfash said this, and it is on the basis of his doctrine of permitting the redundancy of wāw, which is a less favoured doctrine.
On the second [i.e. its being a maṣdar] there are two views on its accusative. [The first:] it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), conjoined to the second object of «يعلّمه», i.e. "and He will teach him the Book and a message", i.e. He will teach him the message as well. The second: it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, and there are in it the well-known interpretations as in "a just (ʿadl) man".
Al-Yazīdī read «ورسولٍ» in the genitive, and al-Zamakhsharī explained it as being conjoined to His words «بكلمة», i.e. "We give you glad tidings of a word and of a messenger". This is far-fetched because of the great separation between the two conjoined elements, but no explanation other than this appears for this irregular (shādhdh) reading.
His words: {إلى بني إِسْرَائِيلَ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «رسولاً» itself, since its verb is made transitive with «إلى». The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a naʿt (adjective) of «رسولاً», so it is in the position of the accusative on the reading of the majority and of the genitive on the reading of al-Yazīdī.
His words: {أَنِّي قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ}: the generality read «أني» with fatḥa on the hamza, and there are three views on it. The first: its position is genitive after the dropping of the preposition, since the original is «بأني», and «بأني» is attached to «رسولاً». This is the doctrine of the two masters, al-Khalīl and al-Kisāʾī. The second: its position is accusative, and there are three views on this. The first: it is accusative after the dropping of the preposition, namely the bāʾ (accusative by removal of the preposition); this is the doctrine of the two disciples, Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ. The second: it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "mentioning that…", «يذكر» being a naʿt of «رسولاً»; the naʿt was omitted and what it governs remained. The third: it is accusative as a badal (substitute) from «رسولاً», i.e. if you make it a maṣdar serving as a direct object, its implied form being: "and He will teach him the Book and teach him that I have come to you". Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it, but it is far-fetched in meaning.
The third of the first [three] views: its position is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is that I have come to you".
Some readers read this hamza with kasra, and there are two interpretations of it. The first: it is on the basis of an implied saying, i.e. "saying: I have come to you"; He omitted the saying, which is a ḥāl in meaning, and kept its object.
The second: «رسولاً» is in the sense of "uttering", so it is made to include the meaning of saying, and whatever is made to include the meaning of [saying] is given the ruling of saying. This is the doctrine of the Kufans.
His words: {بِآيَةٍ}: it is possible that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «جئتكم», i.e. "I have come to you bearing a sign". The second: it is attached to the coming itself, i.e. "my bringing you the sign". His words {مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ} are a naʿt (adjective) of «آية», so it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "with a sign from your Lord"; «مِنْ» is then figuratively for the beginning [of the extent]. «من ربكم» may also be attached to the coming itself. Abū al-Baqāʾ rendered the ḥāl in His words {بِآيَةٍ} as "arguing by a sign". If he means it in terms of meaning, that is correct; if he means it in terms of the grammatical craft, it is not correct, since in these places nothing is implied except general [verbs of] being (al-akwān al-muṭlaqa).
The majority read «بآيةٍ» in the singular in both places, and Ibn Masʿūd «بآياتٍ» in the plural in both places.
His words: {أني أَخْلُقُ}: Nāfiʿ read it with kasra on the hamza and the rest with fatḥa. The kasra is on three views. The first: on the basis of an implied saying, i.e. "and I said: I create". The second: it is on the basis of resumption (istiʾnāf). The third: on the basis of explication (tafsīr): by this sentence He explicated His words «بآية», as if someone had said: "And what is the sign?" and he said these words. Its counterpart is what will come: «إنَّ مثل عيسى عند اللهِ كمثلِ آدمَ», then He said: {خَلَقَهُ مِن تُرَابٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 59], so «خلقه» explicates the likeness. Its counterpart is also the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَعَدَ الله الذين آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصالحات}, then He explicated the promise by His words {لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ} [al-Māʾida: 9]. This view comes down to resumption, since the resumptive sentence is brought to explicate what is before it; but the difference between it and the one before it is that in the view before it you give it no connection at all with what preceded, but it is brought merely to inform of what it contains, whereas on the third view you say that it is connected with what preceded it, explicating it.
As for the reading of the rest, there are four views on it. The first: it is a badal (substitute) from «أني قد جئتكم», so what preceded regarding that applies to it, since its ruling is the same as that one's. The second: it is a badal from «آية», so it takes its position, i.e. "and I have come to you with [the fact] that I create for you", and this is itself one of the signs. This badal may be of the whole from the whole, if by the sign something specific is meant, or a badal of part from whole, if by the sign the genus is meant. The third: it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "it is that I create", i.e. the sign I have brought is that I create. This sentence is in reality an answer to an implied question, as if someone had said: "And what is the sign?" and he said that. The fourth: it is accusative by an implied verb, and it is also an answer to that question, as if he said: "I mean that I create". These two views coincide in meaning with Nāfiʿ's reading on some of its views, since they are resumption.
«لكم» is attached to «أخلق», and the lām is for cause, i.e. "for your sake", meaning: to bring about your faith and to repel your denial of me; otherwise, persons themselves are not causes, but rather the events [connected with] them.
«من الطين» is also attached to it, and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent. The view of whoever said it is for explication (bayān) is lax, since nothing preceded from them [i.e. no vague term] for it to explicate.
His words: {كَهَيْئَةِ الطير}: there are three views on the position of this kāf. The first: it is a naʿt of an omitted object, its implied form being: "that I create for you a form like the form of a bird". Al-hayʾa (form) is either originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) and then applied to the object, i.e. the thing shaped, like al-khalq in the sense of the thing created; or a noun for the state of a thing, not a maṣdar, the maṣdar being al-tahayyuʾ, al-tahyīʾ and al-tahyiʾa. One says: [هاءَ الشيءُ يَهِيءُ هَيْئاً وهَيْئةً when a thing is arranged and settled in a particular state], and it is made transitive by doubling; Allah the Exalted said: {وَيُهَيِّىءْ لَكُمْ مِّنْ أَمْرِكُمْ مِّرْفَقاً} [al-Kahf: 16]. Al-ṭīn (clay) is well known; طانَه الله على كذا and طامه, with the nūn changed to mīm, i.e. He fashioned him with that disposition. Al-nafkh (blowing) is well known.
The second: the kāf is itself the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because it is a noun like other nouns. This is the opinion of al-Akhfash, who makes the kāf a noun wherever it occurs; other grammarians do not hold this except when forced to it, as when it occurs in the genitive by a preposition or by annexation, or occurs as agent or as mubtadaʾ. All the examples of this have preceded, which makes repeating them here unnecessary.
The third: it is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar. Al-Wāḥidī said this, reporting it from Abū ʿAlī after a long discussion. He said: "The kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of the intended maṣdar, its implied form being: that I create for you from clay a creating like the form of a bird." What he said is questionable in terms of meaning, because the challenge only lies in the effect of creating — the created things that arise from it — not in the creating itself; unless you say that by this maṣdar the object is meant, in which case it comes back to what preceded.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "That I shape (uqaddir) for you something like the form of a bird." This is an explicit statement from him that it is a naʿt of an omitted object. His word «أُقَدِّر» is an explanation of al-khalq, because creating here is shaping (taqdīr), as in the poet's words:
1296 - وَلأَنْتَ تَفْري ما خَلَقْتَ وَبعْ ... ضُ القوم يَخْلُق ثم لا يَفْري
(You cut out what you have measured, while some people measure and then do not cut.)
since what is meant is not origination, which belongs exclusively to the Creator, the Exalted. Al-Zuhrī read «كَهَيَةِ», transferring the vowel of the hamza to the yāʾ, and it is eloquent. Abū Jaʿfar read: «كهيئة الطائر».
His words: {فَأَنفُخُ فِيهِ}: there are six views on this pronoun. The first: it refers back to the kāf, since it is a noun according to whoever holds that, i.e. "I blow into the like of the form of a bird". The second: it refers back to «هيئة», because it has the meaning of the thing shaped; for that reason the pronoun referred back to it in the masculine, although it is feminine, in consideration of its meaning rather than its wording. Its counterpart is the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذَا حَضَرَ القسمة} [al-Nisāʾ: 8], then He said: {فارزقوهم مِّنْهُ}, so He referred the pronoun in «منه» back to al-qisma (the division) since it was in the sense of the thing divided. The third: it refers back to that omitted object, i.e. "then I blow into that thing resembling the form of a bird".
The fourth: it refers back to what is indicated in the wording, namely «أني أخلق», with the creating standing in place of the created thing. The fifth: it refers back to the meaning of likeness indicated by the kāf, because the meaning is: "I create from clay the like of the form of a bird", with the kāf in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of the intended maṣdar, its implied form being: "that I create for you a creating like the form of a bird". Al-Fārisī said this, and the discussion with him about it has preceded. The sixth: it refers back to the clay; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. Al-Wāḥidī rejected this view as unsound, for he said: "The pronoun cannot refer back to the clay, because the blowing is only into a specific clay, namely what has been shaped from it, while the clay mentioned before is general, so the pronoun does not refer to it; do you not see that he does not blow into all the clay?" This refutation is questionable, since someone could say: we do not concede that the clay mentioned before is general; rather, part of it is meant, and for that reason «مِنْ», which entails partition, was put before it; and when the meaning becomes "that I create some of the clay", the pronoun refers back to it without difficulty. But al-Wāḥidī made «مِنْ» in «من الطين» for the beginning of the extent, and that is the apparent sense. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "One of the readers read «فأنفخها», referring the pronoun back to the omitted form (hayʾa), since the implied form would be 'a form like the form of a bird', or to the kāf according to the meaning, since it means 'resembling the form of a bird'; so the feminine here would be as it is in the verse of al-Māʾida in His words {فَتَنفُخُ فِيهَا}. In this reading the preposition would have been omitted, as in the poet's words:
1297 - ما شُقَّ جيبٌ ولا قامَتْكَ نائحةٌ ... ولا بَكَتْكَ جيادٌ عند إسْلابِ
(No collar was rent, no wailing woman stood [mourning] over you, and no fine steeds wept for you at the stripping [of the slain].)
and the words of al-Nābigha:
1298 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كالهِبْرِقيِّ تَنَحَّى يَنْفُخُ الفَحْما
(… like the blacksmith who bends aside blowing on the coals.)
He means: 'nor stood over you', and 'blowing into the coals'." And he said: "It is an irregular (shādhdh) reading reported by al-Farrāʾ." I was surprised at him that he did not attribute it, when the author of al-Kashshāf attributed it to ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd], saying: "ʿAbd Allāh read «فأنفخها»", and he recited: «كالهِبْرِقيِّ تَنَحَّى» ….
His words: «فيكون»: there are two views on «يكون». The first: it is complete (tāmm), i.e. "and it comes into existence", and on this view «طيراً» is a ḥāl. The second: it is the incomplete one (nāqiṣa) and «طيراً» is its khabar. This is what it ought to be, because a generic noun occurring as a ḥāl is far-fetched and requires interpretation; that is only apparent on the reading of Nāfiʿ, «طائراً», because it is then a derived noun. If it is held to be incomplete, it may be in its usual sense, or it may be in the sense of incomplete «صار» (become), as in the poet's words:
1299 - بتَيْهاءَ قَفْرٍ والمَطِيُّ كأنَّها ... قَطا الحَزْنِ قد كانَتْ فِراخاً بيوضُها
(In a trackless waterless desert, the mounts like sandgrouse of the rugged ground whose eggs had become chicks.)
i.e. "had become". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«فيكون», i.e. it becomes. So «كان» here may be the complete one, because its meaning is «صار», and «صار» is in the sense of 'moved'; and it may be the incomplete one; «طائراً» on the first is a ḥāl and on the second a khabar."
I say: there is no need for his making it, when complete, in the sense of complete «صار» whose meaning is "moved". Rather, the grammarians only render the complete one as "occurred", "existed", "came about" and the like; and when they make it in the sense of «صار», they only mean incomplete «صار».
Nāfiʿ and Yaʿqūb read «فيكون طائراً» here and in al-Māʾida, and the rest «طَيْراً» in both places. As for Nāfiʿ's reading, some explained it as the meaning being singular, the implied form being: "and what I blow into becomes a bird". It is not to be objected that the noble script is «طير» without an alif, because the script allows the omission of such an alif for lightness; this is indicated by the fact that the words of Allah the Exalted {وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ} [al-Anʿām: 38] were written «ولا طيرٍ» without an alif, and no one read it except as «طائر» with alif. So the script admits it and does not contradict it.
Some said, as though explaining what I put forward: "Nāfiʿ took it as a single kind of bird, because he created nothing but the bat." Others claimed that the meaning of his reading is: "each one of what I blow into becomes a bird". He said: as in the words of Allah the Exalted {فاجلدوهم ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً} [al-Nūr: 4], i.e. flog each one of them; and this is frequent in their speech.
As for the reading of the rest, its meaning may be the generic noun, i.e. the genus of bird, so it may mean one or more; or it may mean the plural, especially according to whoever holds that «طير» is a plural form, like رَكْب, صَحْب and تَجْر as plurals of راكب, صاحب and تاجر — this is al-Akhfash; whereas according to Sībawayh these are collective nouns (asmāʾ jumūʿ), not true plurals. Our discussion of that has preceded in al-Baqara. The reading of the majority is made better by its agreement with what is before it in His words «من الطير», and by its agreeing with the script in wording and meaning.
His words: {بِإِذْنِ الله}: it may be attached to «طائراً» — this on the reading of Nāfiʿ. On the reading of the others it is not attached to it, because «طيراً» is a generic noun; so it is attached to an omitted element as a naʿt of «طير», i.e. "a bird bound up with Allah's permission", i.e. with His enabling and confirming. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Attached to «يكون»"; this is only apparent if one makes «كان» complete; if one makes it incomplete, then on the attachment of the adverbial to it there is the well-known disagreement.
His words: {وَأُبْرِىءُ الأكمه}: «وأبرئ» is conjoined to «أخلق», so it falls within the scope of «أني». One says: أَبْرَأْتُ زيداً من العاهةِ ومن الدَّيْنِ (I freed Zayd from the affliction and from the debt), and بَرَّأْتُكَ من الدَّين with doubling; and بَرِئْتُ من المرض أَبْرَأُ, and also بَرَأْتُ; but for بَرِئْتُ من الدَّين and من الذنب it is بَرِئْتُ only. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "بَرِئْتُ من المرض is the dialect of Tamīm, and بَرَأْتُ the dialect of the Ḥijāz." Al-Rāghib said: "بَرَأْتُ من المرض and بَرِئْتُ, and بَرَأْتُ من فلان." The apparent sense of this is that the two forms — I mean fatḥa and kasra on the rāʾ — are said only of freedom from illness and the like, while for debt, sin and the like it is only fatḥa. [Translator's note: this conclusion contradicts the statement just above that for debt and sin it is بَرِئْتُ (with kasra) only; the source is translated as written.]
Al-barāʾa is getting clear of a disliked thing, passing beyond it; likewise al-tabarrī and al-burʾ.
Al-akmah is one born blind. One says: كَمِه يَكْمَهُ كَمَهاً, so he is akmah. Ruʾba said:
1300 - فارتدَّ عنها كارتدادِ الأكمهِ ...
(He turned back from her as the born-blind man turns back.)
And one says كَمِهْتُها, i.e. I blinded it. Al-Zamakhsharī, al-Rāghib and others said: "Al-akmah is one born with his eyes obliterated." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "No akmah was found in this community other than Qatāda, the exegete." Al-Rāghib said: "One whose eye has gone is also sometimes called akmah"; Suwayd said:
1301 - كَمِهَتْ عيناه حتى ابْيَضَّتا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(His eyes went blind until they turned white …)
Al-baraṣ (leprosy) is a well-known disease; it is a whiteness that afflicts a person, and the Arabs shunned nothing as much as they shunned it. One says بَرِصَ يَبْرَصُ بَرَصاً, i.e. it afflicted him. It is also called al-waḍaḥ; in the ḥadīth: "and she had waḍaḥ". Al-Waḍḍāḥ was one of the kings of the Arabs whom they were in awe of calling al-Abraṣ. The moon is called abraṣ because of its intense whiteness; al-Rāghib said: "because of the spot on it", but that is not evident, since the spot on it is black. The gecko is [called] sāmm abraṣ because of its whiteness. Al-tabrīṣ is that which gleams with the gleam of leprosy, and it approaches [the meaning of] al-baṣīṣ (glittering).
His words: {بِمَا تَأْكُلُونَ}: «ما» may be a nominal relative noun, or a particle (ḥarfiyya, maṣdar-forming), or an indefinite noun qualified [by what follows]. On the first and third it needs a referent pronoun (ʿāʾid), unlike the second according to the majority. Likewise «ما» in His words «وما تدّخرون» admits what was mentioned.
He brought these four extraordinary acts with the imperfect form to indicate their being renewed whenever it was asked of him. He qualified His words «أني أخلق» to the end with «بإذن الله» because it is a tremendous extraordinary act, so He brought it to repel any imagining of divinity, and did not bring it in what was conjoined to it in His words «وأبرئ». Then He qualified the third extraordinary act also with «بإذن الله», because it too is a tremendous extraordinary act, and conjoined to it His words «وأنبئكم» without qualifying it, as an alert to the magnitude of what was before it and to repel the imagining of whoever might imagine divinity in it. Or He omitted the qualification from the two conjoined elements, being content with it in the first. What I put forward is better.
«تدّخرون»: the reading of the generality is with a doubled undotted dāl. Its origin is تَذْتَخِرُون, tafatʿilūn from al-dhukhr, which is hiding away. One says ذَخَر الشيءَ يَذْخَرُه ذُخْراً, so he is dhākhir and it is madhkhūr, i.e. he hid it away. The poet said:
1302 - لها أَشَارِيرُ مِنْ لحمٍ تُتَمِّرُه ... من الثَّعالِي وذُخْرٌ من أَرانيها
(She has strips of meat that she dries, from the foxes, and a store from its hares.)
Al-dhukhr is fuʿl in the sense of al-madhkhūr, like al-akl in the sense of what is eaten. Some grammarians miscopy this verse and say «وَوَخْزٌ» with wāw and zāy. His words «من الثعالي وأرانيها» mean "from the foxes (al-thaʿālib) and its hares (arānib)": he changed the one-dotted bāʾ into a yāʾ with two dots below. Since its origin is «تَذْتَخِرون», the dotted dhāl met the tāʾ — i.e. the tāʾ of iftiʿāl — so the tāʾ of iftiʿāl was changed into an undotted dāl; thereby two close letters met, the dhāl and the dāl, and he assimilated the dotted dhāl into the undotted one, so the word became «تدّخرون» as you see.
Al-Sūsī, in a transmission from Abū ʿAmr, read «تَذْدَخِرون», changing the tāʾ of iftiʿāl into undotted dāl without assimilation; and although that is permissible, assimilation is the eloquent form.
Al-Zuhrī, Mujāhid, Abū al-Sammāl and Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī read «تَذْخَرون» with sukūn on the dotted dhāl and fatḥa on the khāʾ; they brought it as the bare form on faʿala. One says ذَخَرْتُه, i.e. I hid it away. Some Arabs change the tāʾ of iftiʿāl in this kind into a dotted dhāl and say اذَّخَر يَذَّخِر with a doubled dotted dhāl; similar to it is اذَّكر, so he is مُذَّكِر; this will come, if Allah wills.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The origin of «تدّخرون» is تَذْتَخِرون, but the dhāl is voiced (majhūra) and the tāʾ voiceless (mahmūsa), so they did not combine; the tāʾ was changed into dāl because it is from its point of articulation, to bring it close to the dhāl; then the dhāl was changed into dāl and assimilated." «في بيوتكم» is attached to «تدّخرون».
His words: {إِنَّ فِي ذلك}: «ذلك» refers to all the extraordinary acts that preceded. They were referred to with a singular word, although they are plural in meaning, by interpreting it as "what has been mentioned, what has preceded". It has preceded that in the codex and reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «لآياتٍ» in the plural, out of regard for the plural meaning I have mentioned. This sentence may be from the speech of ʿĪsā, or it may be from the speech of Allah the Exalted.
{إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ}: its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "if you are believers, you will benefit from this sign and reflect on it". Some supplied an omitted naʿt for «آية», i.e. "surely a beneficial sign". The Shaykh said: "So that the connection with this condition becomes valid." This is questionable, since the connection with the condition is valid without supplying this naʿt.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ}: «آيات» may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the preposition-phrase as its khabar (predicate). On this [analysis] there are two views regarding the clause. The first: that it is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الكتاب», i.e. "He it is who sent down the Book in this state", i.e. divided into decisive (muḥkam) and ambiguous (mutashābih). It is also possible that «منه» alone is the ḥāl, and «آياتٌ» is nominative by it as its fāʿil (agent).

{هُنَّ أُمُّ الكتاب}: the clause may be a naʿt (adjective) of the indefinite noun before it, or it may be resumptive. He predicated with a singular word, «أمُّ», of a plural, «هُنَّ»: either because what is meant is that each one of them is a «أمّ» (mother/foundation); or because the whole is on a par with a single sign, as in His saying {وَجَعَلْنَا ابن مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُ آيَةً} [al-Muʾminūn: 50]; or because it is a singular occurring in the place of a plural, as in His saying {وعلى سَمْعِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 7] and:

1163 - كُلوا في بعضِ بطنِكُمُ تَعِفُّوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Eat in part of your belly [i.e. bellies], and you will be abstinent …)

[and his saying]:

1164 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وأمَّا جِلْدُها فَصَلِيب
(… as for their skin, it is tough.)

[Al-Akhfash said: "He made «أمّ الكتاب» singular by way of quotation (ḥikāya), on the supposition of an answer, as if it were said: What is the Mother of the Book?"] and He said: "They are the Mother of the Book" — just as it is said: "Who is Zayd's peer?" and some people say: "We are his peer", as though they were quoting that word. This is according to their saying «دعني من تمرتان» "Leave me alone with 'two dates'", i.e. "with what is called 'two dates'". Ibn al-Anbārī said: "This is far from correct in the verse, because no proof has been established for the implication, nor does any need call for it." It has been said: because it means "the root of the Book", and a root is singular.

His saying: «وأُخَرُ» is conjoined (nasaq) to «آيات», and «متشابهاتٌ» is a naʿt of «أُخَر». In reality «أُخَرُ» is a naʿt of something omitted, its implied form being: «وآياتٌ أُخَرٌ متشابهاتٌ» "and other ambiguous verses". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If it is said: The singular of «متشابهات» is «متشابهة», and the singular of «أُخَر» is «أُخْرى», and the singular here cannot validly be described by this singular — one does not say «أخرى متشابهة» unless parts of the single one resemble one another, and that is not the meaning; the meaning is only that each verse resembles another verse — so how is it valid to describe this plural with this plural, while it is not valid to describe its singular with its singular? It is said: Resemblance can only be between two or more; so when resembling things come together, each one of them resembles the other. Since resemblance is valid only in the state of being together, He described the plural with the plural, because each one of them resembles the rest; as for the single one, this meaning is not valid in it. Its parallel is His saying {فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلاَنِ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 15]: He put the pronoun in the dual even though one person does not fight [by himself]." I say: He means that it is not a condition for the validity of a description in the dual or plural that the singulars of the descriptions can be distributed over the singulars of the things described — even if that is the basic rule — just as it is not a condition, in attributing a verb to a dual or plural, that it can validly be attributed to each one on its own.

[Translator's note: the source prints «لى كلِّ»; «إلى كلِّ» is evidently intended.]

Close to that is His saying {حَآفِّينَ مِنْ حَوْلِ العرش} [al-Zumar: 75]: it has been said that «حافِّين» has no singular, because if «حافّ» were said it would not be valid, since surrounding is not realized in one person only; it is realized only by a group who encompass the surrounded thing. The explanation of that will come, if Allah the Exalted wills, in its place.

His saying: {زَيْغٌ}: it may be nominative as a fāʿil, because the preposition-phrase before it is the ṣila (relative clause) of a relative noun; and it may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the preposition-phrase before it.

«الزَّيْغ»: it has been said that it is inclining (al-mayl). Some said: it is more specific than inclining in general, for «الزيغ» is said only of [inclining] from truth to falsehood. Al-Rāghib said: "«الزَّيْغ» is inclining upon rectitude toward one of the two sides. «زاغ», «زال» and «مال» are close [in meaning], but «زاغ» is said only of [turning] from truth to falsehood." End of quotation. One says «زاغَ يزيغُ زَيْغاً وزيغوغَةً وزَيَغاناً وزُيوغاً». Al-Farrāʾ said: "The Arabs say, in most of the yāʾ-[hollow] verbs resembling «زِغْتُ», such as «سِرْتُ», «صِرْتُ» and «طِرْتُ»: «سَيْرورةً», «صَيْرورةً» and «طَيْرورةً»; and «حِدْتُ حَيْدودة», «مِلْتُ مَيْلولة» — I cannot count them for their multitude. As for the wāw-[hollow] verbs, such as «قُلت» and «رضِيت», they did not say that except in four words: «الكَيْنونة», «الدَّيْمومة» from «دام», «الهَيْعُوعة» from «الهُواع», and «السَّيدودة» from «سُدْت»." Then he mentioned much discussion not related to what we are dealing with. The discussion of this maṣdar (verbal noun), and what people have mentioned about it, has already preceded, as well as that its original form, «كَيَّنونة», has been heard, in the saying of the poet:

1165 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... حَتَّى يعودَ البحرُ كَيَّنونَهْ
(… until the sea returns to being [as it was].)

[Translator's note: al-Rāghib's wording is usually cited as «الميل عن الاستقامة» "inclining away from rectitude"; the source here prints «على الاستقامة», translated as written. Also, «رضِيت» is a final-weak verb rather than a wāw-hollow one; it is translated as written.]

His saying: {مَا تَشَابَهَ} is the object of following (al-ittibāʿ). [«ما»] is a relative noun or an indefinite qualified [noun] (mawṣūfa); it cannot be maṣdariyya, because the pronoun in «تَشَابَه» refers back to it — except on a weak opinion. «منه» is a ḥāl from the agent of «تشابه», i.e. "what is ambiguous, it being part of it".

His saying: «ابتغاءَ» is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of seeking", and it is a maṣdar annexed to its object. «التأويل» is the maṣdar of «أَوَّل يُؤَوِّل». Regarding its derivation there are two views. The first: that it is from «آل يَؤُول أَوْلاً ومَآلاً», i.e. "to return, revert"; and «آلُ الرجل» "a man's family" is from this according to some, because they return to him in their important affairs. They say «أَوَّلْتُ الشيءَ فآلَ», i.e. "I turned the thing to a fitting sense, and it turned". The poet said:

1166 - أُؤَوِّلُ الحكمَ على وجهه ... ليس قضائي بالهَوى الجائر
(I turn the judgement to its proper sense; my verdict is not by unjust caprice.)

Some said «أَوَّلْتُ الشيءَ فتأوَّل», making its reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) tafaʿʿala, whereas on the first its reflexive is faʿala. He recited for al-Aʿshā:

1167 - على أنها كانَتْ تَأَوُّلُ حُبِّها ... تَأَوُّلَ رِبْعِيِّ السِّقَابَ فَأَصْحَبَا
(Yet her love grew, as the spring-born young camel grows, until it became tame [i.e. full-grown].)

He means that her love was small and slight, then it grew into greatness, as the young camel (al-saqb) grows into maturity. Then it may be applied to the outcome and the final destination, because the matter comes to them.

The second: that it is derived from «الإِيالة», which is governance. The Arabs say «قد إلْنا وإيل علينا», i.e. "we governed and others governed us". It is as if the one who interprets speech were its governor, the one with power over it, who puts it in its proper place. This was transmitted from al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl. People have distinguished between taʾwīl and tafsīr in technical usage: tafsīr is restricted to what can be known only by transmitted authority (tawqīf), such as the occasions of revelation and the denotations of words, and opinion has no entry into it; while taʾwīl is permitted to one who has acquired the qualities of the people of knowledge and tools by which he is able to speak, provided he refers them back to principles and rules.

His saying: {والراسخون}: two analyses are possible in it. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ, and the pause is on the venerated Divine Name; on this [view] the clause «يقولون» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The second: that they are conjoined to the venerated Divine Name, so they are included in the knowledge of the interpretation. On this [view] there are two possibilities for the clause of saying. The first: that it is a ḥāl, i.e. "they know its interpretation while saying that". The second: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هم يقولون» "they say".

«الرُّسوخ» is firmness and settledness, a deeply rooted firmness; so it is more specific than firmness in general. The poet said:

1168 - لقد رَسَخَتْ في القلبِ مني مودَّةٌ ... لِلَيْلَى أَبَتْ آياتُها أَنْ تُغَيَّرا
(A love for Laylā has become rooted in my heart, whose signs refuse to be altered.)

{آمَنَّا بِهِ} is in the position of the accusative by [the verb of] saying. «كل» is a mubtadaʾ, i.e. «كله» "all of it" or «كلٌّ منه» "each of it", and the preposition-phrase after it is its khabar; and the clause is likewise accusative by [the verb of] saying.

semin-durr:195-195.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَنِّي لاَ أُضِيعُ}: the majority read «أَنَّ» with fatḥa, the original being «بأني», so the two [well-known] views [genitive or accusative position] apply to it. Ubayy read: «بأني», according to this original. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read with kasra, and there are two analyses of it. The first: it is on an implied saying, i.e. and He said: «إني». The second: it is by way of reported speech (ḥikāya) through «استجاب», because it contains the meaning of saying; this is the view of the Kufans.

«استجاب» is in the sense of «أجاب» (to answer), and is transitive by itself and with the lām; its verification has preceded at His saying {فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُواْ لِي} [al-Baqara: 186]. Tāj al-Qurrāʾ reported that «أجاب» is general, while «استجاب» is specific to the attainment of what is sought.

The majority [read]: «أُضيع» from أضاع; and it was read with the shadda and doubling [«أُضَيِّع»], the hamza [of أضاع] in it being for transfer [making the verb transitive], as in the poet's saying:
1515 - كمُرْضِعَة أولادَ أُخرى وضَيَّعَتْ ... بني بَطْنِها، هذا الضلالُ عن القصدِ
(Like a woman suckling another's children while she neglects the children of her own womb — this is straying from the right course.)

His saying: «منكم» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «عامل», i.e. being from among you.

As for «مِنْ ذَكَرٍ», there are five analyses in it. The first: it is to explain the genus (bayān al-jins): it explains the genus of the worker, the implied form being: who is male or female — even though some have stipulated for the explicative [مِنْ] that it enter upon something made definite by the lām of the genus; something of that has preceded. The second: it is redundant (zāʾida) because of the preceding negation in the speech; on this, «مِنْ ذَكَر» is a badal (substitute) of «عامل» itself, as if it were said: a worker, male or female. But this is open to question in that «مِنْ» is not made redundant in a badal. The third: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun latent in «منكم», since when it occurred as a naʿt it bore a pronoun; and the governor of the ḥāl is the governor of «منكم», i.e. a worker being from among you, being male [or female]. The fourth: that «مِنْ ذكرٍ» be a badal of «منكم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is a badal of the thing from the thing, both being for one entity", meaning it is then a detailing badal with repetition of the governor, as in His saying {لِلَّذِينَ استضعفوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 75] and {لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بالرحمن لِبُيُوتِهِمْ} [al-Zukhruf: 33]. There is a difficulty in this from two sides. The first: it is a badal of an overt noun from a present [second-person] pronoun in the badal of the whole for the whole, which is not permissible except according to al-Akhfash. Some restricted its permissibility to its conveying comprehensiveness, as in the poet's saying:
1516 - فما بَرِحَتْ أقدامُنا في مَقامِنا ... ثلاثتُنا حتى أُزيروا المنائيا
(Our feet did not leave our place, the three of us, until they were made to visit death.)
and His saying, the Exalted: {تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيداً لأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا} [al-Māʾida: 114]; since it conveyed comprehensiveness and emphasis, it was permissible. Al-Akhfash cited as proof the poet's saying:
1517 - بكمْ قريشٍ كُفِينا كلَّ مُعْضِلَةٍ ... وأمَّ نهَجَ الهدى مَنْ كان ضِلِّيلا
(Through you, Quraysh, we were spared every hardship, and whoever had been far astray took the road of guidance.)
and the other's saying:
1518 - وشَوْهاءَ تَعْدُو بي إلى صارخِ الوغَى ... بمُسْتَلْئِمٍ مثلِ الفَنيق المُدَجَّل
(And a long-limbed mare that races with me — with a mail-clad warrior like a stallion smeared with tar — towards the battle-cry.)
So «قريش» is a badal of «كم», and «بمستلئم» is a badal of «بي» with repetition of the preposition, and there is neither comprehensiveness nor emphasis there. So his [Abū al-Baqāʾ's] position runs on al-Akhfash's view, not that of the majority.

The second [difficulty]: the detailing badal is not with «أو»; it is only with the wāw, because it is for combining, as in the poet's saying:
1519 - وكنت كذي رِجْلَيْن رِجْلٍ صحيحةٍ ... ورِجْلٍ رَمَى منها الزمانُ فَشَلَّتِ
(I was like one with two legs: a sound leg, and a leg which Time struck, so that it withered.)
It may be possible to answer it that «أو» sometimes comes in the sense of the wāw, as in the poet's saying:
1520 - قومٌ إذا سمعوا الصَّريخَ رأيتَهُمْ ... ما بينَ مُلْجِمِ مُهْرِه أو سافِعِ
(A people who, when they hear the cry for help, you see them between one bridling his colt and one seizing [its forelock].)
So «أو» is in the sense of the wāw, because «بين» enters only upon what is multiple. Likewise here: since «عاملٍ» is general, a substitute was made of it by way of emphasis, and to one of the two parts was conjoined what is indispensable, because generality is emphasised only by generality. The fifth: that «مِنْ ذَكرٍ» be a second naʿt of «عامل», intended for clarification, so it is attached to something omitted, like the one before it.

His saying: {بَعْضُكُم مِّن بَعْضٍ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and there are three analyses in it. The first: this clause is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), brought to make clear the partnership of women with men in the reward that Allah promised His servants who work, because it is narrated among the occasions [of revelation] that Umm Salama, may Allah be pleased with her, asked him, upon him be peace, about that, and it was revealed. The meaning: just as you are from one origin, and some of you are taken from others, so likewise you are in the reward of work: a working man is not rewarded to the exclusion of a working woman.

Al-Zamakhsharī expressed this by [saying] that it is a parenthetical clause (muʿtariḍa). He said: "This is a parenthetical clause by which is made clear the partnership of women with men in what Allah promised those who work." [Translator's note: the printed text reads «جلمةٌ», a misprint for «جملةٌ».] By parenthesis he means that it was brought between His saying {عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ} and that by which the work of the worker is detailed, namely His saying {فالذين هَاجَرُواْ}. Hence al-Zamakhsharī said: "«فالذين هاجروا» is a detailing of the work of the worker among them, by way of magnifying [it]."

The second: that this clause is a naʿt. The third: that it is a ḥāl. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned these two, and did not specify the thing described nor the owner of the ḥāl; this is open to question.

His saying: {فالذين هَاجَرُواْ} is a mubtadaʾ, and His saying {لأُكَفِّرَنَّ} is the answer to an omitted oath, its implied form being: by Allah, I shall surely remove; and this oath and its answer are the khabar of this mubtadaʾ. In this verse and its parallels — such as His saying {والذين جَاهَدُواْ فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 69] and the poet's saying:
1521 - جَشَأَتْ فقلتُ اللَّذْ خَشِيْتِ ليأتِيَنْ ... وإذا أتاكِ فلاتَ حين مَناصِ
(My soul rose up [in fear], and I said: What you feared will surely come; and when it comes to you, it is no time for escape.)
— there is a refutation of Thaʿlab, who claimed that an oath clause does not occur as a khabar. He might say: this is governed by an implied saying, which is the khabar; and that has parallels.

The apparent sense is that these clauses after the relative noun are all ṣilas (relative clauses) of it, so the khabar applies only to one who combines these attributes: emigration, being killed and fighting. It may also be by way of division, the relative nouns having been deleted because the meaning is understood — which is the view of the Kufans, and the discussion of it has preceded — the implied form being: so those who emigrated, and those who were expelled, and those who fought; so the khabar, by His saying «لأكفرنَّ», is about whoever is characterised by one of these.

The majority of the Seven read: «وقاتَلوا وقُتِلوا», with the first active, from mufāʿala, and the second passive; this is a clear reading. Ibn ʿĀmir and Ibn Kathīr [read] likewise, except that they doubled the tāʾ of «قُتِّلوا», for multiplicity. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī [read] the reverse of this, with the first passive and the second active [«وقُتِلوا وقاتَلوا»].

The justification of this reading is by one of two meanings. Either the wāw does not require order, so with it was advanced what comes later in meaning — this if we take it as the same persons from whom these two acts issued. The second: that it be taken as distribution, i.e. among them are those who were killed and among them those who fought. This verse in meaning is like His saying {قُتِلَ مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ فَمَا وَهَنُواْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 146]; and the disagreement in this is like the disagreement in His saying {فَيَقْتُلُونَ وَيُقْتَلُونَ} [verse 111] in Barāʾa, and the justification there is like the justification here.

ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz read: «وقَتَلوا وقُتِلوا», the first active, from the triliteral «فَعَل», and the second passive; it is like the reading of the majority.

Muḥārib ibn Dithār read: «قَتَلوا وقاتلوا», both active. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read: «وقُتِّلوا وقاتَلوا», like the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī except that he doubled the tāʾ; and the analysis is like the analysis of their reading. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] reported from al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ: «قاتلوا وقُتِّلوا» with doubling of the tāʾ of «قُتِّلوا»; but this is the reading of Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir, as preceded, and it is as though he did not know that it is their reading.

His saying: «ثواباً»: regarding its accusative there are eight analyses. The first: it is accusative as an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of the clause before it requires it, the implied form being: I shall surely reward them a rewarding (إثابة or تثويباً); so «ثواباً» was put in the place of one of these two maṣdars, because الثواب is originally a noun for that with which one is rewarded, like العَطاء, a noun for what is given; then they may occur in the place of the maṣdar. It is parallel to His saying {صُنْعَ الله} [al-Naml: 88] and {وَعْدَ الله} [al-Nisāʾ: 122] in their being emphasising. The second: that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جنات», i.e. given as reward; and that is permissible even though it is indefinite, because it is specified by the naʿt. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «وإنْ كنت نكرةً», a misprint for «وإنْ كانت نكرةً».]

The third: it is a ḥāl from the object pronoun, i.e. rewarded. The fourth: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «تجري» which refers to «جنات». Abū al-Baqāʾ restricted its being a ḥāl to making it in the sense of the thing with which one is rewarded. He said: "It may occur in the sense of the thing with which one is rewarded, as in your saying: «هذا الدرهَمُ ثوابُك» (this dirham is your reward); on this it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun of the gardens, i.e. given as reward, and it may be a ḥāl from the object pronoun in «لأَدْخِلنهم»." The fifth: its accusative is by an omitted verb, i.e. He gives them a reward. The sixth: it is a badal of «جنات»; and they said: on the implication of «لأدْخلنهم» with [the meaning of] «لأَعْطِيَنَّهم» (I shall surely give them); since they saw that entering cannot validly be attributed to the reward, they needed that. Someone may say: He made the reward a container for them, by way of hyperbole, as was said about His saying {تَبَوَّءُوا الدار والإيمان} [al-Ḥashr: 9]. The seventh: it is accusative as a tamyīz (specification); this is the view of al-Farrāʾ. The eighth: it is accusative by cutting off (qaṭʿ), which is the view of al-Kisāʾī; however, Makkī, when he reported this from al-Kisāʾī, explained the cutting off as its being a ḥāl. In sum, these are two strange analyses, hard to understand.

And {مِّن عِندِ الله} is a naʿt of it.

His saying: {والله عِندَهُ حُسْنُ}: the best is that «حسن الثواب» be nominative as fāʿil (agent) of the adverbial before it, because it relies on the mubtadaʾ before it, the implied form being: and Allah — with Him is established the best reward. It may also be a mubtadaʾ, with the adverbial before it as its khabar, and the clause the khabar of the first. The first analysis is better only because it involves predicating with a single word, which is the original, unlike the second, in which the predication is by a clause.

semin-durr:196-196.t: Ibn Abī Isḥāq read: {لاَ يَغُرَّنَّكَ} with the nūn lightened [«لا يَغُرَّنْكَ»], and likewise {لاَ يَغُرَّنْكمْ} [Fāṭir: 5], {فَلاَ يَصُدَّنْك} [Ṭāhā: 16] and {وَلاَ يَصُدَّنْكم} [al-Zukhruf: 62].

semin-durr:197-197.t: His saying, the Exalted: {مَتَاعٌ}: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) indicated by the speech, its implied form being: their going about, or their activity, is a little enjoyment. The one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. and wretched is the resting-place — Hell.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمُصَدِّقاً}: it is conjoined (nasaq) to the position of «بآية», because «بآية» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), since the implied form is: "And I have come to you bearing a sign and confirming." Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj said: "«مصدقاً» is accusative as a ḥāl; the meaning is: and I have come to you confirming what is before me. Implying «جئتكم» is permissible because the beginning of the speech indicates it, namely His words {أَنِّي قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِآيَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ}; similar to it in [ordinary] speech is: 'I came to him with what he loves and honouring him.'" Al-Farrāʾ said: "«ومصدقاً» cannot be conjoined to «وجيهاً», because if that were so He would have said «ومُصَدِّقاً لِما بين يديه»" — meaning that if it were conjoined to it, He would have brought with it the pronoun of the absent [third person], not the pronoun of the speaker; others besides al-Farrāʾ mentioned the same. He also prohibited its being conjoined to «رسولاً». He said: "Because if it were referred back to it, He would have said «ومُصَدِّقاً لِما بين يديك», since He addressed Maryam with that, or He would have said «بين يديه»" — meaning that if it were conjoined to «رسولاً», the pronoun of address ought to have been brought, out of regard for Maryam, or the pronoun of absence, out of regard for the overt noun. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "We have mentioned that «ورسولاً» may be accusative by an implied verb, i.e. 'and I have been sent as a messenger'"; on this analysis «مصدقاً» would be conjoined to «رسولاً».
His words: {مِنَ التوراة}: there are two views on it. The first: it is a ḥāl from the relative «ما», i.e. "that which is before me, it being from the Torah"; what governs it is then «مصدقاً», because it governs the one the ḥāl describes. The second: it is a ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the adverbial serving as ṣila (relative clause), and what governs it is the [notion of] being settled (istiqrār) implied in the adverbial, or the adverbial itself because it stands in place of the verb.
His words: {وَلأُحِلَّ}: there are several views on it. The first: it is conjoined to the meaning of «مصدقاً», since the meaning is: "I have come to you to confirm what is before me and to make lawful for you"; similar to it in [ordinary] speech is: "I came to him apologising to him and to win his good pleasure", i.e. I came to apologise and to win. So said al-Wāḥidī, but this is questionable, because what it is conjoined to is a ḥāl, while this is a statement of cause (taʿlīl). The Shaykh said after mentioning this view: "This is conjunction by supposition (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-tawahhum), but this is not an instance of it, because the concept of the ḥāl differs from the concept of the cause, whereas in conjunction by supposition the meaning must be one in the conjoined element and what it is conjoined to. Do you not see in His words {فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن} [al-Munāfiqūn: 10] how the meaning is one in terms of suitability as an answer to the urging (taḥḍīḍ) [Translator's note: the source prints «التخضيض», evidently for «التحضيض»]? And likewise the poet's words:
1303 - تَقِيٌّ نَقِيٌّ لم يُكَثِّرْ غنيمةً ... بنَهْكَةٍ ذي قُرْبى ولا بِحَقَلِّدِ
(God-fearing, pure, he did not increase his spoils by wearing down a kinsman, nor is he ill-natured.)
how the meaning of negation is one in his words «لم يكثّر» and in his words «ولا بحقلّد», i.e. he is neither one who increases nor ill-natured; and likewise whatever comes of this type."
I say: this speaker may mean that it is conjoined to the meaning of «مصدقاً», i.e. by virtue of its indicating an omitted cause that agrees with it in wording; so he attributed the conjunction to its meaning in view of its indicating the omitted cause, because that shares with it the basis of its meaning — I mean what the root signifies — even if what the ḥāl indicates differs from what the cause indicates.
The second: it is conjoined to an implied cause, i.e. "I have come to you with a sign to give you ease and to make lawful", or "to lighten [the burden] for you and to make lawful", and the like.
The third: it is governed by an implied verb, because what preceded indicates it, i.e. "and I have come to you to make lawful"; the governor after the wāw was omitted.
The fourth: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) His words {وَأَطِيعُونِ}, the meaning being: "follow me so that I may make lawful for you". This is very far-fetched, or impossible.
The fifth: «ولأحلّ» is referred back to His words «بآية». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ولأحلّ» refers back to His words {بِآيَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ}, i.e. 'I have come to you with a sign from your Lord and to make lawful.'" The Shaykh said: "«ولأحلّ لكم» cannot properly refer back to «بآية», because «بآية» is in the position of a ḥāl and «لأحلّ» is a cause, and conjoining a cause to a ḥāl is not valid, because conjunction by a particle that makes [the second] share in the ruling requires sharing in the category of what is conjoined to; so if you conjoin to a maṣdar (verbal noun), a direct object, an adverbial, a ḥāl, a cause or anything else, the conjoined element shares with it in that." I say: his answer may be what preceded, namely that he meant referring it back to «بآية» insofar as it indicates an implied governor.
His words: {بَعْضَ الذي حُرِّمَ}: what is meant by «بعض» is its original meaning (some). Abū ʿUbayda said: "It is here in the sense of «كل» (all)", citing as evidence the words of Labīd:
1304 - تَرَّاكُ أمكنةٍ إذا لم أَرْضَها ... أو يَرْتَبِطْ بعضَ النفوسِ حِمامُها
(One who leaves places when I am not pleased with them — unless its fated death seizes some soul.)
People refuted him on the ground that it would then follow that usury, theft and killing would be made lawful for them, since they were forbidden to them; for if the meaning were "and to make lawful for you all that was forbidden to you", he would have made all of that lawful for them. Some cited as evidence that «بعض» is in the sense of «كل» the words of another:
1305 - أبا منذرٍ أَفْنَيْتَ فاستَبِقْ بعضَنَا ... حَنَانَيْكَ بعضُ الشرِّ أهونُ من بعضِ
(Abū Mundhir, you have annihilated [us], so spare some of us; have mercy — some evil is lighter than some.)
i.e. lighter than all evil. Others cited the words of another:
1306 - إنَّ الأمورَ إذا الأحداثُ دَبَّرها ... دونَ الشيوخِ تَرى في بعضِها خَلَلا
(Affairs, when the young manage them without the elders, you will see a flaw in some of them.)
i.e. a flaw in all of them. But there is no need to take the word out of what it signifies when its meaning can be sound, since what Labīd means by "some soul" is his own soul; and the partitive sense in the other two verses is clear, for some evil is lighter than some other evil, not than all of it; and likewise not every matter the young manage has a flaw in it — rather, their management may turn out better than the management of an elder.
The generality read «حُرِّمَ» in the passive, the agent being Allah the Exalted. ʿIkrima read «حَرَّم» in the active, the agent being Allah the Exalted, or the relative noun in His words {لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ}, because it is a revealed Book, or Mūsā, because he is the bearer of the Torah; he was implied because the mention of his Book indicates him.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī read «حَرُمَ» on the pattern of شَرُف and ظَرُف, attributing the verb to it figuratively, since it is known that the one who forbids is Allah the Exalted.
His words: {وَجِئْتُكُمْ}: this sentence may be a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first, since its meaning and wording preceded before that. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This is a repetition for emphasis, because this meaning came before in the verse preceding it." And it may be for establishing [a new meaning] (taʾsīs), since what it is connected to differs from what the one before it is connected to. The Shaykh said: "«وجئتكم بآية من ربكم» is for establishing, not for emphasising His words «قد جئتكم», and this sign would be His words {إِنَّ الله رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فاعبدوه}, because this statement is a witness to the truth of his message, since all the messengers held it and did not differ over it. He made this statement a sign and a mark because he is a messenger like the other messengers, inasmuch as He guided him to reflection on the proofs of reason and to inference; al-Zamakhsharī said this." [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark of the Shaykh's words is missing in the source.]

semin-durr:31-31.t:
The words of the Exalted: {تُحِبُّونَ الله}: the generality read «تُحِبون» with a ḍamma on the imperfect prefix, from أَحَبَّ; and likewise «يُحْبِبْكُم الله». Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī read تَحُبُّون, يَحْببكم with a fatḥa on the imperfect prefix. They are two dialectal forms: one says حَبَّه يَحِبُّه, with ḍamma or kasra on the ḥāʾ in the imperfect, and أَحَبَّه يُحِبُّه; the discussion of that has preceded in al-Baqara. Al-Zamakhsharī transmitted that «يَحِبَّكم» was read, with a fatḥa on the bāʾ and assimilation; this is evident, because whenever the two identical letters are made vowelless, by the jussive or by pausing, two dialectal forms are permissible: separation and assimilation. The verification of that will come in al-Māʾida.
The majority read «فاتِّبعوني» with a light nūn, which is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya). Al-Zuhrī read it doubled, and this was explained as his attaching the nūn of emphasis to the verb and assimilating it into the nūn of protection. He ought then to have dropped the wāw of the pronoun because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, except that he likened it to His words {أتحاجواني} [al-Anʿām: 80]. This is a weak justification, but it serves to account for this irregularity.
Al-Zajjāj attacked those who transmitted from Abū ʿAmr the assimilation of the rāʾ of «يغفر» into the lām of «لكم», and said: "It is an error and a mistake attributed to Abū ʿAmr." The verification of that has preceded, and that it is neither an error nor a mistake; rather it is a dialect of the Arabs that people have transmitted, even though the Basrans, as al-Zajjāj says, do not allow it.

semin-durr:32-32.t: The words of the Exalted: {فإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ}: this allows two aspects. The first: that it is an imperfect verb, the origin being «تتولَّوا», one of the two tāʾs having been dropped — the discussion of that has preceded; on this view the speech runs on one course, namely the second person. The second: that it is a past verb ascribed to a third-person pronoun; it may then be of the type of iltifāt (turning), the absent persons meant being, in meaning, those addressed. It parallels the words of the Exalted {حتى إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي الفلك وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم} [Yūnus: 22].

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His words: {وَنُوحاً}: «نوح» is a foreign noun which has no derivation according to the exacting grammarians. Some claimed that it is derived from al-nuwāḥ (wailing), as they did earlier with Ādam, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb. It is fully declinable (munṣarif), even though it has two secondary causes — being a proper name and personal foreignness — because of the lightness of its structure, being triliteral with a vowelless middle letter. Some allowed treating it as a diptote by analogy with «هند» and its class, but not on the basis of what was heard, since it has been heard only as declinable.
Al-Farrāʾ claimed that in the speech there is the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: «إن الله اصطفى دين آدم» ("Allah chose the religion of Ādam"). Al-Tabrīzī said: "This is nothing, because if the matter were so, it would have been said «ونوحٍ» (in the genitive), since the origin would be: the religion of Ādam and the religion of Nūḥ." This is a gross slip by al-Tabrīzī, since it does not follow that when the muḍāf is omitted the muḍāf ilayhi remains genitive, such that he could refute al-Farrāʾ with that. Rather, the well-known usage, beside which the eloquent know no other, is that the muḍāf ilayhi takes the inflection of the muḍāf when the latter is omitted; its remaining in the genitive is permissible only in a little of speech, on a condition mentioned in grammar, which will come to you in al-Anfāl. On al-Tabrīzī's opinion, the words of the Exalted {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82] ought to have «القرية» in the genitive, because everyone, he and others, says: this is on an omission, its implied form being: «أهلَ القرية» ("the people of the town").
«عِمْران» is a foreign noun; and it was said: an Arabic one derived from al-ʿamr (life). On both views it is a diptote: either because of being a proper name together with personal foreignness, or because of being a proper name together with the added alif and nūn.
The words of the Exalted: {عَلَى العالمين}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) اصطفى. If it is said: اصطفى is made transitive with من, as in «اصطفيتك مِنَ الناس» ("I chose you from among the people"), the answer is that it has been made to contain the meaning of «فَضَّل» ("preferred"), i.e.: He preferred them by choosing.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
The words of the Exalted: {ذُرِّيَّةً}: there are two aspects in its accusative. The first: that it is accusative as a badal (substitute) from what precedes it; and on this view there are three aspects concerning what it substitutes for. The first: that it is a badal from «آدم» and what is conjoined to it. This works only on the view of those who apply «الذرية» (offspring) both to fathers and to sons, and a group held this. Al-Jurjānī said: "The verse requires that the fathers be offspring of the sons and the sons offspring of the fathers; this is permissible because it is from «ذَرَأَ الخَلْقَ» ('He created the creation'), so the father is one from whom the child was produced, and the child is produced from the father." Al-Rāghib said: "Al-dhurriyya is said of one and of many, of the root and of the progeny, as in His words {حَمَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ} [Yā Sīn: 41], i.e.: their fathers; and women are called al-dharārī." On these two aspects it is sound to make «ذرية» a badal from Ādam and what is conjoined to him. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It cannot be a badal from Ādam, because he is not offspring." What he said is evident if he meant Ādam alone without those conjoined to him; if he meant Ādam and those mentioned with him, then the obstacle in his view is that applying "offspring" to fathers is not permissible.
The second of the aspects of the badal: that it is a badal from «نوح» and what is conjoined to him; Abū al-Baqāʾ inclined to this. The third: that it is a badal from the two families, I mean the family of Ibrāhīm and the family of ʿImrān; al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, meaning that the two families are one line of offspring.
The second of the two aspects of the accusative of «ذرية»: the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being: He chose them while they were offspring, some of them from others; what governs it is: اصطفى. The discussion of the derivation of this word, its pattern and its meaning has preceded in full, which makes repeating it unnecessary.
His words: {بَعْضُهَا مِن بَعْضٍ}: this clause is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ذرية.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِذْ قَالَتِ امرأت عِمْرَانَ}: there are several aspects concerning what puts it in the accusative. The first: that it is an implied «اذكر» ("remember"), so that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not an adverb, i.e.: remember for them the time when the wife of ʿImrān said such-and-such. Abū al-Ḥasan (al-Akhfash) and Abū al-ʿAbbās (al-Mubarrad) held this. The second: that what puts it in the accusative is the meaning of choosing, i.e. an implied «اصطفى», indicated by the first اصطفى, the implied form being: and He chose the family of ʿImrān when the wife of ʿImrān said. On this view His words «وآلَ عمران» are of the type of conjoining clauses, not of conjoining single words; for if it were made a conjoining of single words, it would follow that the time of choosing Ādam was the time when the wife of ʿImrān said such-and-such, and that is not so, because the two times differ. For that reason we are compelled to estimate a governing element other than the one pronounced. Al-Zajjāj and others held this.
The third: that it is accusative by «سميع»; Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī stated this explicitly, and al-Zamakhsharī evidently inclined to it, for he said: "Or (He is) All-Hearing, All-Knowing of the saying of the wife of ʿImrān and her intention, and «إذ» is accusative by it." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "That is not sound, because His words «عليم» are either a second khabar (predicate) or a description of His words «سميع». If it is a khabar, it is not permissible to separate the governing element from what it governs, since it is foreign to both of them. If it is a description, then «سميع» may not govern the adverb, because it has been described; and the active participle and what runs like it, when described before taking what it governs, may not then govern — with some Kufans disagreeing on that. And also because His being described as All-Hearing, All-Knowing is not restricted to that time." I say: this excuse is not preventing, because with an adverb and its equivalent there is a latitude not allowed with other things; for that reason it is placed before what lies in the domain of the relative «أل» and in the domain of the maṣdar particle «أَنْ».
The fourth: that «إذ» is redundant (zāʾida); this is the view of Abū ʿUbayda, the implied form being: the wife said. According to the grammarians this is a mistake, and Abū ʿUbayda used to be regarded as weak in grammar.
His words: {مُحَرَّراً}: there are several aspects in its accusative. The first: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun, namely «ما في بطني», so what governs it is «نَذَرْتُ». The second: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun made nominative by the preposition-phrase, since it occurs as the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; this is close to the first, and what governs this ḥāl is the "being established" (al-istiqrār) implied in the preposition and its genitive noun. The third: that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the maṣdar comes on the pattern of the passive participle of verbs exceeding three letters. On this view there may be the omission of a muḍāf in the speech, its implied form being: I vowed to You what is in my womb, a vow of dedication; or it may be among what is accusative according to the meaning, because the meaning of «نَذَرْتُ لك» is: I dedicated what is in my womb, a dedication.
Among cases of the maṣdar coming on the pattern of the passive participle from verbs exceeding three letters are the words of the Exalted {وَمَزَّقْنَاهُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ} [Sabaʾ: 19] and His words {وَمَن يُهِنِ الله فَمَا لَهُ مِن مُّكْرَمٍ} [al-Ḥajj: 18] in the reading of whoever read the rāʾ with fatḥa, i.e.: every tearing, and: he has no honouring. Similar is the poet's words:
1240 - ألم تَعْلَمْ مُسَرَّحِيَ القوافي ... فلاعِيَّاً بهنَّ ولا اجْتِلاَبا
(Do you not know my letting loose of rhymes — without faltering over them and without borrowing?)
i.e.: my letting loose (tasrīḥī) of rhymes. The fourth: that it is the adjective of an omitted object, its implied form being: a dedicated boy; Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib said this, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya found this view questionable. I say: the point of question in it is that «نَذَرَ» has already taken its object, namely His words {مَا فِي بَطْنِي}, so it does not pass on to another object; and that is a sound objection. On the view that it is a ḥāl, it may be a concurrent ḥāl if by dedication (taḥrīr) the meaning of emancipation is intended, or an anticipated (muqaddara) ḥāl if the meaning of serving the church is intended, as came in the exegesis.
Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī paused on «امرأة» with hāʾ rather than tāʾ. They wrote امرأة with (open) tāʾ, while its analogy is the hāʾ, here and in Yūsuf: {امرأة العزيز} [verse: 30], [in] two places, {امرأة نُوحٍ} [al-Taḥrīm: 10], {امرأة لُوطٍ} [al-Taḥrīm: 10] and {امرأة فِرْعَوْنَ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 9]. The people of Medina pause with tāʾ, following the script of the Muṣḥaf; this is a dialect of the Arabs, who say for Ḥamza: حَمْزَتْ. They recited:
1241 - اللهُ نَجَّاكَ بكَفَّيْ مَسْلَمَتْ ... مِنْ بعدِما وبعدِما وبعدِمَتْ
(Allah saved you by the two hands of Maslama, after what, and after what, and after what.)
His words: {مَا فِي بَطْنِي}: He used «ما», which is for the non-rational, because the matter of what was in her womb was undetermined, and what is undetermined may be expressed by «ما». An example: if you see a figure «[Translator's note: the text has شيخاً, "an old man"; evidently شبحاً, "a figure", is meant]» from afar and do not know whether it is a human being or something else: «ما هذا؟» ("what is this?"). And if you knew it was a human being but did not know whether it was male or female, you would also say: «ما هو». The verse is of this kind. This is according to those who hold that «ما» is specific to the non-rational; as for those who hold that it applies to rational beings, they do not need any interpretation. It was also said: since what is in the womb has no discernment or reason, it was expressed with «ما», which is for the non-rational.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِمَ تَلْبِسُونَ}: the majority read it with kasra on the bāʾ, from «لَبَس عليه يَلْبِسُه», i.e. he confused it for him. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it with fatḥa on it, taking it from «لَبِسْت الثوب أَلْبَسُه» (I put on the garment), by way of metaphor. Abū Mijlaz read «تُلبِّسُون» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra and doubling on the bāʾ, from «لَبَّس» with doubling, whose sense is intensification. The bāʾ in «بالباطل» is for the ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. «ملتسباً بالباطل» (mixed with falsehood) [Translator's note: so printed; «متلبِّساً» is presumably meant].

His saying: {وَتَكْتُمُونَ الحق} is a resumptive clause; for that reason it is not put in the accusative by an implied «أَنْ» as the answer to the interrogative. Al-Zajjāj among the Basrans and al-Farrāʾ among the Kufans permitted the accusative in it from the standpoint of Arabic, so the nūn would fall away and it would be accusative by ṣarf (divergence) according to the Kufans, and by an implied «أَنْ» according to the Basrans. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī prohibited this and rejected it, saying: "The interrogative falls on the confusing (al-labs) only; as for «تكتمُون», it is a definite statement in which only the nominative is permissible." He means that it is not conjoined to «تَلْبِسون» but is a resumption: He informed about them that they conceal the truth while knowing that it is the truth. Abū Muḥammad ibn ʿAṭiyya reported from Abū ʿAlī that he also said: "Ṣarf here is ugly, as is implying «أَنْ», because «يكتمون» is conjoined to an implied affirmed statement and is not asked about; He asked only about the cause of the confusing, and the confusing is affirmed. So the verse is not equivalent to their saying «لا تأكلِ السمكَ وتَشْرَب اللبن» (do not eat fish while drinking milk), nor to your saying «أتقومُ فأقومَ» (will you stand, so that I stand?). Conjoining to an established affirmed statement is ugly when it is put in the accusative, except in poetic necessity, as was transmitted:

1328 - . . . . . . . . . . ... وأَلْحَقُ بالحجازِ فاستريحا
(… and I will go off to the Ḥijāz and so find rest.)

Sībawayh said concerning your saying «أَسِرْتَ حتى تَدخُلَها؟» (did you travel so as to enter it?): only the accusative is permissible in «تدخل», because the travelling is asked about and is not affirmed; and when we say «أيُّهم سار حتى يدخُلها؟» (which of them travelled until he entered it?), you put it in the nominative, because the travelling is affirmed and the question falls only on something else."

Al-Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What appears from this report from him is that it contradicts what was reported from him before it. For in what precedes it, the question falls on the confusing only, and «يكتُمون» is a definite statement in which only the nominative is permissible; whereas in what Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported, «يكتمون» is conjoined to an implied affirmed statement and is not asked about, so the conjunction indicates that the two share in the question about the cause of the confusing and the cause of the concealing, both being affirmed. There is a difference between this meaning and «يكتمون» being a pure statement which does not share with the confusing in the question about the cause. What Abū ʿAlī held — that when an interrogative implies the occurrence of the action, the verb is not put in the accusative by an implied «أَنْ» in its answer — was followed by Jamāl al-Dīn ibn Mālik, who said in his «تسهيل»: 'or to an interrogative that does not imply the occurrence of the action'; so if it implies the occurrence of the action, the accusative is impossible in his view, as in «لِمَ ضربْتَ زيداً فيجاريك» (why did you hit Zayd, so that he should requite you?), because the hitting has occurred.

Other grammarians did not stipulate that. Rather, when it is impossible to cast a maṣdar (verbal noun) from what precedes — either because no verb has preceded, or because it is impossible to cast a maṣdar meant for the future on account of the verb being past — a maṣdar whose futurity is implied is supposed from what the meaning indicates. So when you say «لِمَ ضربْتَ زيداً [فأضربك]», the implied meaning is: «ليكنْ منك إعلامٌ بضرب زيد فمجازاةٌ منا» (let there be from you an informing about the hitting of Zayd, and then a requital from us). As for Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī's rejoinder to al-Zajjāj and al-Farrāʾ, it is not binding, because it may be objected that the verb is meant as past, since it is not explicit in that; futurity is possible, given the certainty of its issuing, especially from a person from whom the like of that has issued. And even granting that pastness is certain, it is still not binding on al-Zajjāj, because, as has preceded, when it is not possible to cast a future maṣdar from the interrogative clause, we cast it from what it entails. What indicates the cancellation of this condition and the interpretation in the way we mentioned is what Ibn Kaysān reported of putting the imperfect in the accusative after a past verb whose occurrence is certain and which is asked about, such as «أين ذهب زيد فنتبعَه؟» (where did Zayd go, that we may follow him?), «من أبوك فنكرمَه؟» (who is your father, that we may honour him?), and «كم مالُك فنعرفَه؟» (how much is your wealth, that we may know it?). All that is interpreted in the way I mentioned, by casting a future maṣdar from what the preceding clauses entail; for the implied meaning is: let there be from you an informing about Zayd's going, and then a following from us; let there be from you an informing about your father, and then an honouring of him from us; let there be from you a making known of the amount of your wealth, and then a knowing from us."

This long inquiry is based on supposing something that did not happen, for it was not read, either among the irregular (shādhdh) readings or elsewhere, except with the nūn retained. But scholars have an aim in lengthening the inquiry: sharpening the mind.

Beyond this there is a problematic reading which they transmitted from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, namely «لِمَ تَلْبِسوا وتكتُموا» with the nūn dropped from both verbs. It is a reading not far from sheer error, as though he imagined that «لِمَ» was the jussive «لم» and put the verb in the jussive by it. The exegetes have reported here from some grammarians that they make the verb jussive by «لِمَ», construing it on «لَمْ»; al-Sajāwandī and others reported that from them. I do not think any grammarian says that at all — how could he say of a preposition and its genitive noun that it puts the verb in the jussive!! This is something that is never uttered at all and that one cannot bear to hear. If this is established as a reading, and it must be, then let it be among the cases in which the nūn of the nominative has been dropped for lightness where nothing requires its dropping. Among such is the reading of some {قَالُواْ ساحران تَظَّاهَرَا} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 48] with doubling of the ẓāʾ, the original being «تتظاهران»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ẓāʾ and the nūn dropped for lightness. And in the ḥadīth: «والذي نفسي بيده لا تَدخُلوا الجنةَ حتى تؤمنوا، ولا تُؤمِنوا حتى تَحابُّوا» ("By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another"), by which he, peace be upon him, means «لا تدخلون ولا تؤمنون» [Translator's note: printed «لاتخلون», a misprint for «لا تدخلون»], since a prohibition is impossible in meaning. The poet said:

1329 - أَبِيتُ أَسْرِي وتبيتي تَدْلُكِي ... وجَهكِ بالعنبرِ والمِسْكِ الذَّكي
(I spend the night travelling, while you spend the night rubbing your face with ambergris and fragrant musk.)

meaning «تبيتين» and «تدلكين». Similar is the saying of Abū Ṭālib:

1330 - فإن يَكُ قومٌ سَرَّهُمْ ما صَنَعْتُمُ ... سَتَحْتَلِبُوها لاقِحاً غيرَ باهِلِ
(If there are people whom what you have done has pleased, you will milk it as a pregnant she-camel, not one left untended [i.e. it will bring forth calamity].)
