The second: that it refers to «النار». al-Ṭabarī said: "Some people make it refer to al-shafā, and it was made feminine because al-shafā is annexed to a feminine, as Jarīr said:
1376 - أرى مَرَّ السنين أَخَذْنَ مني ... كما أخَذَ السِّرارُ مِن الهلال
(I see the passing of the years has taken from me, as the last night of the month takes from the crescent.)"
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The matter is not as they said, for no such artifice is needed in the verse, unless we found no antecedent for the pronoun except al-shafā; but since we have a feminine word to which the pronoun can refer, / and the meaning under discussion supports it, there is no need for that artifice." The Shaykh said: "I say: it is not good for it to refer to anything but al-shafā, because their being on the brink is one of the two parts of the predication, so the pronoun can refer only to it. As for the mention of the pit, it came only by way of annexation to it. Do you not see that when you say «كان زيدٌ غلامَ جعفر», Jaʿfar is not the one spoken about and is not one of the two parts of the predication? Likewise if you say «زيد ضربَ غلامَ هندٍ», you have said nothing about Hind; you mentioned Jaʿfar and Hind only to specify the one spoken about. As for the mention of the fire, it was mentioned only to specify the pit, and it is likewise not one of the two parts of the predication, nor is it spoken about. Being rescued from the brink is more eloquent than being rescued from the pit and from the fire, because rescue from the brink [entails rescue from the pit and the fire, while rescue from them does not entail rescue from the brink]. So its reference to al-shafā is the apparent one in wording and in meaning."

al-Zajjāj said: "His saying «منها»: the pronoun refers to the fire, to the brink; because the intent is rescue from the fire, not from the brink of the pit." Another said: "It refers to the pit, for if Allah rescued them from the pit, He rescued them from its brink, because its brink is part of it."

al-Wāḥidī said: "It is permissible to mention the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi and then have the pronoun refer to the muḍāf ilayhi rather than the muḍāf, as in Jarīr's saying «أرى مرَّ السنين أخَذْنَ» (the verse). He mentioned the passing of the years, then reported about the years. Likewise the saying of al-ʿAjjāj:
1377 - طولُ الليالي أَسْرَعَتْ في نَقْضِِي ... طَوَيْنَ طولي وَطَوَيْنَ عَرْضي
(The length of the nights hastened my undoing; they folded up my length and folded up my breadth.)
He said: "This is so when the muḍāf is of the same kind as the muḍāf ilayhi: the passing of the years is the years, and likewise the brink of the pit is part of the pit; so he mentioned the brink and the pronoun returned to the pit." I say: these two statements are explicit in refuting what the Shaykh said, except that the meaning he gave is preferable, because rescuing them from the edge of the pit is more eloquent than rescuing them from the pit; and the artifice he mentioned is also clear.

al-Inqādh is deliverance and removal. al-Azharī said: "One says anqadhtuhu, naqadhtuhu, istanqadhtuhu and tanaqqadhtuhu in one meaning, and 'a faras naqīdh' is said when it was taken from another people, because it was rescued from them." al-Ḥufra is fuʿla in the sense of mafʿūla, like ghurfa in the sense of maghrūfa.

His saying {كذلك يُبَيِّنُ الله} is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar or a ḥāl from its pronoun, i.e. "Allah makes clear to you a clarification like His clarification to you of the evident signs." His saying {مِّنَ النار} is an adjective of «حفرة», and so it is attached to an omitted element.

semin-durr:104-104.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلْتَكُن مِّنْكُمْ أُمَّةٌ}: «تكن» may be the complete verb, i.e. "let there be found among you a community", in which case «أمة» is the fāʿil (agent), and «يَدْعُون» is a clause in the position of nominative as an adjective of «أمة»; «منكم» is attached to «تكن» as partitive. «منكم» may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «أمة», since it could have been made its adjective had it come after it. «مِنْ» may also be explicative (bayān), because the thing explained, although it comes later in wording, is earlier in rank. It may also be the incomplete verb, in which case «أمة» is its subject and «يَدْعُون» its predicate, and «منكم» is attached either to the being, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «أمة». It is also possible that «منكم» is the predicate and «يَدْعُون» an adjective of «أمة», though this is remote. The majority read «ولتكن»; al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī and al-Sulamī read it with kasra [on the lām], which is the original.

His saying: {وَيَأْمُرُونَ بالمعروف وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ المنكر} is a case of mentioning the specific after the general out of concern for it, like His saying {وملائكته وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ} [al-Baqara: 98], because the name "good" applies to both, and indeed they are the greatest of goods. His saying {جَآءَهُمُ البينات}: He did not make the verb feminine, because of the separation and because it is non-literally feminine, meaning "the proofs".

semin-durr:127-127.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِيَقْطَعَ}: There are seven views on what this lām is attached to. The first: that it is attached to his saying {وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ}; al-Ḥawfī said this, and there is remoteness in it because of the length of the separation. The second: that it is attached to the victory (al-naṣr) in his saying {وَمَا النصر إِلاَّ مِنْ عِندِ الله}, and there is something to consider in it, in that the maṣdar and what is attached to it have been separated by a foreign element, namely the khabar. The third: that it is attached to what the khabar is attached to, namely his saying {مِنْ عِندِ الله}, the estimate being: "and victory is only existing, or only resting, from Allah, that He may cut off". The fourth: that it is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being: "He reinforced you" or "He gave you victory that He may cut off". The fifth: that it is conjoined to his saying «ولتطمئِنَّ», the conjunction having been omitted because the meaning is understood, as in his saying {ثَلاثَةٌ رَّابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ} [al-Kahf: 22]; on this, the sentence {وَمَا النصر إِلاَّ مِنْ عِندِ الله} would be parenthetical between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined, and this is of no account. The sixth: that it is attached to the making (al-jaʿl); Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it. The seventh: that it is attached to his saying «يُمْدِدْكم», and there is remoteness in it because of the intervening elements between them.

And al-ṭaraf: what is meant by it is a group and a party. «من الذين» may be attached to the cutting (al-qaṭʿ), in which case «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya); or it may be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «طرفاً», in which case «مِنْ» is partitive (lil-tabʿīḍ).

His saying: {أَوْ يَكْبِتَهُمْ}: conjoined to «لِيقطعَ». As for «أو», it is said that it is in its usual sense of division (tafṣīl), i.e. "that He may cut off a part of some and abase others"; and it is said, rather, that it is in the sense of «و» (and), i.e. "He gathers both things against them".

And al-kabt: inflicting something disagreeable. It is also said to be throwing down upon the face and hands; on these two views the تاء is radical and is not a substitute for anything, but is an independent root. It is also said that its origin is from kabadahu, when he afflicted him with something disagreeable that caused pain in his liver (kabid), like your saying raʾastuhu, i.e. I struck his head. What indicates this is the reading of Lāḥiq ibn Ḥumayd: «أو يكبِدَهم» with دال; and the Arabs substitute the تاء for the دال, saying harata al-thawba and harada-hu, sabata raʾsahu and sabada-hu. It has also been said: "The reading of Lāḥiq originally has the تاء, and it was only substituted by a دال, as they say sabada raʾsahu and harada al-thawba, the origin in both being the تاء."

And his saying: {فَيَنقَلِبُواْ} is consequent upon what has preceded. Al-khayba: not attaining what is sought; khāba yakhību khaybatan. And «خائبين» is accusative as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:128-128.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَوْ يَتُوبَ}: There are several views on its being accusative. The first: that it is conjoined to the accusative verbs before it, its estimate being: "that He may cut off, or abase them, or turn to them in forgiveness, or punish them". On this, his saying «ليس لك من الأمرِ شيءٌ» is a parenthetical sentence between the two conjoined elements. The meaning: Allah the Exalted is the Owner of their affair; if He wills, He cuts off a part of them or defeats them, or turns to them in forgiveness if they submit and return, or punishes them if they persist in their disbelief. A group of grammarians, such as al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj, took this analysis.

The second: that «أو» here is in the sense of «إلاَّ أَنْ» (unless), as in their saying "I will surely cling to you or you pay me my due" (لألزَمَنَّك أو تقضِيَني حقي), i.e. "unless you pay me".

The third: that «أو» is in the sense of «حتى» (until), i.e. "you have no part in the matter until He turns in forgiveness". On these two views the speech is connected with his saying «ليس لك من الأمر شيء», and the meaning is: you have no part in the matter, except that He turns to them in forgiveness through Islam, whereupon joy comes to you through their guidance to it, or He punishes them by killing or by fire in the Hereafter, so that He heals (the hearts) through them. Among those who held this are al-Farrāʾ and Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Like this speech is: 'I will surely blame you or you give me', in the sense of 'unless you give me' and 'until you give me'." And Ibn al-Anbārī recited in that regard the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

1425 - فقلتُ له لاَ تبْكِ عينُك إنَّما ... تحاولُ مُلْكَاً أو تموتَ فَتُعْذَرا
(I said to him: Let not your eye weep; you are only seeking a kingdom, or [else] you die and are excused.)

He meant: "until you die", or "unless you die." I say: In his estimating the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays with «حتى» there is something to consider, since the meaning does not accord with it, because he did not do that for the sake of this goal; and the grammarians did not estimate it except in the sense of «إلاَّ».

[Translator's note: the source numbers this view "the third" a second time; it is the fourth in order.] The third: that it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ», conjoined to his saying «الأمر», as if it were said: "You have nothing of the matter, or of His turning to them in forgiveness, or of His punishing them." Since it is in the interpretation of a noun, it is conjoined to the noun before it. It is of the category of his saying:

1426 - ولولا رجالٌ من رِزامٍ أعِزَّةً ... وآلُ سُبَيْعٍ أو أَسُوْءَكَ علقما
(Were it not for men of Rizām, mighty, and the family of Subayʿ, or I would grieve you [with] colocynth.)

and her saying:

1427 - لَلُبْسُ عباءةٍ وتقرَّ عيني ... أَحَبُّ إليَّ مِنْ لُبْسِ الشُّفوف
(To wear a cloak and have my eye be cooled is dearer to me than wearing fine garments.)

The fourth: that it is conjoined, by the interpretation mentioned, to «شيء», the estimate being: "You have nothing of the matter, nor Allah's turning to them in forgiveness, nor their punishment", i.e. you have no part either in their repentance or in their punishment; that returns only to Allah the Exalted.

Ubayy read: «أو يتوبُ، أو يعذِّبُهم» with both in the nominative, as a resumption in a nominal sentence whose mubtadaʾ is omitted, i.e. "or He turns in forgiveness and punishes them".

semin-durr:130-130.t: His saying, the Exalted: {أَضْعَافاً}: the plural of ḍiʿf. Since it is a plural of paucity while the intent is abundance, He followed it with what indicates that, namely the description with «مضاعفة» (multiplied). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «أضعافاً» is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl from «الربا». Discussion of «أضعاف» and its singular has already been given in al-Baqara. Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read «مُضَعَّفَةً» with doubled ʿayn and no alif, and the rest read it lightened and with the alif. The discussion of doubling and lightening has also already been given in al-Baqara.

semin-durr:133-133.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وسارعوا}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «سارعوا» without the واو, and the rest with the conjunctive واو. Whoever dropped it makes the latter a resumption by that, or intended conjunction but omitted the conjunction because of what indicates it, as in his saying, the Exalted, {ثَلاثَةٌ رَّابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ} [al-Kahf: 22]; the weakness of this position has already been mentioned. Whoever retained the واو conjoined an imperative sentence to a like one. Beyond following the transmitted reports in recitation, each followed the orthography of his codex, for the واو is absent from the codices of Medina and Syria and present in the rest.

His saying: {مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ}: an adjective of «مغفرة», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range, figuratively. And his saying {عَرْضُهَا السماوات} requires an omission, i.e. "like the breadth of the heavens", which is indicated by his saying {عَرْضُهَا كَعَرْضِ}; and the sentence is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «جنة».

His saying: {أُعِدَّتْ}: its position may be genitive as a second adjective of «جنة», and its position may be accusative as a ḥāl from «جنة», because once it was described it became specified and so drew near to the definite nouns. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be a resumption, and it cannot be a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi for three reasons. The first: there is no governing agent, and what has come of that is interpreted away, despite its weakness. The second: al-ʿarḍ here does not mean the true maṣdar but means the distance. The third: that would necessitate separation between the ḥāl and its owner by the khabar." By "the khabar" he means «السماوات"; and this is a sound rebuttal.

semin-durr:134-134.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين يُنفِقُونَ}: the three cases are possible for its position: the genitive, as a naʿt or badal or explicative apposition (bayān); and the accusative and nominative by severance (qaṭʿ) which signals praise.

His saying: {والكاظمين}: the genitive and accusative are possible for it, as has gone before regarding what precedes it. Al-kaẓm: restraining. Kaẓama ghayẓahu means he restrained it; and kaẓama al-qirba wa-l-siqāʾ (the water-skin and the milk-skin) when he tied their two mouths, preventing what is in them from coming out; from it comes al-kiẓām, the thong with which the skin and the water-skin are tied. Originally al-kaẓm is the outlet of the breath; one says "he took him by his kaẓm", i.e. the outlet of his breath. Al-kuẓūm: the holding back of the breath, by which stillness is expressed, as in their saying "so-and-so does not breathe". And al-makẓūm: one filled with rage, as if because of his rage he cannot speak or let out his breath; and al-kaẓīm: one filled with grief. Abū Ṭālib said:

1428 - فَحَضَضْتُ قومي واحتَسَبْتُ قتالَهم ... والقومُ من خوفِ المَنايا كُظَّمُ
(I urged on my people and counted their fighting a reward with Allah, while the people, out of fear of death, were holding their breath.)

And kaẓama al-baʿīr: when the camel stops chewing the cud because of that; from it is the saying of al-Rāʿī:

1429 - وأفَضْنَ بعدَ كُظومِهِنَّ بِجِرَّةٍ ... مِنْ ذي الأباطِحِ إذ رَعَيْنَ حَقِيلا
(And they poured forth, after their holding back, a cud from [the pasture of] Dhū al-Abāṭiḥ when they grazed ḥaqīl.)

And al-ḥaqīl is a plant; it is also said to be a place. On the first view it is a mafʿūl bihi, and on the second it is an adverb, and it would be irregular that it is not governed by «في», because it is a specific adverb of place, and the object would be omitted, i.e. "when they grazed the pasture in Ḥaqīl". Camels cut off their cud only at fright. From it is the saying of Aʿshā Bāhila describing a man who slaughters camels abundantly:

1430 - قد تَكْظِمُ البُزْلُ منه حين تُبْصِرُه ... حتى تَقَطَّع في أَجْوافِها الجِرَرُ
(The mature camels hold back [their breath] at him when they see him, until the cuds are cut off in their bellies.)

Al-jirar is the plural of jirra (cud). Al-kiẓāma: an iron ring at the end of the balance in which its cords are gathered; it is also the thong joined to the bowstring. And al-kaẓāʾim: openings between two hands (channels) from which water flows to the other; all of that by analogy with the passage of the breath.

semin-durr:135-135.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والذين إِذَا فَعَلُواْ}: It may be conjoined to the relative noun before it, in which case the previously mentioned views apply to it, and the sentence {والله يُحِبُّ المحسنين} would be a parenthetical sentence between the two conjoined elements. It is also possible that «والذين» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «أولئك» a second mubtadaʾ, «جزاؤهم» a third mubtadaʾ, and «مغفرةٌ» the khabar of the third; the third with its khabar is the khabar of the second, and the second with its khabar is the khabar of the first. His saying {إِذَا فَعَلُواْ} is a conditional, its apodosis being «ذكروا», and his saying {فاستغفروا} is conjoined to the apodosis; the conditional sentence with its apodosis is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The first object of «استغفر» is omitted, i.e. "they asked Allah's forgiveness for their sins". The discussion of «استغفر» has already been given: it governs two objects, the second with a preposition, and it is not this lām but «مِنْ», and it may be omitted. His saying {وَمَن يَغْفِرُ} is an interrogative whose meaning is negation, and for that reason an exception follows it.

And his saying {إِلاَّ الله} is a badal from the latent pronoun in «يغفرُ»; the estimate: "None forgives sins except Allah". The preferred form here is the nominative as a badal, because the speech is not affirmative; its verification has already been given at his saying, the Exalted, {وَمَن يَرْغَبُ عَن مِّلَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِلاَّ مَن سَفِهَ نَفْسَهُ} [al-Baqara: 130]. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ومَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ, «يغفر» its khabar, and {إِلاَّ الله} a fāʿil or a badal from the pronoun, which is the preferable view, because if you make Allah the Exalted the fāʿil you need to estimate a pronoun, i.e. 'and who forgives sins, [with] him other than Allah'." What he said, I mean his making the Majestic Name a fāʿil, comes close to error, for the interrogative here is not meant in its real sense; negation is what is meant. The correct view is what has preceded, that the Majestic Name is a badal from that latent pronoun referring back to the interrogative «مَنْ».

His saying: {وَلَمْ يُصِرُّواْ}: it may be a ḥāl sentence from the fāʿil of «استغفروا», i.e. "they asked forgiveness without persisting"; and this sentence may be coordinated with «فاستغفروا», i.e. their committing the indecency was followed by mention of Allah the Exalted, asking forgiveness for their sins, and their not persisting in them. On these two views the sentence {وَمَن يَغْفِرُ الذنوب إِلاَّ الله} is parenthetical: between the two conjoined elements on the second view, and between the ḥāl and its owner on the first.

His saying: {وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ}: it may be a second ḥāl from the fāʿil of «استغفروا», and it may be a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يُصِرُّوا». The object of «يَعْلَمُون» is omitted because it is known. It is said that its estimate is: "they know that Allah turns to whoever repents", said by Mujāhid. And it is said: "they know that abandoning it is better", said by Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan. And it is said: "they know the reckoning for it or Allah's pardon of it". As for «ما» in his saying {على مَا فَعَلُواْ}, it may be a noun in the sense of «الذي» (that which), and it may be a maṣdar particle.

And al-iṣrār: persevering in a thing and not desisting from it, and firmly resolving not to leave it, from ṣarra al-danānīr, when he tied them up; from it comes "ṣurrat al-darāhim" (a purse of dirhams) for what is tied up with them. Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said, describing horses:

1431 - عوابِسُ بالشُّعْثِ الكُماةِ إذا ابْتَغَوْا ... عُلالَتَها بالمُحْصَداتِ أَصَرَّتِ
(Scowling, with the dishevelled, armoured warriors, when they sought their last reserve of speed with the tightly-twisted [whips], they persisted.)

i.e. they held firm and stayed, persevering in what they were set upon. And the poet said:

1432 - يُصِرُّ بالليلِ ما تُخْفِي شواكِلُه ... يا ويحَ كلِّ مُصِرِّ القلبِ خَتَّارِ
(He persists at night in what his flanks conceal; alas for every heart-persisting, treacherous one.)

semin-durr:156-156.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذَا ضَرَبُواْ}: «إذا» is an adverb of future time, and for that reason the views of the i'rab scholars here are unsettled, because the operator in it is «قالوا», which is past. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is «إذا ضَرَبوا» said together with «قالوا»? I say: it is a narration of a past state (ḥikāyat ḥāl), like your saying 'when they travel in the land'." And Abū l-Baqāʾ said, after saying something close to al-Zamakhsharī's statement: "It is also permissible that «كفروا» and «قالوا» be past, with the future meant by them, the state being narrated with them; on this the implied form would be: they disbelieve and they say." End of quotation. So in both views there is a narration of a state, but in the first it is the narration of a past state, in the second of a future one, and in this respect it is like His saying, the Exalted: {حتى يَقُولَ الرسول والذين آمَنُواْ} [البقرة: 214], which has already preceded. It is also possible that future time be meant by «قال», not by way of narration but because it occurs as the ṣila (relative clause) of a relative noun. Some have stated explicitly that a past verb, when it occurs as the ṣila of a relative noun, is fit for future meaning, as in {إِلاَّ الذين تَابُواْ مِن قَبْلِ أَن تَقْدِرُواْ عَلَيْهِمْ} [المائدة: 34], and Ibn ʿAṭiyya inclined to this. He said: "«إذا», which is a particle of the future, entered because «الذين» is an indefinite (vague) noun that includes whoever said (it) in the past and whoever says (it) in the future, and because this occurrence can be imagined in the future time." He means that it would then be a narration of a future state.
It was said: «إذا» has the meaning of «إذْ», and that is nothing. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) supposed an omitted muḍāf that is the operator in «إذا», its implied form being: "and they said because of the perishing of their brothers", that is, out of fear that their brothers would perish when they travel or go on a military expedition. So he supposed the operator to be a verbal noun resolvable into «أَنْ» and the imperfect, so that it is future. He said: "But the pronoun in His saying {لَّوْ كَانُواْ عِنْدَنَا} then becomes returning to «إخوانهم» in wording while belonging to others in meaning, that is, it returns to other brothers, namely those whose death occurred earlier because of travel or expedition; and their aim by that was to dishearten those who remained. It is parallel to 'a dirham and half of it', and {وَمَا يُعَمَّرُ مِن مُّعَمَّرٍ وَلاَ يُنقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ} [فاطر: 11], and the saying of al-Nābigha:
1477 - قالَتْ: ألا ليتما هذا الحمامُ لنا ... إلى حمامتِنا ونصفُه فَقَدِ
(She said: 'Would that this dove were ours, together with our dove, and half of it too — then it would be enough.')
that is: half of another dirham, and of another long-lived person, and of another dove."
The lām in «لإِخوانهم» is for cause, and is not here for conveying (tablīgh) as in your saying: "I said to Zayd: do such-and-such".
The majority read «غُزَّى» with shadda, plural of «غازٍ». Its regular form would be «غُزَاة», like kirām and rumāt, but they treated the defective like the sound, as in ḍārib and ḍurrab, ṣāʾim and ṣuwwam. Al-Zuhrī and al-Ḥasan read «غُزَى» without the shadda, and there are two views on it: that he lightened the zāy out of dislike of heaviness in the plural; the second: that its origin is «غُزاة», like quḍāt and rumāt, but he omitted the tāʾ of feminisation, because the pattern itself indicates the plural, so the tāʾ is dispensable.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: This omission is frequent in their speech, and among it is the saying of the poet praising al-Kisāʾī:
1478 - أبى الذَّمُّ أخلاقَ الكسائي وانْتَحى ... به المجدُ أخلاقَ الأُبُوِّ السَّوابقِ
(Blame refused the character of al-Kisāʾī, and glory directed him to the character of the foremost fathers.)
He wants «الأبوة», plural of «أب» (father), just as «العمومة» is the plural of «عَمّ» (paternal uncle) and «البُنُوَّة» the plural of «ابن» (son); and they have said ibn and bunūw. The Shaykh rejected this from him: the omission is not frequent, and his statement "the tāʾ was omitted from «عُمومة»" is not so; rather the origin is «عُموم» without a tāʾ, then they added the tāʾ to it to emphasise the plural. So what comes on fuʿūl without a tāʾ is the origin, as in ʿumūm and fuḥūl, and what comes with the tāʾ is what needs to be interpreted as a plural; it was not built on this tāʾ so that its omission could be claimed. This is unlike «قُضاة» and its type, which are built on it, so claiming omission in them is possible. As for «أُبُوّة» and «بُنُوّة», they are not two plurals but two verbal nouns. As for «أُبُوّ» in the verse, it is anomalous according to the grammarians, in that it should have been subjected to weakening change and said «أُبِيّ», turning the two wāws into yāʾs, as in ʿuṣiyy.
It is also said «غُزَّاء» with the long vowel, which is anomalous. So «غازٍ» has three broken plurals: ghuzāt like quḍāt, ghuzzā like ṣuwwam, and ghuzzāʾ like ṣuwwām; and a fourth plural, the sound plural. The whole sentence is in the position of an accusative as the object of the saying.
His saying: {لِيَجْعَلَ الله}: There are two views about this lām. One: that it is the lām of «kay» (purpose). The second: that it is the lām of consequence and becoming (ʿāqiba, ṣayrūra). On the first view, to what is this lām attached? There are two aspects. It was said: the implied form is: "He brought about that — that is, the saying or the belief — in order that He make it a regret", or their remorse; so Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be attached to the sentence of prohibition, and that is in two senses depending on what the demonstrative is taken to mean, as will come in his words. As for the first consideration, he said: "He means: do not be like them in uttering that saying and believing it, so that Allah may make it a regret in their hearts especially, and preserve your hearts from it." So he made «ذلك» a reference to the saying and the belief. As for the second consideration, he said: "It is also permissible that «ذلك» refer to what the prohibition indicates, that is: do not be like them, so that Allah may make the absence of your being like them a regret in their hearts, because opposing them in what they say and believe is among the things that grieve and enrage them."
The Shaykh rejected the first sense by the second sense that he himself mentioned, and I must cite it so that it becomes clear to you. After relating from him what I quoted on the first sense, he said: "This is a confused statement with no verification in it, because making the regret does not become the reason for the prohibition, as we said. It only becomes the reason for the obeying of the prohibition taking place, which is the absence of resemblance. The occurrence of that absence and opposition in what they say and believe produces what enrages and grieves them, since (the believers) did not agree with them in what they said and believed, so (they say) 'do not travel and do not go on expeditions'. So al-Zamakhsharī confused the calling for the absence of resemblance with the occurrence of the absence, and understanding this involves subtlety and fineness." End of quotation.
I do not know what makes the speech of Abū l-Qāsim confused, nor how he refuted him, by his own claim, with his own words.
The Shaykh also said: "Ibn ʿĪsā — meaning al-Rummānī — and others said: the lām is attached to the being (kawn), that is: do not be like these so that Allah may make that a regret in their hearts and not in yours. From this al-Zamakhsharī took his statement, except that Ibn ʿĪsā stated explicitly what the lām is attached to, whereas that one (al-Zamakhsharī) did not state it; and we have shown the invalidity of this view." End of quotation. As for his saying "that one did not state it", in fact he did state it, saying: "If you say, what is the attachment of «ليجعل»? I say: «قالوا»…" to the end, "or His saying «لا تكونوا»", and what text is plainer than this? It is not permissible for this lām, whose meaning is giving a cause, to be attached to «قالوا», because the meaning would be corrupt, for they did not say it for that purpose but to dishearten the believers from jihad.
On the second view, I mean its being for consequence, it is attached to «قالوا», and the meaning is: they said that for one of their purposes, so the consequence of their saying and its outcome was regret and remorse, like His saying: {فالتقطه آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوّاً وَحَزَناً} [القصص: 8]: they did not pick him up for that, but his end was that. However, most grammarians did not recognise it as being for becoming, and it is something they ascribe to al-Akhfash, and what has come of that they interpret as the reverse of the speech, as in {فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ} [آل عمران: 21]. This is the view of al-Zamakhsharī, for he likened this lām to the lām in {لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوّاً}, while his position on that one is that it is for cause by the interpretation mentioned. «الجعل» here has the sense of making into (taṣyīr), «حسرةً» is the second object, and «في قلوبهم» may be attached to the making, which is more eloquent, or to an omitted word as an adjective of the indefinite noun before it.
There is disagreement about what «ذلك» refers to: from al-Zajjāj, it is the supposition: they supposed that had they not been present, they would not have been killed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the uttering of the saying and the belief." Close to it is Ibn ʿAṭiyya's statement, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya also allowed that it be for the prohibition and the refraining together. It was also said that it is the verbal noun of «قال», indicated by it.
{والله بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ}: Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «يَعْملون» in the third person, referring back to {الذين كفروا}, and the rest read it in the second person, referring back to His saying {لاَ تَكُونُواْ}, so it is addressed to the believers. Here He brought the attribute of seeing. Al-Rāghib said: "He attached that to seeing, not hearing, although what proceeded from them was a heard saying, not a seen deed, because that saying from the disbeliever was an intention toward some action he was trying to do, so he singled out seeing for that, like your saying to someone who says something while intending an action he is attempting: I see what you are doing."

semin-durr:158-158.t:
Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read {مُتُّم} and {مُتُّ} and the like with ḍamma on the mīm, and Ḥafṣ agreed with them here only, in the two places; the rest read it with kasra. As for the ḍamma: it is because the verb is faʿala with fatḥa on the middle letter, from the hollow verbs with wāw, and everything of that kind, by analogy, when it is attached to the first-person yāʾ (i.e. the tāʾ) and its sisters, takes ḍamma on its first letter: either from the first moment, or by turning the fatḥa into a ḍamma and then moving it to the first letter, with disagreement among the morphologists. So one says for «قام», «قال» and «طال»: qumtu, qumnā, qumna, ṭultu, ṭulna and the like, and for this reason its imperfect came on yafʿulu, such as yamūtu. As for the kasra: the sound view of the people of Arabic is that it is from the dialect of those who say māta yamātu like khāfa yakhāfu, the origin being mawita with kasra on the middle letter like khawifa, so its imperfect came on yafʿalu with fatḥa on the middle letter. The poet said:
1479 - بُنَيَّتي سيدةَ البنات ... عِيشي ولا يُؤْمَنُ أَنْ تَماتي
(My little daughter, lady of girls, live on — though it is not safe that you will not die.)
So its imperfect came on yafʿalu with fatḥa. On this dialect it is necessary that the past verb attached to the tāʾ or one of its sisters be said «مِتُّ» with kasra and nothing else, because we moved the vowel of the wāw to the first letter after stripping it of its own vowel, as an indication of the word's original structure. This is preferable to the statement of those who say that «مِتَّ» with kasra is taken from the dialect of those who say «يَمُوت» with ḍamma in the imperfect, and who made that anomalous by analogy though frequent in use, such as al-Māzinī and Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī; some transmitted it from Sībawayh explicitly. If it is established as a dialect, there is no sense in claiming anomaly in it. As for Ḥafṣ, he combined the two dialects.
The group read «تَجْمَعُون» in the second person, in line with His saying «ولئن قُتِلتم», and Ḥafṣ read it in the third person: either as a return to the disbelievers mentioned earlier, or as an iltifāt (shift of person) from addressing the believers.
These are three places: death precedes being killed in the first of them and in the last, and being killed precedes death in the middle one. That is because the first is for the sake of congruity with what precedes it, His saying {إِذَا ضَرَبُواْ فِي الأرض أَوْ كَانُواْ غُزًّى}, so death goes back to the one who travelled in the land, and being killed to the one who went on an expedition. As for the second, it is a place of urging to jihad, so he put first the more important and better known. As for the last, it is because death is more common.
And his saying: {لإِلَى الله}: the lām is the response of the oath, so it enters upon {تُحْشَرُونَ}, and «إلى الله» is attached to it. It was put first only for exclusivity, that is: to Allah, not to another, will be your gathering; or for emphasis of concern, and its being a verse-ending made it good. Were it not for the separation, it would be obligatory to emphasise the verb with a nūn, because the affirmative imperfect, when it is future, must be emphasised along with the lām, contrary to the Kufans, who allow either of the two in place of the other, as in his saying:
1480 - وقتيلِ مُرَّةَ أَثْأَرَنَّ فإنه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And the slain of Murra, I will surely avenge him, for he… [the rest of the verse is elided in the source])
where he brought the nūn without the lām; and his saying:
1481 - لِئَنْ تكُ قد ضَاقَتْ عليكم بيوتُكم ... لَيَعْلَمُ ربي أنَّ بيتيَ واسِعُ
(If your houses have become narrow for you, my Lord surely knows that my house is spacious.)
where he brought the lām without the nūn. The Basrans make it a poetic necessity. If a separation is made between it and the lām by the governed word, as in this verse, or by «قد», as in "By Allah, I do indeed stand", and his saying:
1482 - كَذَبْتِ لقد أُصْبي على المَرْء عِرْسَه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(You lie! I do indeed lure a man's wife from him… [the rest of the verse is elided in the source])
or by a particle of futurity such as {وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ} [الضحى: 4], then it is not permissible to emphasise it with the nūn. Al-Fārisī said: "The nūn entered to distinguish the lām of oath from the lām of inception; and the lām of inception does not enter upon a superfluous element (faḍla), so by the entry of the lām of oath upon a superfluous element the distinction is achieved and there is no need of the nūn; and by its entry upon «سوف» the distinction is also achieved, so there is no need of the nūn. The lām of inception does not enter upon a verb unless it is present-tense, but as for future, no."

semin-durr:93-93.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {حِلاًّ}: الحِلّ has the meaning of الحلال (the lawful), and originally it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of حَلَّ يَحِلُّ, like your saying: عَزَّ يَعِزُّ عِزّاً; then it is applied to persons for emphasis, and for that reason the singular, dual, plural, masculine and feminine are alike in it, as in His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ هُنَّ حِلٌّ لَّهُمْ} [الممتحنة: 10]. In the ḥadīth from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "كنت أُطَيِّبُه صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لحِلّه ولحَرَمِه" (I used to perfume him ﷺ for his being out of iḥrām and for his being in iḥrām), that is, for his becoming lawful and for his entering iḥrām. It is like الحِرْم and اللِّبْس, meaning الحَرام and اللباس. The Exalted said: «وحِرْمٌ», and «وحرام» was read. And «لبني» is attached to حِلّ.
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا حَرَّمَ} is an excepted element from the ism (noun) of كان. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed that it be excepted from a latent pronoun in «حِلاً», saying: "because it is an exception from the ism of كان, and the operator in it is «كان»; and it is permissible that «حِلاً» operate in it and that there be a pronoun in it from which the exception is made; because حِلاً and حَلالاً stand in the place of an active participle meaning permissible and allowed."
There are two views on this exception. One: that it is connected, the implied form being: except what Isrāʾīl (Jacob) forbade himself, which was then forbidden to them in the Torah; so there is not in it what they added of prohibitions, claiming that to be sound. The second: that it is disconnected, the implied form being: but Isrāʾīl forbade it to himself specifically and did not forbid it to them; and the first is the sound one.
His saying: {مِن قَبْلِ أَن تُنَزَّلَ}: two views on it. One: that it is attached to حَرّم, that is: except what he forbade before; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "That is remote, since it is informing of the obvious, for it is known that what Isrāʾīl forbade himself was before the sending down of the Torah, necessarily, because of the great distance between the existence of Isrāʾīl and the sending down of the Torah." The second: that it is attached to His saying «كان حِلاً». The Shaykh said: "It appears that it is attached to His saying {كَانَ حِلاًّ لبني إِسْرَائِيلَ}, that is: before the Torah was sent down, and the exception intervenes, since that is a permissible separation. That is according to the school of al-Kisāʾī and Abū l-Ḥasan, in permitting what precedes «إلا» to operate in what follows it if it is an adverbial, a genitive noun, or a ḥāl (circumstantial), for example: «ما حُبِس إلا زيدٌ عندَكَ، وما أوى إلا عمروٌ إليك، وما جاء إلا زيدٌ ضاحكاً». Al-Kisāʾī permitted that for an accusative absolutely, for example: ما ضَرَب إلا زيدٌ عمراً; and he and Ibn al-Anbārī permitted that for a nominative, for example: ما ضَرَب إلا زيداً عمرو. As for explaining it on other than the school of al-Kisāʾī and Abū l-Ḥasan, an operator of the same kind as what precedes it is implied for it, and its implied form here is: حَلَّ من قبلِ أَنْ تُنَزَّل التوراة (it was lawful before the Torah was sent down)."

semin-durr:86-86.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَيْفَ يَهْدِي} is like His saying: {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [البقرة: 28]. It was said that the interrogative here means negation, and he recited:
1351 - كيفَ نومي على الفراشِ وَلمَّا ... تَشْمَلِ الشامَ غارةٌ شَعْواءُ
(How can I sleep on my bed, when a widespread raid has not yet engulfed al-Shām?)
And the saying of another:
1352 - فهذي سيوفٌ يا صُدَّيُّ بنُ مالكٍ ... كثيرٌ ولكن كيف بالسيفِ ضارِبُ
(These are swords, O Ṣuddayy ibn Mālik, many; but how is it with the swordsman who strikes?)
His saying: {وشهدوا}: in this clause there are three views. First: that it is conjoined to «كفروا», and «كفروا» is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «قوماً», that is: how can He guide one who combined these two things? Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Ḥawfī and Abū l-Baqāʾ held this, except that Makkī rejected this view, saying: "It is not permissible to conjoin «شهدوا» to «كفروا», because of the corruption of the meaning." He did not make clear the aspect of the corruption; it is as though he understood an order between disbelief and the testimony, and so the meaning is corrupted. But this is not necessary, for the wāw does not require order; therefore Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The meaning is understood, that the testimony was before the disbelief, and the wāw does not give order."
Second: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw of «كفروا», the operator in it being the one that governs its owner, and «قد» being implied with it according to one opinion, that is: "they disbelieved when they had (qad qad) testified". A group held this, such as al-Zamakhsharī, Abū l-Baqāʾ and others. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is not permissible that the operator be «يَهْدي», because He guides one who has testified that the Messenger is true"; he means that it cannot be a ḥāl from «قوماً» with «يَهْدِي» as the operator in the ḥāl, because of the corruption of meaning he mentioned. [Translator's note: the source prints «وقد وقد» with «قد» doubled; translated as written.]
Third: that it is conjoined to «إيمانهم» because of the dissolution into a verbal clause that it contains, the implied form being: "after they believed and testified". A group held this. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be conjoined to the verbal meaning in «إيمانهم», because its meaning is: after they believed, as in His saying, the Exalted: {فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن} [المنافقون: 10], and his saying:
1353 - مشائيمُ ليسوا مُصْلِحين عشيرةً ... ولا ناعبٍ إلا بِبَيْنٍ غرابُها
(Ill-omened men, not reformers of a clan, nor a croaker whose raven croaks anything but separation.)"
End of quotation. The point of his comparing that to the verse and to the line is the supposition of the existence of something that would make the conjunction onto it in the sentence allowable. Thus the grammarians say: it was put in the jussive by supposition (tawahhum), that is, because of the dropping of the فاء, for had it been dropped it would have been jussive in the response to an exhortation; and so they say: he supposed the existence of the bāʾ and so put it in the genitive. In this wording, with respect to the Quran, there is a lack of courtesy, but they did not intend that, Allah forbid. Al-Zamakhsharī's comparison with something other than that would have been better, such as His saying: {إِنَّ المصدقين والمصدقات وَأَقْرَضُواْ} [الحديد: 18], since it is equivalent to: "those who gave charity and lent"; and in this verse there is a discussion which will come to you, if Allah the Exalted wills.
Al-Wāḥidī said: "The verb is conjoined to the maṣdar (verbal noun), because by the maṣdar he intended the verb, its implied form being: they disbelieved in Allah after they had believed; so it is a conjunction on the meaning, as he said:
1354 - لَلُبْسُ عباءةٍ وتَقَرَّ عيني ... أَحَبُّ إليَّ مِنْ لُبْسِ الشفوفِ
(To wear a cloak and for my eye to be cooled is dearer to me than wearing fine garments.)
its meaning is: لأِنْ ألبس وتقرَّ عيني (that I wear, and that my eye be cooled)." The apparent sense of the wording of al-Zamakhsharī and al-Wāḥidī is that the first is interpreted for the sake of the second, and this is not apparent, because we need that only when the place requires a verb, as in {إِنَّ المصدقين}, since the relative requires a verbal clause, so we needed to interpret the active participle as a verb and conjoin «وأقرضوا» to it. But as for «بعد إيمانهم» and his saying «للبس عباءة», the place of the noun does not need a verb. What is fitting is that we interpret the second as a noun so that its conjunction onto the explicit noun before it is sound, and its interpretation is that we bring with it the maṣdar particle «أن» implied, its implied form being: بعد إيمانهم وأَنْ شَهِدوا, that is, "and their testifying". For this reason the grammarians interpreted her saying «لَلُبْسُ عباءةٍ وتقرَّ» as «وأَنْ تقرَّ», since the implied form is: "and the cooling of my eye". Abū l-Baqāʾ held what I have mentioned, saying: "The implied form is: بعد أَنْ آمنوا وأن شهدوا, so it is in the position of genitive."
End. He means that it rests on interpreting a maṣdar conjoined to the explicit maṣdar that is made genitive by the adverbial. The words of al-Jurjānī on it bear witness to this and also bear witness to al-Zamakhsharī's implied form, for he said: His saying «وشَهِدوا» is joined on what is possible in the implied sense, in that His saying «بعد إيمانهم» may be "after «أن آمنوا»", and the light «أَنْ» with the verb is in the place of the maṣdar, as in His saying: {وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ} [البقرة: 184], that is: "and fasting". Like it, among what was construed on the meaning, is His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُكَلِّمَهُ الله إِلاَّ وَحْياً أَوْ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ} [الشورى: 51], for it is conjoined to His saying {إِلاَّ وَحْياً}, and it is possible in it: "except that revelation be made to him"; so since His saying {إِلاَّ وَحْياً} means "except that revelation be made to him", he construed it on that. Like it in poetry is the saying:
1355 - فَظَلَّ طُهاةٌ اللحم من بين مُنْضِجٍ ... صَفيفَ شِواءٍ أو قديرٍ مُعَجَّلٍ
(The meat-cooks spent the day, among them one roasting strips of grilled meat, or a quick-cooked stew.)
He put «قدير» in the genitive because it is conjoined to what is possible in His saying «منضجٍ», because it is possible that it be annexed to the «صفيف», so he construed it on that. I say: his bringing this line is like al-Zamakhsharī's bringing the noble verse and the preceding line, because he put «قدير» in the genitive here by supposition, as though he supposed the annexation of the active participle to its object for lightness and so put it in the genitive by supposition, just as the other supposed the existence of the bāʾ in «ليسوا مصلحين», because it is often added in the khabar of ليس. And His saying: {أَنَّ الرسول}: the majority hold that it is an adjective meaning «المُرْسَل» (the one sent); and it was said that it means "the message", so it would be a maṣdar; that has already preceded.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {قُلْ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُمْ}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read the first hamza with taḥqīq (full pronunciation) and the second with tashīl (easing) between the two (bayna bayna), according to what is known of their principles at the beginning of al-Baqara; the rest read both lightly (i.e. both as full hamzas, without easing). Qālūn from Nāfiʿ inserted a lengthening between these two hamzas without disagreement; Abū ʿAmr, and Hishām from Ibn ʿĀmir, with disagreement about them; the rest without lengthening, each according to his principles of taḥqīq and tashīl; and Warsh according to his principle of transferring the vowel of the hamza to the lām of {قل}.

Know that it is necessary to mention the differences of the readers over this word and its like and to verify their positions, for it is a place hard to pin down. So I say, with the help of Allah the Exalted: what occurs of this in the Noble Qur'an is in three places, I mean two hamzas in one word, the first with fatḥa and the second with ḍamma: the first is this place; the second is in Ṣād: {أَأُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذكر مِن بَيْنِنَا} [Ṣād: 8]; the third is in al-Qamar: {أَأُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ} [al-Qamar: 25]. The readers have five grades in them. The first: the grade of Qālūn, which is easing the second hamza between the two, and inserting an alif between the two hamzas, without disagreement; so it was narrated from Nāfiʿ. The second: the grade of Warsh and Ibn Kathīr, which is also easing the second between the two without inserting an alif between the two hamzas, without disagreement; so Warsh narrated from Nāfiʿ. The third: the grade of the Kufans and Ibn Dhakwān from Ibn ʿĀmir, which is full pronunciation of the second without inserting an alif, without disagreement; so Ibn Dhakwān narrated from Ibn ʿĀmir. The fourth: the grade of Hishām, narrated from him in three ways: the first, full pronunciation and no alif between the two hamzas in the three sūras; the second, full pronunciation and an alif between them in the three sūras; the third, distinguishing between the three sūras, namely that he pronounces fully and shortens in this sūra, and eases and lengthens in the other two sūras. The fifth: the grade of Abū ʿAmr, which is easing the second, with the insertion of the alif and without it. I have dispensed with the explanation of lightening, lengthening and shortening, ascribing each of them to the dialect of those who spoke it, because of what I presented at the beginning of al-Baqara, and praise be to Allah.

Abū l-Baqāʾ reported that it was read: "a-wunabbiʾukum" with a pure wāw after the hamza because of its ḍamma, and that is not the sound way. In His saying «أؤنبئكم» there is an iltifāt (shift of address) from the third person in His saying «للناس» to the second person, as an honour to them.

His saying: {بِخَيْرٍ}: attached to the verb. This verb, since it is not made to include the meaning of "ʾaʿlama" (to inform), takes two objects: the first it reaches by itself and the second by the preposition; had it included its meaning, it would have taken three.

And {مِّن ذلكم} is attached to khayr, because it is in its usual sense of being an elative (afʿal tafḍīl); and the pointing with "dhalikum" is to what preceded of the mention of the desires, and the justification of pointing with a singular to a plural has preceded. It is not permissible that khayr be not an elative, the meaning being "a good from among goods", with {مِنْ} an adjective to the word khayr. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "{مِنْ} is in the position of accusative, attached to khayr, the implied form being: 'with what exceeds that'; and it cannot be an adjective of khayr, because that would require that Paradise and what is in it, which they longed for, be a part of what they renounced of wealth and the like." The Shaykh followed him in that.

His saying: {لِلَّذِينَ اتقوا}: four views are permissible for it. The first: that it is attached to khayr, and the speech is complete here, and {جنات} is nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "it is gardens", that is: that which is better than what preceded is gardens; and the clause is an explanation and elucidation of the superiority, like it: {قُلْ أَفَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذلكم} then He said: {النار وَعَدَهَا الله الذين كَفَرُواْ} [al-Ḥajj: 73]. This is supported by the reading of «جنات» with kasra on the tāʾ, as a badal (substitute) for «بخير», so it is an explanation of the good. The second: that the prepositional phrase is a fronted khabar and {جنات} a delayed mubtadaʾ, or that {جنات} is the agent of the preposition before it, even if it does not rely on anything, according to one who holds that. According to these two assumptions the speech is complete at His saying «من ذلكم», then this clause begins, and it too is an explanation and elucidation of the superiority.

As for the other two views, Makkī mentioned them with the genitive of «جنات», meaning that he did not permit the two views except if you put «جنات» in the genitive as a badal of «بخير». The first view: that it is attached to «أؤنبئكم». The second view: that it is an adjective of khayr. His text must be quoted, for it contains a difficulty.

He, may Allah have mercy on him, said, after mentioning that «للذين» is a fronted khabar and «جناتٌ» a mubtadaʾ: "The genitive is permissible in «جنات» as a badal of «بخير», on the basis that you make the lām in «للذين» attached to «أؤنبئكم», or you make it an adjective of khayr; but if you were to make the lām attached to an omitted word that it stands in for, the genitive of «جنات» would not be permissible; because prepositions and adverbs, when attached to an omitted word and standing in its place, come to contain a latent nominative pronoun and need a mubtadaʾ to which that pronoun refers, as in your saying 'For Zayd is wealth, in the house is a man, and behind you is ʿAmr'. So «جنات» must be nominative if the lām is attached to an omitted word; and if it were attached to an omitted word without a pronoun in it, you would make «جنات» nominative as the agent of its verb, and this is the position of al-Akhfash in making what follows adverbs and prepositions nominative by the "settling" (istiqrār); and that is good, according to the skilled grammarians, only when the adverbs or prepositions are adjectives of what precedes them, for then it is possible and good to make the noun nominative by the istiqrār, as we have explained and shown with examples, and likewise when they are circumstantial phrases [from what precedes them]." End of quotation. So he allowed this lām to be attached to «أونبئكم» or to an omitted word as an adjective of khayr, on condition that «جنات» be put in the genitive as badal of «بخير»; and his apparent meaning is that this is not permissible with the nominative of «جنات», and he justified it by saying that prepositions are attached to an omitted word and carry the pronoun, so a mubtadaʾ must be brought for it, and that is «جنات». But what he said from this angle is not necessary, since one may say: "I allow the attachment of the lām to what I mentioned in the two ways with the nominative of «جنات» as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, not as a mubtadaʾ, so that what I mentioned would not be necessary."

But the two views are weak from another side: namely that the meaning is not clear on what he mentioned; although making the lām an adjective of khayr is stronger than making it attached to «أؤنبئكم», since there is no meaning in that. As for his saying about adverbs and prepositions, that according to the skilled they make the agent nominative only when they are adjectives, and his saying "and likewise when they are circumstantial phrases", there is a shortcoming in it, because this ruling holds for them in several places, among them the two places he mentioned. The third: that they occur as a ṣila (relative clause). The fourth: that they occur as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ. The fifth: that they rely on a negation. The sixth: that they rely on an interrogative. The verification of this has preceded, and I have repeated it only because of its distance in time.

His saying: {عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ}: it has four views. The first: that it is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جنات», because it was originally an adjective of it, and when it was fronted it became accusative as a ḥāl. The second: that it is attached to what «للذين» is attached to, namely the istiqrār, if we make it a khabar or the one that makes «جنات» nominative as agent; but if you attach it to khayr or to «أؤنبئكم», then not, because it does not include the istiqrār. The third: that it is governed by «تجري», and the meaning does not support this. The fourth: that it is attached to khayr, as «للذين» is attached to it according to a view that has preceded. It is weak that the speech be complete at His saying «للذين اتقوا» and then begin with His saying {عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتٌ} as mubtadaʾ and khabar, the clause being an explanation and elucidation of the superiority, as preceded elsewhere.

Yaʿqūb read «جنات» with kasra on the tāʾ, and it has three views. The first: that it is a badal of the word «خير», so it is genitive, and it is an explanation of it, as preceded. The second: that it is a badal of the position of «بخير», and its position is accusative, which in meaning is like the first. The third: that it is accusative by an implied "I mean" (أعني), parallel to the view that goes to its being nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ.

His saying: {تَجْرِي}: an adjective of «جنات», so it is in the position of nominative, accusative or genitive, according to the two readings and the analyses of both. And {مِن تَحْتِهَا} is attached to «تجري»; Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be attached to an omitted word, as a ḥāl from «الأنهار». He said: "that is: the rivers flow while being beneath them." This resembles preparing the governor to act on something and then cutting it off from it.

His saying: {خَالِدِينَ}: an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), whose owner is the latent pronoun in «للذين», and the governor in it then is the implied istiqrār. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "if you wish, from the hāʾ in «تحتها»." What he mentioned is only workable on the position of the Kufans, because making it a ḥāl from the "hā" in «تحتها» leads to an adjective running on other than the one it belongs to in meaning, since eternity is among the attributes of those entering Paradise, not of Paradise; and therefore this ḥāl was pluralized in the plural of rational beings; so a detached nominative pronoun, which was latent in the adjective, ought to have been brought, as in "Zayd is Hind's striker, he". The Kufans say: if confusion is not feared, as here, the appearance of the pronoun is not obligatory, otherwise it is obligatory; the Basrans do not distinguish. The discussion of that has preceded.

His saying: {وَأَزْوَاجٌ مُّطَهَّرَةٌ وَرِضْوَانٌ}: for one who makes «جنات» nominative, as is well known, conjoining «أزواج» and «رضوان» is easy. As for one who puts the tāʾ in kasra, on his reading they must be nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is implied, its implied form being: "and for them are spouses, and for them is good pleasure". The discussion of {أَزْوَاجٌ مُّطَهَّرَةٌ} has preceded in [al-Baqara: 25].

In «رضوان» there are two dialects: ḍamma on the rāʾ, which is the dialect of Tamīm, and kasra, which is the dialect of the Hijaz, and the majority read with it, except Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, who read with the dialect of Tamīm throughout the Qur'an, except in the second occurrence in Sūrat al-Māʾida, which is {مَنِ اتبع رِضْوَانَهُ} [verse 16]: some narrated from him the certainty of its kasra, and some narrated from him disagreement about it specifically.

Are the two of one meaning, or is there a difference between them? Two views. The first: that they are two maṣdars of one meaning from raḍiya yarḍā. The second: that the one with kasra is a noun, and from it comes Riḍwān, the keeper of Paradise, may Allah bless our Prophet and His prophets and His angels, while the one with ḍamma is the maṣdar. And {مِن الله} is an adjective of «رضوان».

semin-durr:136-136.t: His saying, the Exalted: {مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ}: in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of «مغفرة», and «مِنْ» is partitive, i.e. "from among the forgivenesses of their Lord". His saying {خَالِدِينَ}: a ḥāl from the pronoun in «جزاؤهم», because it is a mafʿūl bihi in meaning, for the meaning is: "Allah recompenses them with gardens while they abide eternally", and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). It cannot be a ḥāl from «جنات» in the wording while belonging in meaning to its inhabitants, for were that so, the pronoun would be made explicit, since the attribute would be running on someone other than the one it belongs to. The sentence {تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الأنهار} is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of «جنات». The i'rab of the like of this sentence has already been given. The one specified for praise is omitted in his saying {وَنِعْمَ أَجْرُ العاملين}, its estimate being: "and excellent is the reward of the workers: the Garden".

semin-durr:137-137.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِن قَبْلِكُمْ}: it may be attached to «خَلَتْ», and it may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «سنن», because originally it could be an adjective, and when it was put first it became accusative as a ḥāl.

And al-sunan is the plural of «سُنَّة», which is the way that a person follows and keeps to; from it comes "the sunna of the prophets", peace be upon them. Khālid al-Hudhalī said to his maternal uncle Abū Dhuʾayb:

1433 - فلا تَجْزَعَنْ مِنْ سُنَّةٍ أنت سِرْتَها ... فَأَوَّلُ راضٍ سُنَّةً مَنْ يَسيرُها
(So do not be distressed at a custom you yourself set; the first to be content with a custom is the one who sets it.)

And another said:

1434 - وإنَّ الأُلَى بالطَّفِّ مِنْ آلِ هاشمٍ ... تَأَسَّوا فَسَنُّوا للكرامِ التآسِيا
(Those at al-Ṭaff of the family of Hāshim followed one another's example, and so set for the noble the custom of mutual emulation.)

And Labīd said:

1435 - مِنْ أمةٍ سَنَّتْ لهم آباؤُهم ... ولكلِّ قومٍ سُنَّةٌ وإمامُها
(From a community whose forefathers set a custom for them; every people has a custom and its leader.)

And al-Mufaḍḍal said: "al-sunna is the nation (al-umma)", and he recited:

1436 - ما عايَنَ الناسُ مِنْ فضلٍ كفضلكمُ ... ولا رُئِيْ مثلُه في سائِرِ السُّنَنِ
(People have not witnessed any excellence like your excellence, nor was its like seen among all the sunan.)

But there is no proof in it, because it admits another reading. Al-Khalīl said: "sanna al-shayʾa means he shaped it", and from it: {مِّنْ حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ} [al-Ḥijr: 26], i.e. shaped. It is also said: sanna al-māʾa wa-l-dirʿa, when he poured them out; and his saying {مِّنْ حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ} could be from this, but attributing pouring to clay is remote. It is also said that «مَسْنون» means altered. Some of the people of the language said: "It (sunna) is a fuʿla from sanna al-māʾa yasunnuhu, when he poured it continuously. And al-sann is the pouring of water, sweat and the like", and he recited the verse of Zuhayr:

1437 - نُعَوِّدها الطِّرادَ فكلَّ يومٍ ... تُسَنُّ على سنابِكها القُرونُ
(We accustom them to the chase, and every day the sweat [or: the foreheads] is poured over their hooves.)

i.e. sweat is poured upon them. It is also said: sunna is a fuʿla in the sense of a passive participle, like ghurfa and ukla. It is also said that its derivation is from sananta al-naṣl asunnuhu sannan, when you sharpened it, the meaning being that the good path is taken care of as a blade and the like is taken care of. It is also said: from sanna al-ibil, when he pastured them well; the meaning being that the follower of the sunna looks after his companions as the shepherd looks after his camels. A good amount of this has already passed in al-Baqara.

And his saying {فَسِيرُواْ}: a sentence conjoined to what precedes it. The causal connection (tasbīb) in these wordings is evident, i.e. the reason for the command to travel, that they may look with a look of reflection, is the passing away of the nations before you and their ways. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The fāʾ entered «فسيروا» because the meaning is conditional, i.e. 'if you doubt, then travel'."

His saying: {كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ}: «كيف» is a fronted khabar whose fronting is obligatory, because it contains the meaning of interrogation, and it suspends (muʿalliq) «انظروا» before it; the sentence is in the position of the accusative after the dropping of the preposition, since the origin is "look into such and such".

semin-durr:138-138.t: His saying, the Exalted: {لِّلنَّاسِ}: it may be attached to the maṣdar before it, and it may be attached to an omitted element as a description of it. His saying: {لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ}: it may also be a description, and it may be attached to what precedes it. It admits being a case of tanāzuʿ (competition of governors), on the basis of applying the second governor, with omission from the first.

semin-durr:139-139.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تَهِنُوا}: the origin is «تَوْهِنُوا», and the واو was dropped because it fell between a ياء and a kasra in the origin; then the letters of the imperfect were made to follow the same course in that. One says wahana with fatḥa in the past, yahinu with kasra in the imperfect. It is also reported that one says wahuna and wahina, with ḍamma and kasra on the hāʾ in the past. And wahana is used both intransitively and transitively: you say wahana Zaydun, i.e. he became weak; the Exalted said {وَهَنَ العظم مِنِّي} [Maryam: 4]; and wahantuhu, i.e. I weakened him. From it is the ḥadīth: "The fever of Yathrib weakened them (wahanat-hum)." The maṣdar is al-wahan and al-wahn, with fatḥa on the ʿayn and with sukūn. Zuhayr said:

1438 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فأصبحَ الحبلُ مِنْها واهِناً خَلَقَا
(... and the rope between them became frayed and worn.)

i.e. weak.

His saying: {وَأَنْتُمُ الأَعْلَوْنَ}: a ḥāl sentence from the fāʿil of «تَهِنوا» or «تحزنوا»; a resumptive status in it is not evident. And al-aʿlawn is the plural of aʿlā, the origin being aʿlayūn: the yāʾ took a vowel while what precedes it had fatḥa, so it was turned into alif, which was then dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents, and the fatḥa remained to indicate it. If you wish you may say: the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy and dropped, so two quiescents met as well, the yāʾ and the wāw, and the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents. We needed this only because the wāw of the plural is preceded only by a letter with ḍamma, in wording or in estimate, and this is an example of the estimate. His saying: {إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُّؤْمِنِينَ}: its apodosis is omitted, i.e. "so do not weaken and do not grieve".

semin-durr:106-106.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ}: concerning what governs this adverbial there are several aspects. First: that it is the "being established" implied by «لهم», the implied form being: "and those, for them is established a punishment on the day when faces turn white." It is also said: the governing element is an implied one indicated by the preceding sentence, its implied form being "they will be punished on the day when faces turn white." It is also said: the governing element is «عظيم»; this is weakened on the ground that it would require restricting its greatness to this day. This weakening is itself weak, because if it is great on this day, then on other days it is all the more so; and besides, the matter is left unmentioned for the days other than this one. It is also said: the governing element is «عذاب». This is impossible, because a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has been qualified by an adjective does not govern after being qualified.

Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb, Abū Nuhayk and Abū Razīn al-ʿUqaylī read «تِبْيَضُّ وتِسْوَدُّ» with kasra on the tāʾ, which is the dialect of Tamīm. al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū l-Jawzāʾ read «تَبياضُّ وتَسوادُّ» with an alif in both, which is more emphatic, since «ابياضَّ» indicates the thing's being characterised by whiteness more than «ابيضَّ» does. Kasra of the imperfect prefix is also possible with / the alif, except that I do not transmit it as a reading of anyone.

His saying: {أَكْفَرْتُمْ}: this sentence is in the position of accusative by an implied "saying", and that implied "saying", together with an implied fāʾ as well, is the jawāb of «أمّا» (apodosis). Omission of the fāʾ with the "saying" is regular, since "saying" is often implied, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَالمَلاَئِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن كُلِّ بَابٍ سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُم} [al-Raʿd: 23-24]; {والذين اتخذوا مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ إِلاَّ لِيُقَرِّبُونَآ} [al-Zumar: 3]; {وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ القواعد مِنَ البيت وَإِسْمَاعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّآ} [al-Baqara: 127]. As for omitting it without implying the "saying", it is not permitted except in necessity, as in his saying:
1378 - فأمَّا القتالُ لا قِتالَ لديكُمُ ... ولكنَّ سيراً في عِراضِ المواكبِ
(As for fighting, you have no fighting; but only riding along in the processions' flanks.)
that is: «فلا قتالَ».

The author of Asrār al-Tanzīl said: "Indeed an objection has been raised against the grammarians in their saying that when 'it is said' is omitted, the fāʾ is omitted, by His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَمَّا الذين كفروا أَفَلَمْ تَكُنْ آيَاتِي تتلى عَلَيْكُمْ} [al-Jāthiya: 31], where 'it is said' was omitted and the fāʾ was not omitted. When this is invalid, it follows that the apodosis is in His saying {فَذُوقُواْ العذاب بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ}, which then serves as the apodosis for it and for His saying {أَكَفَرْتُم}. It is part of the Arabs' composition that, when they mention a particle requiring an apodosis, they refrain from giving its apodosis until they mention another particle requiring an apodosis, and then give them one single apodosis, as in His saying, the Exalted: {فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ} [al-Baqara: 38], where His saying {فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ} is the apodosis of both conditions together. And «أفلم» is not the apodosis of «أمَّا»; rather the fāʾ is a conjunction upon an implied element, the implied form being: Did I neglect you, so that I did not recite My signs to you?"

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is the speech of a littérateur, not of a grammarian. As for his saying 'an objection has been raised against the grammarians', it suffices to invalidate this objection that it is an objection against all the grammarians, since there is no grammarian who does not explain the verse by an implied element, so that it is said to them: 'Did you disbelieve?' They said: this is the import of the address (faḥwā l-khiṭāb), namely that there is in the speech something implied which the meaning cannot do without; to say otherwise opposes the consensus, so it is not to be heeded.

As for his objection from {وَأَمَّا الذين كفروا أَفَلَمْ تَكُنْ آيَاتِي}, that they implied 'it is said to them: Were My signs not…', so 'it is said' was omitted and the fāʾ not omitted, which shows the invalidity of this implication: it is not sound. Rather, this fāʾ after the hamza in «أفلم» is not the fāʾ of 'fa-yuqālu' which is the apodosis of «أمَّا», such that one could say 'yuqālu' was omitted and the fāʾ remained; rather, the fāʾ that is the apodosis of «أمّا» has 'yuqālu' omitted after it, and the fāʾ of «أفلم» admits two aspects. One: that it is redundant (zāʾida); and the grammarians have recited, as evidence for the redundancy of the fāʾ, the poet's saying:
1379 - يموتُ أُناسُ أو يَشيبُ فتاهُمُ ... ويَحْدُثُ ناسٌ والصغيرُ فكيبُرُ
(Some people die, or their youth grows grey; others come into being, and the small one grows up.)
that is: «والصغيرُ يَكْبُرُ»; and the saying of another:
1380 - لَمَّا اتَّقى بيدٍ عظيمٍ جِرْمُها ... فَتركْتُ ضاحِي كَفِّه يَتَذَبْذَبُ
(When he shielded himself with a hand of great bulk, I left the exposed part of his palm dangling.)
that is: «تركت»; and Zuhayr said:
1381 - أراني إذا ما بِتُّ بِتُّ على هوى ... فَثُمَّ إذا أَمْسَيْتُ أَمْسَيْتُ غادِيا
(I find that when I spend the night, I spend it in desire; then when evening comes, I am headed out at morn.)
he means: «ثم إذا». al-Akhfash said: "They claim that they say «أخوك فوجَد», meaning «أخوك وجَدَ»." The second aspect: that the fāʾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), the implied form being "so it is said to them what grieves them: Were My signs not…". Then care was given to the interrogative particle, so it was put before the explicative fāʾ, just as it is put before the fāʾ of sequence in His saying {أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُواْ فِي الأرض} [Yūsuf: 109]. This is according to the view of those who affirm that the fāʾ can be explicative, as in «توضَّأ زيدٌ فَغَسَل وجهَه ويديه إلى آخر أفعالِ الوضوء» ("Zayd made ablution: he washed his face and his hands, up to the last of the acts of ablution"); the fāʾ here does not signal sequence but explains the ablution. Likewise in {أَفَلَمْ تَكُنْ آيَاتِي تتلى عَلَيْكُمْ} it explains the saying that grieves them.

"As for this man's saying 'when this was invalid, it followed that the apodosis is: فذوقوا', meaning the invalidity of omitting what the grammarians implied, 'fa-yuqālu lahum', because of the presence of this fāʾ in «أفلم تكن»: we have shown that this implication is not invalid and that it is the same in both verses; and if so, the apodosis of «أمَّا» is 'fa-yuqālu' in both places, and the meaning of the speech follows from it. As for his implication 'Did I neglect you, so that My signs were not recited?', this is a Zamakhsharian innovation. For al-Zamakhsharī implies, between the interrogative hamza and the fāʾ, a verb upon which what comes after can be conjoined, and he does not hold that the fāʾ, wāw and thumma, when the hamza enters them, originally come before the hamza, but that care was given to the interrogative so it was put before the conjunction, as Sībawayh and other grammarians held. Al-Zamakhsharī later returned to the school of the majority / in this, and the invalidity of his first view is stated in the books of grammar, and the report of the majority's view was given earlier in this book. And even granting this man's implication of 'Did I neglect you', one must still imply the 'saying', its implied form being 'it is said: Did I neglect you?', because this implied element is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the fāʾ is the apodosis of «أمَّا», and this is what the speech indicates and necessarily requires. As for this man's saying 'so that came as the apodosis for it and for His saying: أكفرتم', meaning that «فذوقوا العذاب» is the apodosis of «أمَّا» and of «أكفرتم»: the interrogative here has no apodosis; it is an interrogative by way of rebuke and degradation of them.

"As for this man's saying 'It is part of the Arabs' composition…' to its end, the speech of the Arabs is not as he claims; rather every [particle] is given an apodosis, which if not apparent is implied, and they do not give the two a single apodosis. As for his claim to that in His saying, the Exalted, {فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدًى} (the verse), and his claim that {فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ} is an apodosis for the two conditions, that is a saying related from al-Kisāʾī; some people claimed that the apodosis of the first condition is omitted, its implied form being 'follow it'; and the sound view is that the second condition and its apodosis are the apodosis of the first condition. These three views were given earlier at His saying, the Exalted: {فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدًى}." End of his words.

His saying: {أَكْفَرْتُمْ}: the hamza is for denunciation of them, rebuke and expression of astonishment at their state. In His saying {أَكْفَرْتُمْ} there is a kind of iltifāt (shift of address), which the scholars of rhetoric call talwīn al-khiṭāb (variation of address): His saying {فَأَمَّا الذين اسودت وُجُوهُهُمْ} is in the rule of the third person, and His saying after it, {أَكْفَرْتُمْ}, is direct second-person address.

semin-durr:107-107.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَفِي رَحْمَةِ الله}: there are two aspects. One: that the prepositional phrase is attached to «خالدون», and «فيها» is a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) of the preposition; the implied form is: "so they are abiding in the mercy of Allah, in it." It has been established that a particle is not given verbal emphasis except by repeating what it governs or by repeating its pronoun, as in this verse; it may not be repeated alone except in necessity, as in his saying:
1382 - حَتَّى [تراها] وكأنَّ وكأنْ ... أعناقَها مُشَدَّدَاتٌ بِقَرَنْ
(Until you see them, as if, as if, their necks were bound with a rope.)
Thus they recite this verse; and more explicit in this chapter is:
1383 - فلا واللهِ لا يُلْفَى لِما بي ... ولا لَلِما بهمْ أبداً دواءُ
(By Allah, no remedy will ever be found for what afflicts me, nor for what afflicts them.)
And that is fine when their wording differs, as in his saying:
1384 - فَأَصْبَحْنَ لاَ يَسْأَلْنَنِي عن بما به ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And they ceased asking me about what is in him …) [Translator's note: the rest of the verse is elided in the source.]
Unless that particle stands in place of a whole sentence, in which case it is repeated alone, like the particles of response such as naʿam naʿam, balā balā and lā lā.

The second: that His saying {فَفِي رَحْمَةِ} is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, and the whole sentence is the apodosis of «أمَّا», the implied form being: "so they are established in the mercy of Allah"; and the sentence after it, {هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ}, is an independent sentence of mubtadaʾ and khabar indicating that the establishment in the mercy is by way of eternal abiding; so it has no connection with the preceding sentence in terms of i'rab.

al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the position of His saying {هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ} after His saying {فَفِي رَحْمَةِ الله}? I say: the position of resumption, as if it were said: how will they be in it? So it was said: they are abiding in it, not departing from it and not dying."

Abū l-Jawzāʾ and Ibn Yaʿmur read «اسوادَّتْ وابياضَّتْ» with alif, and it was mentioned earlier that their reading was «تَبياضُّ وتَسْوَادُّ», and this is its analogical form. The original of this form ifʿalla is to indicate a colour or a physical defect, like iʿwarra, iswadda and iḥmarra; that it not be from a geminated root like uḥimma, nor have a weak lām like alhā; and that it not be for compliance (muṭāwaʿa). Rare are «انهارَّ الليل» and «اشْعارَّ الرجل», meaning his hair was dishevelled, since they indicate neither defect nor colour; rare also is «ارعَوَّى», since it has a weak lām and is a muṭāwaʿ of «رَعَوْتُه» in the sense of "I restrained him", and does not indicate a defect or colour. As for the entry of the alif into this ifʿalla form, it indicates the transience of that meaning, and its absence indicates its permanence and settledness. So if you say «اسودَّ وجهه» it indicates his being characterised by blackness without transience in it, and if you say «اسوادَّ» it indicates its occurrence as new. This is the usual case, and it is sometimes reversed. The Exalted said: {مُدْهَآمَّتَانِ} [al-Raḥmān: 64], the intent being to indicate that the attribute is inherent in the two gardens; and His saying, the Exalted: {تَزْوَرَّ عَن كَهْفِهِم} [al-Kahf: 17], the intent being the transience of the sun's inclining, not permanence and settledness. So it is said, but there is a possible objection in it, because what is intended is describing the sun with this attribute as fixed with respect to these people in particular.

His saying {فَذُوقُواْ} is a case of metaphor: He made the punishment a thing perceived by the sense of eating and tasting, depicting it in the form of something tasted. His saying {بِمَا كُنْتُمْ}: the bāʾ is of causation, and «ما» is maṣdariyya (producing a verbal noun); it cannot be "that which" (alladhī), because it would need a returning pronoun, / and implying it is impermissible because the conditions permitting its omission are absent.

semin-durr:108-108.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الله}: mubtadaʾ and khabar, and «نَتْلوها» is a circumstantial (ḥāl) clause. It is also said: {آيَاتُ الله} is a badal (substitute) from «تلك», and «نتلوها» is a clause serving as khabar of the mubtadaʾ. «بالحق» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «نَتْلوها» or its object, and it is a confirmatory ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), because the Exalted sends them down only in this manner.

al-Zajjāj said: "There is an omission in the speech, the implied form being: these are the verses of the Qur'an, the arguments of Allah and His proofs." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "According to what he implied, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is omitted, because in his view the meaning of the verse is completed by this implication; but this implication is not needed, since the meaning is complete without it." The indication by «تلك» is to the preceding verses that include the punishment of the disbelievers and the bliss of the righteous.

The majority read «نَتْلوها» with the nūn of majesty, and in it is an iltifāt (shift) from the third person to the first. Abū Nuhayk read «يتلوها» with yāʾ, and it has two possibilities: one, that the fāʿil is the pronoun for the Creator, the Exalted, because He was mentioned earlier in His saying {آيَاتُ الله}; there is no iltifāt on this implication, unlike the reading of the majority. The second: that the fāʿil is the pronoun for Jibrīl.

His saying: {لِّلْعَالَمِينَ}: the lām is redundant (zāʾida) and is not attached to anything; it was added to the object of the maṣdar, which is ظلم.
