His saying, the Exalted: {أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تَدْخُلُواْ}: There are several views on this «أم», the most evident being that it is discontinuous (munqaṭiʿa), estimated as «بل» plus the interrogative hamza, and its meaning is rebuke (inkār). It is also said that «أم» is in the sense of the hamza alone, and its meaning, as has gone before, is reproach and rebuke. It is also said that this is an interrogative whose meaning is prohibition; Abū Muslim al-Iṣfahānī said it. It is also said that it is continuous (muttaṣila). Ibn Baḥr said: "It is the counterpart of a hamza that is estimated from the meaning of what has gone before, for his saying {إِن يَمْسَسْكُمْ قَرْحٌ} {وَتِلْكَ الأيام نُدَاوِلُهَا} to the end of the story requires that it be followed by: 'Do you know that the obligation requires that, or did you suppose'." And «حَسِبَ» here is in its normal sense of preferring one of two sides. And {أَن تَدْخُلُواْ} stands in place of the two objects according to Sībawayh, and in place of the first, the second being omitted, according to al-Akhfash.

His saying: {وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ}: a ḥāl sentence. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «ولَمَّا» is in the sense of «لم», except that it has a kind of expectation, so it indicates the negation of striving in the past and its expectation in the future. You say: "He promised me that he would do such and such, and not yet (wa-lammā)", meaning "and he has not done it, and I expect his doing it." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "This which he said about «لَمَّا», that it indicates expectation of the action negated by it in the future, I do not know any of the grammarians to have mentioned; rather they mentioned that when you say «لَمَّا يخرج زيد» it indicates the non-occurrence of the going out in the past, its negation being continuous up to the time of the report; but that it indicates its expectation in the future, no. However, I found in the speech of al-Farrāʾ something close to what al-Zamakhsharī said: he said that «لَمَّا» is for presenting existence as a possibility, unlike «لم»." I say: The grammarians distinguished between them only from the aspect that what is negated by «لَمْ» is a verb not accompanied by «قد», while «لَمَّا» is its negation accompanied by it, and it may indicate expectation, so al-Zamakhsharī's statement is sound from this aspect. What I said, that «لم» is the negation of faʿala and «لَمَّا» the negation of qad faʿala, is indicated by the explicit statement of the grammarians, Sībawayh and those after him. The like of this verse has gone before in al-Baqara with a verification of the discussion that makes its repetition unnecessary, so turn to it.

And his saying «منكم» is a ḥāl from «الذين». And {وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ الله} with kasra on the mīm is on the basis of the meeting of two quiescents. Al-Nakhaʿī and Ibn Wathāb read it with fatḥa on it, and there are two views on this. One: that the fatḥa is a fatḥa of assimilation, the mīm being made to follow the lām before it. The second: that it is based on the intended light nūn (nūn khafīfa), the origin being «ولَمَّا يَعْلَمَنْ»; and what is negated by «لَمَّا» has come emphasized with it, as in his saying:

1447 - يَحْسَبُه الجاهلُ ما لم يَعْلما ... شيخاً على كُرْسِيِّه مُعَمَّماً
(The ignorant, as long as he does not know, takes him to be a sheikh on his chair, turbaned.)

When he dropped the nūn the end of the verb remained with fatḥa, as in his saying:

1448 - لا تُهِينَ الفقيرَ عَلَّك أَنْ تَرْ ... كَعَ يوماً والدهرُ قد رَفَعَهْ
(Do not humiliate the poor man; perhaps you will one day bow down while time has raised him.)

[and on this is analysed the reading «ألم نشرحَ» with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ], and the saying of another:

1449 - في أيِّ يَوميَّ من الموتِ أفِرْ ... أيومَ لم يُقْدَرَ أم يومَ قُدِرْ
(On which of my two days shall I flee from death: the day not decreed, or the day decreed?)

His saying: «ويَعْلَم»: the majority read with fatḥa on the mīm, and there are two analyses of it. The more famous: that the verb is accusative. Then is its being accusative by an implied «أَنْ» after the wāw that signifies concurrence (jamʿ), as in your saying «لا تأكلِ السمكَ وتَشْربَ اللبن» (do not eat fish and drink milk), i.e. do not combine the two, which is the view of the Basrans; or by the wāw of diversion (wāw al-ṣarf), which is the view of the Kufans, meaning that it was proper for this verb to take the same case ending as what precedes it, but when the wāw came it diverted it to another aspect of i'rab. The exposition of the two schools is elsewhere than this topic.

The second: that the fatḥa is the fatḥa of [two quiescents' meeting, the verb being jussive]; when another quiescent followed it, its end needed a vowel, and the fatḥa was preferable because it is lighter and by assimilation to the vowel of the lām, as was said in one of the two analyses of the reading {وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ الله} with fatḥa on the mīm; the first is the better view. [Translator's note: the source text here reads "فتحة التاء ساكنين" and is evidently corrupt; the bracketed rendering is an interpretive reconstruction.]

Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Yaʿmar and Abū Ḥaywa read with kasra on the mīm, conjoining to «يَعْلَمِ» which is jussive by «لم».

ʿAbd al-Wārith read from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ: «وَيَعْلَمُ» in the nominative, with two views. The more evident: that it is a resumption, Allah the Exalted informing of that. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "on the basis that the wāw is circumstantial, as if he said: 'when they have not yet striven while you are steadfast'." The Shaykh said: "What he said is not sound, because the wāw of ḥāl does not enter upon the imperfect; it is not permissible to say «جاء زَيدٌ ويضحك» meaning 'Zayd came laughing', because the imperfect takes the place of the active participle, so just as «جاء زيد وضاحكاً» is not permissible, so «جاء زيد ويضحك» is not permissible. If it is interpreted as the imperfect being the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that estimate is possible, i.e. «وهو يعلمُ الصابرين» ('and He knows the steadfast'), as they interpreted the poet's saying:

1450 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... نَجَوْتُ وَأَرْهُنُهمْ مالِكا
(... I escaped, and I [was] pledging Mālik to them.)

i.e. «وأنا أَرْهُنُهم»." I say: His saying "does not enter upon the imperfect" is not absolute; rather he ought to have said: upon the affirmative imperfect or that negated by «لا», for it enters upon the imperfect negated by «لم» and «لما», as has been known more than once.

semin-durr:143-143.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كُنْتُمْ تَمَنَّوْنَ}: Al-Bazzī, with a variation from him, read «تَّمَنَّوْنَ» with doubling of the تاء, and that is possible only in waṣl; his rule is that he joins the plural mīm with a wāw, and the verification of this has already been given at his saying {وَلاَ تَيَمَّمُواْ الخبيث} [al-Baqara: 267].

The pronoun in «تَلْقَوه» has two views. The more evident: that it refers back to death; the second: that it refers back to the enemy, although it has not been mentioned, because the situation indicates it.

The majority read «قبل» with kasra on the lām, because it is declinable (muʿrab) owing to its being annexed to «أَنْ» and what is in its scope, i.e. "before meeting it". Mujāhid ibn Jabr read «من قبلُ» with ḍamma on the lām, cut off from annexation, as in his saying {لِلَّهِ الأمر مِن قَبْلُ وَمِن بَعْدُ} [al-Rūm: 4]. On this, «أَنْ» and what is in its scope is in the position of the accusative as a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from «الموت», i.e. "you wished for the meeting with death", like your saying «رَهَبْتُ العدوَّ لقاءَه» ("I feared the enemy, meeting him"). Al-Zuhrī and al-Nakhaʿī read «تُلاقُوه», and its meaning is the meaning of «تَلْقَوه», because laqiya customarily calls for being between two, even if it is not on the pattern mufāʿala.

His saying: {فَقَدْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُ}: the apparent view is that the seeing is visual, so it suffices with one object. They allowed that it be mental (ʿilmiyya), in which case it needs a second object, which is omitted, i.e. "you have known it present", meaning death; except that omitting one of the two objects in the chapter of ẓanna is not easy, so that some restrict it to poetic necessity, such as the saying of ʿAntara:

1451 - وَلَقَدْ نَزَلْتِ فلا تَظُنِّي غيرَه ... مِنِّي بمنزلةِ المُحَبِّ المُكْرَمِ
(You have alighted [in my heart], so do not suppose otherwise from me, in the station of the honoured beloved.)

i.e. "so do not suppose anything else to be coming from me."

His saying: {وَأَنْتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ}: it may be circumstantial, and then it is a confirming ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida) that removes what seeing admits of figurative use or homonymy, i.e. between it and seeing with the heart; or it may be a resumption, meaning: "and you are looking into your conduct now after the war has ended, whether you fulfilled or went against it". Ibn al-Anbārī said: "«رأيتموه» means you faced it while you were looking with your eyes, and for this reason He mentioned looking after seeing when their meanings differed, because the first is in the sense of facing and confronting, and the second in the sense of seeing with the eye." This is not known among the people of the language, I mean the use of seeing for facing and confronting; and on the assumption that it is sound, the sentence {وَأَنْتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ} would be a clarifying ḥāl sentence, not a confirming one, because it conveys a meaning additional to the meaning of its governor. An object may be estimated for «ينظرون», and it may not be estimated, since the meaning is: "and you are people of looking." And Allah the Exalted knows best, and to Allah belong praise and favour.

semin-durr:164-164.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَقَدْ مَنَّ الله}: The response of an omitted oath.
It was also read «لِمنْ مَنِّ الله» with the preposition «مِنْ», and «مَنِّ» with shadda is genitive by it. Al-Zamakhsharī analysed it in two ways. One: that this preposition and its genitive noun is a fronted khabar and the mubtadaʾ is omitted, its implied form being: "Of the favour of Allah upon the believers is His favour, or His sending (of a messenger), when He sent"; it was omitted because the indication is present. The second: that the mubtadaʾ is made «إذ» itself, in the sense of "time", and its khabar is the preposition phrase before it, the implied form being: "Of Allah's favour upon the believers is the time of His sending (him)"; and he compared it to their saying: "The most eloquent the emir is when he is standing" (akhṭabu mā yakūnu l-amīru idhā kāna qāʾiman). These two aspects in this reading are among the things that indicate how firmly planted his foot is in this science.
The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān), however, rejected the second aspect from him, because «إذ» is non-declinable (ghayr mutaṣarrifa); it is only an adverb, or has a time noun annexed to it, or is an object of "remember" according to one view. He transmitted the statement of Abū ʿAlī about it and «إذا», that the two are not agents, nor objects, nor mubtadaʾs. He said: "It is not preserved from their speech: 'idh qāma Zaydun ṭawīl'", meaning "the time of his standing is long". And (he rejected it) because his comparison of the reading with their saying «أخطبُ» etc. is an error, in that the thing likened is a mubtadaʾ and the thing likened to [it] is an adverb in the position of the khabar according to the one who gives it this i'rab, and in that this khabar, which he has brought out overtly, must be omitted since the ḥāl takes its place, as the grammarians who give it this i'rab have stated explicitly; so how could he bring it out in the wording?" The answer to this rejection is plain, and would that Abū l-Qāsim had not mentioned an analysis of this reading, so that we might have heard...
The majority read «أنفسهم» with ḍamma on the sīn, that is: from among them and of their kind. ʿĀʾisha, Fāṭima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read it, and Anas related it from him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, from nafāsa, which is nobility, that is: the noblest of them in lineage, creation and character. And from ʿAlī from him, peace be upon him: "I am the noblest of you in lineage, standing and in-law relationship."
This preposition phrase has two possible aspects. One: that it is attached to «بعث» itself. The second: that it is attached to an omitted word as an adjective of «رسولاً», so it would be accusative in position; and this aspect is strengthened on the reading with fatḥa on the fāʾ. His saying {يَتْلُواْ عَلَيْهِمْ} is in the position of a ḥāl or is resumptive, and its parallel has already preceded in al-Baqara.
His saying: {وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِي}: This is the lightened «إنْ», and the lām is the distinguishing one (lām fāriqa); discussion on the verification of this and the disagreement about it has already preceded. Only, here al-Zamakhsharī and Makkī, when they made it lightened, implied for it an omitted noun. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its implied form is: 'and indeed the matter and the affair — they were before'." Makkī said: "As for Sībawayh, he says it is lightened and its noun is a latent pronoun", the implied form, according to his view, being "and indeed they were". This is not good, because the lightened «إنْ» operates only on an overt noun, on a less eloquent usage, and has no operation on a pronoun, and no omitted noun is implied for it at all; rather, it is neglected (made inoperative) or it operates as has preceded. Moreover, al-Zamakhsharī did not state explicitly that its noun is omitted, but said: "«إنْ» is the lightened one and the lām is the distinguishing one, and the implied form is: 'and indeed the matter and the affair were'", so this may be an explanation of meaning, not of i'rab.
There are two views about this sentence. One: that it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The second: that it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl from the object in «يُعَلِّمُهم», and this is the more evident.

semin-durr:165-165.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَوَ لَمَّا أَصَابَتْكُمْ}: The hamza is for denunciation (inkār), and Ibn ʿAṭiyya made it for affirmation (taqrīr). The wāw is a conjunction, and it is intended to be placed before the hamza, as established. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«لَمَّا» is accusative by «قلتم», and «أصابَتْكم» is in the position of genitive through the annexation of «لَمَّا» to it, and its implied form is 'you said when it struck you'; and «أنَّى هذا» is accusative because it is what is said (maqūl). The hamza is for rebuke and affirmation. If you say: to what does the wāw join this sentence? I say: to what has passed of the story of Uḥud, and His saying {وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ الله وَعْدَهُ}; it is also possible that it be conjoined to an omitted sentence, its implied form being: 'Did you do such-and-such, and say at that time such-and-such?'" End of quotation.
As for his making «لَمَّا» have the meaning of «حين», that is an adverb, this is the position of al-Fārisī, and the exposition of the two positions has already preceded. As for his saying "a conjunction upon the story of Uḥud", this is not his position, because what runs from his position is only the implying of a sentence upon which what follows the wāw, or the fāʾ, or «thumma» is conjoined, as he himself laid out in the second aspect.
«أنى هذا»: «أنَّى» has the meaning of «مِن أين» (from where), as has preceded in His saying {أنى لَكِ هذا} [آل عمران: 37]. His saying {مِنْ عِندِ أَنْفُسِكُمْ} and {مِنْ عِندِ الله} indicates this; so said al-Zamakhsharī. The Shaykh rejected this from him, saying that an adverb, when it occurs as a khabar, is not implied as having a preposition other than «في» enter upon it; as for implying «مِنْ» entering upon it, no, because it became accusative only by dropping «في», and for that reason, when the adverb is replaced by a pronoun, [the verb] is made to reach it by «في», unless latitude is used with it. He said: "So his implying it is not valid, and his inference from His saying {مِنْ عِندِ أَنْفُسِكُمْ} {مِنْ عِندِ الله} is a standing on the correspondence of the question to the answer in wording, and a heedlessness of this rule." The Shaykh chose that «أَنَّى» has the meaning of «كيف» (how). He said: "«أنَّى» is a question about the state here, and it does not suit that it mean «أين» or «متى», because the question was not made about a place or time here, but about the state that required that for them. They asked about it by way of wonder, and the answer came in terms of meaning, not wording, in His saying {قُلْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ أَنْفُسِكُمْ}." He said: "The question with «أنَّى» is a question about specifying the manner in which this matter came about, and the answer with His saying {مِنْ عِندِ أَنْفُسِكُمْ} implies the specification of the manner, because by specifying the cause the manner is specified in terms of meaning. If it were said by way of wonder: 'How can righteous Zayd not perform the pilgrimage!' and it were said in answer: 'Because of his inability', the answer would be obtained and the meaning would be arranged: he does not perform the pilgrimage since he is unable." End of quotation.
As for his saying "the adverb is not implied with a preposition other than «في»": al-Zamakhsharī did not imply «في» with «أنَّى» so that what he said would follow for him; he only made «أنَّى» equal «من أين» in meaning. As for his departing from the answer that corresponds in wording, the reverse is preferable.
His saying: {قَدْ أَصَبْتُمْ} is in the position of nominative as an adjective of «مصيبة». And «قلتم», on Sībawayh's position, is the response of «لَمَّا», and on al-Fārisī's position it is the accusing operator of it, according to what has preceded of their two positions. The pronoun in His saying «قل» (as in «هو») refers back to the calamity in terms of meaning. It is also possible that it be on the omission of a muḍāf that is taken into account, that is: its cause; and likewise the reference with His saying «أنّى هذا», because what is meant is the calamity.

semin-durr:166-166.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَآ أَصَابَكُمْ}: «ما» is a relative noun meaning «الذي», in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. {فَبِإِذْنِ الله} is the khabar, and it rests on an implied pronoun, its implied form being: "it is by Allah's leave". The fāʾ entered the khabar because of the mubtadaʾ's resemblance to a condition, as in "the one who comes to me — he has a dirham". On what the majority have established this is problematic, because they established that it is not permissible for this fāʾ to enter the khabar as a redundant letter except under conditions, among them that the ṣila be future in meaning; that is because the fāʾ enters only for resemblance to the condition, and the condition is only in the future, not in the past. If you said "the one who came to me yesterday — he has a dirham", it would not be valid. And «أصابَكم» here is past in meaning, because the story is past; so how was the entry of this fāʾ permissible?
They answered that it is understood as clarification (tabyīn), that is: "and whatever is shown to have struck you", just as they interpreted {وَإِنْ كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ} [يوسف: 27], that is: if it is shown; and this is an explicit condition. I say: if this interpretation is sound, then let «ما» here be made an explicit conditional, and the fāʾ would be entering obligatorily, as it occurs as the apodosis of the condition. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The entry of the fāʾ is good when [it] is the cause of the giving, and so is the arrangement of this; the meaning is only: 'and what Allah gave leave for is what struck you', but he put first what is most important in their souls and nearest to their perception. Idhn (leave) is enabling something with knowledge of it." This is good in terms of meaning, for the striking is ordered after the leave in meaning. By his saying "the most important and the nearest" he pointed to what struck them on the day the two armies met.
His saying: «وَلِيعٍلَمَ» [Translator's note: the source has a stray diacritic in the printed word]: There are two views about this lām. One: that it is conjoined to the meaning of His saying {فَبِإِذْنِ الله}, the conjunction of a cause upon a cause, so it is attached to what the bāʾ is attached to. The second: that it is attached to an omitted word, that is: "and so that He may know, He did that", that is, it struck you. The first is preferable. It has already preceded that the meaning of "so that Allah may know such-and-such" is distinguishing, and showing to people what was in His knowledge. Some claimed that there is a muḍāf there, that is: "so that He may know the faith of the believers and the hypocrisy of those who…", and there is no need of it.
Translator's note: in the source text of this entry the word «إذا» in "«يَحْسُن دخولُ الفاءِ إذ1اكان سببَ الإِعطاءِ»" is printed with a stray digit ("إذ1اكان"); I have translated it as "when it is" (إذا كان).

semin-durr:167-167.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْاْ قَاتِلُواْ}: This sentence has two possible aspects. One: that it is resumptive; Allah informs that they were commanded either to fight or to repel, that is, to swell the ranks of the Muslims. The second: that it is conjoined to «نافقوا», so it falls within the scope of the relative noun, that is: "and so that He may know those from whom hypocrisy and the saying of such-and-such occurred", and «تعالوا» and «قاتِلوا» both stand in the place of the agent for «قيل», because that is what is said, and what is in it has already preceded. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "He did not bring a conjunction — meaning between «تعالوا» and «قاتِلوا» — because he intended that each of the two sentences be meant in itself; it may also be said that what is meant is the command to fight, and «تعالَوا» mentions something which, had it been left unsaid, there would be in the speech what indicates it; and it was said: the second command is a ḥāl." By his saying "«وتعالوا» mentions something which, had it been left unsaid" he means that what is meant is only their being commanded to fight, not their coming alone; and making «قاتلوا» a ḥāl from «تعالوا» is invalid, because a circumstantial clause must be declarative and this one is a request.
His saying: {أَوِ ادفعوا}: «أو» here is in its usual sense of choice and permission. It was said: it has the meaning of the wāw, because he asked them for fighting and repelling; but the first is the sound view. His saying "they said: if we knew" has no conjunction in this sentence because it is the answer to a questioner's question: as though it were said, "So what did they say when that was said to them?" and the answer was that they said that. And «نعلمُ», though imperfect, has a past meaning, because «لو» restricts the imperfect [to the past] since it is used for what would occur because of the occurrence of something else. He made «قتالاً» indefinite, that is: "if we knew some fighting or other".
His saying: {هُمْ لِلْكُفْرِ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَقْرَبُ}: «هم» is the mubtadaʾ and «أقربُ» its khabar, and it is an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl); «للكفر» is attached to it, and likewise «للإِيمان». If it is said: "Two prepositions identical in wording and meaning are not attached to one operator, unless one of them is conjoined to the other or is a badal of it; so how were both attached to «أقرب»?" The answer is that this is particular to the elative; they said: because it has the force of two operators, for your saying "Zayd is more excellent than ʿAmr" means that his excellence exceeds the excellence of ʿAmr. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is permissible for «أقربُ» to operate in both, because the two resemble adverbs, just as «أطيبُ» operates in the saying 'this, as unripe dates, is better than it as ripe dates' in the two implied adverbs, since afʿal indicates two meanings: the base of the verb and its excess, so it operates in each of them with a meaning different from the other, and its implied form is: their nearness to disbelief exceeds their nearness to faith."
There is no need to liken the two prepositional phrases to the two adverbs, for the apparent sense is that the justification for their attachment to a single operator is their resemblance to the two adverbs, and it is not so. His saying "the two implied adverbs" means that the meaning is: this at the time of its being unripe is better than it at the time of its being ripe.
«أقربُ» here is from nearness (qurb), which is the opposite of distance, and it is made transitive by three particles: the lām, «إلى» and «مِنْ»; you say qarubtu laka, ilayka and minka. If you say "Zayd is nearer to knowledge than ʿAmr", the first «مِنْ» is the one carrying the base meaning of nearness, and the second is the one governing the one surpassed. Once this is established, there is no need to claim that the lām has the meaning of «إلى».
«يومئذ» is attached to «أقربُ», and so is «منهم»; this «مِنْ» is the one governing the one surpassed after afʿal, and is not the one carrying the base of the verb. The meaning of {هُمْ لِلْكُفْرِ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَقْرَبُ مِنْهُمْ لِلإِيمَانِ} is that before this time they were concealing hypocrisy, so outwardly they were farther from disbelief; then when what they were concealing appeared from them, they became nearer to disbelief.
«إذ» is annexed to an omitted sentence for which the tanwīn is substituted, as its exposition has already preceded, and the implied form of this sentence is: "they were nearer to disbelief on the day when they said: if we knew fighting we would follow you". It was also said: the meaning is on the omission of a muḍāf, that is: "they are nearer to the people of disbelief than to the people of faith". They are here preferred over themselves with respect to two states and two times. Were it not for that, it would not be permissible. You say: "Zayd sitting is better than he standing", or "Zayd sitting today is better than he sitting tomorrow"; and if you said "Zayd today sitting is better than he today sitting" it would not be permissible.
Al-Naqqāsh related from some of the exegetes that «أقرب» here is not from the meaning of nearness which is the opposite of distance, but from qarab with fatḥa on the qāf and rāʾ, which is seeking water, and from it "he sought the water" (qāraba l-māʾ); laylat al-qarab is the night of coming to water. So the meaning is: they are more eager for disbelief; and on this the transitivity by the lām is determined, as in your saying: "Zayd is a harder hitter of ʿAmr".
His saying: {يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَاهِهِم}: There are two views about this sentence. One: that it is resumptive, with no position. The second: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أقرب», that is: they drew near to disbelief while saying this statement. His saying «بأفواهِهم» was said to be emphasis, like His saying {وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ} [الأنعام: 38]. The apparent sense is that "saying" applies to both the verbal and the mental, so restricting it with "their mouths" is restricting one of two possibilities, unless it is said that its application to the mental is figurative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Mentioning the hearts along with the mouths is a depiction of their hypocrisy, and that their faith exists in their mouths only." By this which al-Zamakhsharī said, its being for emphasis is negated, since it obtains this benefit.

semin-durr:97-97.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فِيهِ آيَاتٌ}: it is permissible that this clause be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial): either from the pronoun of «وُضع», with the difficulty that has preceded; or from the pronoun in «ببكة», which is clear, and this is according to the opinion of one who permits multiple ḥāls for one owner of a ḥāl; or from the pronoun in «للعالمين»; or from «هدى», and that is allowable because it was specified by the description. It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مباركاً». It is also permissible that the clause be in the position of accusative as an adjective of «هدى», after its being described by the preposition-and-noun phrase before it. And it is permissible that this clause be resumptive with no grammatical position, brought only as an explanation and clarification of its blessedness and guidance. It is also permissible that the ḥāl or the description, as detailed above, be only the preposition and its genitive noun, with «آياتٌ» nominative by it as an agent (fāʿil), because the preposition-and-noun phrase, whenever it relies on the things I mentioned at the beginning of this topic, raises an agent. This is preferable to making it a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar, because these things, I mean the ḥāl, the adjective and the khabar, are originally to be single words, so what is closer to them is preferable, and the preposition-and-noun phrase is close to a single word; for that reason the single word is put first, then the adverbial, then the clause, in what I have mentioned. On that is the noble verse: {وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مُّؤْمِنٌ مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَانَهُ} [غافر: 28]; he put first the description by a single word, «مؤمن», second what is close to it, «من آل فرعون», and third the clause, «يكتم إيمانه». The apparent opposite of this has occurred, and I shall make this question clear, if Allah the Exalted wills, at His saying: {يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ أَذِلَّةٍ} [المائدة: 54].
His saying: {مَّقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِناً}: there are several views on it. One: that «مقام» is a badal (substitute) of «آيات». On this it is said that the grammarians stated explicitly that whenever a plural is mentioned, nothing may be substituted for it except what fulfils the plural; so you say: «مررت برجالٍ زيدٍ وعمرٍو وبكر», because the minimum of the sound plural is three. If it does not fulfil it, they said, it is obligatory to cut it off from being a badal: either to the accusative by implying a verb, or to the nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; as you say in the preceding example: «زيداً وعمراً», that is, "I mean Zayd and ʿAmr", or «زيد وعمرو», that is, "among them are Zayd and ʿAmr". For that reason they gave the i'rab of the saying of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
1358 - تَوَهَّمْتُ آياتٍ لها فَعَرَفْتُها ... لستةِ أعوامٍ وذا العامُ سابعُ
رَمادٌ ككحلِ العَيْن لأْياً أُبينه ... ونُؤْيٌ كجِذْم الحَوْضِ أَثْلَمُ خاشعُ
(I made out her signs and recognized them after six years, and this year is the seventh: ashes like eye-kohl that I discern only with difficulty, and a trench like the stump of a trough, notched and humbled.)
according to the cutting-off mentioned above, that is: "among them are ashes and a trench"; and likewise His saying, the Exalted: {حَدِيثُ الجنود فِرْعَوْنَ وَثَمُودَ} [البروج: 17-18], that is: "I mean, or I censure, Pharaoh and Thamūd". Though it may be said that what is meant by Pharaoh and Thamūd is the two together with those of their peoples who followed them, so mentioning them fulfils the plurality. In the noble verse here, after the signs, only two things were mentioned: the Station and the security of whoever enters it; so how can they be a badal? This difficulty also applies to the view of one who made it the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are the Station of Ibrāhīm": how can it inform about a plural with two?
There are replies to it. One: that the minimum of the plural is two, as some held. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is also possible that what is meant is: 'In it are signs: the Station of Ibrāhīm and the security of whoever enters it,' because two is a kind of plural like three and four." Second: that «مقام إبراهيم», although single in wording, includes many signs: for the two feet in the solid rock is a sign; their sinking into it up to the ankles is a sign; the softening of part of the rock and not part is a sign; its preservation through the passing of time and its protection from enemies is a sign; and its continuing, unlike the signs of the other prophets, excepting our Prophet, upon him and upon all of them be peace, is a sign. Al-Zamakhsharī said its meaning. Third: that this is of the category of folding (ṭayy), which is that a plural is mentioned, then part of it is brought and silence is kept on mentioning the rest, for a purpose of the speaker, and it is called ṭayy. Al-Zamakhsharī recited for it the saying of Jarīr:
1359 - كانَتْ حُنَيْفَةُ أثلاثاً فثُلْثُهُمُ ... مِنَ العبيدِ وثُلْثٌ مِنْ مَواليها
(Ḥanīfa were in thirds: a third of them slaves, and a third from its freedmen.)
and he brought from it his saying, upon him be peace and blessing: «حُبِّبَ إليَّ من دُنْياكم ثلاثٌ: الطِّيب والنساء، وقُرَّةُ عيني في الصلاة» (Three things of your world were made beloved to me: perfume, women, and the coolness of my eye is in prayer); he mentioned two, which are perfume and women, and folded the mention of the third. It is not said that the third is his saying «وقُرَّةُ عيني في الصلاة», because it is not of their world; it is only of the matters of the hereafter. The benefit of folding, in their view, is the multiplication of that thing, as though when He the Exalted mentioned the sum of the signs by these two signs, He said: "and many besides them". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The more preferable in my view is that the Station and the security of the one who enters were made an example of the signs in the Sanctuary of Allah the Exalted, and were specified in mention because of their greatness, and because the proof is established by them against the disbelievers, since they perceive these two signs with their senses."
The second view: that «مقامُ إبراهيم» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); al-Zamakhsharī said this, and the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) rejected it from the aspect of their differing in definiteness and indefiniteness, saying: "His statement contradicts the consensus of the Basrans and the Kufans, so no attention is paid to it. The ruling of ʿaṭf bayān with the Kufans is the ruling of the adjective, so they make an indefinite follow an indefinite and a definite a definite, and Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī followed them in that. As for the Basrans, it is not permissible with them except that both be definite, and it is not permissible that both be indefinite. Everything the Kufans brought that suggests the permissibility of its being ʿaṭf, the Basrans made a badal, and no proof has been established for the Kufans." I say: this question will come, if Allah the Exalted wills, in a thorough treatment at His saying, the Exalted: {مِن مَّآءٍ صَدِيدٍ} [إبراهيم: 16] and at His saying, the Exalted: {مِن شَجَرَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ} [النور: 35].
When al-Zamakhsharī gave the i'rab of "the Station of Ibrāhīm and the security of whoever enters it" with the interpretation mentioned, he raised an objection against himself with what I mentioned about substituting a non-plural for a plural, and answered with what has preceded. He also raised an objection against himself as to how a clause could be an explicative apposition of single nouns, and said: "If you say: how did you allow «مقام إبراهيم» and the security to be an ʿaṭf bayān, when His saying {وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِناً} is a resumptive clause, either an initial or a conditional one? I say: I allowed that from the aspect of meaning, because His saying {وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِناً} indicates the security of whoever enters it, so it is as though it were said: 'In it are clear signs: the Station of Ibrāhīm and the security of whoever enters it.' Do you not see that if you said: 'In it is a clear sign: whoever enters it is secure,' it would be sound, because the meaning is: in it is a clear sign, the security of whoever enters it." The Shaykh said: "It is not clear, because his implied form 'and the security of the one who enters' is nominative, conjoined to «مقام إبراهيم», and he explained the signs by the two, whereas the clause {وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِناً} has no position in i'rab, so they conflict, unless one believes that there is an omitted conjoined element that what follows indicates, in which case the explanation is possible; so His saying {وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِناً} is not made to mean 'and the security of its enterer' except from the aspect of explaining the meaning and not of explaining the i'rab." This is a niggling dispute with nothing to it, and there is no conflict in what he said, because whenever a clause is in the interpretation of a single word, its conjunction to it is sound. Then the preferable is that His saying «مقام إبراهيم» be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, not as they implied it, so as to entail the earlier difficulty, but you imply: "one of them is the Station of Ibrāhīm". This is the third view. And «مَنْ» may be conditional or relative, and the discussion on both is not hidden from what has preceded.
Ubayy, ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Jaʿfar and Mujāhid read: «آيةٌ بينة» in the singular. The explanation of «مقام» on the preceding views is easy: as a badal or a bayān according to al-Zamakhsharī, or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. This badal is agreed upon, because the Basrans substitute from an indefinite absolutely, and the Kufans substitute from it only on the condition of its being described, and it has been described.
His saying: {مَنِ استطاع}: there are six views on it. One: that «مَنْ» is a badal of «الناس», a partial substitute (badal baʿḍ min kull); and for the partial badal and the inclusive badal, each requires a pronoun returning to the substituted-for, for example: أَكَلْتُ الرغيفَ ثلثَه, and سُلِب زيدٌ ثوبُه; here there is no pronoun, so it was said that it is omitted, its implied form being: مَنْ استطاع منهم (whoever among them is able). Second: that it is a total badal (badal kull min kull), since what is meant by the people mentioned is specific; and the difference between this view and the previous is that the previous is described as "general made specific" and this one as "general with a specific meaning intended"; and it is a clear difference. These two expressions are taken from the expression of Imām al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him. Third: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: هو مَنْ استطاع. Fourth: that it is accusative by implying a verb, that is: أعني مَن استطاع (I mean whoever is able). These two views are in reality taken from the badal view, for everything that may be substituted for what precedes may also be cut off to the nominative or accusative just mentioned. Fifth: that «مَنْ» is an agent of the maṣdar, which is «حَجٌّ», the maṣdar being annexed to its object, the implied form being: "and Allah has upon the people that whoever among them is able find a way perform pilgrimage to the House". A group rejected this view, from the aspect of craft and from the aspect of meaning. As for the aspect of craft: when an agent and an object come together with the maṣdar that governs both of them, the maṣdar is annexed only to its nominative and not to its accusative, so one says: يعجبني ضَرْبُ زيدٍ عمراً; and if you said «ضربُ عمرٍو زيدٌ» it would not be allowed except in poetic necessity, like his saying:
1360 - أَفْنَى تِلادي وما جَمَّعْتُ مِنْ نَشَبٍ ... قَرْعُ القواقيزِ أفواهُ الأباريقِ
(My inherited wealth and what I gathered of property was consumed by the knocking of goblets on the mouths of the jugs.)
It is related with «أفواه» in the accusative, by annexing the maṣdar, which is «قَرْع», to its agent, and in the nominative by annexing it to its object; and some permitted it in ordinary speech with weakness, while the Quran is not construed on what is in poetic necessity or on what has weakness. As for the aspect of meaning: it leads to charging all the people, those able and those not able, that their able ones perform pilgrimage, so it entails charging the one not able with the able one's performing pilgrimage, and that is not permissible. Some have accepted this and said: yes, we say what it requires, and that Allah the Exalted charged the people with that, so that if the able ones did not perform pilgrimage, it would be obligatory on those not able to command them to pilgrimage as far as possible, because bringing the people to perform pilgrimage to the Kaʿba and ʿArafa is an obligatory duty. «مَنْ» on the five views is a relative with the meaning of «الذي». Sixth: that it is conditional and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what preceded, or is itself what preceded according to one opinion; and there must be a pronoun returning from the condition clause to the people, its implied form being: مَنِ استطاعَ منهم إليه سبيلاً فلله عليه أن يَحُجَّ. This is favoured by its being set against the condition after it, which is His saying: {وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ الله غَنِيٌّ عَنِ العالمين}.
His saying: {وَللَّهِ عَلَى الناس حِجُّ البيت} is a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar, the khabar being His saying «لله»; and «على الناس» is attached to what the khabar is attached to, or is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition-and-noun phrase, the operator in it also being that omitted settledness. It is permissible that «على الناس» be the khabar and «لله» be attached to what the khabar is attached to; and it is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «على الناس», although the reverse is allowable as preceded. The difference is that here the ḥāl would have to precede the abstract operator, and the ḥāl does not precede an abstract operator, unlike the adverbial and the preposition, which precede their abstract operator for latitude in them. It has preceded that Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn ibn Mālik permits its preceding the abstract operator when it is an adverbial or a preposition-and-noun phrase and the operator is likewise, and our question in the noble verse is of this kind.
The Two Brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read «حِج» with kasra on the ḥāʾ, and the rest with fatḥa. It was said that they are two dialects with the same meaning, the kasra being the dialect of Najd and the fatḥa that of the people of al-ʿĀliya. Sībawayh made a distinction, making the kasra form a maṣdar or a noun for the act, while the fatḥa form is only a maṣdar.
It has preceded in al-Baqara that the kasra on the ḥāʾ was read in an irregular reading, and I discussed there these two forms and what people have said about them and the derivation of the root, so repeating it is unnecessary; and to Allah belong praise and favour.
Many exaggerations (emphatic devices) have been brought in this verse, among them His saying: {وَللَّهِ عَلَى الناس حِجُّ البيت}, meaning that it is an obligatory right owed by them to Allah in their time, from whose performance and discharge they are not free. Among them that He mentioned «الناس» and then substituted from them {مَنِ استطاع إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلاً}, and in it are two kinds of emphasis. One: that the substitution is a doubling of what is meant and a repetition of it. The second: that detailing after summarizing and clarifying after vagueness is bringing it in two different forms. Al-Zamakhsharī said this, in the manner of his eloquence and his extracting the meaning in the nearest wording.
The alif and lām in «البيت» are for previous reference ('ahd), because it was mentioned before, and it is a proper name by predominance (ʿalam bi-l-ghalaba) like الثريا and الصَّعِق; so when it is said «زار البيت» (he visited the House), the mind turns only to the Kaʿba, may Allah the Exalted honour it. The poet said:
1361 - لَعَمْرِي لأنت البيتُ أُكْرِمُ أهلَه ... وأَقْعُدُ في أَفْنَائِهِ بالأَصائلِ
(By my life, you are the House whose people I honour, and I sit in its courtyards in the evenings.)
The Shaykh recited this line in this context, and there is some doubt in it, since the Kaʿba is not apparent in it. The pronoun in «إليه»: the apparent is its referring back to the pilgrimage, because it is what is being spoken of; the second: its referring back to the House. «وإليه» is attached to استطاع, and «سبيلا» is a direct object because «استطاع» is transitive; He said: {لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَكُمْ} [الأعراف: 197], and other verses.
His saying: {وَمَن كَفَرَ}: it is permissible that it be the conditional, which is the apparent, and it is permissible that it be the relative, with the فاء entered because of the relative's resemblance to a conditional noun, which has been established more than once; and the state of the two clauses after it is not hidden according to the two considerations mentioned. There must be a link between the condition and its apodosis, or between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar; and whoever permits putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun is content with that in His saying: {فَإِنَّ الله غَنِيٌّ عَنِ العالمين}, as though He said: "independent of them".

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {شَهِدَ الله}: the majority read «شَهِدَ» as an active past verb, with the Majestic Name nominative as its agent. Abū l-Shaʿthāʾ read «شُهِدَ» as passive, with the Exalted Name standing in the place of the agent. On this reading {أَنَّهُ لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ} is in the position of nominative as a badal ishtimāl (inclusion substitute) for the name of Allah the Exalted, the implied form being: "the oneness and divinity of Allah was testified." Since the meaning on this reading is so, conjoining {والملائكة وَأُوْلُواْ العلم} to the Noble Name became problematic; so it was analyzed as not being a conjunction, but either as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with an omitted khabar (predicate) which the speech indicates, its implied form being: "and the angels and those of knowledge testify to that," as His saying {شَهِدَ الله} indicates; or as an agent of an implied verb, the implied form being: "and the angels and those of knowledge testified to that." This is close to His saying, Exalted is He: {يُسَبَّح لَهُ فِيهَا بالغدو والآصال رِجَالٌ} [al-Nūr: 36] in the reading of one who made it passive, and to his saying:

1201 - لِيُبْكَ يزيدُ ضارعٌ لخصومةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Let Yazīd be wept for by one humbled by a dispute...) [the second half-verse is elided in the source]

in one of the two views.

Abū l-Muhallab, the paternal uncle of Muḥārib ibn Dithār, read «شهداءَ الله» as a plural on the pattern fuʿalāʾ, like ẓurafāʾ, accusative; and it was narrated from him and from Abū Nuhayk likewise, except that it is nominative. In both readings it is annexed to the Majestic Name. As for the accusative, it is as ḥāl (circumstantial), whose owner is the latent pronoun in «المستغفرين»; Ibn Jinnī said this, and others followed him, such as al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Baqāʾ. As for the nominative, it is by an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "they are the witnesses of Allah." And «شهداء» may be a plural of shāhir, like shāʿir and shuʿarāʾ, or a plural of shahīd, like ẓarīf and ẓurafāʾ. [Translator's note: the source writes "shāhir" here; the parallel with shāʿir/shuʿarāʾ suggests "shāhid" (witness) was intended.]

Abū l-Muhallab also read, in one narration, «شُهُداً اللهَ» with ḍamma on the shīn and the hāʾ, with tanwīn, and the Majestic Name accusative; it is accusative as a ḥāl, a plural of shahīd, like nadhīr and nudhur, and the name of Allah is accusative for magnification, that is: "they bear witness to Allah," that is, to His oneness.

Al-Naqqāsh narrated that it was read likewise, except that he said: "with ḍamma and with fatḥa on the dāl," and with annexation to the Majestic Name. The accusative and nominative are as preceded in «شهداء». As for the annexation, it may be a pure annexation (maḥḍa), meaning that you defined them by annexing them to Him without reference to the occurrence of an action, as in your saying "servants of Allah"; and it may be from an accusative like the preceding reading, so that it is not pure. Al-Zamakhsharī reported that it was read: «شُهَداء لله», a plural on fuʿalāʾ with an added prepositional lām entering the name of Allah, with nominative and accusative on the hamza, and he analyzed both as above, as ḥāl and khabar.

On all these readings, in the nominative of «الملائكة» and what follows it there are three views. The first: mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar. The second: that it is an agent of an implied verb; their verification has preceded. The third, mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī: coordination (nasaq) on the latent pronoun in «شهداء الله». He said: "That is permissible because of the intervening separator between them."

His saying: «أنه»: the majority read the hamza with fatḥa, and it was given fatḥa only because it is on the omission of a preposition, that is: "Allah bore witness that there is no god but He"; and when the preposition was omitted, it was permissible that its position be accusative or genitive, as its implied form has preceded.

Ibn ʿAbbās read «إنه» with kasra on the hamza, and it has two analyses. The first: treating «شَهِدَ» as speech, because it has its meaning; and so it occurred in the exegesis: «شَهِد الله», that is: "Allah said." This is supported by what al-Muʾarrij transmitted, that «شَهِد» in the sense of «قال» is the dialect of Qays ibn ʿAylān. The second: that it is a parenthetical clause between the governor, namely «شهد», and its object, namely His saying {إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِندَ الله الإسلام}; and that is permissible because of the emphasis and strengthening of meaning in this clause. This is directed only on the reading with fatḥa of «أنَّ» in «أنَّ الدينَ»; on the reading with kasra it is not permissible, so the first view is the only one.

The pronoun in «أنه» may refer to the Creator, because His mention has preceded, and it may be the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-amr); this is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd): {شَهِدَ الله أَنْ لا إلهَ إلا هو}, where «أَنْ» is the lightened form in this reading, and the lightened form governs only the pronoun of the matter, which is then omitted, and it does not govern anything else except by necessity.

Abū ʿAmr, with disagreement reported from him, assimilated the wāw of «هو» into the wāw of conjunction after it; the verification of this question has preceded in al-Baqara at His saying {هُوَ والذين آمَنُواْ مَعَهُ} [verse 249].

His saying: {قَآئِمَاً بالقسط}: there are four views on its accusative. The first: that it is accusative as a ḥāl; those who said this differed. Some made it a ḥāl from the name of Allah, so the governor in it is «شَهِدَ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is accusative as an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida) from Him, like His saying, Exalted is He: {وَهُوَ الحق مُصَدِّقاً}." The Shaykh said: "It is not of the type of the emphatic ḥāl, because it is not of the type {وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَياً} [Maryam: 15], nor of the type 'I am the servant of Allah, brave'; for «قائماً بالقسط» is not in the sense of «شَهِد», and it is not an emphasis of the content of the preceding sentence, as in: 'I am the servant of Allah, brave' and 'He is Zayd, brave'. But in this analysis there is awkwardness in the construction, since it becomes like your saying: 'Zayd ate food, and ʿĀʾisha and Fāṭima, hungry', separating the conjoined-to from the conjoined by the object, and the ḥāl from its owner by the object and the conjoined; but with the possibility that all of them are governed by one governor." End of quotation.

I say: his criticism of him for his saying "emphatic" is not clear. The ḥāl is of two kinds: emphatic or explanatory (mubayyina), which is the basic one. The explanatory is not possible here, because the explanatory is a changing one, and change here is impossible, since the justice of Allah the Exalted does not change. If it is said that we have a third kind, the inseparable ḥāl (ḥāl lāzima), so al-Zamakhsharī had a way out from his saying "emphatic" to saying "inseparable"; the answer is that every emphatic is inseparable and every inseparable is emphatic, so there is no difference between the two expressions, even though the Shaykh claimed that the correction of the expression is achieved by saying "inseparable". What I mentioned, the mutual accompaniment of emphasis and the inseparable ḥāl, is indicated by induction.

And his saying: "The meaning of «قائماً بالقسط» is not the meaning of «شهد»" is disputed; rather the meaning of «شَهِد» with what it is attached to, namely that there is no god but He, is equivalent to His saying «قائماً بالقسط», because oneness is inseparable from justice.

Then al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why is it permissible to single it out for the accusative ḥāl, without the two conjoined to it, when if you said 'Zayd and ʿAmr came, riding' it would not be permissible? I say: this is permissible only because of the absence of confusion, as it was permissible in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 72], if «نافلةً» is accusative as a ḥāl from «يعقوب». And if you said 'Zayd and Hind came, riding', it would be permissible because of his being distinguished by masculinity."

The Shaykh said: "What he mentioned in his saying 'Zayd and ʿAmr came, riding', that it is not permissible, is not as he said; rather this is permissible, because the ḥāl is a restriction on the one from whom or by whom the action occurred or the like, and when it is a restriction it is taken to refer to the nearest mentioned, and «riding» is a ḥāl from what follows it directly; and there is no difference in that between the ḥāl and the adjective: if you said 'Zayd and ʿAmr the tall came', 'the tall' would be an adjective of ʿAmr; and you would not say that this question is impermissible because of confusion, since there is no confusion in it and it is permissible; and likewise the ḥāl. As for his saying that «نافلةً» is accusative as a ḥāl from Yaʿqūb, it is not necessary that it be a ḥāl from Yaʿqūb, as «نافلةً» may be a maṣdar like ʿāqiba and ʿāfiya, its meaning being 'an addition', so that it covers Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb, because they were added to Ibrāhīm after his son Ismāʿīl and others." I say: al-Zamakhsharī's intention in forbidding 'Zayd and ʿAmr came, riding' is when the ḥāl is meant to be from both together; but when it is meant to be a ḥāl from one of them, it is only given to what follows it, because the pronoun returns to the nearest mentioned. And some made it a ḥāl from «هو». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: you made it a ḥāl from the agent of «شَهِدَ»; is it sound for it to be accusative as a ḥāl from «هو» in «لا إله إلا هو»? I say: yes, because it is an emphatic ḥāl, and the emphatic ḥāl does not require that the sentence whose benefit it adds to have a governor in it, as in your saying: 'I am the servant of Allah, brave'." End of quotation. He means that the governor of the emphatic ḥāl is not anything of the preceding sentence before it; rather it is accusative by an implied governor. If the speaker is reporting about himself, as in "I am the servant of Allah, brave", you would imply: "I am truly (uḥaqqu) brave," in the passive; and if he is reporting about another, you would imply it in the active, as in "This is the servant of Allah, brave", that is, "I affirm him": this is the well-known position on the accusative of such a ḥāl.

In the question there is a second view, of Abū Isḥāq, that the governor in it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, because of the derived meaning it includes, since it is in the sense of "the named". A third view: that the governor in it is the mubtadaʾ, because of the meaning of alerting it includes; it is a long question. And some made it a ḥāl from all, considering each one of them as upholding justice; and this contradicts what al-Zamakhsharī said, that the ḥāl is specific to Allah the Exalted and not what is conjoined to Him. This position is rejected, for if it were permissible, it would be permissible to say "the people came, riding", meaning each one of them riding, and the Arabs do not say that at all, so this is corrupt. These are three views on the owner of the ḥāl.

The second view of the views on the accusative of «قائماً»: its being accusative as naʿt (adjective) of the one negated by lā, as if it were said: "no god upholding justice but He." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: is it permissible that it be an adjective of the negated, as if it were said 'no god upholding justice but He'? I say: it is not remote, for we have seen them be broad in separating the adjective from the described." Then he said: "It is more worthy than its being accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «شَهِد», and likewise its being accusative for praise (madḥ)."

The Shaykh said: Al-Zamakhsharī had given, as an example of separation between the adjective and the described, his saying "no man but ʿAbd Allāh, brave." He said: "What he mentioned is not permissible, because he separated the adjective from the described by a stranger, namely the two conjoined items, which are «والملائكةُ وأولوا العلم»; they are not governed by anything of the sentence «لا إله إلا هو» but are governed by «شَهِدَ». It is like: 'Zayd knew that Hind is leaving, and ʿAmr and Jaʿfar, the Tamīmī', where Hind and 'the Tamīmī' are separated by a stranger that does not enter the domain of what governs them, that stranger being 'and ʿAmr and Jaʿfar', the two nominatives conjoined to Zayd. As for the example he gave, 'no man but ʿAbd Allāh, brave', it is not parallel to his analysis in the verse, because your saying 'but ʿAbd Allāh' is a badal on the place of 'no man', so it is a follower on the place, and not a stranger; besides which there is room for consideration in the permissibility of this construction, because it is a badal while «brave» is an adjective, and the rule is that when the badal and the adjective are combined, the adjective is put first; the reason for that is that the badal is on the intention of repeating the governor, according to the sound view, so it becomes part of another sentence according to this position."

The third view: its accusative for praise. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: is it not the case that what is accusative for praise ought to be definite, as in your saying 'Praise be to Allah, the Praiseworthy' and 'We, the company of prophets, are not inherited from'?"

[And his saying]:

1202 - إنا بني نَهْشَلٍ لا نَدَّعي لأبٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(We, the sons of Nahshal, claim no other father...) [the second half-verse is elided in the source]

I say: it has come indefinite just as it has come definite; and Sībawayh recited, from what came indefinite, the saying of the Hudhalī:

1203 - ويَأْوِي إلى نَسْوةٍ عُطَّّلٍ ... وشُعْثَاً مَراضيعَ مثلَ السَّعالِي
(And he takes refuge with unadorned women, and dishevelled, nursing mothers, like ghouls.)

End of quotation.

The Shaykh said: "This question and its answer have ended, and there is confusion in it, in that he did not distinguish between what is accusative for praise, blame or compassion, and what is accusative for specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), and made their ruling one; and he cited one example of the accusative for praise, namely 'Praise be to Allah, the Praiseworthy', and two examples of the accusative for specification, namely 'We, the company of prophets, are not inherited from' and 'We, the sons of Nahshal, claim no other father'. What the grammarians mentioned is that what is accusative for praise, blame or compassion may be definite, with a definite noun before it that is suitable to be followed by it, or may not be suitable; and it may be indefinite likewise; and it may be indefinite with a definite noun before it such that it is not suitable as an adjective of it, as in the saying of al-Nābigha:

1204 - أََقارعُ عَوْفٍ لا أُحاولُ غيرَها ... وجوهَ قرودٍ تَبْتَغي مَنْ تجادِعُ
(Those who wrangle with ʿAwf, I seek nothing else of them, faces of apes looking for whom to mutilate.)

where «وجوه قرود» is accusative for blame, with a definite noun before it, namely «أقارع عوف». As for what is accusative for specification, they stated explicitly that it is neither indefinite nor vague; it is only definite, by the article or by annexation or by being a proper name or the word «أي», and it comes only after a pronoun specific to it or shared by it, and perhaps after a pronoun of the addressee." I say: al-Zamakhsharī intended by "accusative for specification" only what is accusative by a suitable implied verb, whether it is of the specification which has a chapter in grammar or not, and this is the terminology of the people of the sciences of meanings and bayān; and attention to this has preceded more than once.

The fourth view: its accusative by severance (qaṭʿ), that is, it was proper for it to be nominative as an adjective of Allah the Exalted after its being made definite with the article, the original being: "Allah, the Upholder of justice, bore witness"; and when it was made indefinite, following it became impossible, so it was severed to the accusative. This is the position of the Kufans, and some transmitted it from al-Farrāʾ alone; among it, in their view, is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

1205 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وعالَيْن قِنْوَاناً من البُسْر أحمرا
(...and they lifted a cluster of red unripe dates.)

The original being: "of the red unripe dates"; this has preceded with verification. Supporting this position is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «القائم بالقسط», with nominative on «القائم» as a follower of the Name. Al-Zamakhsharī and others analyzed it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "He is the Upholder", [or a badal of «هو»]. The Shaykh said: "That is not permissible, because it contains a separation between the badal and what it substitutes for by a stranger, namely the two conjoined items, since they are governed by other than the governor in what is substituted for; and even if the governor in the conjoined were the governor in what is substituted for, that would also not be permissible, because when conjunction and badal are combined, the badal is put before the conjunction; if you said 'Zayd and ʿĀʾisha, your brother, came' it would not be permissible; the speech is only 'Zayd, your brother, and ʿĀʾisha came'."

So in the nominative of «القائم» on this reading three views result: naʿt, badal, and khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. It was also transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh that he read «قائمٌ بالقسط» indefinite, with its nominative in the two views of badal and khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

Abū Ḥanīfa read: «قَيِّماً» in the accusative, as preceded. These are four views that I have refined from the speech of the people.

The apparent sense is that the nominative of «الملائكة» and what follows is conjoined to the Majestic Name. Some of them said: "The speech is complete at His saying {لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}, and «الملائكة» is nominative by an implied verb, its implied form being: 'and the angels and those of knowledge testified to that.'" It is as if this proponent sees that the testimony of Allah differs from the testimony of the angels and those of knowledge, and does not permit the use of a shared word in both its meanings, so for this reason he needed to imply a verb that agrees with this utterance in wording and differs from it in meaning; and the like of this comes in His saying, Exalted is He: {إِنَّ الله وَمَلاَئِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى النبي} [al-Aḥzāb: 56]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: does His upholding of justice enter into the ruling of the testimony of Allah, the angels and those of knowledge, as oneness entered? I say: yes, if you make it a ḥāl from «هو», or accusative for praise from it, or an adjective of the negated, as if it were said: 'Allah, the angels and those of knowledge bore witness that there is no god but He and that He upholds justice.'"

His saying: {لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}: in this sentence there are two views. The first: that it is repeated for emphasis. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why did He repeat His saying {لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}? I say: He mentioned it first to indicate His specificity in oneness, and that there is no god but that distinguished Essence; then He mentioned it a second time after joining to the affirmation of oneness the affirmation of justice, to indicate His specificity in the two matters, as if He said: 'There is no god but He, who is described by the two attributes'; and for that reason He joined to it His saying {العزيز الحكيم}, because they include the meaning of oneness and justice."

Some of them said: "It is not a repetition; because the first is the testimony of Allah the Exalted alone, and the second is the testimony of the angels and those of knowledge." This is, as preceded, according to the one who makes «الملائكة» nominative by another implied verb, for what I mentioned, that he does not hold the use of a shared word, and that the two testimonies are different; and it is a weaker position. Al-Rāghib said: "He repeated «لا إله إلا هو» only because the attributes of transcendence (tanzīh) are nobler than the attributes of glorification (tamjīd), because most of their words are shared by the servants, so they may be described by them; and for that reason the words of transcendence came more and with more eloquence concerning Him."

His saying: {العزيز الحكيم}: it has three views. The first: that it is a badal of «هو». The second: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. The third: that it is a naʿt of «هو»; and this works only on the position of al-Kisāʾī, who holds that the detached third-person pronoun may be described, and the like of this has preceded in His saying: {لاَّ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ الرحمن الرحيم} [al-Baqara: 163].

semin-durr:144-144.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلاَّ رَسُولٌ}: «ما» is negative and has no governing effect here at all, I mean in the dialect of both the Hijazis and the Tamīmīs, because the Tamīmīs do not make it govern at all, while the Hijazis make it govern under conditions, among them that the negation not be broken by «إلا», since the reason for which it governed disappears, namely its resemblance to «ليس» in negating the present. So «محمد» is a mubtadaʾ and «رسول» its khabar. This is the view of the majority, I mean that it is not made to govern when its negation is broken. Yūnus permitted its governing even with the negation broken by «إلاَّ», and recited:

1452 - وما الدهرُ إلا منجَنوناً بأهلِه ... وما صاحبُ الحاجات إلا مُعَذَّبا
(Time is nothing but a mill-wheel with its people, and the man of needs is nothing but tormented.)

So he put «منجنوناً» and «مُعَذَباً» in the accusative as the khabar of «ما», though they come after «إلاَ». Similar is the saying of another:

[Translator's note: the source numbers this verse "1543"; the sequence indicates 1453.]
1543 - وما حَقُّ الذي يَعْتُو نهاراً ... ويَسْرِقُ ليلَه إلاَّ نَكالا
(The due of one who commits excess by day and steals by night is nothing but exemplary punishment.)

So «حق» is the ism of «ما» and «نَكالاً» its khabar. The majority interpreted these citations as meaning that the khabar is omitted and this accusative is governed by that omitted khabar, the estimate being: "Time is nothing but revolving with the revolving of a mill-wheel", so the verb that governs «دوران» in the accusative was dropped, then the muḍāf was dropped and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place in i'rab. Likewise «إلا معذباً», its estimate being "he is tormented with torment (tuʿadhdhabu taʿdhīban)": the verb was dropped and «مُعَذَّباً» put in the place of «تَعْذيب», as in his saying {وَمَزَّقْنَاهُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ} [Sabaʾ: 19], i.e. every tearing apart; and likewise «إلا نكالاً». And in it is the strain you see.

His saying: {قَدْ خَلَتْ}: there are two views on this sentence. The more evident: that it is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of «رسولِ». The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «رسول»; and there is something to consider in it, because this attribute runs the course of inert nouns (jawāmid), so it does not carry a pronoun.

And «من قبله»: there are also two views on it. One: that it is attached to «خَلَتْ». The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «الرسل», put before it, and it is then a confirming ḥāl, since the mention of passing away signals priority. Ibn ʿAbbās read «رسُل» as indefinite. Abū al-Fatḥ said: "Its aspect is that it is a place of giving good tidings regarding the matter of the Prophet ﷺ in the matter of life, and a place of equating him with mankind in that, and this is done in places of moderation, like {وَقَلِيلٌ مِّنْ عِبَادِيَ الشكور} [Sabaʾ: 13] and {وَمَآ آمَنَ مَعَهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ} [Hūd: 40]." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is close to the meaning of the definite", as if he means that what is intended by "the messengers" is the genus, so the indefinite is close to it in that respect. The reading of the majority is better because it indicates the exaltation and veneration of the messengers.

His saying: {أَفإِنْ مَّاتَ}: the hamza is for the interrogative of rebuke, and the fāʾ is for conjunction, its rank being to come first because it is a conjunction particle; the hamza was put first only because it has the head of the speech; the verification of that has already been given, and that al-Zamakhsharī estimates between them an omitted verb to which the fāʾ conjoins what follows it.

Ibn Khaṭīb Zamalkā said: "The most apt is to estimate an omitted element after the hamza and before the fāʾ, the fāʾ being a conjunction upon it; had it been made explicit it would have been said: 'Do you believe in him during his lifetime, then if he dies you apostatize, and so contravene the ways of the followers of the prophets before you in their steadfastness upon the creeds of their prophets after their deaths?'" This is the school of al-Zamakhsharī, except that al-Zamakhsharī here expressed himself in a way that does not require his school, which is the omission of a sentence after the hamza, for he said: "The fāʾ attaches the conditional sentence to the sentence before it in the sense of causation, and the hamza is for denying that they make the passing away of the messengers before him a cause for their turning back on their heels after his perishing by death or killing, while they know that the passing away of the messengers before him and the survival of their religion, held to, ought to be made a cause for holding fast to the religion of Muḥammad ﷺ, not for turning away from it." The apparent meaning of this statement is that the fāʾ conjoined this sentence containing the rebuke to what precedes it, namely {قَدْ خَلَتْ}, without estimating another sentence.

Abū al-Baqāʾ said something close to this, for he said: "The hamza, according to Sībawayh, is in its place, and the fāʾ indicates the connection of the condition with what precedes it." End. It should not be said that his putting the hamza "in its place" suggests that the fāʾ is not placed before it, because he made this the counterpart of Yūnus's school; Yūnus claims that this hamza in a construction like this enters upon the apodosis, so it is, in his school, not in its place. The verification of all this will come.

«إنْ» is conditional; «ماتَ» and «انقلبتم» are protasis and apodosis, and the hamza's entering upon the conditional particle changes nothing of its ruling. Yūnus claimed that the second verb, which is the apodosis, is not an apodosis of the condition but is what is being asked about, the hamza entering upon it by estimate, so it is intended to be put first, and it is then not an answer but the answer is omitted; and it is necessary then that the verb of the condition be past, since the answer is not omitted unless the condition is past, and poetry is not taken into account, being necessity. So it is not permissible according to him to say «أإنْ تُكْرِمْنِي أُكْرِمْك» [neither with both jussive nor with the first jussive and the second nominative] because the condition is imperfect; nor «أإن أكرمتني أكرمْك» with «أكرمْك» jussive, since it is not the answer but indicates it, and it is intended to be put first; but if you make «أكرمك» nominative and say «أإنْ أكرَمْتَني أكرمُك» it is sound according to him. So the estimate according to Yūnus is: «آنقلبتم على أعقابِكم إنْ ماتَ محمدٌ؟» ("Will you turn back on your heels if Muḥammad dies?") since the aim is rebuke of their turning back on their heels after his death.

Many of the exegetes said what Yūnus said, for they say: the alif of interrogation entered not in its place, because the aim is only: "Will you turn back if Muḥammad dies?" Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Yūnus said: the hamza in the like of this ought to enter upon the apodosis, its estimate being «أتنقلبون إنْ مات», because the aim is warning or reproach for this conditioned act. But the school of Sībawayh is the right one for two reasons. One: that if you put the answer first, the fāʾ would have no basis, since it is not sound to say «أتزورُوني فإنْ زُرْتُكِ»; and from it is His saying, the Exalted, {أَفَإِنْ مِّتَّ فَهُمُ الخالدون} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 34]. The second: that the hamza has the head of the speech and «إنْ» has the head of the speech, so both occurred in their places, and the meaning is complete with the hamza's entering upon the sentence of condition and answer, because the two are like one thing." End. The grammarians have rebutted Yūnus with His saying {أَفَإِنْ مِّتَّ فَهُمُ الخالدون}, for the fāʾ in «فهم» necessitates that it be the apodosis of the condition. This matter has a place more fitting for it than this book. And here He used «إنْ», which indicates doubt, while death is an established matter, but it was brought in the manner of the doubted because of the wavering between death and being killed.

His saying: {على أَعْقَابِكُمْ}: two views. The more evident: that it is attached to «انقلبتم». The second: that it is a ḥāl from the fāʾil of «انقلبتم», as if it were said: "you turned back returning". Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «ومَنْ ينقلِبْ على عَقِبه» in the singular. And «شيئاً» is accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. something of harm, neither little nor much. The like of it has already gone before.

semin-durr:145-145.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تَمُوتَ}: «أَنْ تموتَ» is in the position of the nominative as the ism of «كان»; and «لنفس» is a fronted khabar, attached to an omitted element; and {إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِ الله} is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «تموت», attached to an omitted element; it is a complete exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), the estimate being: "and it was not for it to die except being permitted", the bāʾ being that of accompaniment.

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: {إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِ الله} is the khabar, and the lām is explicative, attached to «كان». It is also said that it is attached to an omitted element, the estimate being "death is for a soul", and «أن تموت» an explication of the omitted; and it is not permissible for the lām to be attached to «تموت», because of the fronting of the ṣila before the relative. Some said that «كان» is redundant, so «أَنْ تموتَ» would be a mubtadaʾ and «لنفسٍ» its khabar. Al-Zajjāj said: "Its estimate: «وما كانت نفسٌ لتموتَ», then the lām was put first", so he made what was the ism of «كان», namely «أن تموتَ», a khabar of it, and what was the khabar, namely «لنفسٍ», its ism. These are five statements, the most evident being the first.

As for Abū al-Baqāʾ's saying "the lām is explicative and so is attached to an omitted element", there is something to consider in it from two aspects. One: the incomplete «كان» does not govern anything other than its ism and khabar; and even if that is granted, the explicative lām is only attached to an omitted element, as they have stated explicitly in the like of «سُقياً لك». As for the one who made «لنفسٍ» attached to an omitted element whose estimate is «الموتُ لنفسٍ», it is invalid, because he claimed the omission of something not permissible; for whether he makes «كان» complete or incomplete, omitting its nominative is impossible, since the fāʿil is not omitted; also in it is the omission of the maṣdar while retaining its object, which is not permissible. Likewise the statement of the one who made «كان» redundant. As for the statement of al-Zajjāj, it is an explanation of meaning, not of i'rab, so the statements return to four.

His saying: {كِتَاباً مُّؤَجَّلاً}: there are three views on its being accusative. The most evident: that it is a confirming maṣdar of the content of the sentence before it, so its governor is implied, its estimate being «كَتَب الله ذلك كتاباً» ("Allah decreed that as a decree"), like {صُنْعَ الله} [al-Naml: 88], {وَعْدَ الله} [al-Nisāʾ: 122] and {كِتَابَ الله عَلَيْكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 24]. The second: that it is accusative as tamyīz (specification); Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned it, and this is not right, because tamyīz is either transformed or not transformed, and its types are limited, and this is none of them; also, where is the vague entity that needs explanation? The third: that it is accusative as incitement (ighrāʾ), the estimate being "keep to a term-fixed decree and believe in the decree (qadar)", and the meaning is not so.

Warsh read «مُوَجَّلاً» with wāw in place of the hamza, which is the analogical form of its lightening.

His saying: {وَمَن يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ}: «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ and is conditional. On the khabar of this mubtadaʾ there is the well-known disagreement. Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Ibn ʿĀmir, with a variation from him, assimilated the دال of «يُرِدْ» into the ثاء, and the rest pronounced it distinctly.

Abū ʿAmr read with sukūn on the hāʾ of «نؤتيه» in both places, in waṣl and waqf; Qālūn and Hishām, with a variation from him, with ikhtilās (partial vowel) in waṣl; and the rest with full extension (ishbāʿ) in waṣl. As for the sukūn, they said: when the hāʾ took the place of that omitted letter it was given what the latter deserved, namely sukūn. As for the ikhtilās, it is to retain what the hāʾ was upon before the lām of the word was dropped, for the origin is «نُؤتيه»; the yāʾ was dropped for the jussive and this incidental was not counted, so the hāʾ remained as it was. As for the ishbāʿ, it is with regard to the wording, because the hāʾ comes after a vowelled letter in the wording, though in origin it was after a quiescent, the yāʾ that was dropped for the jussive. It is better to say that ikhtilās and sukūn after a vowelled letter is an established dialect of Banū ʿUqayl and Banū Kilāb; al-Kisāʾī related: «لَهْ مالٌ وبِهْ داءٌ» with sukūn on the hāʾ, and the ikhtilās of its vowel. By this it is clear that the statement of whoever said "sukūn of the hāʾ and its ikhtilās in this sort is not permitted except by necessity" is nothing. As for others than Banū ʿUqayl and Banū Kilāb, yes, it is not found among them except in necessity, as in his saying:

1454 - لَهُ زَجَلٌ كأنَّهُ صَوْتُ حادٍ ... إذا طَلَبَ الوسيقَةَ أو زميرُ
(It has a shout as if it were the voice of a camel-driver when he pursues the stolen herd, or a piping.)

with ikhtilās of the hāʾ of «كأنه», and the saying of another:

1455 - وأشربُ الماءَ ما بي نحوه عَطَشٌ ... إلاَّ لأنَّ عيونَهْ سَيْلُ وادِيها
(I drink the water though I have no thirst for it, except that its springs are the flood of its valley.)

with sukūn. Ibn ʿUṣfūr held that necessity in the second verse is better than in the first, saying: "because it is the removal of the vowel and its extension, so it is a complete application of necessity." I mentioned these justifications only because of the frequent occurrence of this issue, like {يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ} [al-Zumar: 7] and {فَبِهُدَاهُمُ اقتده} [al-Anʿām: 90]. It was also read «يُؤْتِه» with the third-person yāʾ, the pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, and likewise {وَسَيَجْزِي الشاكرين} with nūn and with yāʾ.

semin-durr:117-117.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَثَلُ مَا يُنْفِقُونَ}: «ما» may be a relative noun, and its returning pronoun is omitted because the conditions are met, i.e. «ينفقونه».

His saying {كَمَثَلِ رِيحٍ} is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
