Fifth: that the governing element is either «سميع» or «عليم», by way of tanāzuʿ (competition between two governors), the matter then being one where the second is applied, since had the first been applied, a pronoun would have been placed in the second and nothing omitted from it, as you have known more than once.
al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or the meaning of «سميع عليم» governs it." The Shaykh said: "This is not precisely stated, because the governing element is not composed of two adjectives; the precise statement is that the meaning of «سميع» or «عليم» governs it, and the matter is one of tanāzuʿ." I say: al-Zamakhsharī meant by that only what I mentioned, the intention of tanāzuʿ; and it is valid to say that this and that govern it, in the sense mentioned, not that they governed it together; though even if that were said, he would not have invented a view, since al-Farrāʾ holds that, and says, in the case of «ضربت وأكرمت زيداً», that «زيداً» is accusative by both and that they both act on it together; and for refining this question there is another place in which I have worked it out, praise be to Allah the Exalted.

al-Hamm is resolve. It is also said that it is less than that, because the first thing that stirs in a person's heart is called a khāṭir (passing thought); when it strengthens it is called ḥadīth nafs (inner speech); when it strengthens it is called hamm; when it strengthens it is called ʿazm (resolve); and after it comes either speech or action. Some express hamm as "intention" (irāda). The Arabs say hamamtu bi-kadhā ahummu bihi, with ḍamma on the hāʾ, and one says «هَمْتُ» with a single mīm, dropping one of the two mīms for lightness, as they said mastu, ẓaltu and ḥastu for masastu, ẓalaltu and ḥasastu; but this is not regular. al-Hamm is also grief that melts its possessor, taken from their saying «هَمَمْتُ الشحم», i.e. I melted the fat. The concern that is in the soul is close to it, because it may affect a person's soul as grief does, and for that the poet said:
1421 - وَهمُّك ما لم تُمْضِه لك مُنْصِبٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Your concern, so long as you do not carry it out, is a source of exhaustion for you …) [Translator's note: the second half is elided in the source.]
that is: when you are concerned about something and do not do it, and it circles in your mind, you are in weariness from it until you accomplish it.

His saying: {أَن تَفْشَلاَ} is attached to «هَمَّتْ», because it takes the bāʾ; the original is «بأن تفشلا», so for the position of «أَنْ» the two well-known aspects apply. al-Fashal is cowardice and weakness. Some said: "Fashal in opinion is incapacity; in the body, exhaustion and inability to rise; in war, cowardice and weakness." The verb from it is fashila with kasra on the ʿayn, and tafāshala l-māʾ when the water flows.
His saying {وَعَلَى الله} is attached to His saying «فَلْيتوكل»; it is put first for restriction and to harmonise with the verse-endings. The discussion of a fāʾ like this has been given earlier. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The fāʾ entered with the meaning of condition, the meaning being: if they are cowardly, then you rely [on Allah]; or if the matter becomes difficult, then rely."

semin-durr:147-147.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ}: The majority read «قولَهم» in the accusative as a fronted khabar, the ism being «أَنْ» and what is in its scope, its estimate being: "and their saying was nothing but this their saying, the supplication", i.e. it was their habit and custom. Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim, in a narration from them, read «قولُهم» in the nominative as the ism, the khabar being «أَنْ» and what is in its scope. The reading of the majority is better, because when two definites come together, it is better to make the more definite the ism, and «أن» with what is in its scope is more definite; they said: because it resembles the pronoun in that it is not made a pronoun, not described and not used to describe; whereas «قولهم» is annexed to a pronoun, so it is at the rank of a proper name, which is less definite.

Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred the reading of the majority for two reasons, one of them this, and the other that what comes after «إلاَّ» is affirmed, and the meaning is: their saying "Our Lord, forgive us" was their habit in supplication, and that is good; and the meaning is: "their saying was nothing of sayings except this particular saying."

And {في أَمْرِنَا}: two views are possible. One: that it is attached to the maṣdar before it; one says "asraftu fī kadhā" (I was excessive in such and such). The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from it, i.e. "while it is resting in our affair"; the first is the more apt.

semin-durr:148-148.t: Al-Jaḥdarī read {فأثابهم}: from the wording of al-thawāb (reward).

semin-durr:149-149.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {يَرُدُّوكُمْ}: the apodosis of {إِن تُطِيعُواْ}. And {خَاسِرِينَ} is a ḥāl.

semin-durr:150-150.t: His saying, the Exalted: {بَلِ الله مَوْلاَكُمْ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar. Al-Ḥasan read «اللهَ» with the Majestic Name in the accusative, by an implied verb indicated by the first condition, the estimate being: "Do not obey those who disbelieve; rather obey Allah." And {مَوْلاَكُمْ} is its description. Makkī said: "Al-Farrāʾ permitted «بل اللهَ» in the accusative," as if he had not been informed that it is a reading.

semin-durr:151-151.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سَنُلْقِي}: The majority read with the nūn of majesty, and it is an iltifāt (shift) from the third person in His saying {وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الناصرين}, in order to draw attention to the greatness of what the Exalted casts. Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī read «سيُلقي» in the third person, following the original. The genitive phrase was put before the direct object out of concern for mentioning the place before mentioning the one that settles in it. Al-ilqāʾ (casting) here is figurative, because its origin concerns solid bodies, so it is borrowed here, as in his saying:

1463 - هما نَفَثا في فِيِّ مِنْ فَمَوَيْهِما ... على النابحِ العاوي أشدُّ رِجامِ
(The two of them spat into my mouth from their two mouths, upon the barking, howling one, the most violent of stonings.)

Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read «الرُّعُب» and «رُعُباً» with ḍamma, and the rest with sukūn. It is said that they are two dialects; and it is said that the origin is ḍamma and it was lightened, and this is a regular analogy; and it is said that the origin is sukūn and it was given ḍamma by assimilation, like al-ṣubḥ and al-ṣubuḥ, and this is the reverse of what is known in the speech of the Arabs.

[And al-ruʿb: fear. One says raʿabtuhu, so he is marʿūb, and its origin is from filling; one says raʿabtu al-ḥawḍ, i.e. I filled it, and sayl rāʿib, i.e. one that filled the valley. And al-sulṭān: the proof and demonstration, and its derivation is either from salīṭ, the oil of the lamp by which it is lit . . . . . ., for its illumination and clarity, or from al-salāṭa, which is sharpness and domination.] [Note: this paragraph is in square brackets in the source, with an ellipsis where the text is evidently incomplete.]

And {فِي قُلُوبِ} is attached to the casting. Likewise {بِمَآ أَشْرَكُواْ}; and the attachment of the two prepositions does no harm because of the difference of their meanings, since «في» is locative and the bāʾ causal. «ما» is a maṣdar particle. The second «ما» is the direct object of «أشْركوا», and it is a relative in the sense of «الذي» or an indefinite described noun. The returning pronoun is the hāʾ in «به»; and it cannot be a maṣdar particle according to the majority, because of the pronoun's referring back to it. The negation bears on the sending down in wording, while what is intended is the negation of authority (sulṭān), i.e. proof, as if it were said: "there is no authority for associating, so that it might be sent down," as in his saying:

1464 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا تَرَى الضَبَّ بها يَنْجَحِرْ
(... and you do not see the lizard burrowing in it.)

i.e. the lizard does not burrow there so that it might be seen; and his saying:

1465 - على لاحِبٍ لا يُهْتَدَى بمَنارِه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(On a clear road, which is not guided by its marker ...)

i.e. it has no marker by which one might be guided; so the meaning is the negation of the authority and of the sending down together. And «سلطاناً» is an object of «يُنَزِّل».

And His saying {وَبِئْسَ مثوى الظالمين}: the one specified for dispraise is omitted, i.e. "their abode" or "the Fire". Al-mathwā is a mafʿal from thawaytu, i.e. I stayed, so its lām is a yāʾ. The ma'wā, which is the place to which a person repairs, was put before al-mathwā, which is the place of staying, because in the order of existence he first repairs and then stays, and repairing does not necessarily entail staying, unlike the converse.

semin-durr:152-152.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {صَدَقَكُمُ}: «صَدَقَ» takes two objects, one by itself and the other by a preposition, which may be omitted, as in this verse, the estimate being: "He was true to you in His promise", like their saying «صدقتُه الحديث» and «في الحديث» ("I told him the truth in the report"). And «إذ تَحُسُّونهم» is governed by «صَدَقَكم», i.e. He was true to you at that time, which is the time of your killing them (ḥassihim). Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be governed by the promise in His saying «وعدَه», and there is something to consider in it because the promise precedes this time. One says «حَسَسْتُه أَحُسُّه», i.e. I killed him. Abū ʿUbayd read «تُحِسُّونهم» in the quadriliteral form, i.e. you removed their sense (ḥiss) by killing. And «بإذنه» is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «تُحِسُّونهم», i.e. you were killing them with permission given you in that.

His saying: {حتى إِذَا فَشِلْتُمْ}: there are two views on this «حتى». The first: that it is a preposition in the sense of «إلى» (until), and there are then three views on what it is attached to. One: that it is attached to «تَحُسُّونهم», i.e. you were killing them until this time. The second: that it is attached to «صدقكم», which is the apparent meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's statement; he said: "The meaning may be: 'Allah was true to you in His promise until the time of your faltering.'" The third: that it is attached to an omitted element indicated by the context; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "its estimate is: 'that continued for you until the time of your faltering.'"

The second view: that it is a particle of commencement (ḥarf ibtidāʾ) entering upon the conditional sentence, «إذا» being in its normal sense of conditional, and there are then three views on its apodosis. One: that it is «وتنازعتم»; al-Farrāʾ said: "and the wāw would be redundant." The second: that it is «ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُم», with «ثُمَّ» redundant; these two statements are very weak. The third, which is the sound one: that it is omitted, and their wordings differ in its estimate. Ibn ʿAṭiyya estimated it as «انهزمتم» ("you were routed"); al-Zamakhsharī estimated it as «مَنَعَكم نَصْرَه» ("He withheld His help from you"); Abū al-Baqāʾ estimated it as «بان لكم أمرُكم» ("your affair became clear to you"), indicated by His saying {مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ الآخرة}; others estimated it as «امتُحِنْتُم» ("you were tested"); and the Shaykh estimated it as «انقسمتم إلى قسمين» ("you split into two groups"), indicated by what follows it, and it is parallel to {فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى البر فَمِنْهُمْ مُّقْتَصِدٌ} [Luqmān: 32]. The Shaykh said: "It is not to be said: how can it be said 'you split into one who wants this world and one who wants the Hereafter' concerning those who faltered, disputed and disobeyed? Because these acts did not issue from all of them but from some of them."

They differed about this «إذا»: is it in its normal sense or in the sense of «إذ»? The sound view is the first, whether we say it is conditional or not.

His saying: {ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ}: conjoined to what precedes it, and the two sentences {مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ الآخرة} are parenthetical between the two conjoined elements. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ثم صرفكم» is conjoined to the omitted verb", meaning the one he estimated as the apodosis of the condition; and there is no need for it. «وليبتليَكم» is attached to «صرفكم», and «أََنْ» is implied after the lām.

semin-durr:154-154.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَمَنَةً نُّعَاساً}: There are four aspects regarding the accusative of each. The first of the aspects of «أَمَنَةً»: that it is the object of «أَنْزَل». The second: that it is a ḥāl from «نُعاساً», because it is originally an adjective of an indefinite noun, and when it was put first it became accusative as a ḥāl. The third: that it is an object of purpose, and this is invalid because a condition is violated, namely the identity of the agent, for the agent of «أَنْزل» is not the agent of the security. The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from the persons addressed in «عليكم», and there are then two interpretations of it: either on the omission of a muḍāf, that is "possessors of security", or that «أَمَنَةً» is a plural of «آمِن», like bārr and bararah, kāfir and kafarah.
As for «نُعاساً»: if we parse «أمنةً» as a direct object, it is a badal, a badal of inclusion, because each of security and drowsiness includes the other; or an ʿaṭf bayān according to other than the majority, for they do not require its occurring in definite nouns; or an object of purpose, which is invalid for the reason preceding. If we parse «أمنةً» as a ḥāl, it is an object of «أَنْزل», conjoined to His saying «فأثابكم», and its agent is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, and the «أل» in «الغمّ» is for a known reference, because it was mentioned earlier.
The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) rejected from al-Zamakhsharī the making of «أمنةً» an object of purpose by what preceded, and there is room for objection in that, for al-Zamakhsharī said: "or an object of purpose, in the sense: you dozed for security", so he implied for it an operator whose agent is identical with the agent of «أمنةً»; it is as though he sensed the question, and therefore implied an operator. Moreover it may be said that the security is from Allah the Exalted, in the sense that He brought it upon them, as though it were said: "He sent down drowsiness upon you in order to give you security by it"; and «أمنة», as it can be a maṣdar for the one upon whom security occurs, can be a maṣdar for the one who brings it about.
The [majority read «أَمَنَةً» with fatḥa on the mīm: either as a maṣdar meaning security, or as the plural of «آمِن» as detailed earlier. Al-Nakhaʿī and Ibn Muḥayṣin] read it with sukūn on the mīm, and it is a maṣdar only; both are of the single-instance (marra) pattern.
His saying: {يغشى}: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read it with the tāʾ from above, and the rest with the yāʾ from below. They analysed the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī as an adjective of «أمَنَة», taking it into account. A detail is necessary: if they parse «نُعاساً» as a badal or ʿaṭf bayān, their statement is problematic in two respects. One: that the grammarians stated explicitly that when an adjective and a badal or ʿaṭf bayān come together, the adjective is put first and the other later; here they put the badal or ʿaṭf bayān before it. The second: that what is known in the language of the Arabs is that one speaks of the badal, not of the thing substituted for; you say "Hind, her beauty is bewitching (fātin)", and "fātina" is not permissible except rarely. So their making «نُعاساً» a badal for «أمنة» is weakened by this. If it is said: taking the substituted-for into account has come in the saying:
1471 - فكأنه لَهِقُ السَّراةِ كأنه ... ما حاجِبَيْهِ مُعَيَّنٌ بِسَوادِ
(As though it were white-backed, as though its two eyebrows were marked with blackness.)
so he said «مُعَيَّن» taking into account the hāʾ in «كأنه», and did not take into account the badal, which is «حاجبيه»; and likewise his saying:
1472 - إنَّ السيوفَ غُدُوَّها ورَواحَها ... تَرَكَتْ هوازنَ مثلَ قَرْن الأعْضَبِ
(The swords, their morning and evening raids, left Hawāzin like the horn of the broken-horned one.)
so he said «تَرَكَتْ» taking the swords into account, and had he taken the badal into account he would have said "tarakā". The answer: this, though some grammarians held it relying on these two verses, is interpreted as: «مُعَيَّن» is a khabar about «حاجبيه», because the two run in the course of a single thing in the speech of the Arabs, and the accusative of «غدوها ورواحها» is as an adverb, not as a badal. Something of this has preceded with us at His saying: {عَلَى الملكين بِبَابِلَ هَارُوتَ وَمَارُوتَ} [البقرة: 102].
If they parse «نُعاساً» as an object of purpose, separation between the adjective and the qualified by the object of purpose becomes necessary; likewise if they parse «نعاساً» as a direct object and «أَمَنَةً» as a ḥāl, separation is also necessary, and there is room for objection in its permissibility. The better then is that this sentence be resumptive, an answer to an implied question, as though it were said: "What is the status of this security?" and He informed with His saying «تَغْشى». And whoever read with the yāʾ returned the pronoun to «نُعاساً», and the sentence is an adjective of it. «منكم» is an adjective of «طائفة», so it is attached to an omitted word.
His saying: {وَطَآئِفَةٌ قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ}: There are three aspects regarding this wāw. One: that it is the wāw of ḥāl, and what follows it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, and the operator in it is «يغشى». The second: that it is the wāw of resumption, which Makkī called the wāw of inception. The third: that it has the meaning of «إذ»; Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is weak. «طائفةٌ» is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is «قد أَهَمَّتْهُمْ أنفسُهم». Beginning with an indefinite noun is permissible for one of two reasons: either because of relying on the wāw of ḥāl, which some counted as a justifier, although most did not mention it, and he cited:
1473 - سَرَيْنا ونجمٌ قد أضاءَ فمذْ بدا ... مُحيِّاكِ أَخْفَى ضَوْءُه كلَّ شارِقِ
(We travelled by night, a star having shone; and when your face appeared, its light hid every rising star.)
or because the place is a place of itemisation, for the meaning is: "it overcame one group, and another group it did not overcome", so it is like his saying:
1474 - إذا ما بكى مِنْ خَلْفِها انصرَفَتْ له ... بشِقٍّ وشِقٌّ عندنا لم يُحَوَّلِ
(When he cried behind her, she turned to him with one half, while the other half with us was not turned.)
If «طائفةً» were read in the accusative, the matter being of the chapter of preoccupation (ishtighāl), it would not be impossible except from the standpoint of transmission, for I do not know it preserved as a reading.
There are four aspects regarding the khabar of this mubtadaʾ. One: that it is «قد أَهَمَّتْهُم», as has preceded. Second: that it is «يظنون», the sentence before it being an adjective of «طائفة». Third: that it is omitted, that is, "and among you is a group"; this strengthens that its meaning is itemisation, and the two sentences are two adjectives of «طائفة», or «يظنون» is a ḥāl from the object of «أهمَّتْهم», or from «طائفة» because of its specification by the adjective, or a khabar after a khabar if we say that «قد أهمتهم» is a first khabar; and in it is the disagreement that has passed more than once.
Fourth: that the khabar is «يقولون», and the two sentences before it are as has preceded of their being two adjectives or two khabars, or one a khabar and the other a ḥāl; and «يقولون» may also be an adjective or a ḥāl if we say that the khabar is the sentence before it, or we say that the khabar is implied.
His saying: {يَظُنُّونَ}: it has two objects. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «غيرَ الحق» is the first object, that is: "a matter other than the truth", and «بالله» is the second object. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «غير الحق» is in the ruling of a maṣdar, and its meaning is: "they think of Allah other than the truth that should be thought of Him", and «ظنَّ الجاهلِية» is a badal of it; and it is possible that the meaning be "they think of Allah the thinking of the Jāhiliyya", and «غيرَ الحق» an emphasis for «يظنون», like your saying "this saying is other than what you say". On what he said, «ظنَّ» is not transitive to two objects, but the bāʾ is locative of the thinking, like your saying "ṭanantu bi-Zaydin", that is, "I made him the place of my thought". On this meaning the grammarians understood the saying:
1475 - فقلت لهم ظُنُّوا بألفَيْ مُدَجَّجٍ ... سَراتُهمُ في الفارسِيِّ المُسَرَّدِ
(I said to them: Think of two thousand armed men, whose chiefs are in the woven Persian mail.)
that is: place your thought in two thousand armed men. In the accusative of «غير الحق» there are two aspects: one, that it is the first object of «يظنون»; the second, that it is a maṣdar emphasising the sentence before it, in the two senses mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī.
In the accusative of «ظنَّ الجاهليةَ» there are also two aspects: a badal from «غيرَ الحق», or a maṣdar emphasising «يظنون»; and «بالله» is either attached to an omitted word, making it a second object, or to the verb of thinking, as has preceded. As for the annexation of «الظن» to «الجاهلية», al-Zamakhsharī said: "like your saying 'Ḥātim of generosity', and 'a man of truthfulness'", he meaning the thinking specific to the Jāhiliyya religion; and it may be meant: the thinking of the people of the Jāhiliyya. Others said: "The meaning is: the Jāhiliyya period, that is, the ancient one before Islam, like 'the zeal of the Jāhiliyya'."
His saying: {هَل لَّنَا مِنَ الأمر مِن شَيْءٍ}: «مِن» in «من شيء» is redundant on the mubtadaʾ, and there are two views about the khabar; the soundest is that it is «لنا», so «من الأمر» would be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from «شيء», because it is an adjective of an indefinite noun put before it, so it becomes accusative as a ḥāl; and it is attached to an omitted word. The second, allowed by Abū l-Baqāʾ: that «من الأمر» is the khabar and «لنا» is for clarification, by which the benefit is completed, like His saying: {وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ} [الإخلاص: 4]. This is nothing, because if he makes it for clarification then it is attached to an omitted word, and if so «لنا» becomes part of another sentence, so the sentence of mubtadaʾ and khabar remains not independent in benefit; and it is not parallel to His saying {وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ}, for «له» in it is attached to «كفواً» itself, not to an omitted word, and it is parallel to "no one was a speaker for Bakr", where «لبكر» is attached to the khabar itself.
Is this question in its true sense? There are two views; the more evident: yes, and by "the matter" they mean victory and prevailing. The second: that it has the meaning of negation, as though they said: "We have nothing of the matter, that is of victory"; to this Qatāda and Ibn Jurayj went. But this is weakened by His saying: {قُلْ إِنَّ الأمر كُلَّهُ للَّهِ}, for whoever negates something from himself is not answered by affirming it for another, because he acknowledges that; unless another affirmative sentence is implied with this sentence, as though they said: "We have nothing of the matter; rather it belongs to the one who compelled us to go out and carried us to it"; then the answer with His saying {قُلْ إِنَّ الأمر كُلَّهُ للَّهِ} is good for this saying of theirs.
This responsive sentence is parenthetical between the sentences that came after His saying {وَطَآئِفَةٌ}, for His saying {يُخْفُونَ في أَنْفُسِهِم}, and likewise the second «يقولون», is either a khabar about «طائفة» or a ḥāl from what is before it.
The group read «كلَّه» in the accusative, and there are two aspects: the more evident, that it is emphasis for the noun of «إن». The second, which Makkī related from al-Akhfash, that it is a badal for it, and it is not clear. «لله» is the khabar of «إنْ». Abū ʿAmr read «كلُّه» in the nominative, and there are two aspects: the better known, that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «لله» its khabar, and the sentence the khabar of «إنَّ», as in "indeed Zayd's property, all of it, is with him". The second: that it is emphasis upon the position, for the noun of «إنَّ» is originally nominative as a mubtadaʾ; this is the position of al-Zajjāj and al-Jarmī, who run all the followers in the course of conjunction (ʿaṭf al-nasaq), so «لله» is also a khabar of «إنَّ». «يُخْفون» is either a khabar of «طائفة» or a ḥāl from what is before it, as has preceded. As for «يقولون», it admits these two aspects, and it may be an explanation of His saying «يُخْفون», in which case it has no position.
His saying: {مَّا قُتِلْنَا}: the response of «لو», and it came in the more eloquent usage: when its response is negated with «ما», most often there is no lām, and in the affirmative the reverse. His saying {لَوْ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ الأمر شَيْءٌ} is like His saying {هَل لَّنَا مِنَ الأمر مِن شَيْءٌ}, and the sound one of the two aspects is already known.
Al-Zamakhsharī parsed these sentences occurring after His saying {وَطَآئِفَةٌ} in an i'rab that led to the mubtadaʾ being left without a khabar, and his text must be cited so that it becomes clear. May Allah have mercy on him, he said: "If you say: what are the positions of these sentences after His saying «وطائفة»? I say: «قد أهَمَّتْهُمْ» is an adjective of «طائفة», and «يظنون» is another adjective or a ḥāl, in the sense: 'their own selves have worried them, while thinking', or a resumption by way of explanation of the sentence before it, and «يقولون» is a badal from «يظنون». If you say: how is it sound that what is a question about the matter occur as a badal for the report of thinking? I say: their question arose from the thinking, so it is permissible to substitute it for it. «يُخفون» is a ḥāl from «يقولون», and {قُلْ إِنَّ الأمر كُلَّهُ للَّهِ} is parenthetical between the ḥāl and its owner, and «يقولون» is a badal for «يُخْفون», and the best is that it be resumptive." End of his words. This, from Abū l-Qāsim, is built on the khabar being omitted, as I laid out for you [in] "and among you a group", because it is a place of itemisation.
His saying: {لَبَرَزَ}: came in the more eloquent usage, namely the presence of the lām in its response when affirmative. The majority read «لبرز» lightened, active voice; Abū Ḥaywa read «لبُرِّز» with shadda, passive voice, making it transitive by doubling. «كَتَب» was also read in the active voice, the agent being Allah the Exalted, with «القتلَ» a direct object; and al-Ḥasan read «القتالُ» nominative.
His saying: {وَلِيَبْتَلِيَ}: There are five aspects in it. One: that it is attached to a verb before it, its implied form being: "Allah made fighting obligatory for you and did not help you on the day of Uḥud, so that He might test what is in your breasts"; and it was said: to a verb after it, that is: "so that He might test, He did these things". It was said: the wāw is redundant and the lām is attached to what is before it. It was said: «وليبتلي» is conjoined to the first «ليبتلي», and was repeated only because of the length of the speech, so «وليمحِّص» was conjoined to it; so said Ibn Baḥr. It was said: it is conjoined to an omitted cause, its implied form being: "so that Allah may decide His affair and so that He may test". And he made what the testing relates to be what the breasts enfold, and what the breast enfolds is the heart, by His saying {القلوب التي فِي الصدور} [الحج: 46]; and he made what purification (tamḥīṣ) relates to, which is clarifying, to be what is in the heart, namely intentions and beliefs.

semin-durr:80-80.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ يَأْمُرَكُمْ}: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read «يأمركم» in the accusative and the rest in the nominative; Abū ʿAmr follows his principle of permitting sukūn on the rāʾ and ikhtilās (partial vowel). The latter is a clear reading, easy to explain in construction and meaning, in that it is on cutting-off and resumption: the Exalted informed that this command does not occur. The agent in it has two possibilities: one, that it is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted; the second, that it is the pronoun of «بَشَر», described as preceded. The meaning, on its referring to «بَشَر», is that it does not occur from a human being described with what he was described with, that he make himself a lord to be worshipped, nor that he command that the angels and the prophets be worshipped instead of Allah; so he is denied calling people to the worship of himself and to the worship of anyone else. And the meaning, on its referring to Allah the Exalted, is that He informed that He did not command that, so Allah's command, and His prophets' command, to worship other than Him the Exalted is negated.
As for the accusative reading, there are [views] in it. One: the saying of Abū ʿAlī and others, that the meaning is: "nor is it for him to command you", so they implied that «أَنْ» is implied after «لا» and that «لا» emphasizes the preceding meaning of negation, as you say: «ما كان من زيد إتيانٌ ولا قيام», meaning the negation of each of the two from Zayd; so «لا» is for emphasis of the preceding meaning of negation, and the meaning of the speech remains: "There was from Zayd no coming and from him no standing."
Second: that its accusative is because of its being conjoined to «يُؤْتِيَه». Sībawayh said: "The meaning is: it is not for a human being to command you to take the angels." Al-Wāḥidī said: "What strengthens this view is what we mentioned, that the Jews said to the Prophet ﷺ: 'Do you want, O Muḥammad, that we take you as a lord?' so it was revealed."
Third: that it is conjoined to «يقول» in the reading of the majority; al-Ṭabarī said this. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is an error with which the meaning does not cohere." Abū Muḥammad did not make clear the aspect of the error nor the incoherence of meaning. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "The aspect of the error is that if it is conjoined to «يقول» and «لا» is made for negation by way of founding and not by way of emphasis, then it is impossible to imply the accusative-governing «أنْ» except before the negative «لا»; and when he implies it before it, there is formed from it and the verb negated by «لا» a negated maṣdar, so the meaning becomes: 'It is not for a human being described with what he was described with that his command to take the angels and the prophets as lords be negated'; and if the negation of the command to that is not for him, then the affirmation of the command to that is for him, which is a manifest error. But if he makes «لا» for emphasizing the negation and not for founding it, then neither error nor incoherence of meaning follows, in that the negation becomes drawn over the two maṣdars whose occurrence is implied, so His saying {كُونُواْ عِبَاداً لِّي} is negated and likewise his command to take the angels and prophets as lords is negated. What makes this meaning clear is putting «غير» in the place of «لا». If you say 'ما لزيد فقهُ ولا نحوٌ', «لا» is for emphasis of the negation and both attributes are negated from him; and if you made «لا» for founding the negation it would mean «غير», so the meaning would become the negation of jurisprudence from him and the affirmation of grammar for him, for if you said 'ما لزيد فقه وغيرُ نحو' there would be in that an affirmation of grammar for him, as though you said: 'He has nothing but grammar'. Do you not see that if you say 'جئتُ بلا زادٍ', the meaning is 'I came without provisions', and if you say 'ما جئت بغير زادٍ', its meaning is that you came with provisions, because «لا» here is for founding the negation? So Ibn ʿAṭiyya's absolute statement of error and incoherence of meaning applies only on one of the two suppositions, namely that «لا» is for founding the negation and not for emphasizing it, and that it is of the conjunction of what is negated with «لا» onto the affirmed element upon which the negation enters, as in: 'ما أريد أن تجهل وأن لا تتعلم', meaning 'I do not want that you do not learn'." End.
Al-Zamakhsharī followed al-Ṭabarī in conjoining «يَأْمركم» to «يقول», and allowed two views for the «لا» entering it: one, that it is for founding the negation; the second, that it is added for emphasizing it. He said: "«ولا يأمركم» was read in the accusative, conjoined to «ثم يقول», and there are two views in it. One: that you make «لا» added to emphasize the meaning of negation in His saying {مَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ}; and the meaning is: it is not for a human being whom Allah appoints as a prophet and installs to call to singling out Allah for worship and abandoning the rivals, then to command people to be servants of him, and to command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords, like your saying: 'It is not for Zayd that I honour him and then he insult me or belittle me.' The second: that you make «لا» not added, and the meaning is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to forbid Quraysh from worshipping the angels, and the Jews and the Christians from worshipping ʿUzayr and the Messiah; so when they said to him: 'Do we take you as a lord?' it was said to them: It is not for a human being whom Allah appoints as a prophet that he then command people to worship him and forbid you from worshipping the angels and the prophets." I say: what al-Zamakhsharī brought is sound speech and a clear meaning on both suppositions, whether «لا» is for founding the negation or for emphasizing it; so how can the Shaykh make al-Ṭabarī's statement invalid on one of the suppositions, namely its being for founding the negation? Thus, praise be to Allah, the soundness of al-Ṭabarī's statement has appeared by the statement of Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī, and it has appeared that Ibn ʿAṭiyya's rebuttal of him is rejected.
People have preferred the nominative reading over the accusative. Sībawayh said: "«ولا يأمركم» is cut off from what precedes them, because the meaning is: and Allah does not command you." Al-Wāḥidī said: "Among what indicates the cutting-off from the first is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «ولَنْ يأمركم»." Al-Farrāʾ said: "This is evidence of its being cut off from the conjunction and that it is resumptive; so when [lā] fell in the place of lan, it made the verb nominative, as the Exalted said: {إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ بالحق بَشِيراً وَنَذِيراً وَلاَ تُسْأَلُ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الجحيم} [البقرة: 119], and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «ولن تُسْأل»." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The reading in the nominative as a start of speech is more apparent, and it is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «ولن يأمركم»." End.
It has already preceded that the pronoun in «يأمركم» may refer back to «الله» and may refer back to the human being described as preceded, who is meant to be the Prophet ﷺ or something more general than that, whether «ولا يأمركم» is read in the nominative or in the accusative when we make it conjoined to «يؤتيه»; but if we make it conjoined to «يقول», the pronoun refers back to «بشر» only. What I have said is supported by what some of them said: "The aspect of the accusative reading is that it be conjoined to the accusative verb before it, so the nominative pronoun is for «بشر» and nothing else," meaning by "what is before it" «ثم يقولَ». When Sībawayh mentioned the nominative reading he made the pronoun refer to Allah the Exalted and mentioned nothing else; it may be that this is the more apparent view with him, and it may be that nothing else is allowed, and the first is the better.
Some of them said: "In the accusative pronoun in «يأمركم», on both readings, there is a departure from the third person to the second person by way of iltifāt." I say: it seems he imagined that since the mention of the people preceded in His saying {ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ}, the composition should have been «ولا يأمرهم» in keeping with what preceded; but it is not so; rather this is a beginning of address in which there is no iltifāt.
His saying: {بَعْدَ إِذْ أَنْتُمْ مُّسْلِمُونَ}: «بعد» is attached to يأمركم, and «بعد» is an adverbial of time annexed to an adverbial of past time, and it has preceded that only time is annexed to it, such as حينئذٍ and يومئذٍ; and {أَنْتُمْ مُّسْلِمُونَ} is in the position of genitive by annexation, because «إذ» is annexed to a clause absolutely, whether nominal or verbal.

semin-durr:153-153.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ}: As for the governor of «إذ», it is said to be implied, i.e. "remember". Al-Zamakhsharī said: «صَرَفَكم إذ ليبتلِيَكم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be an adverb of «عَصَيْتُم» or «تنازَعْتم» or «فَشِلتم»." It is also said: it is an adverb of «عفَا عنكم». All these views are acceptable; its being an adverb of «صرفكم» is good from the aspect of meaning, and of «عفا» is good from the aspect of nearness. On some of the statements the issue belongs to the chapter of tanāzuʿ (competition of governors), and is on the basis of applying the last of them, because there is no pronoun in the first, and the competition is among more than two governors.

The majority read «تُصْعدون» with ḍamma on the تاء and kasra on the ʿayn, from aṣʿada fī al-arḍ, when he went off in it, the hamza in it being for entering, as in «أصْبح زيدٌ» (Zayd entered the morning); so the meaning is "when you were entering into ascent (ṣuʿūd)". This is made clear by the reading of Ubayy: «تُصْعِدون في الوادي» ("you were going up the valley"). Al-Ḥasan and al-Sulamī read «تَصْعَدون», from ṣaʿida fī al-jabal, i.e. he climbed. The combination of the two readings is that they first went up (aṣʿadū) in the valley, and then when the enemy pressed them, they climbed (ṣaʿidū) the mountain; and this is according to the view of whoever distinguishes between aṣʿada and ṣaʿida. Abū Ḥaywa read «تَصَعَّدُون» with doubling, the origin being tataṣaʿʿadūn, so one of the two tāʾs was dropped, either the tāʾ of the imperfect or the tāʾ of tafaʿʿala; and the combination of his reading and the reading of others is as above. The majority read «تُصْعِدون» with the tāʾ of second person; Ibn Muḥayṣin, and it is also related from Ibn Kathīr, with the yāʾ of third person, on iltifāt, and it is good; and it is possible that the pronoun refer back to the believers, i.e. "and Allah is possessed of bounty upon the believers when they were going up", so the governor in «إذ» is «فَضْل».

One says: aṣʿada, i.e. he went far in going; al-Qutabī said: "as if he went far like the distance of ascending." The poet said:

1466 - ألا أيُّهذا السائلي أينَ أَصْعَدَتْ ... فإنَّ لَها في أهل يَثْربَ مَوْعدا
(O you who ask me where she has gone off to: she has an appointment among the people of Yathrib.)

And another said:

1467 - قد كُنْتِ تبكين على الإِصعادِ ... فاليومَ سُرِّحْتِ وصاح الحادي
(You used to weep over the setting out; today you have been sent off, and the camel-driver cries out.)

Al-Farrāʾ and Abū Ḥātim said: "Al-iṣʿād is the beginning of the journey and the departure, while al-ṣuʿūd is the maṣdar of ṣaʿida [when] he climbed from low to high", so these distinguished between ṣaʿida and aṣʿada. Al-Mufaḍḍal said: "ṣaʿida, ṣaʿʿada and aṣʿada are of one meaning, and al-ṣaʿīd is the surface of the earth."

{وَلاَ تَلْوُونَ}: the majority read «تلْوون» with two wāws. It was also read with the first replaced by a hamza, in dislike of the meeting of two wāws, but this is not analogical because the ḍamma is incidental; and a wāw with ḍamma is replaced by a hamza under conditions mentioned before in al-Baqara: that the ḍamma not be incidental, as in this word; that it not be an augment, as in «تَرَهْوَك»; that it not be possible to lighten it, as in «سُوُر» and «نُوُر», plurals of siwār and nuwār, since it is possible to make it quiescent and say suwr and nuwr so that the wording is lightened; and that it not be assimilated into another, as in «تَعَوُّد», the maṣdar of taʿawwada. So the like of «فُوُوج» is regularly replaced, the conditions being complete.

The meaning of «لا تَلْوون» is: you do not turn back. One says «لَوَى به», i.e. he went off with it, and «لَوَى عليه»: he turned to it. He said:

1468 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أخو الجَهْد لا يَلْوي على مَنْ تَعَذَّرا
(... the one in distress does not turn back for whoever falls behind.)

The origin of «تَلْوون» is talwiyūn, which underwent weakening by dropping the lām; this has already gone before in His saying {يَلْوُونَ أَلْسِنَتَهُمْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 78].

Al-Aʿmash read, and it is also related from ʿĀṣim, «تُلْوون» with ḍamma on the تاء, from alwā, which is a dialectal form of «لَوَى», so faʿala and afʿala are of one meaning. Al-Ḥasan read «تَلُون» with a single wāw, and they analysed it as: he replaced the wāw with a hamza, then transferred the vowel of the hamza to the lām, then dropped the hamza by the rule, so nothing remained of the word but the fāʾ, which is the lām. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "One of the two wāws was dropped because of the two quiescents," though he had earlier said that this reading is built on the dialect of those who put a hamza for the wāw and transfer the vowel; and this is strange: after making it of the chapter of transferring the vowel of the hamza, how does he go back and say that one of the two wāws was dropped? The reading of al-Ḥasan can be analysed in two other ways. One: it may be said that the ḍamma was found heavy on the wāw because it is its sister, as if three wāws had met, so the ḍamma was transferred to the lām and two quiescents met, the wāw which is the ʿayn of the word and the wāw which is the pronoun, so the first was dropped for the meeting of two quiescents; had Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it thus it would have been better. The second: that «تَلُون» is the imperfect of «ولِيَ كذا» from wilāya (authority), and it is made transitive with «على» only because it is made to include the meaning of turning to.

Ḥumayd ibn Qays read «على أُحُد» with two ḍammas, meaning the mountain, the meaning being "upon the one on Mount Uḥud", namely the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The well-known reading is stronger, because he was not on the mountain until after the people had fled from him, while their going up occurred while he was calling them."

His saying: {والرسول يَدْعُوكُمْ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, the governor in it being «تَلْوُون».

His saying: {فَأَثَابَكُمْ}: two views. One: that it is conjoined to «تُصْعِدون» and «تَلْوون»; it does no harm that these are imperfect, because they are past in meaning, since «إذ» annexed to them made them past, so it is as if the meaning were "when you went up and turned". The second: that it is conjoined to «صَرَفكم». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «فأثابكم» is conjoined to «صَرَفَكم». There is remoteness in it, because of the length of separation. On its fāʿil there are two statements: one, that it is the Creator the Exalted; the second, that it is the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The pronoun in «فأثابكم» may refer to the Messenger, i.e. he shared with you in the distress, and as what befell him of the breaking of his incisor distressed you, what befell you of the loss of the spoils distressed him."

And «غَمَّاً» is a second object, and as for «بغمٍّ» several views are possible for the bāʾ. One: that it is causal, in the sense that what the first distress relates to is the Companions, and what the second distress relates to is the killing of the polytheists on the day of Badr, the meaning being: "so He repaid you with distress for the distress which He brought about through your hands upon the disbelievers on the day of Badr."

It is also said: "What the distress relates to is the Messenger, and the meaning: Allah made you taste distress because of the distress you caused the Messenger and the believers by your faltering"; or "the Messenger repaid you", i.e. he shared with you distress because of a distress you felt on his account. The second: that the bāʾ is of accompaniment, i.e. distress accompanied by distress, and the two distresses are for the Companions: the first distress being the defeat and killing; the second, Khālid's coming upon them with the cavalry of the disbelievers, or the rumour of the killing of the Messenger, peace be upon him. On the first, the bāʾ is attached to «أَثَابكم»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is said: the meaning is 'because of a distress', so it is a mafʿūl bihi." On the second it is attached to an omitted element, because it is an attribute of «غَمّ», i.e. distress accompanied by distress, or mixed with distress. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that the bāʾ be in the sense of «بعد» (after) or in the sense of «بَدَل» (instead), and made it in these two views an attribute of «غَمَّا»; but its being in the sense of «بعد» or «بدل» is remote, and he seems to intend an explanation of the meaning; likewise al-Zamakhsharī said: "distress after distress."

And His saying {فَأَثَابَكُمْ}: is it literal or figurative? It is said to be figurative, as if He made distress stand in the place of the reward that would have come about had it not been for the flight; so it is like his saying:

1469 - أخافُ زياداً أَنْ يكونَ عَطاؤُه ... أداهِمَ سُوداً أو مُحَدْرَجَةً سُمْرا
(I fear that Ziyād's gift will be black fetters or tightly-twisted brown whips.)

and his saying:

1470 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تحيةُ بيْنِهم ضَرْبٌ وَجِيعُ
(... their greeting among themselves is a painful beating.)

He made fetters and whips stand in the position of a gift, and beating in the position of a greeting. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Al-ithāba here is in the sense of punishment (muʿāqaba)," and that returns to the figurative.

His saying: {لِّكَيْلاَ}: this is the lām of «كي», and it is a lām of genitive, while the accusative here is by «كي», so that a preposition does not have to enter upon its like. There are two statements on what this lām is attached to. One: that it is «فأثابكم»; on this there are two views on «لا». One: that it is redundant, because grief's non-occurrence does not follow from distress, and the meaning is: He distressed them in order to grieve them as a punishment for them for leaving their positions; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it. The second view: that it is not redundant; al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its meaning is: so that you may not grieve, that you might be trained in swallowing distresses and become accustomed to bearing hardships, so that you do not grieve afterwards over a benefit missed nor over a harm that befalls." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The meaning: what befell you was by your own offence, so you yourselves entangled yourselves, and it is the habit of mankind to be patient with punishment when they have offended; its anxiety increases only when one thinks oneself innocent."

The second: that the lām is attached to «عَفا», because His pardon removed all grief. There is remoteness in it because of the length of separation.

semin-durr:178-178.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي}: The majority read «يَحْسَبَنَّ» in the third person, Ḥamza in the second person. Al-Zajjāj related from a great many people a reading like Ḥamza's, except that they put kasra on «إنما» and made «خيراً» accusative, and Ibn Mujāhid denied it; clarification of that will come. Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb read it in the third person with kasra on «إنما», and al-Zamakhsharī also related from him that he read with kasra on the first «إنما» and fatḥa on the second, with the third person. These are five readings.
As for the reading of the majority, its analysis is plain: the verb may be ascribed to «الذين», and «أنَّ» with what is attached to it fills the place of the two objects according to Sībawayh, and the place of one of them with the other omitted according to al-Akhfash, as has preceded more than once. It may also be ascribed to a third-person pronoun by which the Prophet ﷺ is meant, that is: "let not the Prophet, peace be upon him, suppose"; on this «الذين كفروا» is the first object. As for the second, discussion of it will come in the reading of Ḥamza, so on this aspect this reading coincides with the reading of Ḥamza, may Allah have mercy on him, whose analysis will come. «ما» may be a relative noun, in which case the returning pronoun is omitted since the conditions are fulfilled, that is: "that what We prolong"; or it may be a maṣdar particle, that is: "Our prolonging", and it is the noun of «أنَّ» and «خير» its khabar. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is not permissible that it be a restraining or a redundant particle, for if it were so, «خيرٌ» would be accusative by «نُمْلي», and «أنَّ» would need a khabar if «ما» were redundant, or the verb would be implied to follow it, and both are impossible." End of quotation. This is among the plain matters. They wrote «أنما» joined in both places, though the first, by right, should be written separately because it is a relative.
As for the reading of Ḥamza, the views and analyses of people were unsettled about it, so much so that it was transmitted from Abū Ḥātim that it is a solecism. Al-Naḥḥās said: "A great many people followed him in that", and this is not to be heeded, because of its continuous transmission. There are six aspects in its analysis. One: that the agent of «تحسَبَنَّ» is the pronoun of the Prophet ﷺ, {الذين كَفَرُواْ} the first object, and {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ} the second object. On this analysis a muḍāf must be omitted: either from the first, its implied form being "do not suppose the condition of those who disbelieved", or from the second, its implied form being "the possessors of 'that Our prolonging is good for them'". We needed this interpretation only because «أنما نُمْلي» is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, and the maṣdar is a notion that does not apply to «الذين كفروا», and the second object in this chapter is the first in meaning.
Two: that {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ} is a badal for {الذين كَفَرُواْ}. To this al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ went, and a group followed them, among them al-Zamakhsharī, al-Zajjāj and Ibn al-Bādhish.
Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: "The aspect of this reading is repetition and emphasis, and the implied form is: 'do not suppose those who disbelieved, and do not suppose that We prolong'." Al-Farrāʾ said: "And its like is {هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ الساعة أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ} [الزخرف: 66], that is: they only wait for it to come to them." End of quotation. Some have rejected the statement of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, saying that omitting the second object in these verbs is not permissible according to anyone; this rejection is nothing, because what is forbidden is only omission for the sake of restriction (ḥadhf al-iqtiṣār), and verification of that has preceded. Ibn al-Bādhish said: "The second object is omitted because the speech indicates it, and the implied form is: 'do not suppose that those who disbelieved have the goodness of Our prolonging for them established or occurring'."
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is the coming of a badal sound when only one of the two objects is mentioned, and restricting a verb of supposing to one object is not permissible? I say: that is sound because reliance is on the badal, and the substituted-for is in the ruling of the set-aside. Do you not see that you say 'I put your goods, some of them on top of others', although silence on 'goods' alone is impossible?"
Is the badal a badal of inclusion, which is the apparent sense, or a badal of the whole for the whole, in which case it would be on the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being "do not suppose the prolonging of those", omitting «إملاء» and substituting «أنما نملي» for it? Two well-known views.
Three, the strangest of them: that «الذين» is the agent of «تَحْسَبَنَّ», on the interpretation that the tāʾ in the verb is for the feminine, as in His saying: {كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ} [الشعراء: 105], that is: "let not the people who disbelieved suppose", and «الذين» an attribute of «القوم», as in His saying {وَأَوْرَثْنَا القوم الذين كَانُواْ} [الأعراف: 137]. On this, this reading coincides with the reading with the third person, and its analysis is like its analysis. Abū l-Qāsim al-Kirmānī mentioned that in his exegesis called «al-Lubāb». There is room for objection in it, in that «الذين» runs in the course of the sound masculine plural, and the sound masculine plural does not allow feminising its verb according to the Basrans: it is not permissible to say "qāmat al-Zaydūn" nor "taqūmu l-Zaydūn". As for his excuse for this, that «الذين» is an attribute of «القوم», whose verb may be feminised, and that it was omitted, it does not help him, because consideration is given to what is pronounced, not what is implied; none of the Basrans allows "qāmat al-muslimūn" on the intention "the people, the Muslims" at all. Abū l-Ḥasan al-Ḥawfī said: "«أنَّ» and what it governs is in the position of accusative as a badal, «الذين» is the first object, and the second is omitted", which is the meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's statement above.
Four: that {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ} is a badal of inclusion for {الذين كَفَرُواْ}, that is "Our prolonging", and «خيرٌ» in the nominative is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is "it is good for themselves", and the sentence is the second object. Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Shāma transmitted that from some. He said: I say: and like this reading is the verse of the Ḥamāsa:
1496 - مِنَّا الأَناةُ وبعضُ القوم يَحْسَبُنا ... أنَّا بِطاءٌ وفي إبطائنا سَرَعُ
(Deliberation is ours, and some of the people think us slow, while in our slowness there is speed.)
Thus the narration came, with fatḥa on «أنَّا» after the mention of the first object. On this it is permissible to say "ḥasibtu Zaydan annahu qāʾimun", that is, "I supposed him a possessor of standing". The aspect of the fatḥa is that it occurs as an object, and it and what it governs are in the position of a singular, which is the second object of «حسبت». End of quotation. There is room for objection in what he said, because the grammarians stated explicitly that kasra of «إنَّ» is obligatory when it occurs as a second object and the first is a name of a concrete thing, and they cited the aforementioned verse for that, and justified the obligation of kasra by saying that if we put fatḥa it would be in the position of a maṣdar, so predicating the meaning about the concrete thing would be necessary.
Five: that {الذين كَفَرُواْ} is the first object, and {إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ ليزدادوا إِثْمَاً} is in the position of the second object, and {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ} is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, inserted parenthetically between the two objects of «تَحْسَبَنَّ», with fronting and delaying in the speech. That was transmitted from al-Akhfash. Abū Ḥātim said: "I heard al-Akhfash mention the fatḥa of «أَنَّ», arguing by it for the people of qadar (the Qadariyya), because he was one of them, and he placed it on fronting and delaying, as though he said: 'do not suppose those who [disbelieved], "We only prolong for them that they may increase in sin"; that We prolong for them is good for themselves'." End of quotation. It is permissible that the opening «أَنَّ» with fatḥa be used to begin the speech only because that is the position of al-Akhfash, while others forbid it; if its khabar precedes it, as in "in my opinion that you are departing", or the itemising «أما», as in "as for that you are departing, I have…", it is permissible by consensus. Abū Ḥātim's saying "he mentions the fatḥa of «أنَّ»" means by it the one in His saying {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ}. The aspect of the Qadariyya's holding to it is that Allah the Exalted may only prolong for them what is good for themselves, because, according to them, regard for what is most beneficial is obligatory.
[Six: al-Mahdawī said: "A group said:] {الذين كَفَرُواْ} was put first for emphasis, then their condition came from His saying {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ} as a refutation of them, and the implied form is: 'do not suppose that Our prolonging for those who disbelieved is good for themselves'." End of quotation.
As for the reading of Yaḥyā with kasra of «إنما» with the third person, it cannot but be that the verb is ascribed either to «الذين» or to a third-person pronoun. If the first, then «إنما» and what is within its scope is suspended (muʿallaqa) from «يحسبن», and if the lām is not in its khabar in wording it is implied, so «إنما» with kasra is in the position of accusative, because it is suspended from the verb of supposing with the lām intended; its parallel is the suspension of verbs of the heart from two explicit objects by the implying of the lām of inception, in his saying:
1497 - كذاك أُدِّبْتُ حتى صار مِنْ خُلُقي ... إني رأيتُ مِلاكُ الشيمةِ الأَدَبُ
(Thus was I disciplined until it became part of my character: I have seen that the mainstay of good nature is discipline.)
Were it not for the implying of the lām, the accusative of «مِلاك» and «الأدب» would have been obligatory; and likewise in the verse, were it not for the implying of the lām, fatḥa of «إنما» would have been obligatory. It is also possible that the first object is omitted, namely the pronoun of the affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), and this was said in the verse and is the best in it, the origin being "let him not suppose it", that is, the matter, and «إنما نُمْلِي» is in the position of the second object and is the explanation of the pronoun.
If the second, then «الذين» is the first object and «إنما نملي» is in the position of the second.
As for his reading which al-Zamakhsharī related from him, he analysed it himself, saying: "In the sense: 'let not those who disbelieved suppose that Our prolonging is for the increase of sin, as they do, but it is so that they repent and enter into faith'; and His saying {إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ لأَنْفُسِهِمْ} is parenthetical between the verb and its governed word, its meaning being: Our prolonging is good for themselves if they act on it and know Allah's favour to them in extending the period and leaving off hastening the punishment." End of quotation. On this «الذين» is the agent, «أنما» with fatḥa fills the place of the two objects or of one of them, depending on the disagreement, and this sentence is inserted parenthetically between the verb and its governed word. Al-Naḥḥās said: "The reading of Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb with kasra of «إنَّ» is good, as you say: 'ḥasibtu ʿAmran abūhu khārijun'."
As for what al-Zajjāj related as a reading from a great many, which is the accusative of «خيراً» in the apparent sense of his words, he himself mentioned its analysis on the basis that {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْراً لأَنْفُسِهِمْ} is a badal for «الذين», and «خيراً» is the second object. His text must be cited so that it becomes clear to you. May Allah have mercy on him, he said: "Whoever read «ولا تَحْسَبَنَّ» with the tāʾ, only kasra of «إنَّ» was permissible according to the Basrans, and the meaning: 'do not suppose, those who disbelieved: Our prolonging is good for them', and «إنَّ» entered as emphasis; and if you put fatḥa the meaning becomes: 'do not suppose those who disbelieved — Our prolonging — to be good for them'." He said: "And it is permissible, in my view, in this place, as a badal for «الذين»: the meaning: 'do not suppose Our prolonging for those who disbelieved to be good for them', and a great many have read it, and like this reading in poetry is:
1498 - فما كانَ قَيْسٌ هُلْكُه هلكَ واحدٍ ... ولكنه بنيانُ قومٍ تَهَدَّما
(Qays's death was not the death of one man, but the structure of a people collapsed.)
He made «هُلْكُه» a badal for «قيس»; the meaning: 'the death of Qays was not the death of one man'; that is, the first «هُلْك» is a badal for the nominative, leaving «هُلْكَ واحدٍ» accusative as the khabar of «كان». Likewise {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ}: «أن» and its noun, which is the relative «ما» with its ṣila, and the khabar, which is «لهم», are in the position of accusative as a badal for «الذين كفروا», leaving «خيراً» accusative as the second object of «تحسبن»."
Al-Fārisī, however, rejected this from Abū Isḥāq, saying that no one read this reading, I mean the accusative of «خيراً». Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said: "The badal is valid only with the accusative of «خير», since it is the second object of «حسبت»; so as «هلك واحدٍ» in the verse became accusative, when the first was substituted for «قيس», because it is a khabar of «كان», so «خيراً لهم» becomes accusative when «الإملاء» is substituted for {الذين كَفَرُواْ}, because it is a second object of «تحسبَنَّ»." He said: "I asked Aḥmad ibn Mūsā about it and he claimed that no one read it" — by this Aḥmad he means Abū Bakr ibn Mujāhid, the famous imam.
He said in his «al-Ḥujja»: "«الذين كفروا» is in the position of accusative as the first object of «أنَّ», and the second object is the first in this chapter in meaning; so fatḥa of «أنَّ» in His saying {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ} is not permissible, because their being prolonged for is not the same as them." He said: "If you say: why is fatḥa of «أنَّ» not permissible, making it a badal for {الذين كَفَرُواْ}, like His saying {وَمَآ أَنْسَانِيهُ إِلاَّ الشيطان أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُ} [الكهف: 63], and as «أنَّ» is in His saying, the Exalted, {وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ الله إِحْدَى الطائفتين أَنَّهَا لَكُمْ} [الأنفال: 7]? It is said: that is not permissible, otherwise you would have to make «خيراً» accusative, on the implied form: do not suppose the prolonging of those who disbelieved to be good for themselves, since it is the second object of «تحسبنَّ»; and it was said that no one read it so. If it is not made accusative it is known that the badal is not valid in it, and if the badal is not valid, only kasra of «إنَّ» is permissible, making «إنَّ» and its khabar in the position of the second object of «تحسبن»." End of what he rejected it with. So nothing remains but to weigh between the transmission of these two men, I mean al-Zajjāj and Ibn Mujāhid. There is no doubt that Ibn Mujāhid was more attentive to the readings, but al-Zajjāj is reliable and says "a great many read it", and this makes his error in it remote; and affirmation takes precedence over denial. As for what Abū ʿAlī mentioned in his saying "and if the badal is not permissible only kasra of «إنَّ» is permissible" to the end, this also is among what no one read. Makkī said: "The aspect of the reading for whoever read with the tāʾ, I mean the tāʾ of address, is to put kasra on «إنما», so the sentence would be in the position of the second object; and no one read it so, as far as I know."
Abū l-Baqāʾ transmitted the accusative of «خيراً» as an irregular reading; he said: "It has been read irregularly with the accusative, so that «لأنفسهم» is the khabar of «أنَّ», and «لهم» is a clarification or a ḥāl from «خيراً»", meaning that when he made the good for themselves, he made «لهم» either a clarification, its implied form being "I mean, for them", or a ḥāl from the postponed indefinite noun, because it was originally an adjective of it. The apparent sense on this reading is what I presented earlier, namely that «لهم» is the khabar, and «لأنفسهم» is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «خيراً», as it was an adjective of it in the reading of the majority. He also transmitted the reading with kasra of «إنَّ», which is the reading of Yaḥyā, and analysed it as the response of an omitted oath, the oath and its response filling the place of the two objects; there is no need for that, and rather its analysis as preceded is preferable, because the origin is the absence of omission.
Imlāʾ is giving respite and extending life; from it comes "malāwat al-dahr" for a long period, and "al-malawān" are night and day, and their saying "malāka llāhu bi-niʿma" means "He granted it to you for a long life". It was said: al-malawān is the recurrence of night and day and their extension, on the evidence of their being annexed to the two in the poet's saying:
1499 - نهارٌ وليلٌ دائمٌ مَلَواهُما ... على كلِّ حالِ المرءِ يَخْتلفان
(Day and night, their succession constant, alternate upon every state of man.)
Were they the night and the day, they would not be annexed to them, since a thing is not annexed to itself. His saying {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ}: the origin of the yāʾ is wāw, and it was turned into yāʾ only because it occurs in the fourth position.
His saying: {إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ ليزدادوا}: It has already preceded that Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb read with kasra on the first and fatḥa on this one, in what al-Zamakhsharī transmitted from him, and its analysis has preceded. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān), however, said: "No one related it from him except al-Zamakhsharī; rather those who transmitted the reading of Yaḥyā transmitted only his kasra of the first." He said: "It is only that al-Zamakhsharī, because of his fondness for his doctrine, seeks to return everything to it." This is prejudice against him, because he is reliable and does not transmit what has not been narrated.
As for the reading with kasra of it, there are two aspects. One: that it is a resumptive sentence giving a reason for the sentence before it, as though it were said: "What is the matter with them that they suppose the prolonging to be good?" and it was said: "We only prolong for them that they may increase in sin." «إنَّ» here is restrained by «ما», and for that reason it was written joined, on the original. It is not permissible that it be a relative noun or a particle, because the lām of «kay» cannot occur as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ or its operators.
The second aspect: that this sentence is a repetition of the first. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It was said: «أنما» is a repetition of the first, and «ليزدادوا» is the second object of «تَحْسَبَنَّ», this on the reading with the tāʾ, and the implied form: 'do not suppose, O Muḥammad, the prolonging of those who disbelieved to be good so that they increase in sin, but so that they increase in faith', and it is narrated that some of the Companions read it so." End of quotation. I say: there is room for objection in this, in that he made «ليزدادوا» the second object, and it has already preceded that the lām of «kay» does not occur as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ nor of its operators; and because this is complete for him only on the supposition of fatḥa on the second, and it has preceded that no one transmitted it except al-Zamakhsharī from Yaḥyā, and the one who reads «تحسبن» with the tāʾ of address does not put fatḥa on it at all.
As for the lām in «ليزدادوا», there are two views about it. One: that it is the lām of «kay»; the second, that it is the lām of becoming (ṣayrūra).
His saying: {وَلَهْمُ عَذَابٌ} [Translator's note: the source prints «وَلَهْمُ» for «وَلَهُمْ»]: There are two views about this wāw. One: that it is for conjunction; the second: that it is for ḥāl. The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's saying is that it is for ḥāl only in the reading of Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb, for he said: "If you say: what is the meaning of this reading — meaning the reading of Yaḥyā that he transmitted from him — I say: its meaning is 'let him not suppose that Our prolonging is for the increase of sin and punishment', and the wāw is for ḥāl, as though it were said: 'that they may increase in sin, prepared for them being a humiliating punishment'." The Shaykh said, after what he mentioned of his denial of him for transmitting the fatḥa of the second from Yaḥyā as I presented to you: "When he established in this reading that the meaning rests on prohibiting the disbeliever from supposing that Allah prolongs only for the increase of sin, and that He prolongs only for the increase of good, his saying {وَلَهْمُ عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ} would contradict this explanation, so he analysed that with the wāw as ḥāl so that this contradiction between this reading and the end of the verse is removed."
The origin of «ليزدادوا» is "liyaztādū" with a tāʾ, because it is an iftiʿāl form from ziyāda, but the tāʾ of iftiʿāl is turned into dāl after three letters: zāy, dhāl and dāl, as in iddakara and iddāna. The verb here is transitive to one object, and originally it was transitive to two, as in {فَزَادَهُمُ الله مَرَضاً} [البقرة: 10], but with iftiʿāl it always loses an object: if the verb before being built on iftaʿala for the reflexive-passive sense was transitive to one, it becomes intransitive after the reflexive sense, as in "I extended the rope and it extended (famtadda)"; and if it was transitive to two, after iftiʿāl it becomes transitive to one, like this verse.
Each of these three verses ended with a description of the punishment different from the one the other ended with, for a fitting meaning. The first included the report of their hastening in disbelief, and hastening in something and hurrying to obtain it implies its importance and greatness, so their recompense was made "a great punishment" in correspondence to them, and that indicates the baseness of what they hastened into. The second included their buying disbelief with faith; the custom is that the buyer is delighted and pleased with what he bought, and when he loses he feels pain, so this verse ended with the pain of punishment, as the cheated buyer feels the pain of his loss. The third included prolonging, which is being given enjoyment of wealth and the adornment of the world, and that implies pride, arrogance and tyranny, so this verse ended with what implies their humiliation and abasement after their might and arrogance.

ukberi-tibyan:147-147.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَإِسْرَافَنَا فِي أَمْرِنَا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا وَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ (١٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the lām, on the view that the noun (ism) of كَانَ is what comes after «إِلَّا». This is stronger than making it the khabar (predicate) and the first the noun, for two reasons. The first: that (أَنْ قَالُوا) resembles the pronoun in that it cannot be described [by an adjective] [Translator's note: the text reads لَا يُضْمَرُ, "it is not made into a pronoun"; the usual wording of this argument is لَا يُوصَفُ, "it is not qualified by an adjective"], so it is more definite.
The second: that what comes after إِلَّا is affirmed, and the meaning is: their saying «رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا» was their habit in supplication. It is also read with the first in the nominative, on the view that it is the noun of كَانَ, and what comes after إِلَّا is the khabar. (فِي أَمْرِنَا): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar (verbal noun), which is إِسْرَافُنَا; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, i.e. "an excess occurring in our affair".

ukberi-tibyan:150-150.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَلِ اللَّهُ مَوْلَاكُمْ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ النَّاصِرِينَ (١٥٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَلِ اللَّهُ مَوْلَاكُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ permitted the accusative, and it is a reading; the implied form is: "Rather, obey Allah" (بَلْ أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ).

ukberi-tibyan:151-151.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَنُلْقِي فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الرُّعْبَ بِمَا أَشْرَكُوا بِاللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطَانًا وَمَأْوَاهُمُ النَّارُ وَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الظَّالِمِينَ (١٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الرُّعْبَ): it is read with sukūn on the ʿayn and with ḍamma on it, and they are two dialectal forms. (بِمَا أَشْرَكُوا): the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to نُلْقِي, and the fact that «فِي» is also attached to it does not prevent this, because فِي is locative while the bāʾ has the sense of cause, so the two are different. مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the second [مَا] is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, or has the sense of الَّذِي ("that which"), and is not maṣdariyya. (وَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الظَّالِمِينَ): i.e. the Fire; so the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted. مَثْوَى is a mafʿal from ثَوَيْتُ ("I dwelt"), and its final radical (lām) is a yāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:152-152.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ بِإِذْنِهِ حَتَّى إِذَا فَشِلْتُمْ وَتَنَازَعْتُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ وَعَصَيْتُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا أَرَاكُمْ مَا تُحِبُّونَ مِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيَا وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الْآخِرَةَ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَفَا عَنْكُمْ وَاللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (١٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (صَدَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ): صَدَقَ is transitive to two objects in a construction like this one, and it may be transitive to the second by means of a preposition, so one says صَدَقْتَ زَيْدًا فِي الْحَدِيثِ ("you told Zayd the truth in the account"). (إِذْ): an adverb (ẓarf) for صَدَقَ, and it may be an adverb for الْوَعْد. (حَتَّى): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "that continued until the time of your faltering". The correct view is that in a construction like this it is not attached to anything, and that it is not a preposition; rather, it is a particle that enters upon the clause with the meaning of limit (ghāya), just as the fāʾ and the wāw enter upon clauses. The apodosis (jawāb) of «إِذَا» is omitted, its implied form being: "your affair became clear"
and the like; what indicates the omitted element is His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيَا وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الْآخِرَةَ). (ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ): conjoined to the omitted verb.

ukberi-tibyan:153-153.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ وَلَا تَلْوُونَ عَلَى أَحَدٍ وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ فِي أُخْرَاكُمْ فَأَثَابَكُمْ غَمًّا بِغَمٍّ لِكَيْلَا تَحْزَنُوا عَلَى مَا فَاتَكُمْ وَلَا مَا أَصَابَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ (١٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ): its implied form is: "Remember when" (اذْكُرُوا إِذْ); and it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for عَصَيْتُمْ, or تَنَازَعْتُمْ, or فَشِلْتُمْ. (وَلَا تَلْوُونَ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ, and we have mentioned it at His saying: (يَلْوُونَ أَلْسِنَتَهُمْ). It is also read with ḍamma on the tāʾ, its past tense being أَلْوَى, and that is a dialectal form. It is also read: (عَلَى أُحُدٍ) with two ḍammas, and that is the mountain. [Translator's note: the text shows the word as أَحَدٍ with its usual vowelling; the reading meant is أُحُد, the mountain.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ): a clause in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (بِغَمٍّ): the implied form is: "after grief" (بَعْدَ غَمٍّ); on this view it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of غَمًّا. It is also said: the meaning is "because of the grief", so it would be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It is also said: the implied form is "in exchange for grief" (بَدَلَ غَمٍّ), so it would also be an adjective of غَمًّا.
(لِكَيْلَا تَحْزَنُوا): it is said that «لَا» is redundant (zāʾida), because the meaning is that He grieved them in order to sadden them, as a punishment for their abandoning their positions. It is also said that it is not redundant, and the meaning is the negation of sadness from them through repentance. كَيْ here is the one that governs by itself, because of the lām before it.

ukberi-tibyan:154-154.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْغَمِّ أَمَنَةً نُعَاسًا يَغْشَى طَائِفَةً مِنْكُمْ وَطَائِفَةٌ قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ يَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ ظَنَّ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ يَقُولُونَ هَلْ لَنَا مِنَ الْأَمْرِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ قُلْ إِنَّ الْأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ لِلَّهِ يُخْفُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ مَا لَا يُبْدُونَ لَكَ يَقُولُونَ لَوْ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ مَا قُتِلْنَا هَاهُنَا قُلْ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ لَبَرَزَ الَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَتْلُ إِلَى مَضَاجِعِهِمْ وَلِيَبْتَلِيَ اللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ (١٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمَنَةً): the well-known reading has fatḥa on the mīm, and it is a noun for "security" (al-amn). It is also read with sukūn on it, and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like الْأَمْر. (نُعَاسًا): a badal (substitute); it may be an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). It may also be that نُعَاسًا is the object and أَمَنَةً a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, the original being "He sent down upon you drowsiness possessing security" (نُعَاسًا ذَا أَمَنَةٍ), because drowsiness is not itself security; rather, it is that through which security came about. It may also be that أَمَنَة is an object [Translator's note: the text has أَمَنَةٌ in the nominative here, as a cited word]. (يَغْشَى): it is read with the yāʾ, on the view that it is the drowsiness [that overcomes], and with the tāʾ, referring to the أَمَنَة; it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of what precedes it. (طَائِفَةٌ) [Translator's note: the text vowels it طَائِفَةً in the accusative here, but it is discussing the nominative طَائِفَةٌ of the verse]: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ) is its khabar (predicate); «يَظُنُّونَ» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in أَهَمَّتْهُمْ. It may also be that أَهَمَّتْهُمْ is an adjective and يَظُنُّونَ the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl, the governing word being يَغْشَى; this wāw is called the wāw of the ḥāl. It is also said that the wāw has the sense of إِذْ ("when"), but that amounts to nothing.
(غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ): the first object, i.e. "a matter other than the truth", and بِاللَّهِ is the second. (ظَنَّ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ): a maṣdar, its implied form being: "a supposition resembling the supposition of the Jāhiliyya" [Translator's note: the text reads يُمَثِّلُ; the expected wording is مِثْلَ, "like"]. (مِنْ شَيْءٍ): مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida), and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ. On the khabar there are two views. The first: it is لَنَا, so on this view مِنَ الْأَمْرِ is a ḥāl, since the original is "Is there anything of the matter?" (هَلْ شَيْءٌ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ). The second: that مِنَ الْأَمْرِ is the khabar and لَنَا is for clarification (tabyīn), and the meaning is complete, as in His saying: (وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ). (كُلَّهُ لِلَّهِ): it is read in the accusative as a tawkīd (emphasis) or a badal, with لِلَّهِ as the khabar; and in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with لِلَّهِ as the khabar and the clause as the khabar of إِنَّ. (يَقُولُونَ): a ḥāl from the pronoun in يُخْفُونَ. (شَيْءٌ): the noun of كَانَ, and the khabar is لَنَا, or مِنَ الْأَمْرِ, as in «هَلْ لَنَا». (لَبَرَزَ الَّذِينَ): with fatḥa and without doubling [of the rāʾ]; and it is read with doubling (لَبُرِّزَ) as a verb whose agent is not named (passive), i.e. "they were brought out by the command of Allah".

ukberi-tibyan:156-156.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَقَالُوا لِإِخْوَانِهِمْ إِذَا ضَرَبُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَوْ كَانُوا غُزًّى لَوْ كَانُوا عِنْدَنَا مَا مَاتُوا وَمَا قُتِلُوا لِيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ حَسْرَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (١٥٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذَا ضَرَبُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ): it may be that إِذَا here is used to narrate their state, so the future is not necessarily intended by it; on this view قَالُوا may govern it, though it is past. It may also be that كَفَرُوا and قَالُوا are past [in form] while the future is intended by them, the present state being narrated through it; on this view the implied form is: "they disbelieve and say to their brothers".
(أَوْ كَانُوا غُزًّى): the majority read it with doubling of the zāy, and it is the plural of غَازٍ ("one who goes raiding"). The regular form would be غُزَاةٌ, like قَاضٍ and قُضَاةٌ, but it came on the pattern fuʿʿal by analogy with the sound [root], as in شَاهِدٌ / شُهَّدٌ and صَائِمٌ / صُوَّمٌ. It is also read with the zāy undoubled (غُزًى), and there are two views on it. The first: that its origin is غُزَاةٌ, and the hāʾ [i.e. the tāʾ marbūṭa] was dropped for lightness, because the tāʾ is an indication of the plural, and that has already been obtained from the adjective form itself.
